Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā

The Great Sub-commentary on the Visuddhimagga

(Dutiyo bhāgo)

(Second Part)

12. Iddhividhaniddesavaṇṇanā

12. Explanation of the Exposition on the Varieties of Supernormal Power

Abhiññākathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on Direct Knowledge

365. Saṃvaṇṇanāvasena [M 2.0001][V 2.0001] anantarasamādhikathāya āsannapaccakkhataṃ dīpento “ayaṃ samādhibhāvanā”ti āha. “Abhiññā sampādetuṃ yogo kātabbo”ti vatvā tattha payojanavisese dassetuṃ “evañhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi thiratarabhāvo, vipassanābhāvanāsukhatā ca samādhibhāvanāya ānisaṃso eva, tathāpi pañca lokiyābhiññā yathāvuttasamādhibhāvanāya ānisaṃsabhāvena pākaṭā paññātāti tāsaṃyeva vasena yogino adhigatānisaṃsatā vuttā, cuddasadhā cittaparidamanena thirataratā vuttā. Lokiyābhiññāsu vasībhāvopi samādhisseva vasībhāvo, tathā ca “samāhito yathābhūtaṃ pajānātī”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.5; 4.99; 5.1071; netti. 40; mi. pa. 2.1.14) vacanato [V 2.0002] “sukheneva paññābhāvanaṃ sampādessatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā samādhibhāvanāya ānisaṃsalābho thirataratā, sukheneva ca paññābhāvanā ijjhati, tasmā abhiññākathaṃ tāva ārabhissāma, paññābhāvanāya okāse sampattepīti adhippāyo.

365. By way of the explanatory commentary, wishing to show the nearness and direct perceptibility of the immediately preceding discourse on concentration, he said: 'This is the development of concentration.' Having said, 'Effort should be made to accomplish the direct knowledges,' the passage beginning 'For thus...' was stated to show the special purposes therein. Although the state of greater stability and the ease of developing insight are indeed benefits of the development of concentration, nevertheless, the five mundane direct knowledges are manifest and known as a benefit of the development of concentration as described. Therefore, it is by way of these very five that the yogi's state of having attained benefits is stated, and greater stability is stated through the fourteenfold subduing of the mind. Mastery over the mundane direct knowledges is also mastery over concentration itself, and so, from the saying, 'One who is concentrated knows things as they really are,' it is said, 'He will accomplish the development of wisdom with ease.' Therefore, since through the development of concentration the gain of benefits, greater stability, and the development of wisdom with ease are accomplished, for that reason we shall first begin the discourse on the direct knowledges, even though the opportunity for the development of wisdom has arrived—this is the intention.

Bhagavatā pañca lokikābhiññā vuttāti sambandho. Na catukkajjhānamattameva idha sāsane sampādetabbaṃ, napi iddhividhañāṇameva, atha kho aññampi atthīti uttaruttaripaṇītapaṇītadhammadesanatthañca.

The connection is that the five mundane direct knowledges were taught by the Blessed One. Here in this teaching, not only should the mere four jhānas be accomplished, nor only the knowledge of the varieties of supernormal power, but indeed, there is something else as well. And this is also for the purpose of teaching progressively more refined and sublime states.

Iddhivikubbananti [M 2.0002] iddhisaṅkhātaṃ pakativaṇṇajahanakiriyaṃ, idaṃ iddhīsu vikubbaniddhiyā padhānatāya vuttaṃ, iddhiṃ vikubbanañcāti evaṃ vā attho daṭṭhabbo. Vikubbanassa visuṃ gahaṇampi vuttakāraṇeneva daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ākāsakasiṇavasena arūpasamāpattiyo na sambhavanti, ālokakasiṇañca odātakasiṇantogadhaṃ katvā “odātakasiṇapariyantesū”ti vuttaṃ kasiṇānulomādicittaparidamanavidhino adhippetattā, ākāsanimmānādiatthaṃ pana tadubhayampi icchitabbameva. Aṭṭha aṭṭhāti yathāvuttesu kasiṇesu ekekasmiṃ aṭṭha aṭṭha samāpattiyo. Kasiṇānulomatoti kasiṇapaṭipāṭito, paṭipāṭi ca desanāvasena veditabbā. Jhānānulomo pana paṭipattivasenapi. Ukkamanaṃ ukkantaṃ, ukkantameva ukkantikaṃ, jhānassa ukkantikaṃ jhānukkantikaṃ, tato, jhānalaṅghanatoti attho. Aṅgasaṅkantito aṅgātikkamato. Cittaṃ paridametabbaṃ yadicchakaṃ yatthicchakaṃ jhānānaṃ samāpajjanādisukhatthaṃ, tesaṃ ārammaṇānañca sallakkhaṇatthaṃ. Evañhissa tattha visavitā samijjhatīti.

“Psychic transformation” (iddhivikubbana) is the act of abandoning one's natural appearance, which is called psychic power (iddhi). This term is used because the transformative psychic power is pre-eminent among the psychic powers. Or, the meaning should be understood as “psychic power and transformation.” The separate mention of “transformation” should also be understood for the reason already stated. The formless attainments do not arise by means of the space kasiṇa; and having included the light kasiṇa within the white kasiṇa, it is said, “ending with the white kasiṇa,” because the method of taming the mind through kasiṇa-conformity and so forth is intended. However, for the purpose of creating space and so forth, both should indeed be desired. “Eight and eight” means eight attainments in each of the aforementioned kasiṇas. “From kasiṇa-conformity” means from the sequence of the kasiṇas, and the sequence should be known by way of the teaching. Jhāna-conformity, however, is also by way of practice. “Leaping over” (ukkamana) is what is leaped over (ukkanta); what is leaped over itself is ukkantika. The ukkantika of a jhāna is jhānukkantika. Therefore, the meaning is “from leaping over the jhāna.” “From the transition of factors” means from the surpassing of factors. The mind should be tamed, as desired and wherever desired, for the sake of ease in entering the jhānas and so forth, and for the sake of clearly perceiving their objects. For thus, his mastery therein is accomplished.

366. Jhānaṃ samāpajjatīti kiṃ catubbidhampi jhānaṃ samāpajjati, udāhu ekekanti? Kiñcettha yadi catubbidhampi samāpajjati, aṅgasaṅkantito viseso na siyā, atha ekekaṃ ārammaṇasaṅkantito. Nāyaṃ doso ābhogavasena tesaṃ visesasiddhito. Yadā hi kasiṇānulomameva ābhujitvā tattha tattha kasiṇe jhānāni samāpajjati, na aṅgasaṅkantiṃ, tadā kasiṇānulomo. Yadā pana aṅgasaṅkantiṃ ābhujitvā jhānāni samāpajjati, tadā aṅgasaṅkanti veditabbā. Iminā nayena kasiṇānulomaārammaṇasaṅkantiādīnampi aññamaññaṃ viseso veditabbo. Idaṃ kasiṇānulomaṃ nāma cittaparidamananti adhippāyo.

366. Regarding “He enters jhāna”: does he enter all four kinds of jhāna, or one by one? Here there is a supplement: if he enters all four kinds, there would be no distinction from “transition of factors”; if he enters one by one, there would be no distinction from “transition of object.” This is not a fault, because their distinction is established by means of adverting. For when, having adverted only to kasiṇa-conformity, he enters the jhānas in this or that kasiṇa, and not to the transition of factors, then it is kasiṇa-conformity. But when, having adverted to the transition of factors, he enters the jhānas, then it should be known as “transition of factors.” By this method, the distinction among kasiṇa-conformity, transition of object, and so forth, from one another should be known. The intention is: this, called kasiṇa-conformity, is a taming of the mind.

Tathevāti [V 2.0003] “paṭipāṭiyā aṭṭhasu kasiṇesu satakkhattumpi sahassakkhattumpī”ti etassa upasaṃhārattho tathā-saddo. Paṭilomato cettha paṭipāṭi. Tenāha “paṭilomakkamenā”ti. Ayañhettha attho – paṭhamaṃ odātakasiṇe jhānaṃ samāpajjati, tato lohitakasiṇeti yāva pathavīkasiṇā vattabbā.

The word `tathā` has the meaning of summarizing this phrase: "in sequence, a hundred times or even a thousand times, in the eight kasiṇas." And here, the sequence is in reverse order. Therefore, he said, "in reverse order." Indeed, this is the meaning here: first, one attains jhāna in the white kasiṇa, then in the red kasiṇa, and so on, up to the earth kasiṇa; this should be stated.

Punappunaṃ samāpajjananti “satakkhattuṃ sahassakkhattu”nti vuttaṃ bahulākāramāha.

By "attaining again and again," he states the frequent manner which was spoken of as "a hundred times, a thousand times."

Tatthevāti [M 2.0003] pathavīkasiṇeyeva. Tatoti pacchā tatiyajjhānato vuṭṭhānantarakālaṃ. Tadevāti pathavīkasiṇameva. Tato ākiñcaññāyatananti tato pathavīkasiṇugghāṭimākāse pavattitaākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattito vuṭṭhāya viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ amanasikaritvā taṃ laṅghitvā yathāvuttaākāsānañcāyatanaviññāṇassa abhāve pavattitaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjati. Pathavīkasiṇugghāṭimākāsakasiṇaṃ pathavīkasiṇapakkhikameva hotīti vuttaṃ “kasiṇaṃ anukkamitvā”ti. Atha vā aṭṭhasu kasiṇesu kassaci ukkamanaṃ idha kasiṇukkantikaṃ nāmāti āha “kasiṇaṃ anukkamitvā”ti. Jhānukkantikanti ettha icchitaṃ avadhāraṇena nivattetabbaṃ, ukkamanassa ca sarūpaṃ dassetuṃ “evaṃ kasiṇa”ntiādiṃ vatvā puna taṃ pakāraṃ saha nissayena sesakasiṇesu atidisanto “evaṃ āpokasiṇādi…pe… kātabbā”ti āha. Tenāha “iminā nayenā”tiādi. Yathā paṭhamajjhānamūlakaṃ pathavīkasiṇādīsu jhānukkantikaṃ dassitaṃ, evaṃ dutiyajjhānādimūlakampi taṃ yathārahaṃ dassetabbaṃ.

`Tattheva` means in the earth kasiṇa alone. `Tato` means afterwards, the time immediately after emerging from the third jhāna. `Tadeva` means the earth kasiṇa alone. `Tato ākiñcaññāyatananti` means: then, having emerged from the attainment of the base of infinite space which arises in the conceptual space that is the removal of the earth kasiṇa, not paying attention to the base of infinite consciousness and having skipped over it, one attains the base of nothingness, which arises in the absence of the aforesaid consciousness of the base of infinite space. The space kasiṇa that is the removal of the earth kasiṇa is indeed on the side of the earth kasiṇa; therefore, it is said, 'having not skipped over the kasiṇa.' Alternatively, the skipping over of any one of the eight kasiṇas is here called `kasiṇukkantikaṃ` (kasiṇa-skipping); therefore, he said, 'having not skipped over the kasiṇa.' In the term `jhānukkantikaṃ` (jhāna-skipping), the desired emphasis and the meaning to be excluded by it should be understood, and to show the nature of the skipping over, having said "thus the kasiṇa," etc., and again extending that method together with its basis to the remaining kasiṇas, he said, "thus the water kasiṇa... and so on... should be done." Therefore, he said, "by this method," etc. Just as the jhāna-skipping based on the first jhāna has been shown in the earth kasiṇa and others, so too, that which is based on the second jhāna, etc., should be shown accordingly.

Tadevāti paṭhamajjhānameva. Kasiṇukkantikepi āpokasiṇādimūlikā yojanā vuttanayeneva kātabbā, tathā yathārahaṃ dutiyajjhānādimūlikā.

`Tadeva` means the first jhāna itself. Even in the case of kasiṇa-skipping, the application based on the water kasiṇa and so on should be done in the manner already stated; similarly, as appropriate, that which is based on the second jhāna and so on.

Lohitakasiṇato ākiñcaññāyatananti lohitakasiṇaṃ āvajjento abhimukhaṃ katvā tassa ugghāṭanena upaṭṭhite kasiṇugghāṭimākāse amanasikārena ākāsānañcāyatanajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tattha pubbe pavattaviññāṇassa apagamaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjati.

As for 'from the red kasiṇa to the base of nothingness': Adverting to the red kasiṇa and making it face-to-face, having attained the jhāna of the base of infinite space by non-attention to the kasiṇa-removed space that has appeared through its removal, one then makes the absence of the first formless consciousness that had previously arisen there the object and attains the base of nothingness.

Itaresanti avasiṭṭharūpāvacarajjhānānaṃ. Na hi arūpajjhānesu aṅgasaṅkanti atthi, nāpi tāni [V 2.0004] pathavīkasiṇe pavattanti. Yaṃ pana aṅgārammaṇasaṅkantivacane “nīlakasiṇaṃ ugghāṭetvā ākāsānañcāyatana”ntiādi vuttaṃ, taṃ yathālābhavasena vuttaṃ, pariyāyena vāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nippariyāyato pana yathā aṅgasaṅkanti rūpajjhānesu eva labbhati, evaṃ arūpajjhānesu eva ārammaṇasaṅkanti. Tassa tasseva hi jhānassa ārammaṇantare pavatti ārammaṇasaṅkanti. Tenāha “sabbakasiṇesu ekasseva jhānassa samāpajjanaṃ ārammaṇasaṅkantikaṃ nāmā”ti.

By 'the others' is meant the remaining form-sphere jhānas. For in the formless jhānas there is no transition of factors, nor do they occur in the earth kasiṇa. However, that which is stated in the discussion of the transition of both factors and object, such as 'having removed the blue kasiṇa, (one enters) the base of infinite space,' is said according to the appropriate method, or should be regarded as a figure of speech. But in the direct sense, just as the transition of factors is obtained only in the form jhānas, so too in the formless jhānas, only the transition of object is obtained. For the transition of object is the occurrence of that very same jhāna with a different object. Therefore, he said: 'The attainment of one and the same jhāna in all the kasiṇas is called the transition of object.'

Yathā [M 2.0004] pana “sabbakasiṇesū”ti iminā ākāsaviññāṇakasiṇānampi saṅgaho hotīti na sakkā vattuṃ idha aṭṭhannaṃyeva kasiṇānaṃ adhigatattā, evaṃ sabbampi arūpajjhānaṃ “ekaṃ jhāna”nti na sakkā vattuṃ aṭṭhannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ vasena cittaparidamanassa icchitattā. Tasmā āruppajjhānānaṃ vasena aṅgārammaṇasaṅkanti pariyāyena vuttāti veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi pītakasiṇugghāṭimākāse yaṃ paṭhamāruppaviññāṇaṃ, tadārammaṇaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ sandhāyāha “pītakasiṇato viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajjitvā”ti. Iminā nayena sesadvayepi attho veditabbo. Ekantarikavasenāti aññattho antara-saddo. Antarameva antarikaṃ, ekajjhaṃ antarikaṃ etasminti ekantarikaṃ, jhānasamāpajjanaṃ, tassa vasena. Yathā aṅgānaṃ, ārammaṇassa ca ekajjhaṃ aññathā viseso hoti, tathā samāpajjanavasenāti. So pana viseso heṭṭhimānaṃ tesaṃ aṅgārammaṇānaṃ samatikkamanavasena hotīti vuttaṃ “ekantarikavasena aṅgānañca ārammaṇānañca saṅkamana”nti. “Idaṃ jhānaṃ pañcaṅgika”ntiādinā aṅgesu, “idaṃ pathavīkasiṇa”ntiādinā ārammaṇesu ca vavatthāpitesu ekajjhaṃ tesaṃ vavatthāpane na koci viseso atthīti aṭṭhakathāsu ayaṃ vidhi nābhato. Evañca katvā jhānukkantikādīsu paṭilomakkamena, anulomapaṭilomakkamena ca ekantarikabhāvena labbhamānampi jhānādīnaṃ ukkamanaṃ na uddhaṭaṃ, tehi nayehi vināpi cittaparidamanaṃ ijjhatīti papañcaparihāratthaṃ vā te aṭṭhakathāsu anāgatāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Just as it cannot be said that the phrase “in all kasiṇas” includes the space and consciousness kasiṇas, because here only eight kasiṇas are under consideration, so too it cannot be said that all formless jhānas are “one jhāna,” because the training of the mind is desired by means of the eight attainments. Therefore, it should be understood that, with respect to the formless jhānas, the transition of factors and object is spoken of figuratively. For indeed, regarding the statement ‘having attained the base of infinite consciousness from the yellow kasiṇa,’ this is said with reference to the base of infinite consciousness, which has as its object the first formless consciousness that arises in the conceptual space which is the removal of the yellow kasiṇa. By this method, the meaning in the remaining two cases should also be understood. In the phrase ‘by means of a single interval,’ the word `antara` has the meaning of ‘other.’ `Antara` itself is `antarika`; `ekantarika` means ‘in this there is one distinct thing altogether,’ which refers to the attainment of jhāna; it is by means of that. Just as there is a distinction of the factors and the object together in another way, so it is by means of attainment. But that distinction occurs by means of transcending those lower factors and objects, hence it is said: ‘the transition of factors and objects by means of a single interval.’ When the factors are established by such phrases as, ‘This jhāna has five factors,’ and the objects by such phrases as, ‘This is the earth kasiṇa,’ there is no special benefit in establishing them together; therefore, this method is not presented in the commentaries. And for this reason, in the sections on jhāna-transcendence and so on, even though the skipping over of jhānas, etc., is obtainable by reverse order, by forward and reverse order, and by way of a single interval, it is not expounded. It should be understood that either because the training of the mind is accomplished even without those methods, or for the sake of avoiding prolixity, they are not included in the commentaries.

367. Abhāvitabhāvano jhānābhiññāsu akatādhikāro. Tattha upanissayarahitopīti keci. Ādibhūtaṃ yogakammaṃ ādikammaṃ, taṃ etassa atthīti ādikammiko, pubbe akataparicayo bhāvanaṃ anuyuñjanto. Tenāha “yogāvacaro”ti. Kasiṇaparikammampi bhāroti dosavivajjanādividhinā kasiṇamaṇḍale paṭipatti yāva uggahanimittuppatti kasiṇaparikammaṃ, tampi nāma bhāro, pageva iddhivikubbanāti adhippāyo. Nimittuppādananti paṭibhāganimittuppādanaṃ[V 2.0005]. Taṃ vaḍḍhetvāti taṃ nimittaṃ, bhāvanañca vaḍḍhetvā. Na hi bhāvanāya vināva nimittavaḍḍhanaṃ labbhati. Keci upacārasamādhiṃ labhitvā appanāsamādhiṃ adhigantuṃ na sakkonti, tādisāpi bahū hontevāti āha “appanādhigamo bhāro”ti. Appanādhigamoti vā aṭṭhannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ adhigamamāha. Aññova samāpattīnaṃ upanissayo[M 2.0005], añño abhiññānanti āha “paridamitacittassāpi iddhivikubbanaṃ nāma bhāro”ti. Khippaṃ nisanti nisāmanaṃ jhānacakkhunā pathavīkasiṇādijhānārammaṇassa dassanaṃ etassāti khippanisanti, sīghataraṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjitā, tassa bhāvo khippanisantibhāvo. Ambatarunicitaṃ mahāmahindattherādīhi otiṇṇaṭṭhānaṃ therambatthalaṃ. Yathā paṭipakkhavijayāya yodhājīvā nimmalameva asitomarādiṃ gahetvā vicaranti, evaṃ bhikkhunāpi kilesavijayāya nimmalāva jhānābhiññā vaḷañjitabbāti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “tasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

367. One with undeveloped meditation is one who has not made the groundwork in the jhānas and supernormal knowledges. Some say that therein, even a person devoid of a supporting condition is so called. The initial meditative effort is the preliminary work; one for whom this exists is an initial practitioner, one engaging in meditation without prior practice. Hence, it is said, 'a yogi.' As for 'even the preparatory work of the kasiṇa is a burden': the practice on the kasiṇa disc by the method of avoiding faults, etc., up to the arising of the learning sign, is the kasiṇa preparatory work. That too is indeed a burden; how much more so the creation of psychic marvels? Such is the intent. The production of the sign means the production of the counterpart sign. 'Having developed it' means having developed that sign and the meditation. For indeed, without meditation, the development of the sign is not obtained. Some, having obtained access concentration, are not able to attain absorption concentration; such persons are indeed many. Hence, it is said, 'the attainment of absorption is a burden.' Alternatively, 'attainment of absorption' refers to the attainment of the eight attainments. The supporting condition for the attainments is one thing, and for the supernormal knowledges another. Thus, it is said, 'even for one whose mind is tamed, the creation of psychic marvels is indeed a burden.' A `khippanisanti` is one for whom there is swift contemplation (`nisanti`), that is, the seeing of the object of jhāna, such as the earth kasiṇa, with the jhāna-eye; one who enters jhāna very swiftly. The state of such a person is `khippanisantibhāvo`, the state of swift contemplation. `Therambatthala` is the place descended upon by the great elder Mahinda and others, a place clustered with mango trees. Just as warriors, for the sake of conquering the opposing enemy, wander about holding only stainless swords, spears, and so on, so too should a monk, for the sake of conquering the defilements, use only the stainless jhānas and supernormal knowledges. To show this meaning, 'therefore,' and so on, was said.

Patiṭṭhābhāvoti idha parassa upaddavūpasamanaṃ adhippetaṃ. Taṃ hi khippanisantibhāvatopi garutaraṃ accāyikakiccasādhanavasena vidhātabbato durabhisambhavatarattā. Taṃ pana rakkhitattheranidassaneneva siddhampi tato garutarena aṅgāravassaparittāṇena vibhāvetuṃ “giribhaṇḍavāhanapūjāya…pe… thero viyā”ti āha. Giribhaṇḍavāhanapūjā nāma cetiyagirimādiṃ katvā sakaladīpe, samudde ca yāva yojanā mahatī dīpapūjā. Pathaviṃ māpetvāti mārena pavattitaṃ aṅgāravassaṃ phuliṅgamattenapi yāva manusse na pāpuṇāti, tāvadeva ākāse pathaviṃ nimminitvā.

Here, by 'being a support,' the pacification of another's affliction is intended. Indeed, that is weightier even than the state of quick attainment, because it must be undertaken for the accomplishment of an urgent task and is more difficult to bring about. Now, although this was accomplished by the very example of Elder Rakkhita, in order to demonstrate it by means of the protection from a rain of coals—which is weightier than that—he said, “as in the Giribhaṇḍavāhanapūjā… like the elder.” The Giribhaṇḍavāhanapūjā is a great offering of lamps, beginning with Cetiyagiri, extending throughout the entire island and in the ocean for a yojana. As for 'having created the earth,' this means having created an earth in the sky just before the rain of coals set in motion by Māra could reach humans even as a spark.

Balavapubbayogānanti garutarūpanissayānaṃ, iddhividhādīnaṃ hetubhūtamahābhinīhārānanti attho. Aggasāvakādīnanti ādi-saddena ekacce mahāsāvake saṅgaṇhāti. Bhāvanānukkamo yathāvuttaṃ cittaparidamanaṃ. Paṭisambhidādīti ādi-saddena ṭhānāṭhānañāṇādīnampi saṅgaho veditabbo, na sesābhiññānameva. Sāvakānampi hi ṭhānāṭhānañāṇādīni padesavasena ijjhanti. Tasmāti yasmā pubbahetusampannasseva yathāvuttaṃ bhāvanānukkamaṃ vinā abhiññāyo ijjhanti, na itarassa, tasmā. Aggidhamanādīhīti aggimhi tāpanakoṭṭanādīhi. Yathā cāti ca-saddena lākhākārādīnaṃ lākhākoṭṭanādiṃ avuttampi saṅgaṇhāti. Chanda…pe… vasenāti “chandavato ce abhiññā sijjhati, mayhampi sijjhatī”ti kattukamyatāchandaṃ sīsaṃ dhuraṃ jeṭṭhaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā, chandaṃ vā uppādetvā taṃ bhāvanāya mukhaṃ katvā jhānassa samāpajjanavasena. Eseva [V 2.0006] nayo sesesupi. “Āvajjanādivasībhāvavasenā”ti idaṃ aṭṭhasupi samāpattīsu sātisayaṃ vasībhāvāpādanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tañca kho ādikammikavasena, na [M 2.0006] katādhikāravasenāti āha “pubbahetu…pe… vaṭṭatī”ti. Pubbahetusampannassa hi yaṃ jhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā abhiññā nibbattetabbā, tattheva sātisayaṃ ciṇṇavasitāpi icchitabbā, na sabbatthevāti adhippāyo. “Catutthajjhānamatte ciṇṇavasinā”ti vacanato arūpasamāpattiyo vināpi abhiññā ijjhantīti vadanti. Tampi yadi pubbahetusampannassa vasena vuttaṃ, yuttameva. Athetarassa, tesaṃ matimattaṃ. Yathāti yena pakārena yena vidhinā. Etthāti etasmiṃ iddhividhanipphādane.

The expression ‘Balavapubbayogānaṃ’ means 'of those with a weightier supporting condition, whose great aspirations are the cause for the kinds of psychic power and so on.' By ‘chief disciples and others,’ the word ‘others’ includes certain great disciples. ‘The sequence of development’ refers to the taming of the mind as previously described. By ‘analytical knowledges and so on,’ the word ‘so on’ should be understood to include the knowledge of what is possible and impossible, etc., not just the remaining supernormal knowledges. For even for disciples, the knowledge of what is possible and impossible, etc., is accomplished to some extent. ‘Therefore’ means: because the supernormal knowledges are accomplished without the previously described sequence of development only for one endowed with a past cause, not for another, therefore… The expression ‘aggidhamanādīhi’ refers to heating and hammering in a fire, etc. The word ‘ca’ in ‘yathā ca’ also includes, though not explicitly stated, the pounding of lac, etc., by lac-workers and the like. ‘By means of will…’ means: thinking, “If supernormal knowledge is accomplished for one with will, it will be accomplished for me too,” one makes the will to achieve the head, the lead, the chief, the forerunner; or, having aroused will and made it the approach to development, one attains jhāna. The same method applies to the rest. The expression ‘by means of mastery in adverting and so forth’ is said with reference to achieving surpassing mastery in all eight attainments. And this is said from the perspective of a beginner, not of one who has made a prior resolution; hence, it is said, ‘For one endowed with a past cause… it occurs.’ For one endowed with a past cause, when a jhāna is made the basis for producing supernormal knowledges, it is in that very jhāna that surpassing, practiced mastery should be desired, not in all of them. This is the intention. Based on the statement ‘by one who has practiced mastery in the fourth jhāna alone,’ some say that supernormal knowledges are accomplished even without the formless attainments. That too, if said with reference to one endowed with a past cause, is appropriate. But for another, it is merely their opinion. ‘How’ means in what manner, by what method. ‘Here’ means in this production of the kinds of psychic power.

368. Tatrāti ca tadeva paccāmasati. Pāḷinayānusārenevāti pāḷigatiyā anusaraṇeneva, pāṭhasaṃvaṇṇanānukkamenevāti attho. “Catutthajjhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī”ti vatvā “so”ti vuttattā āha “adhigatacatutthajjhāno yogī”ti. “Evaṃ samāhite”ti ettha evaṃ-saddo heṭṭhājhānattayādhigamapaṭipāṭisiddhassa catutthajjhānasamādhānassa nidassanatthoti āha “evanti catutthajjhānakkamanidassanameta”nti, catutthajjhānassa, tassa ca adhigamakkamassa nidassanaṃ. Yena samādhānānukkamena catutthajjhānasamādhi laddho, tadubhayanidassananti attho. Tenāha “iminā…pe… vuttaṃ hotī”ti. Yadipi “eva”nti idaṃ āgamanasamādhinā saddhiṃ catutthajjhānasamādhānaṃ dīpeti. Satipārisuddhisamādhi eva pana iddhiyā adhiṭṭhānabhāvato padhānanti āha “catutthajjhānasamādhinā samāhite”ti. Upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvenāti upekkhāya janitasatipārisuddhisabbhāvena. Sabbapaccanīkadhammūpakkilesaparisuddhāya hi paccanīkasamanepi abyāvaṭāya pārisuddhiupekkhāya vattamānāya catutthajjhānaṃ, taṃsampayuttadhammā ca suparisuddhā, suvisadā ca honti, satisīsena pana tattha desanā katāti āha “upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvena parisuddhe”ti. Parisuddhiyā eva paccayavisesena pavattiviseso pariyodātatā sudhantasuvaṇṇassa nighaṃsanena pabhassaratā viyāti āha “parisuddhattāyeva pariyodāte, pabhassareti vuttaṃ hotī”ti.

368. And by 'tatra' (therein), he reconsiders that very matter: the production of the kinds of psychic power. As for 'Pāḷinayānusāreneva' (only by following the method of the Pāḷi), the meaning is: only by following the course of the Pāḷi, that is, only by the sequence of the textual explanation. Having stated, “he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna,” and because it is then said, “so” (he), it is explained: “a yogī who has attained the fourth jhāna.” Regarding “thus concentrated,” here the word “evaṃ” (thus) indicates the concentration of the fourth jhāna, which is accomplished by the sequence of attaining the three lower jhānas. Thus it is said that 'evaṃ' is an indicator of the sequence for the fourth jhāna; that is, it indicates the fourth jhāna and the sequence of its attainment. The meaning is: it is an indicator of both of those—the concentration and the sequence—by which the fourth jhāna concentration is obtained. Therefore, it is stated: “by this… it is said.” Although this word 'evaṃ' indicates the concentration of the fourth jhāna together with the approach concentrations, nevertheless, because the concentration of pure mindfulness is itself the basis for psychic power, it is pre-eminent. Therefore, it is said: “concentrated by the concentration of the fourth jhāna.” “Through the state of purity of equanimity and mindfulness” means by the state of purity of mindfulness which is produced by equanimity. For when pure equanimity—which is utterly pure from all opposing states and defilements, and is unconcerned even in the pacification of opposing states—is present, the fourth jhāna and its associated states become thoroughly pure and exceedingly clear. However, the teaching there is given with mindfulness as primary, hence it is said: “purified by the state of purity of equanimity and mindfulness.” Due to a special condition in purity itself, a special occurrence, which is utter brightness, arises, like the radiance of well-refined gold from being polished. Therefore, it is said: “Because of its very purity, it is utterly bright; it is said to be radiant.”

Sukhādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ ghātenāti sukhasomanassānaṃ, dukkhadomanassānañca yathākkamaṃ rāgadosapaccayānaṃ vikkhambhanena. “Sukhaṃ somanassassa paccayo, somanassaṃ rāgassa, dukkhaṃ domanassassā”ti hi vuttaṃ. Yathā rāgādayo cetaso malāsucibhāvena “aṅgaṇānī”ti vuccanti, evaṃ upagantvā [M 2.0007] kilesanaṭṭhena upakkilesāti āha “anaṅgaṇattāyeva vigatūpakkilese”ti. Tenāha “aṅgaṇena hi taṃ cittaṃ upakkilissatī”ti, vibādhīyati upatāpīyatīti [V 2.0007] attho. Subhāvitattāti paguṇabhāvāpādanena suṭṭhu bhāvitattā. Tenāha “vasībhāvappatte”ti, āvajjanādinā pañcadhā, cuddasavidhena vā paridamanena vasavattitaṃ upagateti attho. Vase vattamānaṃ hi cittaṃ paguṇabhāvāpattiyā suparimadditaṃ viya cammaṃ, suparikammakatā viya ca lākhā mudunti vuccati. Kammakkhameti vikubbanādiiddhikammakkhame. Tañca ubhayanti mudutākammaniyadvayaṃ.

By 'destroying the conditions of happiness and so forth' is meant the suppression, in due order, of the conditions for greed and aversion, namely, happiness and joy, and suffering and sorrow. For it is said: 'Happiness is a condition for joy, joy for greed, and suffering for sorrow.' Just as greed and the like are called 'stains' because of their nature as filth and impurity of the mind, so too, by approaching in the sense of defiling, they are called 'corruptions.' Hence it is said: 'Because it is without stains, it is free from corruptions.' Therefore it is said: 'For that mind is corrupted by a stain,' meaning it is afflicted and tormented. 'Well-developed' means because it has been thoroughly cultivated by bringing it to a state of proficiency. Therefore it is said: 'Having attained mastery,' meaning it has come under control through the fivefold mastery, such as adverting, or through the fourteenfold taming. Indeed, a mind that is under control, due to having attained a state of proficiency, is called 'pliant,' like a well-kneaded hide or like well-prepared lac. 'Workable' means capable of the work of supernormal power, such as transformation. And 'both' refers to the pair of pliancy and workability.

Nāhantiādīsu na-kāro paṭisedhattho. Ahanti satthā attānaṃ niddisati. Bhikkhaveti bhikkhū ālapati. Aññanti idāni vuccamānacittato aññaṃ. Ekadhammampīti ekampi sabhāvadhammaṃ na samanupassāmīti sambandho. Ayaṃ hettha attho – ahaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbaññutaññāṇena olokentopi aññaṃ ekadhammampi na samanupassāmi. Yaṃ vasībhāvāpādanena bhāvitaṃ, tathā punappunaṃ karaṇena bahulīkataṃ, evaṃ savisesamudubhāvappattiyā muduṃ, kammakkhamatāya kammaniyañca hoti. Yathayidaṃ cittanti attano, tesañca paccakkhatāya evamāhāti. Yathā yathāvuttā parisuddhatādayo na vigacchanti, evaṃ subhāvitaṃ cittaṃ.

In expressions such as 'Nāhaṃ,' the particle 'na' has the meaning of negation. By 'ahaṃ,' the Teacher refers to himself. By 'bhikkhave,' he addresses the monks. By 'aññaṃ' is meant other than the mind now being spoken of. The connection of 'ekadhammampi' is with 'na samanupassāmi' (I do not see) even a single thing with its own nature. Herein, this is the meaning: 'Monks, even when looking with the knowledge of omniscience, I do not see any other single thing.' That which is developed by bringing it to a state of mastery, and made much of by repeated practice, thus becomes pliant by attaining a special state of pliancy, and workable through its fitness for work. He spoke thus, 'as this mind,' because it was directly experienced by himself and by them. The mind is well-developed in such a way that the aforesaid qualities, such as purity, do not depart.

Tattha avaṭṭhitaṃ idha “ṭhitaṃ, āneñjappatta”nti ca vuttanti āha “etesu parisuddhatādīsu ṭhitattā ṭhite, ṭhitattāyeva āneñjappatte”ti. Yathā mudukammaññatā vasībhāvappattiyā lakkhīyanti, evaṃ vasībhāvappattipi mudukammaññatāhi lakkhīyatīti, mudukammaññabhāvena vā attano vase ṭhitattā “ṭhite”ti vuttaṃ. Yathā hi kāraṇena phalaṃ niddharīyati, evaṃ phalenāpi kāraṇaṃ niddharīyatīti niccalabhāvena avaṭṭhānaṃ āneñjappatti. Sā ca sampayuttadhammesu thirabhāvena, paṭipakkhehi akammaniyatāya ca sambhavantī saddhādibalānaṃ ānubhāvena hotīti “saddhādīhi pariggahitattā āneñjappatte”ti saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ vivarituṃ “saddhāpariggahitaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha saddhāpariggahitanti evaṃ subhāvitaṃ vasībhāvappattaṃ etaṃ cittaṃ ekaṃsena abhiññāsacchikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ abhiññāsacchikiriyāya saṃvattatīti evaṃ pavattāya saddhāya pariggahitaṃ yathāvuttasaddhābalena upatthambhitaṃ. Assaddhiyenāti tappaṭipakkhena assaddhiyena hetunā na iñjati na calati na kampati, aññadatthu upari visesāvahabhāveneva tiṭṭhati. Vīriyapariggahitantiādīsupi [M 2.0008] iminā nayena attho veditabbo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – vīriyapariggahitanti vasībhāvāpādanaparidamanasādhanena vīriyena upatthambhitaṃ. Satipariggahitanti yathāvutte bhāvanābahulīkāre asammosasādhikāya, kusalānañca dhammānaṃ gatiyo samannesamānāya satiyā [V 2.0008] upatthambhitaṃ. Samādhipariggahitanti tattheva avikkhepasādhanena samādhānena upatthambhitaṃ. Paññāpariggahitanti tassā eva bhāvanāya upakārānupakāradhammānaṃ pajānanalakkhaṇāya paññāya upatthambhitaṃ. Obhāsagatanti ñāṇobhāsasahagataṃ. Obhāsabhūtena hi yathāvuttasamādhānasaṃvaddhitena ñāṇena saṃkilesapakkhaṃ yāthāvato passanto tato utrasanto ottappanto taṃ adhibhavati, na tena abhibhūyati. Tenāha “kilesandhakārena na iñjatī”ti. Etena ñāṇapariggahitaṃ hirottappabalaṃ dasseti.

Therein, the firmly established mind is, in this teaching, called 'established' and 'attained to the imperturbable.' Therefore, he said: 'Because it stands firm in these purified states and so forth, it is "established"; and because it is established, it is "attained to the imperturbable."' Just as pliancy and workability are characterized by the attainment of mastery, so too is the attainment of mastery characterized by pliancy and workability; or it is called 'established' because it stands firm in its own mastery through its pliant and workable nature. For just as an effect is inferred from a cause, so too is a cause inferred from an effect. The attainment of the imperturbable is the state of being unwavering. And that occurs through the firmness of associated states, the inability to be shaken by opposing states, and through the power of the spiritual powers of faith and other faculties. Hence, to elaborate the meaning briefly stated as 'attained to the imperturbable because it is encompassed by faith and other qualities,' he said, 'Encompassed by faith,' and so on. Here, 'encompassed by faith' means this well-developed, mastery-attained mind is decisively conducive to the direct realization of those states that are to be directly realized. Thus, it is encompassed by faith that operates in this way, and supported by the power of faith as described. It does not waver, tremble, or falter due to the opposing force of lack of faith; rather, it remains steadfast, leading to further distinction. The same method applies to 'encompassed by energy' and so on, but with this distinction: 'encompassed by energy' means it is supported by energy, which serves as the means for inducing mastery and taming. 'Encompassed by mindfulness' means it is supported by mindfulness, which prevents confusion in the previously mentioned repeated cultivation and rightly investigates the courses of wholesome states. 'Encompassed by concentration' means it is supported by concentration, which prevents distraction in that same cultivation. 'Encompassed by wisdom' means it is supported by wisdom, which discerns helpful and unhelpful states in that very development. 'Accompanied by radiance' means accompanied by the light of knowledge. For with knowledge that has become radiance, augmented by concentration as described, one sees the side of defilements as it truly is, and being alarmed by it and feeling moral dread of it, one overcomes it, and is not overwhelmed by it. Hence, it is said, 'It does not waver in the darkness of defilements.' This shows the power of moral shame and moral dread, which is encompassed by knowledge.

Aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatanti catutthajjhānasamādhinā samāhitatā, parisuddhatā, pariyodātatā, anaṅgaṇatā, vigatūpakkilesatā, mudubhāvo, kammaniyatā, āneñjappattiyā ṭhitatā, samāhitassa vā cittassa imāni aṅgānīti “samāhite”ti imaṃ aṅgabhāvena aggahetvā ṭhitiāneñjappattiyo visuṃ gahetvā imehi aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgataṃ. Abhinīhārakkhamanti iddhividhādiatthaṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ tadabhimukhaṃ karaṇayoggaṃ. Tenāha “abhiññāsacchikaraṇīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ abhiññāsacchikiriyāyā”ti.

Endowed with eight factors: Through the concentration of the fourth jhāna, there is the state of being concentrated, the state of being purified, the state of being cleansed, the state of being stainless, the state of being free from corruptions, the state of being pliant, the state of being workable, and the state of being established through the attainment of imperturbability. Alternatively, these are the factors of a concentrated mind; thus, by not taking 'concentrated' as a factor, but by taking stability and the attainment of imperturbability separately, the mind is endowed with these eight factors. 'Capable of directing': Capable of directing it for the purpose of psychic powers and so forth; fit to be made to face that. Therefore, it was said: 'for the direct realization of qualities to be directly realized.'

Kāmaṃ nīvaraṇāni vikkhambhetvā eva paṭhamajjhānasamadhigamo, vitakkādike vūpasame eva ca dutiyajjhānādisamadhigamo, tathāpi na tathā tehi dūrībhūtā apetā vā yathā catutthajjhānato, cetaso malīnabhāvasaṅkhātauppilābhogakarehi nīvaraṇādīhi suṭṭhu vimuttiyā tassa parisuddhi, pariyodātatā ca yuttāti āha “nīvaraṇa…pe… pariyodāte”ti. Jhānapaṭilābhapaccayānanti jhānapaṭilābhahetukānaṃ jhānapaṭilābhaṃ nissāya uppajjanakānaṃ. Pāpakānanti lāmakānaṃ. Icchāvacarānanti icchāya avacarānaṃ icchāvasena otiṇṇānaṃ “aho vata mameva satthā paṭipucchitvā paṭipucchitvā bhikkhūnaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyā”tiādinayappavattānaṃ mānamāyāsāṭheyyādīnaṃ. Abhijjhādīnanti ādi-saddenāpi tesaṃyeva saṅgaho. Abhijjhā cettha paṭhamajjhānena avikkhambhaneyyā, mānādayo ca tadekaṭṭhā daṭṭhabbā [M 2.0009] “jhānapaṭilābhapaccayāna”nti anuvattamānattā. Vikkhambhaneyyā pana nīvaraṇaggahaṇeneva gahitā, kathaṃ pana paṭhamajjhānena avikkhambhaneyyā idha vigacchantīti? “Sabbe kusalā dhammā sabbākusalānaṃ paṭipakkhā”ti sallekhapaṭipattivasena evaṃ vuttaṃ jhānassa aparāmaṭṭhabhāvadassanato. Ye panettha “icchāvacarānaṃ abhijjhādīna”nti imehi padehi kopaapaccayakaāmarāgabyāpādādayo gahitāti adhippāyena “jhānapaṭilābhapaccayāna”nti pāṭhaṃ paṭikkhipitvā “jhānapaṭilābhapaccanīkāna”nti [V 2.0009] pāṭhoti vadanti, taṃ tesaṃ matimattaṃ tathā pāṭhasseva abhāvato. Jhānapaṭilābhapaccanīkā ca nīvaraṇā ceva tadekaṭṭhā ca tesaṃ dūrībhāvaṃ vatvā puna abhāvavigamacodanāya ayujjamānattā. Nanu ca anaṅgaṇasutta- (ma. ni. 1.57 ādayo) vatthasuttesu (ma. ni. 1.70 ādayo) ayamattho na labbhati, oḷārikānaṃyeva pāpadhammānaṃ tattha adhippetattā? Saccametaṃ, idha pana adhigatacatutthajjhānassa vasena vuttattā sukhumāyeva te gahitā, aṅgaṇūpakkilesatāsāmaññena panettha suttānaṃ apadisanaṃ. Tathā hi “suttānusārenā”ti vuttaṃ, na pana suttavasenāti. Avassaṃ ce tamevaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ adhigatajjhānānampi kesañci icchāvacarānaṃ pavattisabbhāvato.

Indeed, it is only by having suppressed the hindrances that there is the attainment of the first jhāna; and it is only with the stilling of initial thought and so on that there is the attainment of the second jhāna and so on. Even so, they are not as thoroughly removed or absent by means of those earlier jhānas as they are from the fourth jhāna. Therefore, its purity and complete clarity are fitting due to thorough liberation from the hindrances and so forth, which cause the state of mental stain and agitation. Hence it was said, 'from the hindrances... purified... clarified.' 'Conditioned by the attainment of jhāna' refers to those states that have the attainment of jhāna as their cause and arise dependent on the attainment of jhāna. 'Evil' means base. 'Those that move by desire' refers to those that roam by desire, those that arise by the power of desire, such as conceit, deceit, and hypocrisy, which proceed in the manner of 'Oh, how wonderful it would be if the Teacher, having questioned me again and again, were to teach the Dhamma to the bhikkhus!' and so on. 'Of covetousness and so on': by the word 'and so on,' these very same states are included. Here, covetousness is not to be suppressed by the first jhāna, and conceit and the like should be understood as having the same basis, because 'conditioned by the attainment of jhāna' is continuing. But those states that are to be suppressed are already included by the taking up of 'hindrances.' But how do those states not to be suppressed by the first jhāna depart here? It is stated thus by way of the practice of effacement, 'All wholesome states are the opposite of all unwholesome states,' because this shows the jhāna's state of not being wrongly grasped. Some, with the intention that by these words 'of those that move by desire, of covetousness and so on,' sensual lust, ill-will, and so forth, which are conditioned by anger, are taken, reject the reading 'conditioned by the attainment of jhāna' and say the reading is 'opposed to the attainment of jhāna.' That is merely their opinion, because such a reading does not exist. And those things opposed to the attainment of jhāna are the hindrances and those states with the same basis; having already spoken of their being far removed, it is unfitting to again urge their absence and disappearance. Is it not the case that this meaning is not found in the Anaṅgaṇa Sutta and the Vatthasutta, since only gross evil states are intended there? This is true. But here, because it is spoken by way of one who has attained the fourth jhāna, those subtle states are taken, and here the suttas are referred to by way of the commonality of being a stain and a defilement. For that reason it was said 'in accordance with the suttas,' and not 'by way of the suttas.' And this must certainly be accepted thus, because for some, even those who have attained jhāna, there is the existence of the occurrence of those states that move by desire.

Iddhipādabhāvūpagamenāti iddhiyā pādakabhāvassa padaṭṭhānabhāvassa upagamanena. Bhāvanāpāripūriyāti ito paraṃ kattabbassa abhāvavasena abhinīhārakkhamabhāvanāya paripuṇṇattā. Paṇītabhāvūpagamenāti tato eva padhānabhāvaṃ nītatāya uttamaṭṭhena, atittikaraṭṭhena ca paṇītabhāvassa upagamanena. Ubhayañcetaṃ ṭhitiyā kāraṇavacanaṃ paripuṇṇāya bhāvanāya paṇītabhāvappattiyā “ṭhite”ti. “Āneñjappatte”ti idaṃ ṭhitiyā visesanaṃ. Tenāha “yathā āneñjappattaṃ hoti, evaṃ ṭhite”ti. Imasmiṃ pakkhe “ṭhite āneñjappatte”ti ubhayamekaṃ aṅgaṃ, “samāhite”ti pana idampi ekamaṅgaṃ. Tenevassa paṭhamavikappato visesaṃ sandhāyāha “evampi aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgata”nti.

By approaching the basis of psychic power: by approaching the state of being the foundation and proximate cause of psychic power. By the fulfillment of development: because, there being nothing further to be done beyond this, it is complete by means of a development firm through aspiration. By approaching the excellent state: by approaching the excellent state, which is led to that very pre-eminence, supreme in the sense of being ultimate, and excellent in the sense of being beyond satisfaction. And both of these are a statement of the reason for stability: due to the attainment of the excellent state through complete development, it is 'stable.' 'Attained to the imperturbable': this is a qualification of stability. Hence it is said, 'as it is attained to the imperturbable, so it is stable.' In this alternative, 'stable and attained to the imperturbable' together form one factor, while 'composed' is also a single factor. Therefore, to show the difference from the first alternative, it is said, 'thus also endowed with eight factors.'

Dasaiddhikathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the Ten Psychic Powers

369. Nipphattiatthenāti sijjhanaṭṭhena. Paṭilābhaṭṭhenāti pāpuṇanaṭṭhena. Tanti kāmitaṃ vatthuṃ. Samijjhatīti nipphajjati. Pabbajjaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva jhānamaggā [M 2.0010] idha nekkhammaṃ. Ijjhatīti pāpuṇīyati. Paṭiharatīti pāṭihāriyanti yasmā paṭipakkhaṃ harati apaneti, tasmā pāṭihāriyaṃ. Attano paṭipakkhaṃ haratīti paṭihāriyaṃ, nekkhammādi, paṭihāriyameva pāṭihāriyaṃ, yathā “vekataṃ, vesama”nti ca.

369. ‘In the sense of accomplishment’ means in the sense of success. ‘In the sense of attainment’ means in the sense of reaching. ‘That’ refers to the desired object. ‘It succeeds’ means it is accomplished. Here, renunciation extends from taking up the going forth up to jhāna and the path. ‘It is achieved’ means it is attained. ‘A marvel’ is so called because it removes (paṭiharati); since it carries away and dispels the opposing state, it is therefore a marvel. Because it removes its own opposing state, it is a marvel; renunciation and so on are marvels. A marvel is just a marvel, just as in ‘vekata’ and ‘vesama’.

Ijjhanaṭṭhenāti nipphajjanaṭṭhena. Upāyasampadāyāti sampannaupāyassa, ñāyārambhassāti attho. Ijjhatīti pasaveti. Sīlavāti ācārasīlena sīlavā. Kalyāṇadhammoti dasakusalakammapathavasena [V 2.0010] sundaradhammo. Sīlasampattiyā vā sīlavā. Dānādisesapuññakiriyavatthuvasena kalyāṇadhammo. Paṇidahissatīti patthessati.

‘In the sense of achievement’ means in the sense of accomplishment. ‘By the accomplishment of means’ means of one with accomplished means, that is, of one who undertakes the right method. ‘It is achieved’ means it produces. ‘Virtuous’ means one is virtuous by means of ethical conduct. ‘Of excellent qualities’ means one is of beautiful qualities by way of the ten courses of wholesome action. Or, one is virtuous by the accomplishment of virtue. One is ‘of excellent qualities’ by way of the remaining bases for meritorious actions such as giving and so on. ‘He will aspire’ means he will long for.

Ijjhantīti vaḍḍhanti, ukkaṃsaṃ pāpuṇantīti attho. Sātisayanipphajjanapaṭilābhasijjhanabuddhiatthe hi iddhi vuttā. Sā dasavidhāti sabbā iddhiyo ānetvā atthuddhāravasena idhādhippetaṃ iddhiṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Bahubhāvādikassa adhiṭṭhānaṃ adhiṭṭhahanaṃ etissā atthīti adhiṭṭhānā. Vividhaṃ rūpanimmānasaṅkhātaṃ kubbanaṃ etissā atthīti vikubbanā. Manomayāti jhānamanena nibbattibhāvato manomayā. Ñāṇassa vipphāro vegāyitattaṃ etissā atthīti ñāṇavipphārā. Ariyānaṃ ayanti ariyā. Yato kutoci kammavipākato jātā iddhi kammavipākajā. Sātisayapuññanibbattā iddhi puññavato iddhi. Kammavipākajā iddhi jātito paṭṭhāya hoti, itarā yadā tadā puññassa vipaccanakāleti evaṃ vā imāsaṃ viseso veditabbo. Āthabbanavijjābhinibbattā vijjāmayā. Sammāpayogo upāyapayogo ñāyārambho.

‘They succeed’ (ijjanti) means they grow (vaḍḍhanti), they attain (pāpuṇanti) excellence (ukkaṃsaṃ). Indeed, ‘iddhi’ is stated in the sense of extraordinary accomplishment (nipphajjana), attainment (paṭilābha), success (sijjhana), and growth (buddhi). This was stated—‘It is of ten kinds’—in order to show the iddhi intended here, by bringing in all kinds of iddhi by way of extracting the meaning. It is ‘adhiṭṭhānā’ (of determination) because for this there is ‘adhiṭṭhāna’ (determination), which is the act of determining to become many and so on. It is ‘vikubbanā’ (of transformation) because for this there is ‘kubbana’ (the act of making), which is called the creation of various forms. ‘Manomayā’ (mind-made) is so called because it is produced by the jhāna-mind. It is ‘ñāṇavipphārā’ (pervasion of knowledge) because for this there is the swift pervasion of knowledge. ‘Ariyā’ (noble) is so called because this belongs to the noble ones. The iddhi that is born from any karmic result whatsoever is ‘kammavipākajā’ (born of karmic result). The iddhi produced by extraordinary merit is the ‘iddhi of a meritorious one’ (puññavato iddhi). The iddhi born of karmic result exists from birth onwards, while the other arises whenever the merit ripens; or, the distinction between them should be understood in this way. That which is produced by the Atharvan spells is ‘vijjāmayā’ (produced by spells). ‘Sammāpayoga’ (right application) is the application of means (upāyapayogo) and the right undertaking (ñāyārambho).

370. Pakatiyā ekoti sabhāvena eko. Bahukanti bahuṃ. Tena aggahitaparicchedaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbassa anekabhāvaṃ dassetvā puna paricchedato dassetuṃ “sataṃ vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āvajjatīti parikammasaṅkhātena ābhogena ābhujati bhāvirūpe tena parikammamanasikārena manasi karoti. Ñāṇena adhiṭṭhātīti tathā parikammaṃ katvā abhiññāñāṇena yathādhippete bahuke adhiṭṭhāti, adhiṭṭhānacittena saheva bahubhāvāpattito bahubhāvāpādakaṃ iddhividhañāṇaṃ pavattento ca tathā adhiṭṭhātīti vuccati. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Evanti [M 2.0011] pakārattho evaṃ-saddo, tena sabbampi adhiṭṭhānappakāraṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Adhiṭṭhānavasenāti “ñāṇena adhiṭṭhātī”ti (paṭi. ma. 3.10) evaṃ vuttaadhiṭṭhānavasena nipphannattā.

370. ‘One by nature’ (pakatiyā eko) means one by its own intrinsic nature (sabhāvena). ‘Numerous’ (bahukaṃ) means many (bahuṃ). By this, having shown the unquantified multiplicity of what is to be determined, it was then stated, ‘a hundred, or…’ and so on, in order to show it by way of specific limitation. ‘He adverts’ (āvajjati) means: with the advertence (ābhogena) called preliminary work (parikammasaṅkhātena), he inclines (ābhujati) toward the future form (bhāvirūpe); with that preliminary attention (parikammamanasikārena), he brings it to mind (manasi karoti). ‘He determines with knowledge’ (ñāṇena adhiṭṭhāti) means that having performed the preliminary work in this way, he determines the desired multiple forms by means of supernormal knowledge; and because the attainment of multiplicity occurs simultaneously with the determining mind, while causing the knowledge of psychic power that brings about multiplicity to arise, he is thus said to determine. The same method applies in the remaining cases. The word ‘evaṃ’ (thus) has the sense of manner, and thereby it encompasses every kind of determination. ‘By way of determination’ (adhiṭṭhānavasena) means because it is accomplished by way of the determination stated thus: ‘he determines with knowledge’ (Paṭisambhidāmagga 3.10).

371. Pakativaṇṇanti pakatisaṇṭhānaṃ attano pākatikarūpaṃ. Pakativaṇṇavijahanavikāravasenāti attano pakativaṇṇavijahanapubbakassa kumārakavaṇṇādivaṇṇavikārassa vasena.

371. ‘Pakativaṇṇa’ means one’s natural shape, one’s own natural form. ‘Pakativaṇṇavijahanavikāravasena’ means by way of a transformation of form, such as the form of a young boy, that is preceded by abandoning one’s natural form.

372. Imamhā kāyāti paccakkhabhāvena “imamhā”ti vuttā bhikkhussa karajakāyā. Aññaṃ kāyanti aññaṃ iddhimayaṃ kāyaṃ. Tato eva iddhimayarūpavantatāya rūpiṃ. Abhiññāmanena [V 2.0011] nibbattattā manomayaṃ. Nipphattivasenāti nipphajjanavasena. Abhiññāñāṇassa hi yathā manomayo kāyo nipphajjati, tathā pavatti manomayiddhi. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Yadi evaṃ kathamayameva manomayiddhīti? Ruḷhīvesā veditabbā yathā “manomayo attabhāvo”ti, yathā vā “gosamaññā visāṇādimati piṇḍe”. Atha vā abbhantarato nikkhante, iddhimatā ca ekantasadise imasmiṃ nimmāne supākaṭo manasā nibbattitabhāvoti yathā sātisayo manomayavohāro, na tathā aññāsu adhiṭṭhānavikubbaniddhīsu samaññantaravantāsūti veditabbaṃ.

372. ‘From this body’ refers to the monk’s physical body, which is called ‘this’ by way of its perceptibility. ‘Another body’ means another body made of psychic power. For that very reason, because it is endowed with form made of psychic power, it is termed ‘material.’ Because it is produced by the mind of supernormal knowledge, it is ‘mind-made.’ ‘By way of production’ means by way of accomplishment. For the functioning of the supernormal knowledge in such a way that a mind-made body is produced is the mind-made psychic power. This same method applies also in the remaining cases. If so, how is it that this one alone is called mind-made psychic power? It should be understood as an established usage, just as there is the expression ‘a mind-made existence,’ or just as the designation ‘cow’ applies to a mass possessing horns and so forth. Alternatively, in this creation, which emerges from within and is absolutely similar to the possessor of psychic power, the fact of being created by the mind is very evident. Therefore, it should be understood that the expression ‘mind-made’ is especially prominent here in a way that it is not in the other psychic powers of determination and transformation, which have different conventional designations.

373. Ñāṇuppattito pubbe vāti arahattamaggañāṇuppattito pubbe vā vipassanākkhaṇe, tatopi vā pubbe antimabhavikassa paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāya. Pacchā vā yāva khandhaparinibbānā. Taṅkhaṇe vā magguppattisamaye. Ñāṇānubhāvanibbatto visesoti sūriyassa uṭṭhitaṭṭhāne, samantato ca ālokakaraṇasamatthatā viya tasseva ñāṇassa ānubhāvena nibbatto sabbaso pahātabbapahānabhāvetabbabhāvanāpāripūrisaṅkhāto viseso. Vatthūni pana anantarāyatāvasena āgatāni. Aniccānupassanāyāti saṅkhāre aniccato anupassantiyā balavavipassanāya. Āraddhavipassanassa hi yathāvuttavipassanāya pavattikkhaṇe tato pubbe, pacchā ca pakiṇṇakasammasanavāre niccasaññāya pahānaṭṭho ijjhati. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Kāmaṃ ettakāya saṅkhepakathāyapi adhippetattho pakāsitova[M 2.0012], vitthārakathāya pana vibhūtataro hotīti āha “vitthārena kathetabba”nti.

373. ‘Before the arising of knowledge’ means either before the arising of the knowledge of the path to Arahantship, during a moment of insight, or even before that, starting from the taking of rebirth-linking of one in their final existence. ‘After’ means up until the final passing away of the aggregates. ‘At that moment’ means at the time of the arising of the path. ‘The distinction produced by the power of knowledge’ refers to a distinction brought about by the power of that very knowledge—like the sun's ability to produce light at the place where it rises and all around—that is called the complete fulfillment of the abandoning of what is to be abandoned and the development of what is to be developed. The objects, however, are presented by way of being free from obstruction. ‘By the contemplation of impermanence’ means by strong insight that contemplates formations as impermanent. For one who has undertaken insight, the purpose of abandoning the perception of permanence is accomplished at the moment of the occurrence of the aforementioned insight, both before and after it, and during the phase of reviewing scattered formations. This is the method in all cases. Although the intended meaning is indeed clarified even by this brief account, it becomes especially clear through a detailed account; therefore, he said, ‘it should be explained in detail.’

Gabbhagatassevāti anādare sāmivacanaṃ. Vuttanayenāti “pacchimabhavikassā”tiādinā bākulattheravatthumhi vuttanayena.

‘Gabbhagatasseva’ is a genitive expression denoting disregard. ‘Vuttanayena’ (in the way stated) means in the manner stated in the story of Elder Bākula, beginning with ‘pacchimabhavikassa’ (of one in his final existence).

Dārubhāraṃ katvāti dārubhāraṃ sakaṭe katvā, āropetvāti attho. Ossajjitvāti chaḍḍetvā. Sakaṭamūleti sakaṭasamīpe. Vāḷayakkhānucariteti kururehi yakkhehi anuvicaritabbe. Yakkhapariggahitañhi rājagahanagaraṃ.

‘Having made a load of wood’ means having made a load of wood on a cart, that is, having loaded it. ‘Having let go’ means having discarded. ‘At the foot of the cart’ means near the cart. ‘Frequented by fierce yakkhas’ means to be frequented by cruel yakkhas. For the city of Rājagaha was indeed possessed by yakkhas.

374. Samādhitoti paṭhamajjhānādisamādhito. Pubbeti upacārajjhānakkhaṇe. Pacchāti samāpattiyā ciṇṇapariyante. Taṅkhaṇeti samāpannakkhaṇe. Samathānubhāvanibbatto visesoti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ [V 2.0012] jhāne samādhitejena nibbatto nīvaraṇavikkhambhanavitakkādisamatikkamasaññāvedayitanirodhaparissayasahanādiko viseso.

374. ‘From concentration’ means from the concentration beginning with the first jhāna. ‘Before’ means at the moment of access jhāna. ‘After’ means at the end of having practiced the attainment. ‘At that moment’ means at the moment of entering the attainment. ‘The distinction produced by the power of serenity’ means a distinction arising from the power of concentration in each respective jhāna, a distinction that begins with the suppression of the hindrances, the overcoming of initial thought and so on, and the enduring of dangers related to the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.

Kapotakandarāyanti evaṃnāmake araññavihāre. Juṇhāya rattiyāti candālokavatiyā rattiyā. Navoropitehi kesehīti itthambhūtalakkhaṇe karaṇavacanaṃ. Yassāti pahārassa. Tassāti yakkhassa. Khippanisantibhāvassa ukkaṃsagatattā thero tasmiṃ paharante eva samāpattiṃ samāpajjīti āha “paharaṇasamaye samāpattiṃ appesī”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “nisinno hoti aññataraṃ samādhiṃ samāpajjitvā”ti (udā. 34) vuttaṃ. Ime pana therā samāpattito vuṭṭhānasamakālaṃ tena pahāro dinnoti vadanti.

“In Kapotakandara” means in a forest monastery of that name. “On a moonlit night” means on a night bright with moonlight. “With freshly shaved hair” is an instrumental expression denoting a characteristic. “Of which” means of the blow. “Of that” means of the yakkha. Due to the supreme swiftness of his attainment of quiescence, it is said that the elder entered attainment at the very moment he was being struck: “At the moment of the blow, he applied attainment.” In the Pāḷi text, however, it is said: “He sat down, having entered a certain absorption” (Ud 34). But these elders say that the blow was given at the very moment of emerging from attainment.

Sañjīvattheranti kakusandhassa bhagavato dutiyaṃ aggasāvakaṃ mahātheraṃ sandhāyāha. So hi āyasmā araññādīsu yattha katthaci nisinno appakasireneva nirodhaṃ samāpajjati, tasmā ekadivasaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nirodhaṃ samāpajji, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “nirodhasamāpanna”ntiādi. Cīvare aṃsumattampi na jhāyittha, sarīre kā kathā. Teneva hi thero “sañjīvo” tveva paññāyittha. Ayamassāti assa āyasmato sañjīvattherassa yo nirodhasamāpattiyaṃ aggiparissayābhāvo, ayaṃ samādhivipphārā [M 2.0013] iddhīti yojanā. Kathaṃ pana nirodhasamāpattiyaṃ samādhivipphārasambhavoti āha “anupubba…pe… nibbattattā”ti.

“The elder Sañjīva” is said with reference to the great elder, the second chief disciple of the Blessed One Kakusandha. For wherever this venerable one sat in the forest or elsewhere, he attained cessation without difficulty. Therefore, one day, at the foot of a certain tree, he attained cessation; with reference to this it is said, “having attained cessation,” etc. Not even a fiber of his robe was burnt, what then of his body? For that very reason, the elder was known as “Sañjīva.” “This of his” means: for this venerable elder Sañjīva, the absence of danger from fire while in the attainment of cessation is a psychic power that is the pervasion of concentration—this is the connection. But how is the arising of the pervasion of concentration possible in the attainment of cessation? He said, “Because it is produced in sequence…”

Paṭhamaṃ ṭhapitabhaṇḍakassāti sabbapaṭhamaṃ ṭhapitabhaṇḍakassa. Tañhi gahaṇakāle sabbapacchimaṃ gayhati. Kālaparicchedavasenāti “ettake kāle gate vuṭṭhahissāmī”ti samāpattito pubbe katakālaparicchedavasena. Bhītā viraviṃsūti rattandhakāre rūpadassanena “pisāco uṭṭhahatī”ti maññamānā. Ettakehi nāma bhaṇḍakehi ajjhotthaṭo nibbikāro “aho mahānubhāvo, aho vivekavāsī”ti ca theragatena pasādena.

“Of the first-placed bundle” means of the very first bundle that was placed. For that is taken last at the time of taking. “By means of determining the time” means by means of the determination of time made before the attainment, thus: “I shall emerge after so much time has passed.” “Terrified, they cried out” means that, upon seeing a form in the darkness of night, they thought, “A goblin is rising!” And with faith directed towards the elder, who was unperturbed though covered by so many goods, they thought: “Oh, what great power! Oh, what a dweller in seclusion!”

Tattatelakaṭāhanti ādhārasīsena ādheyyamāha, kaṭāhe tattatelaṃ kaṭāhena āsiñcīti adhippāyo. Vivaṭṭamānanti katthacipi alagganavasena bhassantaṃ.

“A cauldron of boiling oil” refers to the contained (the oil) by way of the container. The meaning is that one sprinkled the boiling oil in the cauldron with the cauldron. “Rolling freely” means slipping off without sticking anywhere.

Saparivārāti pañcahi itthisatehi saparivārā. Rājānaṃ mettāya pharīti odissakamettāsamāpattiyā [V 2.0013] rājānaṃ phusi. Khipitunti vijjhituṃ. Oropetunti sarasannāhaṃ paṭisaṃharituṃ.

“With her retinue” means with a retinue of five hundred women. “He suffused the king with loving-kindness” means he touched the king with the attainment of loving-kindness specifically directed at him. “To shoot” means to pierce. “To lower” means to withdraw the nocked arrow.

375. Paṭikkūlādīsūti aniṭṭhādīsu. Aniṭṭhaṃ hi paṭikkūlaṃ, amanuññampi “paṭikkūla”nti vuccati. Ādi-saddena apaṭikkūlādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tatthāti paṭikkūlārammaṇe. Upekkhakoti chaḷaṅgupekkhāya upekkhako. Tatthāti paṭikkūlāpaṭikkūlabhede vatthusmiṃ. Satoti sativepullappattiyā satimā. Sampajānoti paññāvepullappattiyā sampajānakārī. Ayanti ayaṃ paṭikkūlādivatthūsu apaṭikkūlasaññīvihārādikā khīṇāsavānaṃ aggamaggādhigamasiddhā cittissariyatā. Tenāha “cetovasippattānaṃ…pe… vuccatī”ti.

375. “In the repulsive, etc.” means in the undesirable, etc. For the undesirable is repulsive, and the unpleasant is also called “repulsive.” By the word “etc.,” it includes the non-repulsive, etc. “Therein” means in a repulsive object. “Equanimous” means one who is equanimous by way of six-factored equanimity. “Therein” means in an object differentiated as repulsive and non-repulsive. “Mindful” means one who is mindful by way of attaining the fullness of mindfulness. “Clearly comprehending” means one who acts with clear comprehension by way of attaining the fullness of wisdom. “This” means this mastery of mind of those whose taints are destroyed—which consists of dwelling with the perception of non-repulsiveness, etc., in objects such as the repulsive, and which is accomplished through the attainment of the supreme path. Therefore he said, “For those who have attained mastery over the mind… it is said.”

Aniṭṭhe vatthusmiṃ sattasaññite mettāpharaṇaṃ vā dhātuso paccavekkhaṇāya dhātumanasikāraṃ vā gūthādike dhātumanasikāraṃ karontoti yojetabbaṃ. Apaṭikkūlasaññī viharatīti hitesitāya, dhammasabhāvacintanāya ca na paṭikkūlasaññī hutvā iriyāpathavihārena viharati. Iṭṭhe vatthusmiṃ ñātimittādike. Kesādiasucikoṭṭhāsamattamevāti asubhapharaṇaṃ vā asubhamanasikāraṃ vā. Tattha rūpadhammajātaṃ aniccanti ādiattho iti-saddo, tasmā aniccadukkhānattavipariṇāmadhammoti manasikāraṃ [M 2.0014] vā karontoti yojanā. Paṭikkūlāpaṭikkūlesūti iṭṭhāniṭṭhāni vatthūni ekajjhaṃ gahetvā vadati. Esa nayo itarattha. Yaṃ vā sattānaṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭikkūlato upaṭṭhitameva pacchā apaṭikkūlato upatiṭṭhati, yañca apaṭikkūlato upaṭṭhitameva pacchā paṭikkūlato upatiṭṭhati, tadubhayepi khīṇāsavo sace ākaṅkhati, vuttanayena apaṭikkūlasaññī vā vihareyya, paṭikkūlasaññī vāti ayamariyiddhi vuttā.

It should be connected thus: in an undesirable object perceived as a being, one applies either the pervasion of loving-kindness or mental advertence to the elements by reflecting on them as elements; in things like excrement, one applies mental advertence to the elements. “Dwells perceiving non-repulsiveness” means that through the desire for welfare and through contemplation of the nature of phenomena, one dwells by means of the postures, having become one who does not perceive repulsiveness. In a desirable object, such as relatives and friends, one applies either the pervasion of foulness or mental advertence to foulness, regarding it as nothing more than the collection of impure parts such as hair. Therein, the word “iti” in “aniccanti” has the meaning of “etc.”; therefore, the connection is that one applies mental advertence as “impermanent, suffering, non-self, and subject to change.” “In the repulsive and non-repulsive” is said taking desirable and undesirable objects together. This is the method elsewhere. Or, that which for beings first appears as repulsive but later appears as non-repulsive, and that which first appears as non-repulsive but later appears as repulsive—in both these cases, if one whose taints are destroyed so wishes, one may dwell, by the method described, either perceiving non-repulsiveness or perceiving repulsiveness. This is called the noble psychic power.

Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvāti kāraṇavasena “cakkhū”ti laddhavohārena rūpadassanasamatthena cakkhuviññāṇena, cakkhunā vā kāraṇabhūtena, dvārabhūtena vā rūpaṃ passitvā. Neva sumano hotīti gehassitasomanassassāyaṃ paṭikkhepo, na nekkhammapakkhikāya kiriyāsomanassavedanāya. Chaḷaṅgupekkhanti iṭṭhāniṭṭhachaḷārammaṇāpāthe parisuddhapakatibhāvāvijahanalakkhaṇaṃ chasu dvāresu pavattiyā “chaḷaṅgupekkhā”ti laddhanāmaṃ tatramajjhattupekkhaṃ. Yathāvuttamatthaṃ pāḷiyā samatthetuṃ “paṭisambhidāya”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

“Having seen a form with the eye” means having seen a form with eye-consciousness, which is capable of seeing forms and is conventionally termed “eye” by way of its cause; or, having seen a form with the eye, which is the cause and the door. “Is not pleased” is a rejection of the joy associated with household life, not of the functional feeling of joy pertaining to renunciation. “Six-factored equanimity” refers to the equanimity of impartiality, which is so named because of its arising in the six doors, and which is characterized by not abandoning the pure natural state when in the sphere of the six desirable and undesirable sense-objects. In order to support the stated meaning with the Pāḷi text, it is said, “in the Paṭisambhidā,” etc.

376. Pakkhīādīnanti [V 2.0014] ādi-saddena devādīnaṃ saṅgaho. Vehāsagamanādikāti pana ādi-saddena cakkhuvisuddhiādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kusalakammena nibbattitvāpi akusalavipākānubhāvena sukhasamussayato vinipatitattā vinipātikānaṃ. Jhānanti abhiññāpattaṃ jhānaṃ sandhāyāha. Vipassanāpi ukkaṃsagatā ubbegapītisahitā ākāse laṅghāpanamattāpi hotīti vuttaṃ “vipassanaṃ vā”ti. “Paṭhamakappikāna”nti idaṃ “ekaccānaṃ manussāna”nti imassa visesanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evamādīnanti ādi-saddena punabbasumātādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.

376. In the term pakkhīādīnaṃ ('of birds, etc.'), by the word 'etc.' (ādi), the inclusion of deities, etc., is to be understood. Moreover, in the term vehāsagamanādikā ('traveling through the air, etc.'), by the word 'etc.' (ādi), it includes the special purity of the eye, etc. The term vinipātikānaṃ ('of those in downfall') is used because, although they arise due to wholesome kamma, they have fallen from an abundance of happiness due to the power of the result of unwholesome kamma. By jhāna, he spoke referring to the jhāna that has attained supernormal knowledge. Because even insight (vipassanā), when it has reached excellence and is accompanied by uplifting rapture, is capable of causing merely leaping in the air, it was said, 'or insight' (vipassanaṃ vā). This term paṭhamakappikānaṃ ('of those of the first aeon') should be seen as a qualifier of the term ekaccānaṃ manussānaṃ ('of some humans'). In the term evamādīnaṃ ('and so on'), by the word 'etc.' (ādi), the inclusion of Punabbasu's mother, etc., should be understood.

377. Vehāsanti bhummatthe upayogavacanaṃ, accantasaṃyoge vā. Cakkavattī hi cakkaratanaṃ purakkhatvā attano bhavanato abbhuggantvā ākāseneva sineruṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā sakalacakkavāḷaṃ anusaṃyāyatīti. Assabandhāti assapālā, ye assānaṃ yavadāyakā. Tathā gobandhā.

377. The word vehāsaṃ is an accusative used in the locative sense, or in the sense of continuous connection. For a wheel-turning monarch, having the wheel-treasure as his vanguard, rises up from his palace and, traveling only through the sky, circumambulates Mount Sineru to the right before traversing the entire world-system. Assabandhā are horse-keepers, those who provide barley for horses. Similarly, gobandhā are cattle-keepers.

Cakkavattiādīnaṃ puññiddhiyā vitthāriyamānāya atipapañco hotīti puññavato iddhiṃ lakkhaṇato dassentena “paripākaṃ gate puññasambhāre ijjhanakaviseso”ti [M 2.0015] vatvāpi jotikādīnaṃ puññiddhiṃ ekadesena dassetuṃ “ettha cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha suvaṇṇapabbatoti sabbasuvaṇṇamayo pabbato. Tassa kira gahitagahitaṭṭhāne odhi na paññāyati. Ekasītāmatteti ettha sītā nāma kasanavasena naṅgalassa gatamaggo. Tumbaṃ nāma āḷhakaṃ. Cuddasa maggāti catuddasa kasanamaggā.

When the psychic power of merit of wheel-turning monarchs and others is elaborated upon, it would become too extensive. Therefore, wishing to show the psychic power of a meritorious one by its characteristic, even after having said, "When the accumulation of merit has reached maturity, it is a special kind of success," in order to show in part the psychic power from the merit of Jotika and others, "and here..." etc., was said. Therein, suvaṇṇapabbato is a mountain made entirely of gold. It is said that wherever one takes from it, its limit is not perceived. Herein, in ekasītāmatta, sītā is the name for the path taken by the plough by means of ploughing. Tumba is the name for an āḷhaka. Cuddasa maggā means fourteen plough-paths.

378. Vijjaṃ parijapitvāti gandhārīvijjādikaṃ attano vijjaṃ katūpacāraṃ parivattetvā mantapaṭhanakkamena paṭhitvā.

378. 'Having recited a spell' (vijjaṃ parijapitvā) means: having performed the preliminary rites for one's own spell-craft, such as the Gandhārī spell, having recited it repeatedly, and having chanted it according to the sequence of mantra-recitation.

379. Sammāpayogenāti upāyapayogena, yathā yathicchitatthasiddhi hoti, tathā pavattitañāyārambhena. Tassa tassa kammassāti yathādhippetassa nipphādetabbakammassa. Ettha cāti “tattha tattha sammāpayogappaccayā ijjhanaṭṭhena iddhī”ti (paṭi. ma. 3.18) imissā dasamāya iddhiyā niddesepi. Purimapāḷisadisāvā”ti samādhivipphāraiddhiādīnaṃ niddesasadisāva. Sakaṭabyūhādikaraṇavasenāti sakaṭabyūhacakkabyūhapadumabyūhādīnaṃ saṃvidhānavasena nibbattavisesoti [V 2.0015] sambandho. Gaṇitagandhabbādi sippakammaṃ. Sallakattakādi vejjakammaṃ. Irubbedādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ.

379. ‘Through right application’ means through the application of skillful means, by initiating a method that leads to the achievement of the desired goal. ‘Of each task’ means of each task to be accomplished as intended. And here too, in the explanation of this tenth psychic power: ‘psychic power in the sense of success on account of right application in each case.’ ‘Is just like the previous Pāḷi’ means it is just like the description of the psychic power of pervading concentration and so on. ‘By way of making formations like the cart-array’ means the specific result produced by way of arrangements such as the cart-array, wheel-array, lotus-array, and so on; this is the connection. Calculation, the art of music, and so on, is the work of the crafts. Surgery and so on is the work of medicine. Of the three Vedas, beginning with the Ṛgveda.

“Ekopi hutvā bahudhāva hotī”tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.238; ma. ni. 1.147; saṃ. ni. 5.834; paṭi. ma. 1.102; 3.10) adhiṭṭhāniddhiyā eva gahitattā āha “adhiṭṭhānā iddhiyeva āgatā”ti. Imasmiṃ panattheti imasmiṃ abhiññānisaṃsasaṅkhāte, iddhividhasaṅkhāte vā atthe.

Since the phrase ‘Being one, he becomes many,’ and so on is taken as referring to the psychic power of determination, it is said, ‘It is indeed the psychic power of determination that has come forth.’ ‘In this matter’ refers to this matter, which is termed the benefit of higher knowledge, or to the topic which is termed the mode of psychic power.

380. “Ekavidhena ñāṇavatthu”ntiādīsu (vibha. 751) koṭṭhāsattho vidhasaddo, “vividhampi senābyūhaṃ dassetī”tiādīsu (paṭi. ma. 3.13) vikappattho, tadubhayampettha yujjatīti dassento āha “iddhividhāyāti iddhikoṭṭhāsāya, iddhivikappāya vā”ti. Iddhi hi abhiññāsu eko koṭṭhāso, vakkhamānehi bhedehi anekappabhedā ca. Vuttappakāravasenāti vuttassa cuddasappakārassa, cittaparidamanassa samāhitatādippakārassa ca vasena. “Iddhividhāyā”ti tadatthassa sampadānavacananti āha “iddhividhādhigamatthāyā”ti. “Kasiṇārammaṇato apanetvā”ti idaṃ abhiññāpādakaparikammacittānaṃ [M 2.0016] samānasantānatāya vuttaṃ, na parikammacittassa kasiṇārammaṇattā. Iddhividhābhimukhaṃ pesetīti nipphādetabbassa iddhividhassa abhimukhabhāvena pavatteti. Yaṃ hi “sataṃ homī”tiādinā parikammacittassa pavattanaṃ, tadevassa abhinīharaṇaṃ, iddhividhābhimukhapesanañca tatheva iddhividhassa pavattanato abhininnāmanaṃ idha parikammacittassa iddhividhe adhimuttīti āha “adhigantabbaiddhipoṇaṃ iddhipabbhāraṃ karotī”ti. Idha paccanubhavanaphusanā sacchikiriyāpattipariyāyā evāti dassento “pāpuṇātīti attho”ti āha. Assāti iddhividhassa.

380. In phrases such as 'a knowledge-object of one kind', the word 'vidha' has the meaning of 'part'; in phrases such as 'he displays various army formations', it has the meaning of 'variety'. Showing that both are applicable here, he said: 'iddhividhāya means for a part of psychic power, or for a variety of psychic power.' For psychic power is one part among the higher knowledges, and it is of many varieties by way of the distinctions to be spoken of. 'By way of the kinds spoken of' refers to the fourteen kinds spoken of, and to the kinds, such as concentration, of the mental subjugation. The expression 'iddhividhāya' is a term in the dative case for that purpose; hence, he said: 'for the purpose of attaining the manifestation of psychic power.' The phrase 'having removed it from the kasiṇa object' is said because the preliminary consciousnesses that are the basis for higher knowledge have a similar continuum, not because the preliminary consciousness has the kasiṇa as its object. 'He directs it towards the manifestation of psychic power' means he causes it to proceed in the manner of facing the manifestation of psychic power that is to be accomplished. For whatever proceeding of the preliminary consciousness there is by way of thoughts such as 'May I become a hundred', that itself is its application and its directing towards the manifestation of psychic power, because the manifestation of psychic power proceeds in that very same way. Here, the inclining is the resolve of the preliminary consciousness upon the manifestation of psychic power; hence, he said: 'it makes it inclined towards the psychic power to be attained, sloped towards psychic power.' Showing that here, experiencing, touching, and realizing are indeed synonyms for attainment, he said: ''pāpuṇāti' means 'attains'.' 'Assa' refers to 'of the manifestation of psychic power' (iddhividhassa).

Ekopīti pi-saddo vakkhamānaṃ bahubhāvaṃ upādāya sampiṇḍanattho. So hissa paṭiyogī “ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hotī”ti. So ca kho bahubhāvaṃ nimminitvā ṭhitassa antarāva ekabhāvūpagamo. Yathākālaparicchedaṃ pana saraseneva ekabhāvūpagamo idha nādhippeto aniddhinimmānabhāvato. Tampi pubbe katakālaparicchedavasena siddhattā iddhānubhāvoyevāti keci. Aṭṭhāne vāyaṃ pi-saddo, eko hutvā bahudhāpi hoti, bahudhā hutvā ekopi hotīti sambandho. Imasmiṃ pakkhe pi-saddo vakkhamānaṃ ekabhāvaṃ upādāya [V 2.0016] “sampiṇḍanattho”ti vatvā “so hī”tiādi sabbaṃ yathārahaṃ vattabbaṃ. Bahubhāvanimmāne payojanaṃ dassetuṃ “bahūnaṃ santike”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha bahūnaṃ santiketi attanā nimmitānaṃ bahūnaṃ samīpe, tehi parivārito hutvāti adhippāyo. Vā-saddo avuttavikappattho, tena “dhammaṃ vā kathetukāmo”ti evamādi saṅgayhati. “Ñāṇena adhiṭṭhahanto evaṃ hotī”ti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ.

In 'ekopi', the particle 'pi' has the meaning of aggregation, taking into consideration the multiplicity that will be described. Its counterpart is: 'Being one, he becomes many; being many also, he becomes one.' And that attainment of oneness is an intermediate stage for one who, having created multiplicity, remains established. However, an attainment of oneness according to a temporal division, by its own nature, is not intended here, since it is not a creation by psychic power. Some say this too is indeed the might of psychic power, by reason of its accomplishment through a temporal division made previously. Alternatively, this particle 'pi' is out of place, and the connection is: 'Being one, he becomes many also; being many, he becomes one also.' In this alternative view, having stated that 'the particle 'pi' has the meaning of aggregation,' taking into consideration the oneness that will be described, everything beginning with 'so hī' should be explained as appropriate. To show the purpose of creating multiplicity, 'in the presence of many' and so on was said. Therein, 'in the presence of many' (bahūnaṃ santike) means in the presence of the many created by oneself, the intention being 'having been surrounded by them.' The particle 'vā' expresses an unstated alternative; thus, 'or wishing to teach the Dhamma' and so on are included. 'Determining with knowledge, he becomes thus' should be brought in and connected.

381. Bhavati ettha iddhīti bhūmiyo, jhānāni. Etthāti ca hetumhi bhummavacanaṃ. Vivekato jātā bhūmi vivekajabhūmi. Vivekajaṃ hi paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ nīvaraṇavivekasambhūtattā. Pītisukhabhūtā bhūmi pītisukhabhūmi. Dutiyajjhānañhi pītisukhabhūmibhūtañceva pītisukhasañjātañca samādhivasena. Upari dvīsupi eseva nayo. Iddhilābhāyāti iddhiyā adhigamāya. Iddhipaṭilābhāyāti iddhiyā punappunaṃ labhamānāya, bahulīkaraṇāyāti attho. Iddhivikubbanatāyāti iddhiyā vividharūpakāraṇāya, vikubbaniddhiyāti attho[M 2.0017]. Iddhivisavitāyāti iddhiyā vividhānisaṃsapasavanāya. Iddhivasitāyāti iddhiyā khippanisantiādibhāvāvahavasībhāvatthāya. Iddhivesārajjāyāti iddhiyā paṭipakkhadūrībhāvena vigatasaṃkilesatāya suṭṭhu visāradabhāvāya. Catutthajjhānaṃ tāva iddhiyā bhūmi hotu tattha patiṭṭhāya nipphādetabbato, itarāni pana kathanti āha “ettha cā”tiādi. Tattha tīṇi jhānāni sambhārabhūmiyoti veditabbānīti sambandho. Tatiyajjhāne sukhapharaṇena, paṭhamadutiyesu pītipharaṇena sukhapharaṇena ca hetubhūtenāti yathārahavasena yojanā. Pharaṇaṃ cettha jhānassa subhāvitabhāvena sātisayānaṃ pītisukhānaṃ vasena jhānappaccayādinā sahajātanāmakāyassa paribrūhanaṃ, rūpakāyassa ca taṃsamuṭṭhānehi paṇītarūpehi paripphuṭatā. Tenāha bhagavā “pītisukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharatī”ti (dī. ni. 1.226; ma. ni. 1.427). Sukhasaññanti jhānasukhena sahagataṃ saññaṃ. Lahusaññanti taṃsampayuttalahutāsahagataṃ saññaṃ. Okkamitvāti anupavisitvā. Tesu hi jhānesu sātisayāya lahutāya sampayuttaṃ sukhaṃ santānavasena pavattento yogī taṃ samokkanto viya hotīti evaṃ vuttaṃ. Saññāsīsena niddeso. Jhānasampayuttā hi lahutā vināpi iddhiyā ākāsaṃ laṅghāpanappamāṇappattā viya hoti. Lahubhāvaggahaṇeneva cettha mudukammaññabhāvāpi gahitā eva. Tenāha “lahumudukammaññakāyo hutvā”ti.

381. 'Psychic power comes to be on account of this' (bhavati ettha iddhi), therefore they are called 'grounds' (bhūmiyo); these grounds are the jhānas. And 'ettha' is a locative expression in the sense of cause. 'A ground born from seclusion' (vivekato jātā bhūmi) is the seclusion-born ground. For the first jhāna is seclusion-born, due to its arising from seclusion from the hindrances. 'A ground that has become joy and happiness' (pītisukhabhūtā bhūmi) is the joy-and-happiness ground. The second jhāna is indeed both what has become the joy-and-happiness ground and is born of joy and happiness by means of concentration. This same method applies to the two higher grounds as well. 'For the attainment of psychic power' (iddhilābhāya) means for achieving psychic power. 'For the re-attainment of psychic power' (iddhipaṭilābhāya) means for repeatedly obtaining psychic power, that is, for its cultivation. 'For transformation by psychic power' (iddhivikubbanatāya) means for the creation of various forms by means of psychic power; the meaning is the psychic power of transformation. 'For the producing by psychic power' (iddhivisavitāya) means for producing the various benefits of psychic power. 'For mastery in psychic power' (iddhivasitāya) means for the state of mastery that brings about swiftness and so on in psychic power.
