'For confidence in psychic power' (iddhivesārajjāya) means for the state of being thoroughly confident in psychic power, through being far from opposition and due to the absence of defilements. Let the fourth jhāna be the ground for psychic power, since it is to be accomplished by being established therein; but how are the others grounds? Thus, he said, 'And here...' and so on. Therein, the connection is that the three jhānas are to be known as preparatory grounds. The connection is to be made according to what is appropriate: in the third jhāna, by the pervasion of happiness; in the first and second, by the pervasion of joy and the pervasion of happiness, which have become the cause. And here, 'pervasion' is the augmentation of the co-arisen mental body through the power of the abundant joy and happiness—due to the well-developed state of the jhāna—by means of the jhāna-condition and so on, and the suffusion of the physical body with the refined material forms produced from that. Therefore, the Blessed One said: 'With joy and happiness he drenches, saturates, fills, and pervades.' 'Perception of happiness' (sukhasaññaṃ) means the perception associated with the happiness of jhāna. 'Perception of lightness' (lahusaññaṃ) means the perception associated with the lightness connected to it. 'Having entered' (okkamitvā) means having penetrated. For in those jhānas, the yogī who causes happiness connected with abundant lightness to proceed by way of a continuum is as if he has thoroughly penetrated it; therefore, it is stated thus. This is an exposition with perception as the heading. Indeed, the lightness associated with jhāna, even without psychic power, is as if it has reached the measure of being able to cause leaping into the sky. And here, by the taking up of the state of lightness, the states of pliancy and wieldiness are also included. Therefore, he said: 'having become light, pliant, and wieldy in body.'

Iminā [V 2.0017] pariyāyenāti tiṇṇaṃ jhānānaṃ samāpajjanena sukhalahubhāvappattanāmarūpakāyassa sati cittaparidamane catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sukheneva iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattatīti iminā pariyāyena. Pakatibhūmiyā hi adhiṭṭhānabhūtā sambhārabhūmiyo pākārassa nemippadeso viyāti.

By this method means: for a person whose mental and physical body has reached a state of happiness and lightness through entering into the three jhānas, when there is subjugation of the mind, the fourth jhāna conduces with ease to the re-attainment of psychic power. Thus, by this method. Indeed, for the natural ground (which is the fourth jhāna), the preparatory grounds (the three lower jhānas), being its foundation, are like the foundation-course of a rampart.

382. Iddhipādaniddese cattāroti gaṇanaparicchedo. Iddhipādāti ettha ijjhatīti iddhi, samijjhati nipphajjatīti attho. Ijjhanti vā etāya sattā iddhā vuddhā ukkaṃsagatā hontīti iddhi. Paṭhamenatthena iddhi eva pādoti iddhipādo, iddhikoṭṭhāsoti attho. Dutiyenatthena iddhiyā pādoti iddhipādo. Pādoti patiṭṭhā, adhigamūpāyoti attho. Tena hi uparūparivisesasaṅkhātaṃ iddhiṃ pajjanti pāpuṇanti. Ayaṃ tāva aṭṭhakathānayo. Tattha iddhi-saddassa paṭhamo kattuattho, dutiyo karaṇattho [M 2.0018] vutto. Pāda-saddassa eko karaṇatthova. Pajjitabbāva iddhi vuttā, na ca ijjhantī, pajjitabbā ca iddhi pajjanakaraṇena pādena samānādhikaraṇā hotīti paṭhamena atthena “iddhi eva pādo iddhipādo”ti na sakkā vattuṃ. Tathā iddhikiriyākaraṇena sādhetabbāva vuddhisaṅkhātā iddhi pajjanakiriyākaraṇena pajjitabbāti dvinnaṃ karaṇānaṃ na asamānādhikaraṇatā sambhavatīti dutiyenatthena “iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo”ti ca na sakkā vattuṃ. Tasmā paṭhamenatthena samānādhikaraṇasamāso, dutiyena sāmivacanasamāso na yujjatīti paṭhamenatthena iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo, dutiyenatthena iddhi eva pādo iddhipādoti samāso yutto, yathāvuttopi vā, pādassa ijjhamānakoṭṭhāsaijjhanakaraṇūpāyabhāvato.

382. In the exposition of the bases of psychic power, 'four' is the definition of the number. Here, in the term 'iddhipāda', because 'it succeeds' (ijjhati), it is called 'iddhi'; the meaning is 'it is accomplished' (samijjhati), 'it is completed' (nipphajjati). Or, by this, beings prosper, grow, and become exalted; hence, it is 'iddhi'. By the first meaning (agentive), ''iddhi' itself is the 'pāda'' is 'iddhipāda'; the meaning is 'a portion of that which is accomplished'. By the second meaning (instrumental), ''the pāda of iddhi'' is 'iddhipāda'. 'Pāda' means foundation; the meaning is 'a means of attainment'. For by this they reach and attain the 'iddhi' known as ever higher and higher distinction. This, for now, is the method of the commentary. Therein, for the word 'iddhi', the first meaning is stated as agentive, the second as instrumental. For the word 'pāda', only one instrumental meaning is stated. 'Iddhi' is spoken of as that which is to be reached, not as that which is accomplishing. And 'iddhi', which is to be reached, cannot have the same locus as 'pāda', the instrument for reaching. Therefore, by the first meaning, it is not possible to say, ''Iddhi' itself is the 'pāda', [hence] 'iddhipāda'.' Similarly, the 'iddhi' called 'growth', which is to be accomplished by the instrument of the action of prospering, is to be reached by the instrument of the action of reaching. Since it is not possible for the two instruments to share the same locus, it is also not possible, by the second meaning, to say, ''the pāda of iddhi', [hence] 'iddhipāda'.' Therefore, an appositional compound (kammadhāraya) by the first meaning, and a genitive compound (tappurisa) by the second meaning, are not suitable. Thus, the suitable compound is: by the first meaning, ''the pāda to iddhi'' is 'iddhipāda' (a tappurisa compound); and by the second meaning, ''iddhi' itself is the 'pāda'' is 'iddhipāda' (a kammadhāraya compound). Or, even the analysis as stated [in the commentary] is suitable, because the 'pāda' has the nature of being both a portion of that which is being accomplished and the means which is the instrument for prospering.

Pubbabhāgachandavasena chandahetuko. Sampayuttachandavasena chandādhiko. Pubbābhisaṅkhāravasena eva pana sahajātachandassāpi adhikatā veditabbā. Atha vā “chandañce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ, labhati cittassekaggataṃ, ayaṃ vuccati chandasamādhī”ti imāya pāḷiyā chandādhipatisamādhi chandasamādhīti adhipati-saddalopaṃ katvā samāso vuttoti viññāyati. Adhipatisaddatthadassanavasena pana aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “chandahetuko chandādhiko vā samādhī”ti vuttaṃ. Tenevāha “chandaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā”tiādi. Padhānabhūtāti vīriyabhūtāti keci vadanti. Saṅkhatasaṅkhāranivattanatthaṃ pana padhānaggahaṇaṃ. Atha vā taṃ taṃ visesaṃ saṅkharotīti saṅkhāro, sabbampi vīriyaṃ. Tattha catukiccasādhakato aññassa nivattanatthaṃ padhānaggahaṇaṃ. Padhānabhūtā seṭṭhabhūtāti attho. Catubbidhassa pana vīriyassa adhippetattā bahuvacananiddeso. Yo pana “iddhiyā pādo iddhipādo”ti evaṃ samāsayojanāvasena pādassa upāyatthataṃ gahetvā iddhipādattho [V 2.0018] vutto, so paṭilābhapubbabhāgānaṃ kattukaraṇiddhibhāvaṃ “chandiddhipādo”tiādinā (vibha. 457) vā abhidhamme āgatattā chandādīhi iddhipādehi sādhetabbāya vuddhiyā kattiddhibhāvaṃ, chandādīnaṃ karaṇiddhibhāvañca sandhāya vuttoti veditabbo.

In terms of desire in the preliminary stage, it is caused by desire. In terms of associated desire, it is predominant in desire. However, the predominance even of co-arisen desire should be understood only in terms of prior volitional formation. Alternatively, it is understood that by this Pāli passage: 'If a bhikkhu, making desire the dominant factor, gains concentration, gains one-pointedness of mind, this is called concentration of desire,' the compound 'concentration of desire' is stated by eliding the word 'dominant factor' from 'concentration with desire as the dominant factor'. However, in the commentary, in order to show the meaning of the word 'dominant factor,' it is stated: 'concentration caused by desire or predominant in desire.' Therefore, it is said: 'making desire the dominant factor,' etc. Some say 'principal' means 'consisting of energy.' But the term 'principal' is used for the purpose of removing conditioned formations. Alternatively, 'saṅkhāra' is that which forms this or that distinction; all energy is such. Here, the term 'principal' is used to exclude that which is other than what accomplishes the fourfold task. The meaning is that they are principal, supreme. However, the plural designation is used because four kinds of energy are intended. As for that meaning of 'basis of psychic power' which is explained by taking 'pāda' in the sense of 'means' through a compound analysis such as 'the pāda of iddhi is iddhipāda,' it should be understood as being stated with reference to the agentive-iddhi and instrumental-iddhi nature of the attainment and its preliminary stages—since it is found in the Abhidhamma as 'the basis of psychic power that is desire,' etc. (Vibha. 457)—and with reference to the agentive-iddhi nature of the growth to be accomplished by the bases of psychic power such as desire, and the instrumental-iddhi nature of desire and the others.

Vīriyiddhipāde “vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgata”nti dvikkhattuṃ vīriyaṃ āgataṃ. Tattha purimaṃ samādhivisesanaṃ vīriyādhipati samādhi vīriyasamādhīti. Dutiyaṃ samannāgamaṅgadassanaṃ. Dve eva hi sabbattha samannāgamaṅgāni samādhi[M 2.0019], padhānasaṅkhāro ca. Chandādayo samādhivisesanāni, padhānasaṅkhāro pana padhānavacaneneva visesito, na chandādīhīti na idha vīriyādhipatitā padhānasaṅkhārassa vuttā hoti. Vīriyañca samādhiṃ visesetvā ṭhitameva samannāgamaṅgavasena padhānasaṅkhāravacanena vuttanti nāpi dvīhi vīriyehi samannāgamo vutto hotīti. Yasmā pana chandādīhi visiṭṭho samādhi, tathā visiṭṭheneva ca tena sampayutto padhānasaṅkhāro, sesadhammā ca, tasmā samādhivisesanānaṃ vasena cattāro iddhipādā vuttā. Visesanabhāvo ca chandādīnaṃ taṃtaṃavassayavasena hotīti.

In the basis of psychic power of energy, the word 'energy' appears twice in the phrase 'endowed with concentration of energy and with principal volitional formation'. Here, the first instance is a qualifier of concentration: concentration with energy as its dominant factor is 'concentration of energy'. The second instance indicates a factor of endowment. Indeed, everywhere there are only two factors of endowment: concentration and principal volitional formation. Desire and the others are qualifiers of concentration, but the principal volitional formation is qualified by the word 'principal' itself, not by desire and the others. Thus, the dominance of energy over the principal volitional formation is not stated here. And energy, having qualified concentration, is itself expressed by the word 'principal volitional formation' by way of being a factor of endowment; thus, endowment by two energies is also not stated. However, because concentration is distinguished by desire and the others, and because the principal volitional formation and the remaining states are associated with that very concentration thus distinguished, therefore the four bases of psychic power are stated in terms of the qualifiers of concentration. And the status of desire and the others as qualifiers occurs by way of their respective basis.

Atha vātiādinā nissayaṭṭhepi pāda-sadde upāyaṭṭhena chandādīnaṃ iddhipādatā vuttā. Teneva abhidhamme uttaracūḷabhājanīye “cattāro iddhipādā chandiddhipādo”tiādinā (vibha. 457) chandādīnameva iddhipādatā vuttā. Pañhāpucchake ca “cattāro iddhipādā idha bhikkhu chandasamādhī”tiādināva (vibha. 462) uddesaṃ katvāpi puna chandādīnaṃyeva kusalādibhāvo vibhatto. Upāyiddhipādadassanatthameva hi sutte, abhidhamme ca nissayiddhipādadassanaṃ kataṃ, aññathā catubbidhatā na hotīti.

By the passage beginning 'Atha vā' ('Alternatively'), it is stated that the status of desire and the others as bases of psychic power is due to the meaning of 'means,' even when the word 'pāda' has the meaning of 'support'. For this very reason, in the Abhidhamma, in the Uttara Cūḷabhājanīya, the status of desire and the others themselves as bases of psychic power is stated, as in 'The four bases of psychic power: the basis of psychic power of desire,' etc. (Vibha. 457). And in the Pañhāpucchaka, even after making the exposition 'The four bases of psychic power: here, a bhikkhu, concentration of desire,' etc. (Vibha. 462), the status of desire and the others themselves as wholesome, etc., is further analyzed. For indeed, in the Sutta and in the Abhidhamma, the showing of the basis of psychic power as a support is done for the very purpose of showing the basis of psychic power as a means; otherwise, the fourfold nature would not exist.

383. Chandādīni aṭṭhāti chandasamādhi vīriyasamādhi cittasamādhi vīmaṃsāsamādhīti evaṃ chandādīni aṭṭha. Kāmaṃ cettha catūsupi ṭhānesu samādhi samādhi eva, tathāpi iddhiṃ uppādetukāmatāchandasahitova samādhi iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattati, na kevalo. Evaṃ vīriyasamādhiādayopi. Tasmā chandādisahitā ete cattāro ca samādhī, chandādayo ca cattāroti aṭṭha pajjati iddhi etehi pāpuṇīyati, sayaṃ vā pajjanti iddhipaṭilābhāya sampajjantīti padānīti vuccanti. Tenāha “iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattantī”ti. Yaṃ pana pāḷiyaṃ “chando na samādhī”tiādi, taṃ yadipi chandādayo samādhisahitāva iddhiṃ nipphādenti, tathāpi visuṃ [V 2.0019] nesaṃ padabhāvadassanaṃ. Ekato niyuttova, na ekeko hutvāti adhippāyo. Niyuttovāti sahito eva, na viyutto.

383. The eight beginning with zeal are: concentration of zeal, concentration of energy, concentration of mind, and concentration of investigation—thus, these eight beginning with zeal. Although in all four instances here concentration is indeed concentration, nevertheless, only concentration accompanied by the zeal which is the desire to generate psychic power leads to the attainment of psychic power, not concentration alone. The same applies to concentration of energy and the others. Therefore, these four concentrations accompanied by zeal and the others, and the four qualities beginning with zeal—these eight—are called 'bases' (padāni) because psychic power is produced or attained by them, or because they themselves arise for the attainment of psychic power. Thus it is said, 'They lead to the attainment of psychic power.' As for what is said in the Pāḷi, 'Zeal is not concentration,' etc., that is a statement showing their distinct nature as bases, even though zeal and the other factors produce psychic power only when accompanied by concentration. The meaning is that they are yoked together, not that each exists alone. 'Yoked together' means associated, not separate.

384. Anonatanti na onataṃ, vīriyena paggahitattā alīnanti attho. Tenāha “kosajje na iñjatī”ti, kosajjanimittaṃ na calatīti [M 2.0020] attho. Uddhaṃ nataṃ unnataṃ, uddhataṃ vikkhittaṃ. Na unnataṃ anunnataṃ, avikkhittaṃ samāhitanti attho. Tenāha “uddhacce na iñjatī”ti. Abhisaṅgavasena nataṃ abhinataṃ, na abhinataṃ anabhinataṃ, arattaṃ. Apagamanavasena nataṃ apanataṃ, kodhavasena vimukhaṃ. Na apanataṃ anapanataṃ, aduṭṭhaṃ. Diṭṭhiyā “ahaṃ, mama”nti nissayavasena na nissitanti anissitaṃ. Chandarāgavasena na paṭibaddhanti appaṭibaddhaṃ. Rāgo kevalaṃ āsattimattaṃ, chandarāgo pana bahalakileso. Tathā hissa dūre ṭhitampi ārammaṇaṃ paṭibaddhameva. Vippamuttanti visesato pamuttaṃ. Jhānānaṃ kāmarāgapaṭipakkhatāya āha “kāmarāge”ti. Visaṃyuttanti vivittaṃ saṃkilesato, na vā saṃyuttaṃ catūhipi yogehi. Vimariyādikataṃ kilesamariyādāya, yathā īsakampi kilesamariyādā na hoti, tathā paṭipannaṃ. Ekattagatanti ekaggataṃ upagataṃ accantameva samāhitaṃ. Tato eva nānattakilesehi nānāsabhāvehi kilesehi na iñjati.

384. 'Not bent down' (anonata) means not bent down (na onataṃ); the meaning is 'unflagging' (alīna) because it is upheld by energy. Therefore, it is said, 'it does not waver in laziness,' meaning it does not stir on account of the cause of laziness. Bent upwards (uddhaṃ nataṃ) is 'lofty' (unnataṃ), meaning agitated, scattered. Not lofty is 'not lofty' (anunnataṃ), meaning unscattered, composed. Therefore, it is said, 'it does not waver in restlessness.' Bent by way of clinging is 'inclined' (abhinataṃ); not inclined is 'uninclined' (anabhinataṃ), meaning not impassioned. Bent by way of departing is 'turned away' (apanataṃ), meaning averse on account of anger. Not turned away is 'not turned away' (anapanataṃ), meaning not hostile. Not dependent (na nissitaṃ) by way of reliance on the view 'I am, this is mine' is 'independent' (anissitaṃ). Not bound by way of desire-and-lust is 'unbound' (appaṭibaddhaṃ). Lust (rāga) is merely attachment, but desire-and-lust (chandarāga) is a gross defilement. For indeed, even an object standing at a distance is bound by it. 'Especially freed' (vippamutta) means distinctly freed. Because the absorptions are the opposite of sensual lust, it is said, 'from sensual lust.' 'Disjoined' (visaṃyutta) means secluded from defilements, or not conjoined with the four yokes. 'Made without boundary' (vimariyādikataṃ) with respect to the boundary of defilements means practicing in such a way that there is not even a slight boundary of defilements. 'Gone to a unified state' (ekattagata) means having reached one-pointedness, utterly composed. For that very reason, it does not waver due to defilements of various kinds and diverse natures.

Esa atthoti kosajjādinimittaṃ. Imassa cittassa āneñjanattho siddho eva āneñjappattiyā pakāsanavasena dassitattā. Puna vuttoti iddhiyā bhūmipādapadadassanappasaṅgena “imāni mūlāni nāmā”ti mūlabhāvadassanatthaṃ puna vutto. Purimoti “saddhādīhi pariggahitattā”tiādinā pubbe chadhā dassitanayo. Ayanti adhunā soḷasadhā dassitanayo. Suttanaye, paṭisambhidānaye ca dassite tattha sammoho na hoti, na adassiteti āha “ubhayattha asammohattha”nti.

This is the meaning regarding the cause of laziness, etc. The meaning of the unshakability of this mind is indeed established, as it is shown by way of revealing the attainment of unshakability. It is stated again: in connection with showing the bases, constituents, and factors of psychic power, it is stated again for the purpose of showing their fundamental nature, saying, 'these are the roots.' The former is the method previously shown in six ways, beginning with 'because it is embraced by faith,' etc. This is the method now shown in sixteen ways. It is said 'for the purpose of non-confusion in both' because there is no confusion when it is shown in both the method of the Suttas and the method of the Paṭisambhidā, whereas there would be if it were not shown.

385. Ñāṇena adhiṭṭhahantoti “kathaṃ panāyaṃ evaṃ hotī”ti ettha pubbe attanā vuttapadaṃ uddharati adhiṭṭhānavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “abhiññāpādakaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāyā”ti. Ettha anupubbena cattāri jhānāni samāpajjitvā catutthajjhānato vuṭṭhāyāti keci, taṃ ayuttaṃ. Yathicchitajjhānasamāpajjanatthañhi cittaparidamanaṃ, catutthajjhānameva ca abhiññāpādakaṃ, na itarāni. Parikammaṃ katvāti pādakajjhānato vuṭṭhāya kāmāvacaracittena “sataṃ homī”tiādinā [V 2.0020] cintanamevettha parikammakaraṇaṃ, tathāvajjanameva ca āvajjanaṃ. Dutiyampīti pi-saddo samuccayattho, tena tatiyampi, tato bhiyyopīti imamatthaṃ dīpeti. Yathā hi jhānabhāvanā, evamabhiññābhāvanāpi. “Ekavāraṃ dvevāra”nti idampi nidassanamattaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nimittārammaṇanti paṭibhāganimittārammaṇaṃ. Parikammacittānīti ettha ekekassa parikammacittassa satārammaṇatā [M 2.0021] daṭṭhabbā “sataṃ homī”ti pavattanato. Sahassārammaṇānīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Vaṇṇavasenāti attanā parikappitavaṇṇavasena. No paṇṇattivasenāti na sattapaṇṇattivasena. Taṃ adhiṭṭhānacittaṃ appanācittamivāti ivaggahaṇaṃ abhiññācittassa jhānacittassa paṭhamuppattisadisabhāvato vuttaṃ, na tassa appanābhāvato. Rūpāvacaracatutthajjhānikanti rūpāvacaracatutthajhānavantaṃ, tena sampayuttaṃ.

385. Regarding 'One resolves with knowledge': In this question, 'How then does this come to be?', one brings forth the phrase previously spoken by oneself in order to show the method of resolution, thus: 'Having attained the base-jhāna for direct knowledge and emerging.' Here, some say that one attains the four jhānas in sequence and emerges from the fourth jhāna, but this is incorrect. For the taming of the mind is for the purpose of attaining any desired jhāna, and only the fourth jhāna serves as the base for direct knowledge, not the others. As for 'having done the preliminary work': having emerged from the base-jhāna, the very thinking 'May I be a hundred,' and so on, with a sense-sphere mind is the performance of the preliminary work here, and the adverting is just such an adverting. Regarding 'And a second time': the word 'pi' has the meaning of accumulation, thereby indicating 'a third time' and 'even more than that.' For just as there is the development of jhāna, so too is there the development of direct knowledge. 'Once, twice': this too should be seen as a mere illustration. 'Having the sign as its object' means having the counterpart sign as its object. Regarding 'preliminary minds': here, it should be understood that each preliminary mind has a hundred as its object, because of the occurrence of the thought 'May I be a hundred.' Regarding 'having a thousand as their object': here too, this is the same method. 'By way of appearance': by way of the appearance conceptually constructed by oneself. 'Not by way of concept': not by way of the concept of a being. That resolution-mind is like an absorption-mind: the word 'like' is used because the first arising of the direct-knowledge-mind is similar to that of a jhāna-mind, not because it is an absorption. 'Belonging to the fourth jhāna of the form sphere': possessing the fourth jhāna of the form sphere, and associated with it.

386. Yadi evaṃ “āvajjitvā ñāṇena adhiṭṭhātī”ti paṭisambhidāvacanaṃ kathanti āha “yampī”tiādi. Tatrāpīti paṭisambhidāyampi. Āvajjatīti “bahukaṃ āvajjatī”ti idaṃ pāṭhapadaṃ parikammavaseneva vuttaṃ, na āvajjanavasena. Āvajjitvā ñāṇena adhiṭṭhātīti abhiññāñāṇavasena vuttaṃ, na parikammacittasampayuttassa, aññassa vā kāmāvacarassa ñāṇassa vasena. Na hi tassa tādiso ānubhāvo atthīti. Tasmāti yasmā appanāppattassa abhiññāñāṇasseva vasena adhiṭṭhānaṃ, tasmā. Ayamadhiṭṭhānakkamoti dassento “bahukaṃ āvajjatī”tiādimāha. Tattha sanniṭṭhāpanavasenāti nipphādanavasena.

386. If that is so, how is the Paṭisambhidā statement, 'Having adverted, one resolves with knowledge,' to be understood? To answer this, he says, 'And also,' and so on. Here too (tatrāpi) means also in the Paṭisambhidā. 'One adverts' (āvajjatīti): the text-word 'one adverts much' (bahukaṃ āvajjatīti) is stated only by way of the preliminary work, not by way of adverting. 'Having adverted, one resolves with knowledge' (āvajjitvā ñāṇena adhiṭṭhātīti): this is stated by way of the knowledge of direct-knowledge, not by way of the knowledge associated with the preliminary-work mind or any other sense-sphere knowledge. For that knowledge does not have such power. Therefore (tasmā): because the resolution is stated only by way of the direct-knowledge that has attained absorption, therefore. Showing that 'This is the order of resolution,' he says, 'one adverts much,' and so on. There, 'by way of establishing' (sanniṭṭhāpanavasenāti) means by way of bringing to completion (nipphādanavasena).

Kāyasakkhidassanatthanti na kevalaṃ vacanamattameva, atha kho ayametassatthassa attano kāyena sacchikatattā kāyasakkhīti sakkhidassanatthaṃ.

For the purpose of showing a body-witness (kāyasakkhidassanatthaṃ): it is not merely a matter of words, but rather, because this one has realized this meaning with his own body, he is a 'body-witness' (kāyasakkhī); thus, it is for the purpose of showing a direct witness.

Kokanadanti padumavisesanaṃ yathā “kokāsaka”nti. Taṃ kira bahupattaṃ, vaṇṇasampannaṃ, ativiya sugandhañca hoti. Pātoti pageva. Ayañhettha attho – yathā kokanadasaṅkhātaṃ padumaṃ pāto sūriyassuggamanavelāyaṃ phullaṃ vikasitaṃ avītagandhaṃ siyā virocamānaṃ, evaṃ sarīragandhena, guṇagandhena ca sugandhaṃ saradakāle antalikkhe ādiccamiva attano tejasā tapantaṃ aṅgehi niccharaṇakajutitāya aṅgīrasaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ passāti.

Kokanada: a specific type of lotus, like 'kokāsaka'. It is said to have many petals, to be endowed with color, and to be exceedingly fragrant. 'In the morning' (pāto): means 'early'. The meaning here is this: just as the lotus called kokanada, in the morning at the time of the sun's rising, would be bloomed, opened, with unfading fragrance, and shining; so too, behold the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, the Aṅgīrasa, who is fragrant with the fragrance of his body and the fragrance of his virtues, shining with his own radiance like the sun in the autumn sky, having rays issuing from his body due to the radiance emanating from his limbs.

Abhabboti paṭipattisāramidaṃ sāsanaṃ, paṭipatti ca pariyattimūlikā, tvañca pariyattiṃ uggahetuṃ [V 2.0021] asamattho, tasmā abhabboti adhippāyo. Abhabbo nāma na hoti vāsadhurasseva padhānabhāvato.

'You are incapable' (abhabboti): This teaching has practice as its essence, and practice is rooted in learning. Since you are unable to learn the scriptures, the meaning is therefore, 'you are incapable.' The term 'incapable,' however, does not apply, because the burden of insight-practice (vāsadhura) is itself the primary thing.

Bhikkhūti pabbajitavohārena vuttaṃ, bhāvinaṃ vā bhikkhubhāvaṃ upādāya yathā “agamā rājagahaṃ buddho”ti (su. ni. 410). Pilotikakhaṇḍanti suvisuddhaṃ coḷakhaṇḍaṃ[M 2.0022]. Rajo haratīti rajoharaṇaṃ. Abhinimminitvā adāsi tattha pubbe katādhikārattā. Tathā hi yoniso ummujjanto “attabhāvassa panāyaṃ doso”ti asubhasaññaṃ, aniccasaññañca paṭilabhitvā nāmarūpapariggahādinā pañcasu khandhesu ñāṇaṃ otāretvā kalāpasammasanādikkamena vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā udayabbayañāṇādipaṭipāṭiyā vipassanaṃ anulomagotrabhusamīpaṃ pāpesi. Obhāsavissajjanapubbikā bhāsitagāthā obhāsagāthā.

‘Bhikkhu’ is said by the conventional designation of one gone forth, or with reference to the future state of being a bhikkhu, just as in the phrase ‘The Buddha went to Rājagaha,’ where ‘Buddha’ refers to the Bodhisatta. ‘A piece of rag cloth’ means a very pure piece of cloth. It carries away dust, therefore it is a ‘dust-remover.’ He fashioned and gave it there because of having made a resolution in the past. For, reflecting wisely, thinking, ‘Indeed, this is a fault of individual existence,’ he acquired the perception of foulness and the perception of impermanence, and then, by means of the comprehension of name-and-form and so on, having made knowledge descend into the five aggregates, and having developed insight through the sequence beginning with the comprehension of groups, he brought insight, by the sequence beginning with the knowledge of arising and passing away, to the vicinity of conformity and change-of-lineage. The verses spoken, which were preceded by the emission of light, are the ‘verses of light’.

Rāgo rajo ariyassa vinaye, na ca pana reṇu vuccati “rajo”ti. Kasmā? Cittassa malīnabhāvakaraṇato. Rāgassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ “rajo”ti. Etaṃ rajanti etaṃ rāgasaṅkhātaṃ rajaṃ. Vippajahitvāti aggamaggena visesato pajahanahetu. Paṇḍitā viharanti teti te pajahanakā paṇḍitā hutvā viharanti. Vītarajassa sabbaso pahīnarāgādirajassa buddhassa bhagavato sāsane. Tathā hi vadanti –

In the discipline of the Noble One, lust is called ‘dust’; but ordinary dust is not called ‘dust.’ Why? Because it causes the state of defilement of the mind. ‘Dust’ is a designation for lust. ‘This dust’ means this dust called lust. ‘Having abandoned’ is because of abandoning it specifically by the supreme path. ‘They, the wise, dwell’ means: those who abandon it, having become wise, dwell. In the dispensation of the Blessed One, the Buddha, who is without dust, whose dust of lust and so on is completely abandoned. For thus they say:

“Cittamhi saṃkiliṭṭhamhi, saṃkilissanti māṇavā;

Citte suddhe visujjhanti, iti vuttaṃ mahesinā”ti. (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.373; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.106; saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 2.3.100; itivu. aṭṭha. 88);

“When the mind is defiled, beings are defiled; when the mind is pure, beings are purified—thus it was spoken by the Great Sage.”

Chaḷabhiññāgahaṇena gahitāya chaḷabhiññāya vibhāvitepi ariyamagge anuttarabhāvasāmaññena phalanibbānehi saddhiṃ saṅgaṇhanto āha “nava lokuttaradhammā”ti.

Although the noble path is made manifest by the sixth direct knowledge—which is included by the term ‘the six direct knowledges’—wishing to group it together with the fruits and Nibbāna due to the commonality of being unsurpassed, he said, ‘the nine supramundane states’.

Pattassa pidahanākārena hatthaṃ ṭhapento “hatthaṃ pidahī”ti vutto. Hatthanti vā karaṇatthe upayogavacanaṃ, hatthena pidahīti attho.

Placing his hand in the manner of covering the bowl, he was called ‘Hatthaṃpidahi’. Or, the word ‘hatthaṃ’ is a usage in the instrumental sense; the meaning is, ‘he covered with the hand’.

Sahassakkhattunti [V 2.0022] sahassadhā. Sahassadhā hi attānaṃ ekacitteneva nimminantopi sahassavāraṃ nimminanto viya hoti. Asatipi kiriyābyāvuttiyaṃ tadatthasiddhitoti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “sahassakkhattu”nti vuttaṃ. Ambavaneti ambavane katavihāre. Rammeti ramaṇīye. Yāva kālappavedanā, tāva nisīdīti yojanā.

‘A thousand times’ (sahassakkhattuṃ) means a thousandfold (sahassadhā). For indeed, although creating oneself a thousandfold with just a single thought, it is as if creating a thousand times. The phrase ‘a thousand times’ was said to show this meaning: that the purpose is accomplished even without the repetition of the act. ‘In the mango grove’ (ambavane) means in the monastery built in the mango grove. ‘Delightful’ (rammeti) means pleasing (ramaṇīye). The construction is: ‘He sat until the meal time was announced’.

Aniyametvāti vaṇṇāvayavasarīrāvayavaparikkhārakiriyāvisesādīhi niyamaṃ akatvā. Nānāvaṇṇeti nānākāre yathāvuttavaṇṇādivasena nānāvidhe. Missakakeseti palitehi missitakese. Upaḍḍharattavaṇṇaupaḍḍhapaṇḍuvaṇṇādīsu aññataravaṇṇanti evaṃ upaḍḍharattacīvare. Padavasena atthassa[M 2.0023], gamanavasena pāḷiyā bhaṇanaṃ padabhāṇaṃ. Parikathādivasena dhammassa kathanaṃ dhammakathā. Sarena bhaññaṃ suttādīnaṃ uccāraṇaṃ sarabhaññaṃ. Aparepīti vuttākārato aññepi dīgharassakisathūlādike nānappakārake. Icchiticchitappakārāyeva hontīti yathā yathā icchitā, taṃtaṃpakārāyeva honti. Yattakā hi visesā vaṇṇādivasena tesu icchitā, tattakavisesavantova te honti. Te pana tathā bahudhā bhinnākārepi vaṇṇavasena ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekameva adhiṭṭhānacittaṃ pavattati. Ayaṃ hissa ānubhāvo – yathā ekāva cetanā nānāvisesavantaṃ attabhāvaṃ nibbatteti, tattha bhavapatthanā kammassa visesapaccayo hoti. Acinteyyo ca kammavipākoti ce, idhāpi parikammacittaṃ visesapaccayo hoti, acinteyyo ca iddhivisayoti gahetabbaṃ. Esa nayoti yvāyaṃ bahubhāvanimmāne “abhiññāpādakaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā”tiādinā adhiṭṭhānanayo vutto, esa nayo itaresupi adhiṭṭhānesu.

'Not fixing it' (aniyametvā) means not determining it by color, parts, body parts, requisites, special actions, and so on. 'Of various colors' (nānāvaṇṇe) means of various kinds, in various forms as described by color and so on. 'With mixed hair' (missakakese) means hair mingled with grey hairs. 'Half red in color, and half of another color among pale colors and so on'; in this way, it refers to 'those with half-red robes'. 'Recitation by word' (padabhāṇaṃ) is the recitation of the meaning according to each word, and of the text according to its sequence. 'Dhamma talk' (dhammakathā) is the teaching of the Dhamma through discussions and so on. 'Intoned recitation' (sarabhaññaṃ) is the utterance of suttas and so on with a melodious voice. 'Others too' (aparepi) means other various kinds such as long, short, thin, thick, etc., beyond what has been described. 'They are just as desired' (icchiticchitappakārāyeva honti) means they are exactly of the kind as wished. For whatever distinctions are desired in them in terms of color and so on, they possess exactly those distinctions. However, though they are thus of many different forms, having made them the object by way of their appearance, a single resolve-consciousness (adhiṭṭhānacittaṃ) proceeds. This is its power: just as a single volition (ekāva cetanā) produces a being with many distinctions, there the aspiration for existence (bhavapatthanā) is the specific condition (visesapaccayo) for kamma. And if one says the result of kamma is inconceivable, here too the preliminary consciousness (parikammacittaṃ) is the specific condition, and the sphere of psychic power (iddhivisayo) should be understood as inconceivable. This is the method (esa nayo): just as in the creation of many forms, the method of resolve (adhiṭṭhānanayo) was explained by 'having attained the jhāna that is the base for direct knowledge,' and so on, this same method applies to other resolves as well.

Iti avisesaṃ atidesena dassetvā visesaṃ sarūpato dassetuṃ “ayaṃ pana viseso”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha iminā bhikkhunā icchantenāti sambandho. Maṃ jānissantīti “iddhimā”ti maṃ jānissanti. Antarāvāti paricchinnakālassa abbhantare eva. Pādakajjhānantiādi parikammakaraṇākāradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, itaraṃ pana atideseneva vibhāvitanti. Evaṃ akarontoti “eko homī”ti antarā adhiṭṭhānaṃ akaronto. “Yathāparicchinnakālavasenā”ti iminā “sataṃ homī”tiādinā adhiṭṭhānaṃ karontena kālaparicchedavaseneva kātabbanti dasseti. Sayameva eko hoti adhiṭṭhānassa paṭippassaddhattā. Ettha ca parikammādhiṭṭhānacittānaṃ iddhimā vaṇṇavasena sayameva ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Tesu parikammacittāni [V 2.0023] santatipaccuppannārammaṇāni. Adhiṭṭhānacittaṃ sampativattamānārammaṇaṃ adhiṭṭhānassa ekacittakkhaṇikattāti vadanti.

Having thus shown the general aspect by way of extension, in order to show the specific aspect in its own form, the words, 'But this is the distinction,' and so on, were stated. Therein, the connection is: 'by this monk who desires.' 'They will know me' means: 'they will know me as "one with psychic power."' 'Within the interval' means: within the limited time itself. The words, 'foundational jhāna,' and so on, were stated to show the manner of performing the preliminary work; the rest, however, has been explained by way of extension. 'Not doing so' means: not making the determination, 'I will be one,' in the interval. By the words, 'according to the power of the delimitation of time,' it is shown that for one making the determination, 'I will be a hundred,' and so on, it should be done only by the power of the delimitation of time. One becomes one by oneself because of the subsiding of the determination. And here, for the preliminary and determination consciousnesses, the one with psychic power himself becomes the object by way of appearance. Among those, the preliminary consciousnesses have a serially-present object. The determination consciousness has a presently-occurring object, because the determination is of a single mind-moment—so they say.

387. “Āvibhāva”nti padassa heṭṭhā vuttena hoti-saddena sambandho na yujjati upayogavacanena vuttattā, tathā vakkhamānena ca gacchati-saddena attano, paresañca āvibhāvassa icchitattā, nāmapadañca kiriyāpadāpekkhanti kiriyāsāmaññavācinā karoti-saddena yojetvā āha “āvibhāvaṃ karotī”ti. Tirobhāvanti etthāpi eseva nayo[M 2.0024]. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ paṭisambhidāyanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “idameva hī”tiādi. Kāmaṃ paṭisambhidāyaṃ “āvibhāvanti kenaci anāvaṭaṃ hotī”tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 3.11) āgataṃ, tampi idameva āvibhāvakaraṇaṃ, tirobhāvakaraṇañca sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sesapadāni tesaṃyeva vevacanāni. Andhakāranti rattandhakāraṃ, divāpi vā bilaguhādigataṃ andhakāraṃ. Paṭicchannanti kuṭṭakavāṭādinā paṭicchāditaṃ. Anāpāthanti dūratāsukhumataratādinā na āpāthagataṃ. Ayanti iddhimā. Paṭicchannopi dūre ṭhitopi attā vā paro vā yathā dissatīti vibhattiṃ pariṇāmetvā yojetabbaṃ. Ālokajātanti ālokabhūtaṃ, jātālokaṃ vā.

387. The connection of the word 'āvibhāva' with the word 'hoti' stated before is not suitable, because it is stated with the accusative case. Similarly, the connection with the word 'gacchati' which will be stated is also not suitable, because the manifestation of oneself and of others is desired. And because a noun is dependent on a verb, having connected it with the word 'karoti', which expresses a general action, it is said, 'āvibhāvaṃ karoti' (he makes manifest). Here in the case of 'tirobhāva' also, this is the same method. If so, how is it stated in the Paṭisambhidā? Referring to this objection, he said 'idameva hi', etc. It is true that in the Paṭisambhidā it is stated by way of 'āvibhāva means it becomes unobstructed by anything', etc. (Paṭi. Ma. 3.11), but that too was said in reference to this very making of manifestation and making of disappearance. The remaining words are synonyms of those very words. 'Andhakāra' means the darkness of night, or the darkness found in a hole, cave, etc., even during the day. 'Paṭicchanna' means covered by a wall, door-leaf, etc. 'Anāpātha' means not having come into range on account of being distant, being extremely subtle, etc. 'Ayaṃ' means one with psychic power. It should be connected by changing the case ending to mean: 'so that oneself or another is seen, even if concealed, even if standing far away'. 'Ālokajāta' means having become light, or that which has arisen as light.

388. Etaṃ pana pāṭihāriyanti āvibhāvapāṭihāriyamāha. Kena katapubbanti tattha kāyasakkhiṃ pucchitvā “satthā tāva kāyasakkhī”ti dassentena “bhagavatā”ti vatvā tamatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “bhagavā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sāvatthivāsike passantīti ānetvā sambandho, tathā “yāva avīciṃ dassesī”ti. Ākāsagatesu heṭṭhimaheṭṭhimavimānesu uparūparivimānaṃ byavadhāyakesu byūhiyamānesu taggataṃ ākāsaṃ byūḷhaṃ nāma hotīti vuttaṃ “ākāsañca dvidhā viyūhitvā”ti.

388. By the text 'This, however, is a miracle', he speaks of the miracle of manifestation. Having asked about a bodily witness in that regard with the words 'By whom was this done previously?', and showing 'The Teacher, indeed, was the bodily witness', he said 'by the Blessed One'. To clarify that meaning, 'For the Blessed One...', etc., was said. The connection is made by bringing in the words 'they see the residents of Sāvatthī', and similarly, 'he showed as far as Avīci'. Because, when the lower and lower celestial mansions situated in the sky, which obstruct the upper and upper mansions, are removed, the space occupied by them is called 'removed' (byūḷhaṃ); therefore, it is said 'and having parted the sky in two'.

Ayamatthoti āvibhāvapāṭihāriyassa satthārā katabhāvo. Purimabuddhānaṃ paṭipattiāvajjanaṃ buddhappaveṇiyā anupālanatthaṃ. “Ekena pādenā”tiādi tivikkamadassanaṃ. Nayaṃ deti yassa nayassa anusārena vācanāmaggaṃ ṭhapesi.

This is the meaning: the state of the miracle of manifestation having been performed by the Teacher. The reflection on the practice of former Buddhas is for the purpose of maintaining the tradition of the Buddhas. The words beginning with 'With one foot...' demonstrate the three strides. He gives the method, according to which method he established the path of recitation.

Cūḷaanāthapiṇḍiko nāma anāthapiṇḍikamahāseṭṭhissa kaniṭṭhabhātā.

Cūḷaanāthapiṇḍika by name was the younger brother of the great merchant Anāthapiṇḍika.

Sinerupabbataṃ [V 2.0024] nibbijjhitvāti taṃ parisāya dissamānarūpaṃyeva katvā nibbijjhitvā. Nanti sinerupabbataṃ.

'Having pierced Mount Sineru' means: having made it visible to the assembly, he then pierced it. 'Naṃ' refers to Mount Sineru.

Anekasatasahassasaṅkhassa okāsalokassa, taṃnivāsisattalokassa ca vivaṭabhāvakaraṇapāṭihāriyaṃ lokavivaraṇaṃ nāma. Mahābrahmāti sahampatimahābrahmā.

The miracle of making open the world-space, numbering many hundreds of thousands, and the world of beings dwelling therein, is called the 'world-revealing' (lokavivaraṇa). 'Mahābrahmā' refers to Sahampati Mahābrahmā.

Passatha [M 2.0025] tāva apaṇṇakapaṭipadāya phalanti nirayabhayena tajjetvā satthu anupubbikathānayena saggasukhena palobhetvā, na pana saggasampattiyaṃ ninnabhāvāpādanena.

'First, see the fruit of the unerring practice' means frightening them with the fear of hell and, by way of the Teacher's gradual discourse, enticing them with the bliss of heaven; but not by causing an inclination towards heavenly attainments.

389. Yathā āvibhāvakaraṇe ālokakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitabbaṃ ālokanimmānāya, evaṃ tirobhāvakaraṇe andhakāranimmānāya nīlakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitabbaṃ. Kāmañcetaṃ pāḷiyaṃ sarūpato nāgataṃ, “vivaṭaṃ āvaṭa”nti (paṭi. ma. 3.11) pana vacanato atthato āgatameva. Odātakasiṇantogadhaṃ vā ālokakasiṇanti vuttovāyamattho. Andhakāranti andhakāravantaṃ.

389. Just as in causing manifestation, the light-kasiṇa must be attained for the creation of light, so in causing disappearance, the blue-kasiṇa must be attained for the creation of darkness. And although this is not found in its own form in the Pāli, it is nevertheless arrived at by meaning on account of the words, “what was closed becomes open” (Paṭisambhidāmagga 3.11). Or, this meaning has already been stated thus: the light-kasiṇa is included within the white-kasiṇa. 'Andhakāra' means 'possessing darkness'.

390. Avasese iṭṭiyattherādike.

390. Regarding the remaining ones, such as the Elder Iṭṭhiya and others.

391. Pākaṭo iddhimā etassa atthīti pākaṭaṃ, pākaṭañca taṃ pāṭihāriyañcāti pākaṭapāṭihāriyaṃ. Na ettha iddhimā pākaṭoti apākaṭaṃ, apākaṭañca taṃ pāṭihāriyañcāti apākaṭapāṭihāriyaṃ. Iddhimato eva hi pākaṭāpākaṭabhāvenāyaṃ bhedo, na pāṭihāriyassa. Na hi taṃ apākaṭaṃ atthi.

391. It is called 'manifest' (pākaṭa) because for this miracle there is a manifest psychic power wielder. It is 'manifest' and it is a miracle, therefore it is a 'manifest miracle' (pākaṭapāṭihāriya). It is called 'unmanifest' (apākaṭa) because here the psychic power wielder is not manifest. It is 'unmanifest' and it is a miracle, therefore it is an 'unmanifest miracle' (apākaṭapāṭihāriya). For this distinction, based on the state of being manifest or unmanifest, applies only to the one with psychic power, not to the miracle. Indeed, that miracle is never unmanifest.

Uttarimanussadhammāti manussadhammo vuccati dasa kusalakammapathadhammā, tato manussadhammato uttari. Iddhisaṅkhātaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ. Āḷindeti pamukhe. Okāsehīti pakira. Iddhābhisaṅkhāranti iddhipayogaṃ. Abhisaṅkhāsīti abhisaṅkhari, akāsīti attho. Tālacchiggaḷenāti kuñcikacchiddena. Aggaḷantarikāyāti piṭṭhasaṅghātānaṃ antarena.

'Uttarimanussadhamma' (superhuman states): The ten courses of wholesome action are called 'human states' (manussadhamma); 'superhuman' (uttari) means superior to those human states. The miracle (pāṭihāriya) reckoned as psychic power (iddhi) is the miracle of psychic power. 'Āḷinde' means 'in the porch' (pamukhe). 'Okāsehi' means 'scatter' (pakira). 'Iddhābhisaṅkhāra' means 'the application of psychic power' (iddhipayogaṃ). 'Abhisaṅkhāsi' means 'he prepared' (abhisaṅkhari), 'he made' (akāsi); that is the meaning. 'Tālacchiggaḷena' means 'through the keyhole' (kuñcikacchiddena). 'Aggaḷantarikāya' means 'through the space between the door-posts' (piṭṭhasaṅghātānaṃ antarena).

Antarahitoti antaradhāyitukāmo. Bako brahmā yathā antaradhāyituṃ na sakkoti, tathā katvā bhagavā sayaṃ tassa, brahmagaṇassa ca anāpāthabhāvagamanena antarahito hutvā “samaṇassa gotamassa [V 2.0025] imasmiṃ ṭhāne atthibhāvo vā natthibhāvo vā na sakkā jānitu”nti evaṃ brahmagaṇassa vacanokāso mā hotūti “bhavevāha”nti imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi.

'Antarahito' means 'wishing to disappear.' Having acted in such a way that Baka Brahmā was unable to disappear, the Blessed One, having himself disappeared by becoming unobservable to that Baka Brahmā and to the host of Brahmās, and with the intention, 'Let there be no opportunity for the host of Brahmās to say, "It is not possible to know of the ascetic Gotama's existence or non-existence in this place,"' spoke this verse beginning with 'bhavevāhaṃ'.

Tattha bhavevāhaṃ bhayaṃ disvāti ahaṃ bhave saṃsāre jātijarādibhedaṃ bhayaṃ disvā eva. Bhavañca vibhavesinanti imañca kāmabhavādiṃ tividhampi [M 2.0026] sattabhavaṃ, vibhavesinaṃ vibhavaṃ gavesamānampi pariyesamānampi punappunaṃ bhave eva disvā. Bhavaṃ nābhivadinti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena kiñci bhavaṃ na abhivadiṃ na gahesiṃ. Nandiñca na upādiyinti bhavataṇhaṃ na upagacchiṃ, na aggahesinti attho.

Therein, regarding 'bhavevāhaṃ bhayaṃ disvā': I, having indeed seen the danger in existence, in saṃsāra, which has the distinctions of birth, aging, and so on. Regarding 'bhavañca vibhavesinaṃ': And having seen this threefold existence beginning with sense-sphere existence—this existence of beings—and having seen those seeking non-existence, those searching and seeking for non-existence, repeatedly within existence itself. Regarding 'bhavaṃ nābhivadiṃ': I did not praise nor grasp any existence whatsoever by way of craving and views. Regarding 'nandiñca na upādiyiṃ': I did not approach nor cling to craving for existence; that is the meaning.

392. Alaggamānoti vinivijjhitvā gamanena kuṭṭādīsu katthaci na laggamāno. Āvajjitvā kataparikammenāti yassa parato gantukāmo, taṃ āvajjitvā “ākāso hotu, ākāso hotū”ti evaṃ kataparikammena iddhimatā. Pākārapabbatāpekkhāya “susiro, chiddo”ti ca pulliṅgavasena vuttaṃ. Ubbedhavasena pavattaṃ vivaraṃ susiraṃ. Tiriyaṃ pavattaṃ chiddaṃ.

392. 'Alaggamāno' means: not sticking anywhere to walls and so on, by going right through them. 'Āvajjitvā kataparikammena' means: by one endowed with psychic power who, wishing to go to the other side of something, has made the preliminary preparation by adverting to it with the thought, 'Let it be space, let it be space.' With reference to a wall and a mountain, 'susiro' and 'chiddo' are stated in the masculine gender. An opening that occurs by way of height is a 'susira'; an opening that occurs horizontally is a 'chidda'.

Yattha katthaci kasiṇe parikammaṃ katvāti pathavīkasiṇādīsu yattha katthaci kasiṇe jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā parikammaṃ katvā “ākāso hotū”ti adhiṭṭhātabbo. Tattha kāraṇamāha “aṭṭhasamāpattivasībhāvoyeva pamāṇa”nti. Tasmā yaṃ yaṃ icchati, taṃ tadeva hoti. Etena pathaviyā ummujjananimujjane āpokasiṇasamāpajjanaṃ, udakādīsu pathavīnimmāne pathavīkasiṇasamāpajjanaṃ na ekantato icchitabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Etanti etaṃ tirokuṭṭādigamanapāṭihāriyakaraṇe ākāsakasiṇasamāpajjanaṃ avassaṃ vattabbaṃ anucchavikabhāvato. Evañca katvā “ākāsakasiṇavasena paṭicchannānaṃ vivaṭakaraṇa”ntiādivacanaṃ viya pathavīkasiṇavasena “ekopi hutvā bahudhā hotī”tiādibhāvo “ākāse vā udake vā pathaviṃ nimminitvā padasā gamanaṃ icchatī”tiādinā yaṃ pakiṇṇakanaye vuttaṃ, tampi samatthitaṃ hoti.

“Having performed the preliminary work on any kasiṇa” means: having attained jhāna in any kasiṇa whatsoever among the earth-kasiṇa and so on, and having performed the preliminary work, one should resolve, “Let there be space.” There, he states the reason: “Mastery over the eight attainments alone is the standard.” Therefore, whatever one wishes, that very thing comes to be. By this, it is meant that the attainment of the water-kasiṇa for emerging from and submerging in the earth, and the attainment of the earth-kasiṇa for creating earth in water and the like, are not necessarily desired. This refers to the attainment of the space-kasiṇa, which must necessarily be stated in performing the miracle of passing through walls and so on, because it is appropriate. And by doing so, just as the statement, “the making manifest of what is covered by means of the space-kasiṇa,” and so on, is established, so too, by means of the earth-kasiṇa, the state of “being one, he becomes many,” and so on, and also that which was stated in the miscellaneous section with passages such as, “in space or in water, having created earth, going on foot is accomplished,” becomes established.

“Doso natthī”ti dvikkhattuṃ baddhaṃ subaddhaṃ viya daḷhīkaraṇaṃ nāma hotīti adhippāyena vatvā tena payojanābhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “puna samāpajjitvā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Adhiṭṭhitattā ākāso hotiyevāti sacepi kiñci antarā upaṭṭhitaṃ pabbatādi siyā, tampi “ākāso hotū”ti adhiṭṭhitattā [V 2.0026] ākāso hotiyeva. Idampi aṭṭhānaparikappanamattaṃ, tādisassa upaṭṭhānameva natthīti dassetuṃ “antarā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Having said, “There is no fault,” with the intention that this serves as a “making firm”—just as something tied twice is well-tied—the phrase “having attained again,” etc., was then stated to show the absence of purpose in that. “Because it has been resolved, it becomes space indeed” means that even if something like a mountain were to arise in between, that too, because it has been resolved with “Let it be space,” becomes space indeed. This too is merely a conjecture about an impossible matter; to show that the arising of such a thing simply does not occur, “in between,” etc., was stated.

393. Paricchinditvāti yathicchitaṭṭhānaṃ ñāṇena paricchinditvā. Tatrāti tasmiṃ pathaviyā udakabhāvādhiṭṭhāne ayaṃ yathāvuttapaṭipattivibhāvinī pāḷi[M 2.0027]. Parato “tatrāyaṃ pāḷī”ti āgataṭṭhānesupi iminā nayena attho veditabbo.

393. “Having delimited” means: having delimited the desired place with knowledge. “There” means: in that resolution of earth into the state of water, this is the Pāḷi text that clarifies the practice as stated before. Hereafter, also in places where “there, this is the Pāḷi” occurs, the meaning should be understood by this method.

Soti iddhimā. Adhiṭṭhānakāle kālaparicchedaṃ katvā adhiṭṭhātīti vuttaṃ “paricchinnakālaṃ pana atikkamitvā”ti. Pakatiyā udakaṃ animmānaudakaṃ.

“He” means the one with psychic power. It is said that at the time of resolve, having made a time limit, he resolves, as in “but having passed the delimited time.” By nature, water is uncreated water.

394. Viparītanti yaṃ udakaṃ akkamitvā akkamanto na saṃsīdati, taṃ panettha iddhiyā pathavīnimmānavasena veditabbaṃ. Pathavīkasiṇanti pathavīkasiṇajjhānaṃ.

394. “The opposite” means that the water, upon which one who is stepping does not sink, should be understood here by means of creating earth through psychic power. “Earth kasiṇa” means the earth-kasiṇa absorption.

395. Pallaṅkanti samantato ūrubaddhāsanaṃ. Chinnapakkho, asañjātapakkho vā sakuṇo ḍetuṃ na sakkotīti pāḷiyaṃ “pakkhī sakuṇo”ti (paṭi. ma. 3.11) pakkhī-saddena visesetvā sakuṇo vuttoti “pakkhehi yuttasakuṇo”ti āha. Parikammaṃ katvāti “pathavī hotū”ti parikammaṃ katvā.

395. “Cross-legged” means the sitting posture with thighs bound all around. A bird with broken wings or with undeveloped wings cannot fly; therefore, in the Pāḷi text, the word `sakuṇo` (bird) is specified by the word `pakkhī` in the phrase `pakkhī sakuṇo`. Therefore, he said, “a bird endowed with wings.” “Having done the preliminary work” means having done the preliminary work, “Let it be earth.”

Ākāse antalikkheti antalikkhasaññite ākāse. Yattha yattha hi āvaraṇaṃ natthi, taṃ taṃ “ākāsa”nti vuccati. Ayañca iddhimā na pathaviyā āsanne ākāse gacchati. Yattha pana pakkhīnaṃ agocaro, tattha gacchati, tādisañca loke “antalikkha”nti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ “antalikkhasaññite ākāse”ti.

“In the sky, in the atmosphere” means in the space designated as the atmosphere. Indeed, wherever there is no obstruction, that is called 'space.' And this one with psychic power does not go in the space near the earth. But where it is beyond the range of birds, there he goes; and such a place is called 'atmosphere' in the world. Therefore it is said, 'in the space designated as the atmosphere.'

Theroti pubbe vutta tipiṭakacūḷābhayatthero. Samāpattisamāpajjananti puna samāpattisamāpajjanaṃ. Nanu samāhitamevassa cittanti iddhimato pāṭihāriyavasena pavattamānassa cittaṃ accantaṃ samāhitameva hoti, na aññadā viya asamāhitanti adhippāyo. Taṃ pana therassa matimattaṃ. Pubbe hi pathavīkasiṇaṃ samāpajjitvā pathaviṃ adhiṭṭhāya gacchati, idāni pana ākāso icchitabbo, tasmā ākāsakasiṇaṃ samāpajjitabbameva. Tenāha “kiñcāpī”tiādi. Tirokuṭṭapāṭihāriye [V 2.0027] vuttanayeneva paṭipajjitabbanti yathā tattha kuṭṭādi “ākāso hotū”ti adhiṭṭhānena ākāso hoti, evaṃ idhāpi pabbatarukkhādiṃ adhiṭṭhānena ākāsaṃ katvā gantabbanti attho. Atha vā tirokuṭṭapāṭihāriye vuttanayenevāti “sace panassa bhikkhuno adhiṭṭhahitvā gacchantassā”tiādinā (visuddhi. 2.392) tattha [M 2.0028] vuttanayena. Etena “purimādhiṭṭhānabaleneva cassa antarā añño pabbato vā rukkho vā utumayo uṭṭhahissatīti aṭṭhānameveta”nti nāgādīhi kayiramāno vibandho gamanantarāyaṃ na karotīti dasseti.

“The Elder” means the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷābhaya, mentioned previously. “Entering attainment” means re-entering the attainment that is the base jhāna. “Surely his mind is concentrated”—the meaning is that the mind of one performing psychic feats is utterly concentrated, not unconcentrated as at other times; this is the opinion of the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷābhaya. But that is merely the Elder's opinion. For previously, having entered the earth-kasiṇa, he resolved upon the earth and moved; now, however, space is desired, therefore the space-kasiṇa must be entered. Hence it is said, “even though,” etc. “One should proceed just as explained in the feat of passing through walls” means that just as there, walls, etc., become space through the resolve, “Let it be space,” so here too, the meaning is that one should make mountains, trees, etc., into space by resolve and then go. Alternatively, “as explained in the feat of passing through walls” refers to the method stated there: “if for a monk, while going, having resolved,” etc. (Visuddhimagga 2.392). By this, it is shown that “due to the power of the initial resolve, it is impossible for another mountain or tree to arise seasonally in between,” and thus obstacles created by nāgas, etc., do not hinder the movement.

Okāseti janavivitte yuttaṭṭhāne. Pākaṭo hoti ākāsacārī ayaṃ samaṇoti.

“He makes space” means in a suitable, secluded place. This ascetic becomes known as a sky-walker.

396. Dvācattālīsayojanasahassaggahaṇaṃ paṭhamakappavasena kataṃ, tato paraṃ pana anukkamena pathaviyā ussitabhāvena tato katipayayojanūnatā siyā, appakaṃ adhikaṃ vā ūnaṃ vā gaṇanūpagaṃ na hotīti tathā vuttaṃ. Tīsu dīpesu ekakkhaṇe ālokakaraṇenāti yadā yasmiṃ dīpe majjhe tiṭṭhanti, tadā tato purimasmiṃ atthaṃ gacchantā pacchime udentā hutvā ālokakaraṇena. Aññajotīnaṃ vā abhibhavanena, duddasatāya ca mahiddhike. Sattānaṃ sītapariḷāhavūpasamanena, osadhitiṇavanappatīnaṃ paribrūhanena ca mahānubhāve. Chupatīti phusati. Parimajjatīti hatthaṃ ito cito ca sañcārento ghaṃseti. Abhiññāpādakajjhānavasenevāti yassa kassaci abhiññāpādakajjhānavasena. Eva-kārena pādakajjhānavisesaṃ nivatteti, na adhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tenevāha “natthettha kasiṇasamāpattiniyamo”ti. Tirokuṭṭapāṭihāriyādīsu viya imasmiṃ nāma kasiṇe jhānaṃ samāpajjitvā adhiṭṭhātabbanti na ettha koci niyamo atthīti attho. Tathā hi pāḷiyaṃ kiñci samāpattiṃ aparāmasitvā “idha so iddhimā”tiādi (paṭi. ma. 3.10-11) vuttaṃ. Hatthapāse hoti “candimasūriye”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ candimasūriyamaṇḍalaṃ. Rūpagataṃ hatthapāseti hatthapāse ṭhitaṃ rūpagataṃ, hatthapāse vā rūpagataṃ. Hatthaṃ vā vaḍḍhetvā parāmasatīti yojanā.

396. The measurement of forty-two thousand yojanas was made according to the first aeon; but thereafter, due to the gradual rising of the earth, it might be less by a few yojanas. It is said thus because whether it is slightly more or less, it does not enter into the calculation. The phrase “by illuminating the three continents in a single moment” means: when they stand in the middle of one continent, at that time, they are setting in the preceding continent and rising in the subsequent continent, thus making light. They are of great psychic power (mahiddhike) either because they overpower other lights or because they are difficult to look at. They are of great influence (mahānubhāve) by pacifying the cold and heat of beings, and by fostering the growth of medicinal plants, grasses, and forest trees. “Chupati” means to touch. “Parimajjati” means to stroke, that is, to rub by moving the hand here and there. The phrase “by the power of a jhāna that is a basis for direct knowledge alone” means by the power of any jhāna whatsoever that is a basis for direct knowledge. The particle “eva” (alone) excludes a specific basic jhāna, not the resolve. Therefore, it was said, “There is no fixed rule here regarding the attainment of a kasiṇa.” The meaning is that, just as in the case of miracles such as passing through a wall, there is no rule here that one must make a resolve after having attained jhāna in such-and-such a kasiṇa. Indeed, in the Pāḷi text, without referring to any particular attainment, it is said, “Here, that one with psychic power…” etc. The orb of the moon and sun, spoken of thus as “the moon and sun,” is within arm's reach. “A material object within arm's reach” means a material object situated within arm's reach, or a material object brought within arm's reach. Or, having extended the hand, one touches it—this is the construction.

Upādinnakaṃ nissāya anupādinnakassa vaḍḍhanaṃ vuttaṃ. Yuttiyā panettha upādinnakassapi vaḍḍhanacchāyā dissati. Attano aṇumahantabhāvāpādane upādinnakassa hāpanaṃ viya vaḍḍhanampi labbhateva. Yathā āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa nandopanandadamaneti evaṃ pavattaṃ sahavatthunā theravādaṃ āharitvā tamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “tipiṭakacūḷanāgatthero āhā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Kiṃ pana na hoti, hotiyevāti [V 2.0028] adhippāyo. Dve hi paṭisedhā [M 2.0029] pakatiṃ gamentīti. “Tadā mahantaṃ hoti mahāmoggallānattherassa viyā”ti idaṃ yathādhikatatthadassanavasena vuttaṃ, khuddakabhāvāpādanampettha labbhateva.

It is stated that the growth of the non-clung-to form is dependent on the clung-to form. However, in this context, by way of logic, a semblance of growth is also seen even in the clung-to form. In bringing about for oneself the state of being small or large, just as a decrease of the clung-to form is possible, so too is an increase indeed possible. As in the subduing of Nandopananda by the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, in order to show that meaning by bringing forth the Theravāda tradition together with the story that occurred thus, the passage beginning with “the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷanāga said” was begun. Why does it not happen? It indeed happens—this is the intention. For two negations lead to the natural meaning. This statement, “Then it becomes great, like that of the Elder Mahāmoggallāna,” was said by way of showing the meaning as it applies; here, bringing about the state of being small is also indeed possible.

Nandopanandanāgadamanakathāvaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Account of the Subduing of the Nāga Nandopananda

Olokesi buddhāciṇṇavasena “atthi nu kho assa upanissayo”ti. Lokiyaṃ ratanattaye pasādalakkhaṇaṃ sāsanāvatāraṃ sandhāyāha “appasanno”ti. Micchādiṭṭhito vivecetvā pasādetabboti adhippāyo. Tenāha “ko nu kho…pe… viveceyyā”ti.

He surveyed by way of the custom of the Buddhas, “Is there indeed a supporting condition for him?” With reference to the worldly entry into the Dispensation, which has the characteristic of faith in the Triple Gem, he said, “He is without faith.” The intention is that he should be made to have faith, having been separated from wrong view. Therefore, he said, “Who indeed…pe… should separate [him]?”

Taṃ divasanti yadā bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto tāvatiṃsabhavanābhimukho gacchati, taṃ divasabhāgaṃ. Āpānabhūmiṃ sajjayiṃsūti yattha so nisinno bhojanakiccaṃ karoti, taṃ parivesanaṭṭhānaṃ sittaṃ sammaṭṭhaṃ bhojanūpakaraṇūpanayanādinā sajjayiṃsu paṭiyādesuṃ. Tividhanāṭakehīti vadhūkumārikaññāvatthāhi tividhāhi nāṭakitthīhi. Olokayamānoti pekkhanto, vicārento vā.

“Taṃ divasaṃ” means that portion of the day when the Blessed One, surrounded by the community of monks, goes facing the Tāvatiṃsa abode. “Āpānabhūmiṃ sajjayiṃsu” means they prepared the serving place where he, having sat down, performs the duty of eating, by sprinkling and sweeping, and by bringing food and utensils, etc.; they made preparations. “Tividhanāṭakehi” means by three kinds of female dancers: married women, maidens, and young girls. “Olokayamāno” means looking, or investigating.

Uparūparīti matthakamatthake. Bhavanenāti bhavanapadesena. Bhogehīti sarīrabhogehi. Avakujjenāti nikujjitena. Gahetvāti yathā tāvatiṃsabhavanassa padesopi nāvasissati, evaṃ pariyādāya.

“Uparūpari” means on the very top. “Bhavanena” means by a region of the mansion. “Bhogehī” means by the coils of the body. “Avakujjena” means overturned. “Gahetvā” means having completely encompassed it in such a way that not even a part of the Tāvatiṃsa abode remains.

Sineruparibhaṇḍanti sinerumekhalaṃ. Sinerussa kira samantato bahalato, puthulato ca pañcayojanasahassaparimāṇāni cattāri paribhaṇḍāni tāvatiṃsabhavanassa ārakkhāya nāgehi, garuḷehi, kumbhaṇḍehi, yakkhehi ca adhiṭṭhitāni, tāni paribhaṇḍabhāvasāmaññena ekajjhaṃ katvā “paribhaṇḍa”nti vuttaṃ. Tehi kira sinerussa upaḍḍhaṃ pariyādinnaṃ.

“Sineruparibhaṇḍanti” means the girdle of Sineru. It is said that around Sineru, there are four girdles, each five thousand yojanas in thickness and breadth, which are governed by nāgas, garuḷas, kumbhaṇḍas, and yakkhas for the protection of the Tāvatiṃsa abode. Due to the commonality of being girdles, they are collectively called “paribhaṇḍa.” It is said that they encompass half of Sineru.

Attabhāvaṃ vijahitvāti manussarūpaṃ antaradhāpetvā. Bādhatīti khedamattaṃ uppādeti.

“Attabhāvaṃ vijahitvāti” means having caused the human form to disappear. “Bādhatīti” means it produces mere distress.

Attabhāvaṃ vijahitvāti sukhumattabhāvanimmānena nāgarūpaṃ vijahitvā. Mukhaṃ vivari “mukhagataṃ [V 2.0029] samaṇaṃ saṃkhādissāmī”ti. Pācīnena ca pacchimena cāti nāgassa tathānipannattā vuttaṃ. Suṭṭhu satiyā paccupaṭṭhāpanatthamāha “manasi karohī”ti.

“Attabhāvaṃ vijahitvāti” means: having abandoned the nāga form by creating a subtle individual existence. It opened its mouth, thinking, “I will chew the ascetic who is in my mouth.” “Pācīnena ca pacchimena cāti” is said because of the nāga’s lying in that way. For the purpose of firmly establishing mindfulness, he said, “Manasi karohi (bear it in mind).”

Ādito [M 2.0030] paṭṭhāya sabbapāṭihāriyānīti tadā therena katapāṭihāriyāni sandhāya vuttaṃ. Imaṃ pana ṭhānanti imaṃ nāsāvātavissajjanakāraṇaṃ.

“Ādito paṭṭhāya sabbapāṭihāriyānīti” is said with reference to the miracles performed by the Elder at that time. “Imaṃ pana ṭhānanti” means this reason, which is the releasing of the breath from the nose.

Anubandhīti “na sakkā evaṃmahiddhikassa imassa samaṇassa paṭipaharitu”nti bhayena palāyantaṃ anubandhi.

“Anubandhīti” means: he pursued the one fleeing out of fear, thinking, “It is not possible to strike back at this ascetic of such great psychic power.”

Ekapaṭipāṭiyāti ekāya paṭipāṭiyā, nirantaranti attho. Ayamevāti yā upādinnakaṃ nissāya anupādinnakassa vaḍḍhi, ayameva. Ettha edise hatthavaḍḍhanādipāṭihāriye yutti yuttarūpā cittato, ututo vā upādinnakarūpānaṃ anuppajjanato. Atha vā upādinnanti sakalameva indriyabaddhaṃ adhippetaṃ. Evampi tassa tathā vaḍḍhi na yujjati evāti vuttanayeneva vaḍḍhi veditabbā. Ekasantāne upādinnaṃ, anupādinnañca sambhinnaṃ viya pavattamānampi atthato asambhinnameva. Tattha yathā āḷhakamatte khīre anekāḷhake udake āsitte yadipi khīraṃ sabbena sambhinnaṃ sabbatthakameva lambamānaṃ hutvā tiṭṭhati, tathāpi na tattha khīraṃ vaḍḍhati, udakameva vaḍḍhati, evamevaṃ yadipi upādinnaṃ anupādinnañca sambhinnaṃ viya pavattati, tathāpi upādinnaṃ na vaḍḍhati, iddhānubhāvena cittajaṃ, tadanusārena utujañca vaḍḍhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

“Ekapaṭipāṭiyā” means by a single sequence; “without interval” is the meaning. “Ayameva” means: this very increase of the non-appropriated that is dependent on the appropriated. Here, in such a miracle as the extension of the hand, this is the suitable reasoning, because appropriated matter does not arise from mind or from temperature. Alternatively, by “upādinna” is meant all matter that is bound to the sense faculties. Even so, for that matter, an increase in such a way is not at all suitable; thus, the increase should be understood only in the way that has been stated. In a single continuum, although the appropriated and the non-appropriated proceed as if mixed, in reality they are not mixed at all. Therein, just as when a measure of milk is poured into many measures of water, although the milk stands mixed with all the water and is obtainable everywhere, nevertheless the milk does not increase, only the water increases; so too, although the appropriated and the non-appropriated proceed as if mixed, nevertheless the appropriated does not increase. It should be understood that through the power of psychic potency, the mind-born matter increases, and in accordance with that, the temperature-born matter also increases.

Soti so iddhimā. Evaṃ katvāti vuttākārena hatthaṃ vā vaḍḍhetvā te vā āgantvā hatthapāse ṭhite katvā. Pādaṭṭhapanādipi vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Aparopi iddhimā. Tathevāti pāṭihāriyakaraṇato pubbe viya. Tathūpamametanti yathā udakapuṇṇāsu nānāpātīsu bahūhi nānācandamaṇḍalesu dissamānesu na tena candamaṇḍalassa gamanādiuparodho, bahūnañca paccekaṃ dassanaṃ ijjhati, tathūpamametaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ candimasūriyānaṃ gamanādiuparodhābhāvato, bahūnañca iddhimantānaṃ tattha iddhipayogassa yathicchitaṃ samijjhanatoti adhippāyo.

“So” means: that one with psychic power. “Evaṃ katvā” means: having done thus in the manner stated, either by extending the hand, or by making them come and stand within reach of the hand. The placing of the foot and so on should also be understood in the very way that has been stated. “Aparopi iddhimā” means another one with psychic power also. “Tatheva” means: just as before the performance of the miracle. “Tathūpamametaṃ” means this miracle has that as its simile: just as when various moon-discs are seen by many people in various vessels filled with water, there is no obstruction to the movement of the actual moon-disc, and the individual seeing by many people is accomplished, so too is this miracle. This is because there is no obstruction to the movement of the moon and sun, and because the application of psychic power upon them by many with psychic power is accomplished as desired. This is the intention.

397. Paricchedaṃ katvāti abhividhivasena pana paricchedaṃ katvā, na mariyādavasena. Tathā hesa brahmaloke attano kāyena vasaṃ vatteti. Pāḷīti paṭisambhidāmaggapāḷi.

397. “Paricchedaṃ katvā” means: having made a demarcation by way of inclusion (abhividhi), not by way of exclusive limit (mariyāda). For indeed, this one wields mastery with his own body in the Brahma-world. “Pāḷi” means the Pāḷi of the Paṭisambhidāmagga.

Yāva [V 2.0030] brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattetīti ettha yasmā na brahmalokasseva gamanaṃ adhippetaṃ, nāpi brahmalokassa gamanameva, atha kho [M 2.0031] aññathā aññampi. Yāva brahmalokāti pana dūrāvadhinidassanametaṃ, tasmā “sace brahmalokaṃ gantukāmā hotī”ti vatvāpi itarampi dassetuṃ “santikepi dūre adhiṭṭhātī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha pi-saddo samuccayattho, tena vuttāvasesassa adhiṭṭhāniddhiyā nipphādetabbassa sabbassāpi saṅgaho, na vuttassevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Herein, in the phrase “wields mastery with the body even up to the Brahma-world,” because it is not intended that going to the Brahma-world alone is meant, nor is merely the act of going to the Brahma-world intended, but rather another act in another way is also intended. The phrase “even up to the Brahma-world” is an illustration of a distant limit. Therefore, even after saying, “if one wishes to go to the Brahma-world,” in order to show another act as well, it is stated, “one can resolve upon what is near or far,” and so on. Therein, the particle “pi” has the meaning of aggregation. By it, there is the inclusion of all that which remains from what has been said and is to be accomplished by the power of determination; it is not the inclusion of only what has been said. Thus it should be understood.

Yamakapāṭihāriyāvasānetiādinā tivikkamassa adhiṭṭhāniddhinipphannatā vuttā, aññattha pana lakkhaṇānisaṃsatā. Tadubhayaṃ yathā aññamaññaṃ na virujjhati, tathā vicāretvā gahetabbaṃ.

By the phrase “at the conclusion of the Twin Miracle,” and so on, the fact that the three strides were accomplished by the power of determination is stated. But in another place, the fact that this was a beneficial result of the characteristic [of well-placed feet] is stated. Those two statements should be accepted after having investigated in such a way that they do not contradict each other.

Nīlamātikanti nīlavaṇṇodakamātikaṃ.

“Nīlamātikaṃ” means a small channel with blue-colored water.

Mahābodhinti aparājitapallaṅkaṃ mahābodhiṃ. Citte uppanne santike akāsīti tathā cittuppattisamanantarameva pathaviṃ, samuddañca saṃkhipitvā mahābodhisantike akāsi.

“Mahābodhiṃ” means the Mahābodhi which has the unconquered throne. “Citte uppanne santike akāsīti” means that immediately after the thought arose, having contracted the earth and the ocean, he brought himself to the vicinity of the Mahābodhi.

Nakkhattadivaseti mahadivase. Candapūveti candasadise candamaṇḍalākāre pūve. Ekapattapūramattamakāsīti yathā te pamāṇato sarūpeneva antopattapariyāpannā honti, tathā akāsi.

“Nakkhattadivase” means on a great day. “Candapūve” means cakes that are like the moon, having the shape of the moon's orb. “Ekapattapūramattamakāsi” means he acted in such a way that those cakes, in terms of quantity and by their very own form, were contained within the bowl.

Kākavaliyavatthusmiñca “bhagavā thokaṃ bahuṃ akāsī”ti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Taṃ pana vatthuṃ saṅkhepatova dassetuṃ “mahākassapatthero kirā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Samāpattiyāti nirodhasamāpattiyā.

And in the story of Kākavaliya, the statement “the Blessed One made a little into much” should be brought and connected. However, in order to show that story only in brief, the phrase “the Elder Mahākassapa, it is said,” and so on, was stated. “Samāpattiyā” means by the attainment of cessation.

Gaṅgātīreti tambapaṇṇidīpe gaṅgānadiyā tīre. Saññaṃ adāsīti yathā te yathādhiṭṭhitaṃ sappiṃ passanti, tathā saññaṃ adāsi.

“Gaṅgātīre” means on the bank of the Gaṅgā river on the island of Tambapaṇṇi. “Saññaṃ adāsi” means he gave a sign in such a way that those novices would see the ghee as it had been determined.

Tassāti yassa brahmuno rūpaṃ daṭṭhukāmo, tassa brahmuno rūpaṃ passati. Saddaṃ suṇātīti dibbāya sotadhātuyā brahmuno saddaṃ suṇāti. Cittaṃ pajānātīti cetopariyañāṇena brahmuno cittaṃ pajānāti. Karajakāyassa vasenāti cātumahābhūtikarūpakāyassa vasena. “Cittaṃ pariṇāmetī”ti ettha kiṃ taṃ cittaṃ, kathaṃ vā pariṇāmananti āha “pādakajjhānacittaṃ gahetvā kāye āropetī”ti. Kathaṃ [V 2.0031] pana kāye āropetīti āha “kāyānugatikaṃ karotī”ti. Evampi saddadandharovāyanti vacanapathaṃ pacchindanto āha “dandhagamana”nti. Karotīti [M 2.0032] sambandho. Kāyagamanaṃ hi dandhaṃ, dandhamahābhūtapaccayattāti adhippāyo. Ayañhettha attho – dissamānena kāyena gantukāmatāya vasena cittaṃ pariṇāmento yogī pādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya “idaṃ cittaṃ kāyo viya dandhagamanaṃ hotū”ti parikammaṃ karoti. Tathā parikammakaraṇaṃ hi sandhāya “pādakajjhānacittaṃ gahetvā”ti vuttaṃ. Parikammaṃ pana katvā puna samāpajjitvā ñāṇena adhiṭṭhahanto taṃ cittaṃ kāye āropeti, kāyānugatikaṃ dandhagamanaṃ karoti.

The word `tassa` means: of whichever Brahmā one desires to see the form, one sees the form of that Brahmā. 'He hears the sound' means: with the divine ear-element he hears the sound of the Brahmā. 'He knows the mind' means: with the knowledge of others' minds he knows the mind of the Brahmā. 'By means of the body born of action' means: by means of the physical body composed of the four great elements. 'He inclines the mind': here, what is that mind, and how is the inclining? To this, it is said: 'having taken the mind of the base-jhāna, he places it on the body.' But how does he place it on the body? It is said: 'He makes it conform to the body.' Even so, this explanation is like a verbal thicket. Therefore, wishing to cut off the path of speech, he said, 'slow-moving.' 'He makes': this is the connection. For the body's movement is slow because its cause is the slow great elements; this is the intention. Herein, this is the meaning: a yogī, inclining the mind by way of the desire to go with the visible body, having attained and emerged from the base-jhāna, performs the preliminary work, thinking: 'Let this mind, like the body, become slow-moving.' It is with reference to performing the preliminary work in such a way that it is said: 'having taken the mind of the base-jhāna.' Then, having done the preliminary work, having attained the jhāna again and determining with knowledge, he places that mind on the body; he makes it conform to the body, slow-moving.

Sukhasaññanti sukhasahagataṃ saññaṃ, saññāsīsena niddeso. Lahubhāvena saññātanti lahusaññaṃ. Kathaṃ pana iddhicittena saha sukhasaññāya sambhavoti āha “sukhasaññā nāma upekkhāsampayuttā saññā”ti. Sukhanti saññātanti vā sukhasaññaṃ. Tenevāha “upekkhā hi santaṃ sukhanti vuttā”ti ekantagarukehi nīvaraṇehi, oḷārikehi anupasantasabhāvehi ca vitakkādīhi vippayogo cittacetasikānaṃ lahubhāvassa kāraṇanti dassento āha “sāyeva…pe… veditabbā”ti. Taṃ okkantassāti taṃ sukhalahusaññaṃ anuppattassa. Assāti yogino. Gantukāmatā eva ettha pamāṇanti ettha etasmiṃ dissamānena kāyena gamane yaṃ ṭhānaṃ gantukāmo, taṃ uddissa gantukāmatāvasena pavattaparikammādhiṭṭhānāni eva pamāṇaṃ, tāvatā gamanaṃ ijjhati. Tasmā magganimmānavāyuadhiṭṭhānehi vināpi icchitadesappatti hotīti. Idāni tamevatthaṃ pākaṭataraṃ kātuṃ “sati hī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

The perception of happiness (sukhasaññā) is a perception accompanied by happiness; the explanation is a designation by way of perception. It is 'light perception' (lahusaññā) because it is perceived by way of lightness. But how can the perception of happiness arise together with the mind of psychic power? He says: ‘The perception of happiness is a perception associated with equanimity.’ Or, it is the 'perception of happiness' (sukhasaññā) because it is perceived as ‘happiness’ (sukhaṃ). Therefore, he says: ‘Equanimity is indeed said to be a peaceful happiness.’ Showing that disassociation from extremely heavy hindrances, and from coarse, unpeaceful factors such as applied thoughts, is the cause of the lightness of mind and mental factors, he says, ‘That very… should be understood.’ ‘For one who has approached that’ (taṃ okkantassa) means for one who has attained that perception of happiness and lightness. ‘His’ (assa) means of the yogī. ‘Here, the mere wish to go is the criterion’ (gantukāmatā eva ettha pamāṇaṃ) means that in this case, regarding the movement of the visible body, the preliminary work and resolutions that arise based on the wish to go to whatever place one desires are the criterion; to that extent, the going is accomplished. Therefore, even without creating a path and determining the wind, arrival at the desired place occurs. Now, to make this meaning even clearer, it is said, ‘For indeed…’ and so on.

Kāyaṃ gahetvāti karajakāyaṃ ārammaṇakaraṇavasena parikammacittena gahetvā. Citte āropetīti “ayaṃ kāyo idaṃ cittaṃ viya hotū”ti pādakajjhānacitte āropeti taggatikaṃ karoti. Tenāha “cittānugatikaṃ karoti sīghagamana”nti. Cittagamananti cittappavattimāha. Idaṃ pana cittavasena kāyapariṇāmanapāṭihāriyaṃ. Cittagamanamevāti cittena samānagamanameva. Kathaṃ pana kāyo dandhappavattiko lahuparivattinā cittena samānagatiko hotīti? Na sabbathā samānagatiko. Yatheva hi kāyavasena cittapariṇāmane cittaṃ sabbathā kāyena samānagatikaṃ na hoti. Na hi tadā cittaṃ sabhāvasiddhena attano khaṇena avattitvā garuvuttikassa rūpadhammassa khaṇena vattati. “Idaṃ cittaṃ ayaṃ kāyo viya hotū”ti pana adhiṭṭhānena [M 2.0033] dandhagatikassa kāyassa anuvattanato yāva icchitaṭṭhānappatti, tāva kāyagatianulomeneva hutvā santānavasena [V 2.0032] pavattamānaṃ cittaṃ kāyagatiyā pariṇāmitaṃ nāma hoti, evaṃ “ayaṃ kāyo idaṃ cittaṃ viya hotū”ti adhiṭṭhānena pageva sukhalahusaññāya sampāditattā abhāvitiddhipādānaṃ viya dandhaṃ avattitvā yathā lahukatipayacittavāreheva icchitaṭṭhānappatti hoti, evaṃ pavattamāno kāyo cittagatiyā pariṇāmito nāma hoti, na ekacittakkhaṇeneva icchitaṭṭhānappattiyā.

‘Taking the body’ (kāyaṃ gahetvā) means taking the physical body (karajakāya) as an object by means of the preparatory mind. ‘He places it upon the mind’ (citte āropeti) means he places it upon the mind of the base jhāna (pādakajjhānacitte), thinking, ‘May this body become like this mind,’ making it have a similar movement. Hence it is said: ‘He makes it follow the mind, moving swiftly.’ ‘Moving with the mind’ (cittagamanaṃ) refers to the occurrence of the mind. This, however, is the miracle of transforming the body by means of the mind. ‘Moving with the mind itself’ (cittagamanameva) means moving in unison with the mind. But how can the body, which has a slow occurrence, move in unison with the swiftly changing mind? It does not move in unison in every way. Just as when transforming the mind by means of the body, the mind does not move in unison with the body in every way. For at that time, the mind, not proceeding according to its own naturally established moment, does not proceed according to the moment of the material phenomenon, which has a heavy occurrence. However, through the resolve, ‘May this mind become like this body,’ the mind, proceeding by way of a continuum, is said to be transformed by the body’s movement, in that it follows the slow-moving body until it reaches the desired destination, thus moving in accordance with the body’s movement. Similarly, through the resolve, ‘May this body become like this mind,’ and because the perception of happiness and lightness has already been produced, the body, unlike for those who have not developed the bases of psychic power, does not proceed slowly. Rather, the desired destination is reached through just a few swift mind-processes. Thus, the body proceeding in this way is said to be transformed by the movement of the mind, not by reaching the desired destination in a single mind-moment.

Evañca katvā “seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyyā”ti idampi upamāvacanaṃ nippariyāyeneva samatthitaṃ hoti. Avassaṃ cetaṃ evaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ, aññathā suttābhidhammapāṭhehi, vinayaaṭṭhakathāya ca virodho siyā, dhammatā ca vilomitā. “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampī”ti (a. ni. 1.11 ādayo) hi ettha aññagahaṇena rūpadhammā gahitā alahuparivattitāya. Abhidhamme (paṭṭhā. 1.1.10-11) ca purejātapaccayo rūpameva vutto, pacchājātapaccayo ca tasseva. Yattha yattha ca dhammā uppajjanti, tattha tattheva bhijjanti. Natthi desantarasaṅkamanaṃ, na ca sabhāvo aññathā hotīti. Na hi iddhibalena dhammānaṃ kenaci lakkhaṇaṃ aññathattaṃ kātuṃ sakkā, bhāvaññathattameva pana kātuṃ sakkā. “Tīsupi khaṇesū”ti idampi gamanārambhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na gamananiṭṭhānanti vadanti. Theroti aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ antare eko thero. Idhāti idaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ vibhajitvā vuttapāṭhe. Sayaṃ gamanameva āgataṃ “brahmalokaṃ gacchatī”ti vuttattā.

And for this very reason, this simile, ‘just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm, or bend his extended arm,’ is also unequivocally established. And this must certainly be accepted in this way; otherwise, there would be conflict with the texts of the Suttas and Abhidhamma, as well as the Vinaya commentary, and the natural order would be subverted. For in the statement, ‘Monks, I do not see even a single other phenomenon’ (Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.11, etc.), by the term ‘other,’ material phenomena are included because of their slow transformation. Moreover, in the Abhidhamma (Paṭṭhāna 1.1.10-11), the pre-nascence condition is stated to be only material form, and the post-nascence condition is also stated for that very material form. And wherever phenomena arise, right there they also cease. There is no transference to another place, nor does their intrinsic nature change. Indeed, it is not possible for anyone to alter any characteristic of phenomena through psychic power, but it is possible only to alter their state. ‘In three moments’ this too is said with reference to the beginning of movement, not its completion—so they say. ‘The Elder’ refers to one elder among the commentary teachers. ‘Here’ refers to the passage where this miracle is analyzed and taught. Going itself is what is meant, since it is stated that ‘he goes to the Brahma-world.’
