In whatever place the power of the Tathāgata's rebirth-consciousness, sharpened by the fruit of merit, flourishes exceedingly by its own nature, all that is called the field of arising for the Buddha-sprout; thus, it is said, 'The birth-field extends to the limit of ten thousand world-systems.' As for 'the power operates': here, a person with psychic power who has attained mastery of mind, standing in any world-system whatsoever within the field of authority and having made a protection for his own benefit, remains under that protection even after going to another world-system within that same field. Or else, when a protection is made for the benefit of all beings while standing in one world-system, the power of the protection indeed reaches all beings throughout the field of authority, because the deities there are to accept the authority of the protection. Referring to the field of range, it was said by the Blessed One, who affirms his ability to make things known by voice and to show his own form in a single moment, 'Or as far as he might wish.' 'Wherever' means in that immeasurable, infinite field of range. Whatever the Tathāgata wishes, that he knows, because the Buddha's knowledge has a nature that is bound to occur merely by his wish. 'Remaining firm' means unfolding, arising.

405. Gokhāyitakamattesūti gohi khāditabbappamāṇesu. Yanti yasmiṃ samaye. Pupphaphalūpajīviniyo ca devatā brahmaloke nibbattantīti sambandho.

405. 'In quantities that can be consumed by cattle' means in quantities that can be consumed by cattle. 'Yanti' means 'at which time.' The connection is: 'and deities who subsist on flowers and fruits are reborn in the Brahma world.'

Etesanti “vassūpajīvino”tiādinā vuttasattānaṃ. Tatthāti brahmaloke. So ca kho parittābhādibrahmaloko veditabbo. “Paṭiladdhajjhānavasenā”ti vatvā jhānappaṭilābhassa sambhavaṃ dassetuṃ “tadā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Lokaṃ byūhenti sampiṇḍentīti lokabyūhā. Te kira disvā manussā tattha tattha ṭhitāpi nisinnāpi saṃvegajātā, sambhamappattā [M 2.0051] ca hutvā tesaṃ āsanne ṭhāne sannipatanti. Sikhābandhassa muttatāya muttasirā. Ito cito ca vidhūyamānakesatāya vikiṇṇakesā. Lokavināsabhayena sokavantacittatāya ativiya virūpavesadhārino. Mārisāti devānaṃ [V 2.0048] piyasamudācāro. Kathaṃ panete kappavuṭṭhānaṃ jānantīti? Dhammatāya sañcoditāti ācariyā. Tādisanimittadassanenāti eke. Brahmadevatāhi uyyojitāti apare.

'Of these' refers to the beings mentioned by 'those who subsist on rain' and so on. 'There' refers to the Brahma world. And that should be understood as the Brahma world of Limited Radiance and so on. Having stated 'by means of the attainment of jhāna,' the words 'for then indeed,' and so on, were stated to show the possibility of attaining jhāna. Because they assemble and condense the world, they are called 'world-assemblers' (lokabyūhā). It is said that upon seeing them, humans—whether standing or sitting in whatever place—become agitated and, having fallen into panic, gather in a place near them. Because their topknots are untied, their heads are unbound. Because their hair is shaken to and fro, their hair is disheveled. Because their minds are sorrowful due to fear of the world's destruction, they wear extremely disordered attire. 'Mārisa' is a term of affectionate address among the devas. But how do they know about the dissolution of the eon? The teachers say they are prompted by the nature of things. Some say it is through seeing such a sign. Others say they are urged by the Brahma deities.

Mettādīnīti mettāmanasikārādīni kāmāvacarapuññāni. Devaloketi kāmadevaloke. Devānaṃ kira sukhasamphassavātaggahaṇaparicayena vāyokasiṇe jhānāni sukheneva ijjhanti. Tena vuttaṃ “vāyokasiṇe parikammaṃ katvā jhānaṃ paṭilabhantī”ti. Tadaññe panāti āpāyike sandhāyāha. Tatthāti devaloke.

'Loving-kindness and so on' means the wholesome deeds of the sense-sphere, beginning with attention to loving-kindness. 'In the world of the devas' means in the desire-realm world of devas. It is said that for the devas, the jhānas on the wind kasiṇa are accomplished with ease due to their familiarity with grasping wind that has a pleasant touch. Therefore, it is said: 'Having performed the preliminary work on the wind kasiṇa, they attain jhāna.' 'But others' refers to those in the woeful states. 'There' means in the world of the devas.

Dutiyo sūriyoti dutiyaṃ sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ. Sattasūriyanti sattasūriyapātubhāvasuttaṃ. Pakatisūriyeti kappavuṭṭhānakālato pubbe uppannasūriyavimāne. Kappavuṭṭhānakāle pana yathā aññe kāmāvacaradevā, evaṃ sūriyadevaputtopi jhānaṃ nibbattetvā brahmalokaṃ upapajjati, sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ pana pabhassaratarañceva tejavantatarañca hutvā pavattati. Taṃ antaradhāyitvā aññameva uppajjatīti apare. Gaṅgā yamunā sarabhū aciravatī mahīti imā pañca mahānadiyo.

'The second sun' means the second solar orb. 'Seven suns' refers to the Sutta on the Appearance of Seven Suns. 'The natural sun' refers to the solar mansion that arose before the time of the eon's dissolution. At the time of the eon's dissolution, however, just as other devas of the desire realm, so too the sun-deity produces jhāna and is reborn in the Brahma realm; the solar orb, for its part, continues to exist, having become even more radiant and more powerful. Others say that it disappears and a completely different one arises. The Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarabhū, Aciravatī, and Mahī—these are the five great rivers.

Pabhavāti uppattiṭṭhānabhūtā. Haṃsapātanoti mandākinimāha.

'Sources' (pabhavā) means which are the places of origin. 'Haṃsapātana' refers to the Mandākinī.

Na saṇṭhātīti na tiṭṭhati.

'It does not remain' means it does not stand.

Pariyādinnasinehanti parikkhīṇasinehaṃ. Yāya āpodhātuyā tattha tattha pathavīdhātu ābandhattā sampiṇḍatā hutvā tiṭṭhati, sā chasūriyapātubhāvena parikkhayaṃ gacchati. Yathā cidanti yathā ca idaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ. Evaṃ koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷānipīti vipattimahāmeghuppattito paṭṭhāya idha vuttaṃ sabbaṃ kappavuṭṭhānaṃ, taṃ tattha atidisati.

'Having its moisture exhausted' means having its moisture depleted. The water element, by which the earth element is bound and consolidated in various places, goes to destruction due to the manifestation of the sixth sun. 'Just as this' means just as this world-system. Similarly, regarding the hundred thousand koṭis of world-systems also, starting from the arising of the great destructive cloud, all the cosmic dissolution spoken of here is applied to them.

Palujjitvāti chijjitvā. Saṅkhāragatanti bhūtupādāyappabhedaṃ saṅkhārajātaṃ. Sabbasaṅkhāraparikkhayāti jhāpetabbasaṅkhāraparikkhayā. Sayampi saṅkhāragataṃ samānaṃ indhanābhāvato chārikampi asesetvā niḍḍahitvā vūpasamatīti āha “sappi…pe… nibbāyatī”ti.

'Having disintegrated' means having been broken apart. 'Conditioned phenomena' means the collection of conditioned things which are divided into primary elements and derived materiality. 'Due to the exhaustion of all conditioned things' means due to the exhaustion of the conditioned things that are to be burned. Being itself a conditioned phenomenon, it is extinguished due to the absence of fuel, after having burned up even the ash without remainder. Therefore, it is said, 'ghee... is extinguished.'

406. Dīghassa [M 2.0052] addhunoti saṃvaṭṭaṭṭhāyīasaṅkhyeyyakappasaṅkhātassa dīghassa kālassa accayena[V 2.0049]. Tālakkhandhādīti ādi-saddena sākasālādirukkhe saṅgaṇhāti. Ghanaṃ karotīti visarituṃ adatvā piṇḍitaṃ karoti. Tenāha “parivaṭuma”nti, vaṭṭabhāvena paricchinnaṃ. Tanti udakaṃ. Assāti vātassa. Vivaraṃ detīti yathā ghanaṃ karoti sampiṇḍeti, evaṃ tattha antaraṃ deti. Parikkhayamānanti pubbe yāva brahmalokā ekoghabhūtena vātena parisosiyamānatāya parikkhayaṃ gacchantaṃ. Brahmaloko pātubhavatīti yojanā. Brahmalokoti ca paṭhamajjhānabhūmimāha. Upari catukāmāvacaradevalokaṭṭhāneti yāmadevalokādīnaṃ catunnaṃ patiṭṭhānaṭṭhāne. Cātumahārājikatāvatiṃsabhavanānaṃ pana patiṭṭhānaṭṭhānāni pathavīsambandhatāya na tāva pātubhavanti.

406. 'After a long time' means after the passing of a long time, designated as the dissolution-remaining incalculable eon. In 'tālakkhandhādi,' by the word 'ādi,' it includes trees such as teak and sal. 'Makes it dense' means it makes it consolidated, not allowing it to disperse. Therefore, he said 'parivaṭumaṃ,' meaning defined by its roundness. 'That' refers to the water. 'Of it' means of the wind. 'Gives an interval' means that just as it makes it dense and consolidates it, so it creates an interval therein. 'Going to destruction' refers to that which is going to destruction due to being dried up by the wind that had formerly become a single flood up to the Brahma-world. 'The Brahma-world appears' is the syntactical connection. And by 'Brahma-world,' he refers to the plane of the first jhāna. 'In the location of the four sense-sphere divine worlds above' means in the base-location of the four, such as the Yāma deva-world. However, the base-locations of the Cātumahārājika and Tāvatiṃsa abodes, due to their connection with the earth, do not yet appear.

Rundhantīti yathā heṭṭhā na bhassati, evaṃ nirodhenti.

"They obstruct" means: they stop it in such a way that it does not fall down below.

“Paṭhamatarābhinibbattā”ti idaṃ āyukkhayassa sambhavadassanaṃ, tena dvinnaṃ, catunnaṃ, aṭṭhannaṃ vā kappānaṃ ādimhi nibbattāti dasseti. Tatoti ābhassarabrahmalokato. Parittābhaappamāṇābhāpi hi ābhassaraggahaṇeneva saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. “Te honti sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā”ti idaṃ upacārajjhānapuññassa mahānubhāvatāya vuttaṃ. Āluppakārakanti ālopaṃ katvā katvāti vadanti, āluppanaṃ vilopaṃ katvāti attho.

The phrase "First to be reborn" indicates the possibility of the exhaustion of the lifespan; by this, it shows that they are reborn at the beginning of two, four, or eight eons. "From there" means from the Ābhassara Brahma world. Indeed, the Parittābha and Appamāṇābhā Brahmas are also included by the taking of the term "Ābhassara." The phrase "They are self-luminous and move through the sky" is said due to the great power of the merit from access concentration. Regarding "Āluppakāraka," they explain it as "making into morsels"; alternatively, the meaning is "having plundered."

Haṭṭhatuṭṭhāti ativiya haṭṭhā uppilāvitacittā. Nāmaṃ karontīti tathā voharanti.

"Overjoyed" means exceedingly delighted, with minds uplifted. "They make a name" means they speak thus.

Sinerucakkavāḷahimavantapabbatāti ettha dīpasamuddāpīti vattabbaṃ. Tathā hi vakkhati “ninnaninnaṭṭhāne samuddā, samasamaṭṭhāne dīpā”ti. Thūpathūpāti unnatunnatā.

"Sineru, Cakkavāḷa, and Himavanta mountains"—here, "islands and oceans" should also be stated. For thus it will be said: "The oceans are in the low-lying places, the islands are in the level places." "Thūpathūpā" means elevated and elevated.

Atimaññantīti atikkamitvā maññanti, hīḷentīti attho. Teneva nayenāti “ekacce vaṇṇavanto hontī”tiādinā (dī. ni. 3.123) vuttena nayeneva. Padālatāti evaṃnāmikā latājāti. Tassā kira pārāsavajāti gaḷocīti vadanti. Akaṭṭhe eva bhūmippadese paccanako akaṭṭhapāko. Akaṇoti kuṇḍakarahito.

"Atimaññanti" means they think beyond, that is, they despise. "By that same method" refers to the very method stated in "some are of fair complexion, etc." "Padālatā" is a species of creeper so named. They say that its Pārāsava species—a creeper that arose in a later period—is, it is said, called Gaḷocī. Rice that ripens in an uncultivated region of earth itself is "akaṭṭhapāka" (that which ripens without ploughing). "Akaṇa" means devoid of broken grains or of fine bran.

Sumanasaṅkhātajātipupphasadiso [M 2.0053] sumanajātipupphasadiso. Yo yo raso etassāti yaṃyaṃraso, odano, taṃ yaṃyaṃrasaṃ, yādisarasavantanti attho. Rasapathavī, bhūmipappaṭako, padālatā ca [V 2.0050] paribhuttā sudhāhāro viya khuddaṃ vinodetvā rasaharaṇīhi rasameva brūhentā tiṭṭhanti, na vatthuno sukhumabhāvena nissandā, sukhumabhāveneva gahaṇindhanameva ca honti. Odano pana paribhutto rasaṃ vaḍḍhentopi vatthuno oḷārikabhāvena nissandaṃ vissajjento passāvaṃ, kasaṭañca uppādetīti āha “tato pabhuti muttakarīsaṃ sañjāyatī”ti. Purimattabhāvesu pavattaupacārajjhānānubhāvena yāva sattasantāne kāmarāgavikkhambhanavego na samito, na tāva balavakāmarāgūpanissayāni itthipurisindriyāni pāturahesuṃ. Yadā panassa vicchinnatāya balavakāmarāgo laddhāvasaro ahosi, tadā tadupanissayāni tāni sattānaṃ attabhāvesu sañjāyiṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ “purisassa…pe… pātubhavatī”ti. Tenevāha “tatra suda”ntiādi.

Like the flower of the species called sumana means like the flower of the sumana species. "Yo yo raso etassā"ti "yaṃyaṃraso": because it has whatever flavor. "Odano": rice. "Taṃ yaṃyaṃrasaṃ": that rice which has whatever flavor. "Yādisarasavanta"nti "attho": this is the meaning, possessing such a flavor. The flavor-earth, the earth-scum, and the padālatā creeper, when consumed, like ambrosial food, having dispelled hunger, they exist, increasing only the nutritive essence by means of the channels that carry the nutritive essence. Due to the subtlety of the substance, there are no excretions; and due to its very subtlety, they become only fuel for the digestive fire. But rice, when consumed, although it increases the nutritive essence, due to the coarseness of the substance, while discharging the consequence, produces urine and the coarse dregs which are feces. Therefore, he said, “From then on, urine and feces are produced.” In previous states of existence, by the power of the access concentration that had occurred, as long as the force of suppressing sensual desire had not subsided in the continuity of beings, the female and male faculties, which are the supporting conditions for strong sensual desire, had not yet manifested. But when, due to the interruption of this force, strong sensual desire found an opportunity, then those faculties, which are its supporting conditions, arose in the beings' states of existence. Therefore, it was said, “For a man… it becomes manifest.” For that very reason, he said, “There indeed…” and so on.

Alasajātikassāti sajjukameva taṇḍulaṃ aggahetvā paradivasassatthāya gahaṇena alasapakatikassa.

"Alasajātikassa" means: of one with a lazy nature, characterized by taking rice for the sake of the next day, not taking it just for the same day.

Anutthunantīti anusocanti. Sammanneyyāmāti samanujāneyyāma. Noti amhesu. Sammāti sammadeva yathārahaṃ. Khīyitabbanti khīyanārahaṃ nindanīyaṃ. Garahitabbanti hīḷetabbaṃ.

"Anutthunanti" means: they lament or yearn for. "Sammanneyyāma" means: we should approve well, or we should acknowledge. "No" means: among us. "Sammā" means: just properly, fittingly. "Khīyitabba" means: worthy of condemnation, blameworthy. "Garahitabba" means: to be censured or reproached.

Ayameva bhagavā paṭibalo paggahaniggahaṃ kātunti yojanā. Rañjetīti saṅgahavatthūhi sammadeva rameti pīṇeti.

The construction is: "This Blessed One alone is capable of showing favor and disfavor." "Rañjeti" means: with the bases of sympathy, he perfectly causes delight and pleases.

Vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyīasaṅkhyeyyaṃ catusaṭṭhiantarakappasaṅgahaṃ. Vīsatiantarakappasaṅgahanti keci. Sesāsaṅkhyeyyāni kālato tena samappamāṇāneva.

The vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyī-asaṅkhyeyya (incalculable aeon of evolving-and-remaining) is a collection of sixty-four intermediate aeons. Some say it is a collection of twenty intermediate aeons. The remaining incalculable aeons, in terms of time, are of the very same measure as that.

407. Mahādhārāhīti tālasālakkhandhappamāṇāhi mahatīhi khārudakadhārāhi. Samantatoti sabbaso. Pathavitoti pathaviyā heṭṭhimantato pabhuti. Tena hi khārudakena phuṭṭhaphuṭṭhā pathavīpabbatādayo udake [M 2.0054] pakkhittaloṇasakkharā viya vilīyanteva, tasmā pathavīsandhārudakena saddhiṃ ekūdakameva taṃ hotīti keci. Apare “pathavīsandhārakaṃ udakakkhandhañca udakasandhārakaṃ vāyukkhandhañca anavasesato vināsetvā sabbattha sayameva ekoghabhūtaṃ tiṭṭhatī”ti vadanti, taṃ yuttaṃ. Tayopi brahmaloketi parittābhaappamāṇābhaābhassarabrahmaloke, tayidaṃ “ayaṃ pana viseso”ti āraddhattā vuttaṃ, aññathā “chapi brahmaloke”ti vattabbaṃ siyā. Subhakiṇheti ukkaṭṭhaniddesena [V 2.0051] tatiyajjhānabhūmiyā upalakkhaṇaṃ. Parittāsubhaappamāṇāsubhepi hi āhacca udakaṃ tiṭṭhati. Heṭṭhā “ābhassare āhacca tiṭṭhatī”ti etthāpi eseva nayo. Tanti taṃ kappavināsakaudakaṃ. Udakānugatanti udakena anugataṃ phuṭṭhaṃ. Abhibhavitvāti vilīyāpetvā.

407. "Mahādhārāhi" means by great streams of caustic water, the size of palm and sal tree trunks. "Samantato" means completely. "Pathavito" means from the lowest edge of the earth. Indeed, whatever is touched again and again by that caustic water—the earth, mountains, and so on—dissolves just like salt and sugar put into water. Therefore, some say that it becomes a single mass of water together with the earth-supporting water. Others say, “Having completely destroyed the water-mass that supports the earth and the wind-mass that supports the water, it itself alone remains everywhere as a single flood.” That is reasonable. "Tayopi brahmaloke" refers to the Brahma worlds of Limited Radiance, Immeasurable Radiance, and Streaming Radiance. This is said because it was begun with “this, however, is the distinction”; otherwise, it should have been said, “the six Brahma worlds.” "Subhakiṇha" is a designation for the third jhāna plane by way of a superlative indication. Indeed, the water stands, having reached even the realms of Limited Beauty and Immeasurable Beauty. Below, in the text “it stands, having reached the Ābhassara realm,” this is the same method. "Taṃ" means that world-destroying water. "Udakānugataṃ" means followed by and touched by the water. "Abhibhavitvā" means causing it to dissolve.

Idamekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyanti idaṃ saṃvaṭṭasaṅkhātaṃ kappassa ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ.

"Idaṃ ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ" means: this, which is reckoned as the contraction, is one incalculable period of the aeon.

408. Thūlaraje apagate eva pathavīnissitaṃ saṇharajaṃ apagacchatīti vuttaṃ “tato saṇharaja”nti. Samuṭṭhāpetīti sambandho. “Visamaṭṭhāne ṭhitamahārukkhe”ti idaṃ paṭhamaṃ samuṭṭhāpetabbataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

408. Because "only when the coarse dust has departed, the fine dust adhering to the earth departs," it is said "tato saṇharajaṃ" (then the fine dust). The connection is with "samuṭṭhāpeti" (uproots). "Visamaṭṭhāne ṭhitamahārukkhe" (the great trees standing in uneven places) is said with reference to being what should be uprooted first.

Cakkavāḷapabbatampi sinerupabbatampīti mahāpathaviyā viparivattaneneva viparivattitaṃ cakkavāḷapabbatampi sinerupabbatampi vāto ukkhipitvā ākāse khipati. Te cakkavāḷapabbatādayo. Abhihantvāti ghaṭṭetvā. Aññamaññanti ekissā lokadhātuyā cakkavāḷahimavantasineruṃ aññissā lokadhātuyā cakkavāḷādīhīti evaṃ aññamaññaṃ samāgamavasena ghaṭṭetvā. Sabbasaṅkhāragatanti pathavīsandhārakaudakaṃ, taṃsandhārakavātanti sabbaṃ saṅkhāragataṃ vināsetvā sayampi vinassati avaṭṭhānassa kāraṇābhāvato.

‘The Cakkavāḷa mountain and the Sineru mountain’ means: by the very overturning of the great earth, the wind lifts up even the Cakkavāḷa mountain and the Sineru mountain, which have been overturned, and tosses them into the sky. Those are the Cakkavāḷa mountains and so forth. ‘Abhihantvā’ means having struck. ‘Aññamaññaṃ’ means having struck against each other in this way, by the coming together of the Cakkavāḷa, Himavanta, and Sineru of one world-system with the Cakkavāḷa and so forth of another world-system. ‘Sabbasaṅkhāragataṃ’ means: having destroyed all that has come to be conditioned—that is, the earth-supporting water and the wind that supports it—it itself also perishes due to the absence of a cause for its stability.

409. Yadipi saṅkhārānaṃ ahetuko sarasanirodho vināsakābhāvato, santānanirodho pana hetuvirahito natthi yathā taṃ sattakāyesūti. Bhājanalokassāpi sahetukena vināsena bhavitabbanti hetuṃ pucchati “kiṃ kāraṇā evaṃ loko vinassatī”ti. Itaro yathā tattha nibbattanakasattānaṃ puññabalena paṭhamaṃ loko vivaṭṭati, evaṃ tesaṃ pāpabalena saṃvaṭṭatīti dassento “akusalamūlakāraṇā”ti āha. Yathā hi rāgadosamohānaṃ adhikabhāvena yathākkamaṃ rogantarakappo, satthantarakappo, dubbhikkhantarakappoti ime tividhā [M 2.0055] antarakappā vivaṭṭaṭṭhāyimhi asaṅkhyeyyakappe jāyanti, evamete yathāvuttā tayo saṃvaṭṭā rāgādīnaṃ adhikabhāveneva hontīti dassento “akusalamūlesu hī”tiādimāha. Ussannatareti ativiya ussanne. Dose ussannatare adhikataradosena viya tikkhatarena khārudakena vināso yuttoti vuttaṃ “dose ussannatare udakena vinassatī”ti. Pākaṭasattusadisassa dosassa aggisadisatā, apākaṭasattusadisassa rāgassa khārudakasadisatā ca yuttāti adhippāyena “dose ussannatare agginā, rāge ussannatare udakenā”ti [V 2.0052] kecivādassa adhippāyo veditabbo. Rāgo sattānaṃ bahulaṃ pavattatīti rāgavasena bahuso lokavināso.

409. Although the cessation of formations by their own nature is causeless due to the absence of a destroyer, the cessation of continuity is not without cause, as is the case in the bodies of beings. Therefore, the destruction of the receptacle world must also have a cause. Thus, the question is asked: “For what reason does this world perish?” The other, showing that just as the world first evolves through the power of merit of the beings born there, so too does it devolve through the power of their demerit, said: “Because of unwholesome roots.” For just as, due to the predominance of greed, hatred, and delusion, respectively, these three kinds of intermediate aeons—the disease-aeon, the weapons-aeon, and the famine-aeon—arise in the incalculable aeon of the evolving-and-remaining stage, so too do these three aforesaid devolutions occur only through the predominance of greed and so forth. Showing this, he said: “Because of unwholesome roots…” and so on. `Ussannatare` means ‘exceedingly predominant’. Because when hatred is more predominant, destruction by sharper alkaline water is deemed fitting, as if by a more excessive hatred, it was said: “When hatred is more predominant, it perishes by water.” The opinion of some who say, “When hatred is more predominant, by fire; when greed is more predominant, by water,” should be understood with this intention: the fire-like nature of hatred, which is like an obvious enemy, is fitting, and the alkaline-water-like nature of greed, which is like a hidden enemy, is fitting. Greed occurs frequently among beings; therefore, the destruction of the world is often due to greed.

410. Evaṃ pasaṅgena saṃvaṭṭādike pakāsetvā idāni yathādhikataṃ nesaṃ anussaraṇākāraṃ dassetuṃ “pubbenivāsaṃ anussarantopī”tiādi āraddhaṃ.

410. Having thus explained devolution and so forth in passing, now, to show the manner of their recollection as is relevant to the topic, the text beginning with ‘pubbenivāsaṃ anussarantopi’ and so on is introduced.

“Amumhi saṃvaṭṭakappe”ti idaṃ saṃvaṭṭakappassa ādito pāḷiyaṃ (dī. ni. 1.244) gahitattā vuttaṃ. Tatthāpi hi imassa katipayaṃ kālaṃ bhavādīsu saṃsaraṇaṃ upalabbhatīti. Saṃvaṭṭakappe vā vaṭṭamānesu bhavādīsu imassa upapatti ahosi, taṃdassanametaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Atha vā amumhi saṃvaṭṭakappeti ettha vā-saddo luttaniddiṭṭho daṭṭhabbo, tena ca aniyamatthena itarāsaṅkhyeyyānampi saṅgaho siddho hoti. Bhave vātiādīsu kāmādibhave vā aṇḍajādiyoniyā vā devādi gatiyā vā nānattakāyanānattasaññīādiviññāṇaṭṭhitiyā vā sattāvāse vā khattiyādi sattanikāye vā. Āsinti ahosiṃ. Vaṇṇasampattiṃ vāti vā-saddena vaṇṇavipattiṃ vāti dasseti.

“‘In that devolution-aeon’—this is stated because it is taken from the beginning of the devolution-aeon in the Pāḷi. For indeed, even there, this one’s wandering for some time among existences and so forth is found. Or, this one’s rebirth occurred in the existences and so forth that were occurring during the devolution-aeon; this phrase should be seen as an indication of that. Alternatively, herein in ‘amumhi saṃvaṭṭakappe’, the word ‘vā’ should be seen as indicated elliptically, and by that word, which has the meaning of non-restriction, the inclusion of other incalculable aeons is also established. In ‘in an existence, or…’ and so on: in an existence of sensuality and so forth, or in a destiny of devas and so forth, or in a station of consciousness such as those with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, or in an abode of beings, or in a class of beings such as khattiyas. ‘Āsiṃ’ means ‘I was’. In ‘vaṇṇasampattiṃ vā’ (or perfection of appearance), by the word ‘vā’, it indicates ‘or imperfection of appearance’.

Sālimaṃsodanāhāro vā gihikāle. Pavattaphalabhojano vā tāpasādikāle. Sāmisā gehassitā somanassādayo. Nirāmisā nekkhammassitā. Ādi-saddena vivekajasamādhijasukhādīnaṃ saṅgaho.

‘Or one who had food of fine rice with meat’—this was during the time as a householder. ‘Or one who ate naturally occurring fruit’—this was during the time as an ascetic and so forth. Gladness and so forth connected with the household life are carnal. Those connected with renunciation are non-carnal. By the word ‘ādi’ (and so forth), the inclusion of bliss born of seclusion, bliss born of concentration, and so forth is meant.

“Amutrāsi”ntiādinā sabbaṃ yāvadicchakaṃ anussaraṇaṃ dassetvā idāni aññathā atthaṃ dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha amutrāsinti sāmaññaniddesoyaṃ, byāpanicchālopo vā, amutra amutrāsinti vuttaṃ hoti. Anupubbena ārohantassa yāvadicchakaṃ anussaraṇanti ettha [M 2.0056] ārohantassāti paṭilomato ñāṇena pubbenivāsaṃ ārohantassa. Paccavekkhaṇanti anussaritānussaritassa paccavekkhaṇaṃ, na anussaraṇaṃ. Itīti vuttatthanidassanaṃ. Tañca kho yathārahato, na yathānupubbatoti dassento “nāmagottavasenā”tiādimāha. Vaṇṇādīhīti vaṇṇāhāravedayitāyuparicchedehi. Odātotīti ettha iti-saddo ādiattho, pakārattho vā, tena evamādi evaṃpakāranānattatoti dassitaṃ hoti.

Having shown by ‘amutrāsiṃ’ (I was there) and so on all recollection as far as one wishes, now, in order to show the meaning in another way, ‘apicā’ (moreover) and so on is stated. Herein, ‘amutrāsiṃ’ is a general designation. Or, it is an elision implying distribution; it means ‘amutra amutra āsiṃ’ (in that and that existence, I was). Herein, in the phrase ‘recollection as far as one wishes for one ascending sequentially’, ‘for one ascending’ means for one ascending to past lives with knowledge in reverse order. `Paccavekkhaṇaṃ` (reviewing) is the reviewing of what has been repeatedly recollected; it is not the recollection itself. The word `iti` is an indication of the meaning stated. And showing that this is according to suitability, not according to sequence, he said ‘nāmagottavasena’ (by way of name and clan) and so on. `Vaṇṇādīhi` (by appearance, etc.) means by appearance, food, feeling, and the limitation of the lifespan. Herein in ‘odāto’ti (was white), the word ‘iti’ has the meaning of ‘and so forth’ or the meaning of ‘manner’. By that, it is shown that there is variety such as ‘of this sort’ and ‘of this kind’.

Pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the discourse on the knowledge of recollecting past abodes is finished.

Cutūpapātañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Discourse on the Knowledge of the Passing Away and Reappearance of Beings

411. Cutiyāti [V 2.0053] cavane. Upapāteti upapajjane. Samīpatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ, cutikkhaṇasāmantā, upapattikkhaṇasāmantā cāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tathā hi vakkhati “ye pana āsannacutikā”tiādi (visuddhi. 2.411). Dibbacakkhuñāṇeneva sattānaṃ cuti ca upapatti ca ñāyatīti āha “dibbacakkhuñāṇatthanti vuttaṃ hotī”ti. Dibbasadisattātiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Ayaṃ pana viseso – tattha “sotadhātū”ti padaṃ apekkhitvā itthiliṅgavasena vuttaṃ, idha napuṃsakaliṅgavasena vattabbaṃ. Tattha ca ālokapariggahena payojanaṃ natthi, idha atthīti vuttaṃ “ālokapariggahena mahājutikattāpi dibba”nti, kasiṇālokānuggahena pattabbattā, sayaṃ ñāṇālokapharaṇabhāvena ca mahājutikabhāvatoti attho. Mahājutikampi hi “dibba”nti vuccati “dibbamidaṃ byamha”ntiādīsu. Mahāgatikattāti mahanīyagamanattā, vimhayanīyapavattikattāti attho. Vimhayanīyā hissa pavatti tirokuṭṭādigatarūpadassanato. “Dibbasadisattā”ti ca hīnūpamādassanaṃ devatānaṃ dibbacakkhutopi imassa mahānubhāvattā. Tena dibbacakkhulābhāya yogino parikammakaraṇaṃ tappaṭipakkhābhibhavassa atthato tassa vijayicchā nāma hoti, dibbacakkhulābhī ca iddhimā devatānaṃ vacanaggahaṇakkhamanadhammadānavasena mahāmoggallānattherādayo viya dānaggahaṇalakkhaṇe, vohāre ca pavatteyyāti evaṃ vihāravijayicchāvohārajutigatisaṅkhātānaṃ atthānaṃ vasena imassa abhiññāñāṇassa dibbacakkhubhāvasiddhito[M 2.0057]. Saddavidū ca tesu eva atthesu divu-saddaṃ icchantīti vuttaṃ “taṃ sabbaṃ saddasatthānusārena veditabba”nti.

411. Cutiyāti means in passing away. Upapāteti means in arising. This is a locative case in the sense of proximity; thus, it is said to mean ‘near the moment of passing away’ and ‘near the moment of reappearance.’ For thus it will be said: ‘Those who are near passing away,’ etc. The passing away and reappearance of beings are known only by the knowledge of the divine eye; hence, it is said, ‘It is for the purpose of the knowledge of the divine eye.’ What needs to be said regarding terms like ‘resembling the divine’ has already been explained below. This, however, is the difference: there, with reference to the term ‘ear-element’ (sotadhātu), it was stated in the feminine gender; here, it should be stated in the neuter gender. And there, there is no purpose for the inclusion of light, but here there is; thus it is said: ‘It is divine also because of its great radiance through the inclusion of light,’ meaning it is attainable through the aid of kasiṇa light and because of its nature of spreading the light of knowledge by itself, it is of great radiance. For even that which is of great radiance is called ‘divine,’ as in phrases like ‘this divine Brahma-dwelling.’ Mahāgatikattā means ‘because of its worthy going,’ that is, ‘because its occurrence is astonishing.’ Its occurrence is astonishing because it sees forms that have gone beyond walls, etc. And ‘because it resembles the divine’ is the showing of an inferior simile, because this knowledge is of greater power than even the divine eye of devas. Therefore, a meditator's performance of preliminary work for the attainment of the divine eye is, in essence, what is called the desire for victory over its opponent. And one who has attained the divine eye, being endowed with psychic power, like the Elder Mahāmoggallāna and others, by means of receiving the words of devas and giving the Dhamma, might also engage in transactions characterized by giving and receiving. Thus, by means of the meanings designated as dwelling, desire for victory, transaction, radiance, and going, the divine-eye nature of this higher knowledge is established. And grammarians desire the word ‘divu’ in these very meanings; thus it is said: ‘All this should be understood in accordance with the science of grammar.’

Dassanaṭṭhenāti rūpadassanabhāvena. Cakkhunā hi sattā rūpaṃ passanti. Yathā maṃsacakkhu viññāṇādhiṭṭhitaṃ samavisamaṃ ācikkhantaṃ viya pavattati, na tathā idaṃ. Idaṃ pana sayameva tato sātisayaṃ cakkhukiccakārīti āha “cakkhukiccakaraṇena cakkhumivātipi cakkhū”ti. “Diṭṭhivisuddhihetuttā”ti saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ vivarituṃ “yo hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ucchedadiṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti parato upapattiyā adassanato etthevāyaṃ satto ucchinno, evamitarepīti. Navasattapātubhāvadiṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti lābhī adhiccasamuppattiko viya. Buddhaputtā passantiyevāti uttarapadāvadhāraṇaṃ, na purimapadāvadhāraṇaṃ. Evaṃ hi jayaddisajātakādīhi avirodho siddho hoti.

‘By the state of seeing’ means by the nature of seeing form. For beings see form with the eye. Just as the fleshly eye, established in consciousness, functions as if indicating what is even and uneven, this is not so. This, however, itself performs the function of an eye in a superior way to that; hence it was said, ‘It is an eye, and also like an eye, because it performs the function of an eye.’ To explain the meaning stated in brief as ‘because it is a cause for the purification of view,’ the passage beginning with ‘For he…’ was stated. He adopts the annihilation view because of not seeing rebirth hereafter, thinking, ‘This being is annihilated right here, and so are others.’ The attainer adopts the view of the appearance of a new being, like one who holds the view of spontaneous origination. ‘The sons of the Buddha indeed see’—the emphasis is on the latter word, not the former word. For in this way, non-contradiction with the Jayaddisa Jātaka and others is established.

Manussānaṃ [V 2.0054] idanti mānusakaṃ, manussānaṃ gocarabhūtaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ. Tadaññassa pana dibbatirohitātisukhumādibhedassa rūpassa dassanato atikkantamānusakaṃ. Evarūpañca manussūpacāraṃ atikkantaṃ nāma hotīti āha “manussūpacāraṃ atikkamitvā rūpadassanenā”ti. Evaṃ visayamukhena dassetvā idāni visayīmukhena dassetuṃ “mānusakaṃ vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tatthāpi maṃsacakkhātikkamo tassa kiccātikkameneva daṭṭhabbo.

‘This of humans,’ thus it is ‘human’ (mānusakaṃ); it is the form-object that is the resort of humans. But because of seeing form of other kinds, such as the divine, the hidden, and the extremely subtle, it ‘surpasses the human.’ And such a thing is called ‘surpassing the human range’; hence it was said, ‘by seeing forms, having surpassed the human range.’ Having thus shown it by way of the object, now, to show it by way of the subject, the passage beginning ‘or the human…’ was stated. There too, the surpassing of the fleshly eye should be understood as the surpassing of its function.

Dibbacakkhunāti dibbacakkhuñāṇenapi. Daṭṭhuṃ na sakkā khaṇassa atiittaratāya atisukhumatāya kesañci rūpassa. Apica dibbacakkhussa paccuppannaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ, tañca purejātapaccayabhūtaṃ, na ca āvajjanaparikammehi vinā mahaggatassa pavatti atthi, nāpi uppajjamānameva rūpaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo bhavituṃ sakkoti, bhijjamānaṃ vā. Tasmā “cutūpapātakkhaṇe rūpaṃ dibbacakkhunā daṭṭhuṃ na sakkā”ti suvuttametaṃ. Yadi dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ rūpārammaṇameva, atha kasmā “satte passatī”ti vuttanti? Yebhuyyena sattasantānagatarūpadassanato evaṃ vuttaṃ. Sattagahaṇassa vā kāraṇabhāvato vohāravasena vuttantipi keci. Te cavamānāti adhippetāti sambandho. Evarūpeti na cutūpapātakkhaṇasamaṅginoti adhippāyo.

By ‘divine eye’ is meant also the divine-eye-knowledge. It is not possible to see the form of certain beings due to the extreme brevity of the moment and its extreme subtlety. Moreover, the divine eye has a present form as its object, and that is a pre-nascent condition. And without adverting and preliminary work, there is no occurrence of sublime consciousness; nor can a form that is just arising, or one that is perishing, become an object-condition. Therefore, this statement, ‘At the moment of passing away and reappearance, form cannot be seen with the divine eye,’ is well-spoken. If the divine-eye-knowledge has only form as its object, then why is it said, ‘one sees beings’? It is said thus because, for the most part, one sees the form that has gone into the continuity of beings. Or, some say it is spoken by way of conventional usage because it is the cause for the concept of ‘being.’ The connection is thus: by ‘they,’ ‘those who are passing away’ is intended. By ‘in such a nature,’ the meaning is ‘not those endowed with the moment of passing away and reappearance.’

Mohūpanissayaṃ nāma kammaṃ nihīnaṃ nihīnaphalaṃ hotīti āha “mohanissandayuttattā”ti. Tabbiparīteti tassa hīḷitādibhāvassa viparīte[M 2.0058], ahīḷite anohīḷite anoññāte anavaññāte cittīkateti attho. Suvaṇṇeti sundaravaṇṇe. Dubbaṇṇeti asundaravaṇṇe. Sā panāyaṃ suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇatā yathākkamaṃ kammassa adosadosūpanissayatāya hotīti āha “adosanissandayuttattā”tiādi. Sundaraṃ gatiṃ gatā sugatāti āha “sugatigate”ti, sugatiṃ upapanneti attho. Alobhajjhāsayā sattā vadaññū vigatamaccherā alobhūpanissayena kammunā subhagā samiddhā hontīti āha “alobhanissandayuttattā vā aḍḍhe mahaddhane”ti. Dukkhaṃ gatiṃ gatā duggatāti āha “duggatigate”ti. Lobhajjhāsayā sattā luddhā maccharino lobhūpanissayena kammunā duggatā durupetā hontīti āha “lobhanissandayuttattā vā dalidde appannapāne”ti.

An action that has delusion as its decisive support condition is base and has a base result; thus, He said, ‘because of being connected with the result of delusion.’ By ‘in the opposite of that’ is meant: in the opposite of that state of being despised, etc., that is, not despised, not looked down upon, not held in contempt, not disdained, esteemed. By ‘of good complexion’ is meant having a beautiful color. By ‘of poor complexion’ is meant having an unattractive color. Now, this state of having a good or poor complexion occurs, respectively, because of the action having non-aversion or aversion as its decisive support condition. Therefore, He said, ‘because of being connected with the result of non-aversion,’ etc. Having gone to a good destination, they are ‘well-gone’ (sugatā); thus, He said, ‘gone to a good destination,’ the meaning of which is ‘reborn in a good destination.’ Beings whose disposition is non-greed, being generous and free from stinginess, become fortunate and prosperous through an action that has non-greed as its decisive support condition. Therefore, He said, ‘or because of being connected with the result of non-greed, they are affluent, of great wealth.’ Having gone to a woeful destination, they are ‘ill-gone’ (duggatā); thus, He said, ‘gone to a woeful destination.’ Beings whose disposition is greed, being covetous and miserly, become wretched and unfortunate through an action that has greed as its decisive support condition. Therefore, He said, ‘or because of being connected with the result of greed, they are poor, lacking food and drink.’

Upacitanti phalāvahabhāvena kataṃ. Yathā kataṃ hi kammaṃ phaladānasamatthaṃ hoti, tathā kataṃ upacitaṃ. Cavamānetiādīhi dibbacakkhukiccaṃ vuttanti visayamukhena visayībyāpāramāha. Purimehīti vā “dibbena cakkhunā”tiādīni padāni sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ādīhīti ettha ca-saddo luttaniddiṭṭho[V 2.0055]. Tasmā “dibbena…pe… passatī”ti imehi, “cavamāne”tiādīhi ca dibbacakkhukiccaṃ vuttanti attho.

'Accumulated' means done in a way that brings forth a result. For just as an action that has been done is capable of giving fruit, so an action thus done is called 'accumulated'. By 'passing away,' etc., the function of the divine eye is stated; this speaks of the activity of the subject by way of the object. Alternatively, it is said with reference to the preceding words, such as 'with the divine eye,' etc. Here, in 'etc.,' the particle 'ca' (and) is understood though unexpressed. Therefore, the meaning is that the function of the divine eye is stated by these words, namely, 'with the divine eye... sees,' and by 'passing away,' etc.

Iminā pana padenāti “yathākammūpage satte pajānātī”ti iminā vākyena. Idha bhikkhūti imasmiṃ sāsane bhikkhu, dibbacakkhuñāṇalābhīti adhippāyo. So ca dibbacakkhuñāṇalābhī nerayike ca satte paccakkhato disvā ṭhito. Evaṃ manasi karotīti tesaṃ nerayikānaṃ nirayasaṃvattaniyassa kammassa ñātukāmatāvasena pādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya parikammavasena manasi karoti. Kiṃ nu khotiādi manasikāravidhidassanaṃ. Evaṃ pana parikammaṃ katvā pādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhitassa taṃ kammaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā āvajjanaṃ uppajjati, tasmiṃ niruddhe cattāri, pañca vā javanāni javantītiādi sabbaṃ vuttanayameva. “Visuṃ parikammaṃ nāma natthī”ti idaṃ pana dibbacakkhuñāṇena vinā yathākammūpagañāṇassa visuṃ parikammaṃ natthīti adhippāyena vuttaṃ. Evañcetaṃ icchitabbaṃ, aññathā yathākammūpagañāṇassa mahaggatabhāvo eva na siyā. Devānaṃ dassanepi eseva nayo. Nerayikadevaggahaṇaṃ cettha nidassanamattaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ākaṅkhamāno hi dibbacakkhulābhī [M 2.0059] aññagatikesupi evaṃ paṭipajjatiyeva. Tathā hi vakkhati “apāyaggahaṇena tiracchānayoniṃ dīpetī”ti (visuddhi. 2.411), “sugatiggahaṇena manussagatipi saṅgayhatī”ti (visuddhi. 2.411) ca. Taṃ nirayasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ ārammaṇaṃ etassāti taṃkammārammaṇaṃ. Phārusakavanādīsūti ādi-saddena cittalatāvanādīnaṃ saṅgaho.

By this phrase is meant this sentence: 'He understands beings who fare according to their kamma.' Here, 'bhikkhu' means a bhikkhu in this Dispensation; the meaning is one who has gained the knowledge of the divine eye. And that one who has gained the knowledge of the divine eye, having directly seen beings in hell, stands. Thus he attends: desiring to know the hell-leading kamma of those hell-beings, he enters the base jhāna, emerges, and attends by way of preliminary work. 'What indeed?' and so on, shows the method of attention. However, having thus performed the preliminary work, for one who has entered the base jhāna and emerged, adverting arises taking that kamma as object; when that has ceased, four or five impulsions run—all this is according to the stated method. 'There is no separate preliminary work'—this is said with the intention that without the knowledge of the divine eye, there is no separate preliminary work for the knowledge of beings who fare according to their kamma. And this should be accepted thus; otherwise, the exalted nature of the knowledge of beings who fare according to their kamma would not exist at all. The same method applies to seeing devas. Here, the mentioning of hell-beings and devas should be seen as a mere illustration. For one who has obtained the divine eye, if he wishes, proceeds in this same way even regarding those gone to other destinations. For so it will be said: 'By the mentioning of the lower realms, the animal womb is indicated' (Visuddhimagga 2.411), and 'by the mentioning of the happy destinies, the human destination is also included' (Visuddhimagga 2.411). That hell-leading kamma is the object for this; thus, it has that kamma as its object. In 'in the Phārusaka Forest, etc.', the word 'etc.' includes the Cittalatā Grove and others.

Yathā cimassāti yathā ca imassa yathākammūpagañāṇassa visuṃ parikammaṃ natthi, evaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇassapīti visuṃ parikammābhāvaṃ nidasseti. Tattha kāraṇamāha “dibbacakkhupādakāneva hi imānī”ti. Tatrāyamadhippāyo – yathā dibbacakkhulābhī nirayādiabhimukhaṃ ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā, nerayikādike satte disvā tehi pubbe āyūhitaṃ nirayasaṃvattaniyādikaṃ kammaṃ tādisena samādānena, tajjena ca manasikārena parikkhate citte yāthāvato jānāti, evaṃ yassa yassa sattassa samanantarā anāgataṃ attabhāvaṃ ñātukāmo taṃ taṃ odissa ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā tena tena atīte, etarahi vā āyūhitaṃ tassa nibbattakaṃ kammaṃ yathākammūpagañāṇena disvā tena nibbattetabbaṃ anāgataṃ attabhāvaṃ ñātukāmo tādisena samādānena, tajjena ca manasikārena parikkhate citte yāthāvato jānāti. Eseva nayo tato paresupi [V 2.0056] attabhāvesu. Etaṃ anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ nāma. Yasmā etaṃ dvayaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇe satiyeva sijjhati, nāsati. Tena vuttaṃ “imāni dibbacakkhunā saheva ijjhantī”ti.

Just as for this knowledge of beings faring according to their kamma there is no separate preparatory work, so too for the knowledge of the future; thus, this indicates the absence of separate preparatory work. Therein, the reason is stated: 'For these have the divine eye as their basis.' Therein, this is the meaning: Just as one who has obtained the divine eye, having expanded the light towards hell and so on, sees beings such as those in hell, and then, with such concentration and with attention appropriate thereto, in a mind that has been prepared, truly knows the kamma leading to hell and so on that was previously accumulated by them; so too, one who desires to know the immediately succeeding future existence of any particular being, having focused on that very being and expanded the light, and having seen with the knowledge of beings faring according to their kamma the kamma accumulated by that being in the past or in the present that will produce that existence, and desiring to know the future existence to be produced by that kamma, truly knows it with such concentration and with attention appropriate thereto, in a mind that has been prepared. This is the same method for other existences beyond that one as well. This is called the knowledge of the future. Because this pair is accomplished only when the knowledge of the divine eye is present, and not when it is absent. Therefore it is said: 'These are accomplished only together with the divine eye.'

Kāyena duṭṭhu caritaṃ, kāyato vā uppannaṃ kilesapūtikattā duṭṭhaṃ caritaṃ kāyaduccaritanti evaṃ yojetabbo. Kāyoti cettha copanakāyo adhippeto. Kāyaviññattivasena pavattaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ kāyaduccaritanti. Itaresūti vacīmanoduccaritesu. Yasmiṃ santāne kammaṃ katūpacitaṃ, asatissa antarupacchede vipākārahabhāvassa avigacchanato so tena sahitoyevāti vattabboti āha “samannāgatāti samaṅgībhūtā”ti. “Anatthakāmā hutvā”ti etena mātāpitaro viya puttānaṃ, ācariyupajjhāyā viya ca nissitakānaṃ atthakāmā hutvā garahakā upavādakā na hontīti dasseti. Guṇaparidhaṃsanenāti vijjamānānaṃ guṇānaṃ viddhaṃsanena, vināsanenāti attho. Nanu ca [M 2.0060] antimavatthunāpi upavādo guṇaparidhaṃsanamevāti? Saccametaṃ. Guṇāti panettha jhānādivisesā uttarimanussadhammā adhippetāti sīlaparidhaṃsanaṃ visuṃ gahitaṃ. Tenāha “natthi imesaṃ samaṇadhammo”tiādi. Samaṇadhammoti ca sīlasaṃyamaṃ sandhāya vadati. Jānaṃ vāti yaṃ upavadati, tassa ariyabhāvaṃ jānanto vā. Ajānaṃ vāti ajānanto vā. Jānanaṃ ajānanaṃ cettha appamāṇaṃ, ariyabhāvo eva pamāṇaṃ. Tenāha “ubhayathāpi ariyūpavādova hotī”ti. “Ariyo”ti pana ajānato aduṭṭhacittasseva tattha ariyaguṇābhāvaṃ pavedentassa guṇaparidhaṃsanaṃ na hotīti tassa ariyūpavādo natthīti vadanti. Satekicchaṃ pana hoti khamāpanena, na anantariyaṃ viya atekicchaṃ.

Conduct that is corrupt through the body, or corrupt conduct arisen from the body due to the putrid nature of defilements, is bodily misconduct—thus it should be construed. Here, 'body' refers to the composite body. Unwholesome bodily action, occurring as bodily expression, is bodily misconduct. As for the others—in verbal and mental misconducts. In whichever continuum kamma has been done and accumulated, because the state of being fit to give its result does not depart even when there is no interim cessation or final destruction of that continuum, it should be said that that continuum is indeed together with that kamma. Therefore, he said, 'endowed with' means 'possessed of'. By the phrase 'not desiring their welfare,' it is shown that, like parents for their children, or teachers and preceptors for their dependents, those who censure while desiring their welfare are not accusers. 'By destroying virtues' means by destroying or annihilating existing virtues. But isn’t criticism by the final object also a destruction of virtues? Indeed, it is so. Here, however, 'virtues' are intended to be superior human states, special qualities such as jhāna; therefore, the destruction of morality is taken separately. Hence, it is said, 'They have no ascetic practice,' etc. 'Ascetic practice' here refers to moral restraint. Whether knowing the noble state of the one whom one criticizes, or not knowing—here, knowing or not knowing is not the measure; the state of being a noble one alone is the measure. Therefore, it is said, 'In either case, it is criticism of a noble one.' However, they say that for one who does not know he is a noble one and speaks without a corrupt mind, merely declaring the absence of a noble one's qualities in that person, there is no destruction of virtues; thus, for that person, there is no accusation of a noble one. However, it is remediable by asking for forgiveness, not irremediable like an action with immediate consequence.

Rujjhatīti tudati, dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ uppādetīti attho. Tanti taṃ theraṃ, taṃ vā kiriyaṃ. Jānanto eva thero “atthi te, āvuso, patiṭṭhā”ti pucchi. Itaropi saccābhisamayo sāsane patiṭṭhāti āha “sotāpanno aha”nti. Thero taṃ karuṇāyamāno “khīṇāsavo tayā upavadito”ti attānaṃ āvikāsi.

`Rujjhati` means it pricks; it produces a painful feeling—this is the meaning. `Tanti` refers to that elder or that action. Knowing just this, the elder asked, “Friend, do you have a support?” The other, thinking, “The comprehension of the truths is the support in the Teaching,” said, “I am a stream-enterer.” The elder, feeling compassion for him, revealed himself, saying, “One whose taints are destroyed has been reproached by you.”

Sace navakatarā honti tasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū. Sammukhā akhamāpentepīti purato khamāpane asambhavantepi. “Akhamante”ti vā pāṭho. Taṃ sotāpannassa vasena veditabbaṃ.

If the monks in that monastery are very junior. `Sammukhā akhamāpentepi` means even when causing one to ask for forgiveness in person is not possible. Or, `akhamante` is the reading. That should be understood with reference to a stream-enterer.

Parinibbutamañcaṭṭhānanti pūjākaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ sandhāyāha.

`Parinibbutamañcaṭṭhānaṃ` is said with reference to a place for making offerings.

Samādātabbaṭṭhena [V 2.0057] samādānāni, kammāni samādānāni yesaṃ, te kammasamādānā, micchādiṭṭhivasena kammasamādānā, hetuatthaṃ vā antogadhaṃ katvā micchādiṭṭhivasena pare kammesu samādāpakā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Tayimamatthaṃ dassento “micchādiṭṭhivasenā”tiādimāha. Sīlasampannotiādi paripakkindriyassa maggasamaṅgino vasena vuttaṃ. Aggamaggaṭṭhe pana vattabbameva natthi. Aññanti arahattaṃ. Evaṃsampadanti yathā taṃ avassambhāvī, evamidampīti attho. Taṃ vācaṃ appahāyātiādīsu ariyūpavādaṃ sandhāya “puna evarūpiṃ vācaṃ na vakkhāmī”ti vadanto vācaṃ pajahati nāma, “puna evarūpaṃ cittaṃ na uppādessāmī”ti cintento cittaṃ pajahati nāma, “puna evarūpiṃ diṭṭhiṃ na gaṇhissāmī”ti pajahanto diṭṭhiṃ pajahati nāma, tathā akaronto neva pajahati, na paṭinissajjati. Yathābhataṃ [M 2.0061] nikkhitto, evaṃ nirayeti yathā nirayapālehi āharitvā niraye ṭhapito, evaṃ niraye ṭhapitoyevāti attho. Micchādiṭṭhivasena akattabbaṃ nāma pāpaṃ natthi, yato saṃsārakhāṇubhāvopi nāma hotīti āha “micchādiṭṭhiparamāni, bhikkhave, vajjānī”ti.

By the meaning of 'to be undertaken,' they are called undertakings. Those for whom actions are undertakings are 'those of action-undertakings.' Those who undertake actions by means of wrong view are `kammasamādānā`; or, having internalized the causative meaning, those who induce others to undertake actions by means of wrong view are `micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā`. To show this meaning, he said, “by means of wrong view,” and so on. “Endowed with virtue,” and so on, was said with reference to one whose faculties are mature, one endowed with the path. However, for one standing in the highest path, there is nothing further to be said. “Another” means Arahantship. “Thus accomplished” means: just as that is inevitable, so too is this; such is the meaning. In “not abandoning that speech,” and so on, with reference to slandering noble ones: one who says, “I will not speak such speech again,” is called one who abandons speech; one who thinks, “I will not produce such a thought again,” is called one who abandons thought; one who abandons, thinking, “I will not take up such a view again,” is called one who abandons the view. One who does not act in this way neither abandons nor relinquishes. “As if brought and placed, so in hell” means: just as one is brought by the wardens of hell and placed in hell, so one is indeed placed in hell; such is the meaning. By means of wrong view, there is no evil that would not be done, because of which one can even become like a stump in saṃsāra. Thus he said, “Wrong views are the highest faults, O monks.”

“Ucchinnabhavanettiko, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa kāyo tiṭṭhati, ayañceva kāyo, bahiddhā ca nāmarūpa”nti (dī. ni. 1.147) evamādīsu viya idha kāya-saddo khandhapañcakavisayoti āha “kāyassa bhedāti upādinnakkhandhapariccāgā”ti. Avītarāgassa maraṇato paraṃ nāma bhavantarūpādānamevāti āha “paraṃ maraṇāti tadanantaraṃ abhinibbattikkhandhaggahaṇe”ti. Yena tiṭṭhati, tassa upacchedeneva kāyo bhijjatīti āha “kāyassa bhedāti jīvitindriyassa upacchedā”ti.

“With the craving for existence cut off, O monks, the Tathāgata’s body remains; and this very body, and name-and-form externally” (Dī. Ni. 1.147)—as in such passages, the word ‘body’ here has the five aggregates as its domain. Thus he said: “'Breakup of the body' means the abandoning of the appropriated aggregates.” For one not free from passion, what is called ‘after death’ is simply the grasping of another existence. Thus he said: “'After death' means the grasping of newly produced aggregates immediately thereafter.” The body breaks up only by the cutting off of that by which it remains. Thus he said: “'Breakup of the body' means the cutting off of the life faculty.”

Eti imasmā sukhanti ayo, puññanti āha “puññasammatā ayā”ti. Ayanti etasmā sukhānīti āyo, puññakammādisukhasādhanaṃ. Tenāha “sukhānaṃ vā āyassa abhāvā”ti. Iyati assādiyatīti ayo, assādoti āha “assādasaññito ayo”ti.

`Eti imasmā sukhaṃ` (Happiness comes from this), hence `ayo`. It is merit; thus, he said, '`ayo` is considered merit.' `Ayanti etasmā sukhāni` (Happinesses come from this), hence `āyo`; it is the means for accomplishing happiness, such as meritorious kamma. Therefore, he said, 'or because of the absence of the source of happinesses.' `Iyati assādiyati` (It is enjoyed), hence `ayo`. It is enjoyment; thus, he said, '`ayo` is designated as enjoyment.'

Nāgarājādīnanti ādi-saddena supaṇṇādīnaṃ saṅgaho. Asurasadisanti petāsurasadisaṃ. Soti asurakāyo. Sabbasamussayehīti sabbehi sampattisamussayehi. Vuttavipariyāyenāti “suṭṭhu caritaṃ, sobhanaṃ vā caritaṃ anavajjattā”tiādinā “kāyaduccaritenā”tiādīnaṃ padānaṃ vuttassa atthassa vipariyāyena.

In `Nāgarājādīnaṃ`, by the word `ādi`, the inclusion of Supaṇṇas and others is to be understood. `Asurasadisaṃ` means similar to the Peta-asuras. `So` refers to the realm of the Asura-group. `Sabbasamussayehi` means with all collections of accomplishments. `Vuttavipariyāyena` means by way of the opposite of the meaning explained for terms such as `kāyaduccaritena`, through explanations such as, 'well-practiced,' or 'excellent conduct because of being blameless.'

Nigamanavacanaṃ [V 2.0058] vuttassevatthassa puna vacananti katvā. Ayamettha saṅkhepatthoti “dibbena cakkhunā…pe… passatī”ti ettha ayaṃ yathāvutto saṅkhepattho.

It is a concluding statement because it is a restatement of the very meaning that has been stated. As for `Ayamettha saṅkhepattho`: Herein, in the text 'with the divine eye... he sees,' this, as stated, is the brief meaning.

412. Kasiṇārammaṇanti aṭṭhannampi kasiṇānaṃ vasena kasiṇārammaṇaṃ. Sabbākārenāti “cuddasavidhena cittaparidamanena aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgamena bhūmipādapadamūlasampādanenā”ti iminā sabbappakārena. Abhinīhārakkhamaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇābhimukhaṃ pesanārahaṃ pesanayoggaṃ katvā. Āsannaṃ kātabbanti dibbacakkhuñāṇuppattiyā samīpabhūtaṃ kātabbaṃ. Tattha upacārajjhānaṃ paguṇataraṃ katvā ārammaṇañca vaḍḍhetabbaṃ. Tenāha “upacārajjhānagocaraṃ katvā [M 2.0062] vaḍḍhetvā ṭhapetabba”nti. Tatthāti tasmiṃ vaḍḍhite kasiṇārammaṇe. Appanāti jhānavasena appanā. Na hi akataparikammassa abhiññāvasena appanā ijjhati. Tenāha “pādakajjhānanissayaṃ hotī”ti, pādakajjhānārammaṇaṃ hotīti attho. Na parikammanissayanti parikammassa taṃ kasiṇārammaṇaṃ apassayo na hoti. Tathā sati rūpadassanaṃ na siyā. Imesūti yathāvuttesu tejokasiṇādīsu tīsu kasiṇesu. Uppādetvāti upacārajjhānuppādanena uppādetvā. Upacārajjhānapavattiyā hi saddhiṃ paṭibhāganimittuppatti. Tatthāti kasiṇaniddese.

412. Having the kasiṇa as its object: This means having the kasiṇa as its object by way of all eight kasiṇas. In every way: 'Through the fourteenfold taming of the mind, the eightfold attainment, and the fulfillment of the base, foot, and root'—in every possible manner. Having made it capable of being directed forward, oriented toward the knowledge of the divine eye, worthy of being sent forth, and suitable for being sent forth. It should be made near: It should be made proximate to the arising of the knowledge of the divine eye. Therein, the access concentration should be made more proficient, and the object should also be expanded. For that reason, it is said: 'Having made it the domain of access concentration, it should be expanded and established.' Therein: In that expanded kasiṇa-object. Absorption: Absorption is by way of jhāna. For indeed, for one who has not done the preliminary work, absorption by way of direct knowledge does not succeed. For that reason, it is said, 'It is dependent on the foundational jhāna'; the meaning is, it has the foundational jhāna as its object. Not dependent on the preliminary work: That kasiṇa-object is not a support for the preliminary work. That being so, the seeing of forms would not occur. Among these: Among the three aforementioned kasiṇas, beginning with the fire kasiṇa. Having produced: Having produced by means of the arising of access concentration. For the arising of the counterpart sign occurs together with the occurrence of the access concentration. Therein: In the exposition of the kasiṇa.

Antoyeva rūpagataṃ passitabbaṃ na bahiddhā vikkhepāpattihetubhāvato. Parikammassa vāro atikkamatīti idha parikammaṃ nāma yathāvuttakasiṇārammaṇaṃ upacārajjhānaṃ, taṃ rūpagataṃ passato na pavattati. Kasiṇālokavasena ca rūpagatadassanaṃ, kasiṇāloko ca parikammavasenāti tadubhayampi parikammassa appavattiyā na hoti. Tenāha “tato āloko antaradhāyati, tasmiṃ antarahite rūpagatampi na dissatī”ti. Rūpagataṃ passato parikammassa vāro atikkamati, parikammamatikkantassa kasiṇārammaṇaṃ ñāṇaṃ na hotīti rūpagataṃ na dissati, kathaṃ pana paṭipajjitabbanti āha “athānenā”tiādi. Evaṃ anukkamenāti punappunaṃ pādakajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā tato tato vuṭṭhāya abhiṇhaṃ ālokassa pharaṇavasena āloko thāmagato hoti ciraṭṭhāyī. Tathā ca sati tattha sucirampi rūpagataṃ passateva. Tena vuttaṃ “ettha āloko…pe… hotī”ti.

The collection of forms should be seen only within, not externally, because it is a cause for the occurrence of distraction. As to the phrase, 'The turn for the preliminary work is surpassed': here, 'preliminary work' is the access concentration which has the aforesaid kasiṇa as its object. For one who sees the collection of forms, it does not proceed. And the seeing of the collection of forms is by means of the kasiṇa-light, and the kasiṇa-light is by means of the preliminary work; thus, due to the non-occurrence of the preliminary work, both of them do not occur. Therefore, he said, 'Then the light disappears; when it has disappeared, the collection of forms is also not seen.' For one who sees the collection of forms, the turn for the preliminary work passes away. For one who has surpassed the preliminary work, there is no knowledge with the kasiṇa as its object, therefore the collection of forms is not seen. But how should one practice? To this, he said, 'Then by this means,' and so on. 'Thus, in sequence' means: by repeatedly attaining the foundational jhāna and emerging from it again and again, through the constant diffusion of the light, the light becomes powerful and long-lasting. And when that is so, one certainly sees the collection of forms there even for a very long time. Therefore, it was said, 'Here the light... becomes.'

Svāyamattho tiṇukkūpamāya vibhāvetabboti dassento āha “rattiṃ tiṇukkāyā”tiādi. Tattha punappunaṃ pavesananti punappunaṃ pādakajjhānasamāpajjanaṃ. Thāmagatālokassa [V 2.0059] yathāparicchedena ṭhānanti yattakaṃ ṭhānaṃ paricchinditvā kasiṇaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ, thāmagatassa ālokassa tattakaṃ pharitvā avaṭṭhānaṃ.

Showing that this meaning should be illustrated by the simile of the grass torch, he said, 'At night with a grass torch,' and so on. There, 'repeated entry' is the repeated attainment of the foundational jhāna. 'The standing of the powerful light according to the delimitation' means: whatever extent of space was delimited and the kasiṇa expanded, it is the pervading and standing of the powerful light over that same extent.

Anāpāthagatanti āpāthagamanayogyassa vasena vuttaṃ. Antokucchigatādi pana tadabhāvato tena visesitabbameva. Tadevāti dibbacakkhumeva[M 2.0063]. Etthāti etesu rūpamārabbha pavattacittesu. Rūpadassanasamatthanti rūpaṃ sabhāvato vibhāvanasamatthaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ viya. Pubbabhāgacittānīti āvajjanaparikammasaṅkhātāni pubbabhāgacittāni. Tāni hi ārammaṇaṃ karontānipi na yāthāvato taṃ vibhāvetvā pavattanti āvajjanasampaṭicchanacittāni viya.

Not come into range: This is stated in terms of what is suitable for coming into range. But what is within the womb, etc., should indeed be specified by this term on account of its not coming into range. That very thing: The divine eye itself. Here: In these mind-moments occurring in dependence on form. Capable of seeing forms: Capable of making form clear by its own nature, like eye-consciousness. Preliminary mind-moments: The preliminary mind-moments called adverting and preparation. For even while taking an object, they do not proceed having discerned it as it actually is, like the adverting and receiving consciousnesses.

Taṃ panetaṃ dibbacakkhu. Paripanthoti antarāyiko. Jhānavibbhantakoti jhānummattako jhānabhāvanāmukhena ummādappatto. Appamattena bhavitabbanti “dibbacakkhu mayā adhigata”nti santosaṃ anāpajjitvā vipassanānuyogavasena vā saccābhisamayavasena vā appamattena bhavitabbaṃ.

But this is that divine eye. 'Obstruction' means an obstacle. 'Deranged from jhāna' means one who is mad through jhāna, one who has reached madness by way of jhāna cultivation. 'One must be heedful' means: one should be heedful by way of devotion to insight or by way of the realization of the truths, without falling into contentment with the thought, 'The divine eye has been attained by me.'

“Evaṃ passitukāmenā”tiādinā dibbacakkhussa nānāvajjanaparikammañceva dibbacakkhuñāṇañca dassitaṃ, na tassa uppattikkamoti taṃ dassetuṃ “tatrāya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Taṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā suviññeyyameva.

By the passage beginning, 'Thus by one who wishes to see,' both the preparation with its various advertings for the divine eye and the knowledge of the divine eye are shown, but not the process of its arising. To show that, the passage beginning, 'Therein, this...' is stated. That is easy to understand because the method has been stated previously.

Cutūpapātañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the discourse on the knowledge of passing away and reappearance is concluded.

Pakiṇṇakakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Miscellaneous Discourses

413. Itīti evaṃ vuttappakārenāti attho. Tena “so evaṃ samāhite citte”tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.244-245; ma. ni. 1.384, 431-433; pārā. 12-14) yathādassitapāḷigatiṃ, tassā atthavivaraṇanayañca paccāmasati. Saccesu viya ariyasaccāni khandhesu upādānakkhandhā antogadhā. Tadubhaye ca sabhāvato, samudayato, atthaṅgamato, assādato, ādīnavato, nissaraṇato ca yathābhūtaṃ sayambhuñāṇena avedi aññāsi [V 2.0060] paṭivijjhi pavedesi vāti sātisayena pañcakkhandhāvabodhena bhagavāva thometabboti āha “pañcakkhandhavidū”ti. Ñatvā viññeyyāti sambandho. Tāsūti pañcasu abhiññāsu. Taggahaṇeneva ca paribhaṇḍañāṇānaṃ gahitattā “pañcā”ti vuttaṃ. Tenāha “etāsu hī”tiādi.

413. The word iti means 'in the manner thus described.' By this, with the phrase 'when his mind is thus concentrated,' and so on (Dī. Ni. 1.244–245; Ma. Ni. 1.384, 431–433; Pārā. 12–14), one considers the course of the Pāḷi as shown and its method of explaining the meaning. Just as the Noble Truths are included among truths, so too the aggregates of clinging are included within the aggregates. And he knew, understood, penetrated, and taught both of these according to reality with self-originated knowledge in terms of their nature, origin, cessation, gratification, danger, and escape. Therefore, because of his pre-eminent comprehension of the five aggregates, the Blessed One alone is to be praised; thus, it is said, 'knower of the five aggregates.' The connection is: 'having known, they are to be understood.' Tāsu means 'in the five direct knowledges.' And because the auxiliary knowledges are included by the very taking up of those, 'five' is stated. Therefore, it is said: 'for in these,' and so on.

Tattha paribhaṇḍañāṇānīti parivārañāṇāni. Yathā hi sinerussa parivāraṭṭhānāni yāni taṃsiddhiyā siddhāni mekhalaṭṭhānāni paribhaṇḍānīti vuccanti, evaṃ imānipi dibbacakkhusiddhiyā siddhāni tassa paribhaṇḍānīti vuttāni. Idhāgatānīti ettha idhāti yathādassitāni suttapadāni sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tato [M 2.0064] aññesu pana sāmaññaphalādīsu manomayañāṇampi visuṃ abhiññāñāṇabhāvena āgataṃ.

Herein, paribhaṇḍañāṇāni means attendant knowledges. For just as the attendant regions of Sineru—those terrace-regions that are established by its own establishment—are called its 'attendant gear' (paribhaṇḍāni), so too these knowledges, established by the establishment of the divine eye, are called its 'attendant gear'. Herein, in the phrase idhāgatāni, the word idha is stated with reference to the sutta passages as shown. But in other texts apart from these, such as in the Sāmaññaphala Sutta and so on, the knowledge of the mind-made body also comes separately as a direct knowledge.

“Tesū”ti idaṃ paccāmasanaṃ kiṃ tikānaṃ, udāhu ārammaṇānanti? Kiñcettha yadi tikānaṃ, tadayuttaṃ. Na hi tikesu abhiññāñāṇāni pavattanti. Atha ārammaṇānaṃ, tampi ayuttaṃ. Na hi aññaṃ uddisitvā aññassa paccāmasanaṃ yuttanti. Yathā icchati, tathā bhavatu tāva tikānaṃ, nanu vuttaṃ “na hi tikesu abhiññāñāṇāni pavattantī”ti? Nāyaṃ virodho tikavohārena ārammaṇānaṃyeva gayhamānattā. Atha vā pana hotu ārammaṇānaṃ, nanu vuttaṃ “na hi aññaṃ uddisitvā aññassa paccāmasanaṃ yutta”nti? Ayampi na doso yathāvuttakāraṇenevāti.

Is this referring back by 'Among these' to the triads, or to the objects? If it is to the triads, that is unsuitable, for supernormal knowledges do not occur in the triads. If it is to the objects, that too is unsuitable, for it is not proper to refer back to one thing after having pointed out another. Let it be as one wishes. For now, let it be of the triads. But was it not said, 'supernormal knowledges do not occur in the triads'? This is not a contradiction, because by the designation 'triads', only the objects are being taken. Or alternatively, let it be of the objects. But was it not said, 'it is not proper to refer back to one thing after having pointed out another'? This too is not a fault, for the very reason already stated.

414. Asatipi vatthubhede bhūmikālasantānabhedavasena bhinnesu sattasu ārammaṇesu. Tikavasena hesa bhedo gahito. Iddhividhañāṇassa maggārammaṇatāya abhāvato idha maggārammaṇatiko na labbhati. Tanti iddhividhañāṇaṃ. Kāyaṃ cittasannissitaṃ katvātiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Upayogaladdhanti laddhaupayogavacanaṃ. Dutiyāvibhattivasena vuttaṃ “kāyaṃ pariṇāmetī”ti. Tenāha “rūpakāyārammaṇato”ti, rūpakāyassa vaṇṇārammaṇatoti attho.

414. Even if there is no difference in the substance, this concerns the seven objects that are different by way of distinctions of plane, time, and continuity. Indeed, this difference is taken by way of triads. Because the knowledge of psychic power does not have the path as its object, the person with the path as object is not obtained here. That refers to the knowledge of psychic power. Whatever is to be said regarding such phrases as 'having made the body dependent on the mind' has already been said below. The word 'upayogaladdham' is a term meaning 'obtained application'. It is said by way of the second case ending, 'he transforms the body' (kāyaṃ pariṇāmeti). Therefore, he said, 'because the material body is its object' (rūpakāyārammaṇato); the meaning is, because its object is the color of the material body.

Tadeva cittanti yadeva kāyavasena cittapariṇāmane vuttaṃ pādakajjhānacittaṃ, tadeva. Rāmagāme cetiyaṃ ṭhapetvā sesesu sattasu cetiyesu dhātuyo iddhiyā āharitvā rājagahe bhūmigharamaṇḍape kataṃ mahādhātunidhānaṃ. “Ime gandhā”tiādinā paccuppanne gandhādike gahetvāpi asussanādivisesayuttaṃ [V 2.0061] anāgatameva nesaṃ rūpaṃ adhiṭṭhānacittassa ārammaṇaṃ hoti anāgatādhiṭṭhānattā. Vattaniyasenāsanaṃ nāma viñjhāṭaviyaṃ vihāro. Dadhirasanti dadhimaṇḍo, taṃ adhiṭṭhahantassa anāgataṃ dadhivaṇṇaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hoti. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ hoti paccuppannassa rūpakāyassa ārammaṇakaraṇato.

The term `tadeva cittaṃ` refers to that very foundational jhāna-mind which was spoken of in the context of inclining the mind by means of the body. Having left the cetiya in the village of Rāma, and having brought the relics by psychic power from the remaining seven cetiyas, the great enshrinement of relics was made in the underground chamber shaped like a pavilion in Rājagaha. Even having taken present things such as scents with the phrase 'These scents,' etc., their future form, which is endowed with special qualities such as not drying up, becomes the object of the mind of determination, because of the determination of the future. What is called the Vattaniya residence is a monastery in the Viñjhā forest. The term `dadhirasaṃ` means the clear liquid of curd (whey); for him who determines it, the future color of the curd becomes the object. It has a present object because of making the present physical body the object.

Sakāyacittānanti attano kāyassa, cittassa ca.

The term `sakāyacittānaṃ` means: of one's own body and mind.

415. Saddo ca paritto sabbassa rūpassa kāmāvacarabhāvato. Vijjamānamevāti vattamānaṃyeva.

415. Sound is also of the sense-sphere because all form is of the sense-sphere. The term `vijjamānameva` means: only what is presently occurring.

416. Sotāpannassa [M 2.0065] cittanti sotāpannassa āveṇikaṃ cittaṃ. Sakadāgāmissātiādīsupi eseva nayo. Yāva arahato netabbanti “sakadāgāmī anāgāmino cittaṃ na jānāti, anāgāmī arahato”ti evaṃ netabbaṃ. Sabbesanti sabbesaṃ ariyānaṃ jānāti, ko pana vādo anariyānaṃ. Aññopi ca uparimo anāgāmiādi heṭṭhimassa sakadāgāmiādikassa cittaṃ jānātīti sambandho.

416. The term `sotāpannassa cittaṃ` means the unique mind of a stream-enterer, that is, the path-mind and fruition-mind. In the phrases beginning with `sakadāgāmissa` also, this is the same method. The phrase `yāva arahato netabbaṃ` means it should be construed thus: 'A once-returner does not know the mind of a non-returner; a non-returner does not know the mind of an Arahant.' The term `sabbesaṃ` means: he knows the minds of all noble ones; what then is to be said about knowing the minds of non-noble ones? And also, a higher one, such as a non-returner and so forth, knows the mind of a lower one, such as a once-returner and so forth—thus is the connection.

Atītassa, anāgatassa ca parassa cittassa jānanaṃ sambhavati, paccuppannassa pana na sambhavatīti adhippāyena pucchati “kathaṃ paccuppannaṃ ārammaṇaṃ hotī”ti. Itaro yattha sambhavati, taṃdassanatthaṃ paccuppannaṃ tāva vibhajitvā dassento “paccuppannaṃ nāma tividha”ntiādimāha. Tattha uppādaṭṭhitibhaṅgappattanti uppādaṃ, ṭhitiṃ, bhaṅgañca pattaṃ, khaṇattayapariyāpannanti attho. Etthantare ekadvesantativārā veditabbāti etthantare pavattā rūpasantativārā ekadvesantativārā nāmāti veditabbāti attho. Ālokaṭṭhānato ovarakaṃ paviṭṭhassa pageva tattha nisinnassa viya yāva rūpagataṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti. Tattha upaḍḍhavelā avibhūtavārā, upaḍḍhavelā vibhūtavārā, tadubhayaṃ gahetvā “dve santativārā”ti vuttaṃ. Tayidaṃ na sabbasādhāraṇaṃ, ekaccassa sīghampi pākaṭaṃ hotīti “ekadvesantativārā”ti ekaggahaṇampi kataṃ, atiparittasabhāvautuādisamuṭṭhānā vā ekadvesantativārā veditabbā.

Knowing the past and future mind of another is possible, but knowing the present mind is not possible. With this intention, he asks, 'How does the present become an object?' The other (the commentator), in order to show that present wherein knowing is possible, first analyzes the present and, while showing it, states what begins with, 'The present, by name, is threefold.' Therein, 'having reached arising, presence, and dissolution' means having reached arising, presence, and dissolution; the meaning is that it is included in the triad of moments. The phrase 'one or two series of continuity are to be known within this interval' means that the series of material continuity that have occurred within this interval are to be known as 'one or two series of continuity.' For one who has entered a chamber from a place of light, just as for one who was already sitting there before, to that extent the group of material phenomena becomes manifest. Therein, half the time is mostly unmanifest, and half the time is mostly manifest. Taking both of these, it is said, 'two series of continuity.' This becoming manifest is not common to all; for a certain person, it becomes manifest even quickly. Therefore, in the phrase 'one or two series of continuity,' the inclusion of 'one' is also made. Alternatively, material phenomena arisen from extremely brief, similar temperature, etc., are to be known as one or two series of continuity.

Tīre akkantaudakalekhā nāma kālussiyaṃ gatā tīrasamīpe udakarāji. Yāva na vippasīdatīti [V 2.0062] kālussiyavigamena yāva vippasannā na hoti. Keci pana “atinte tīre allapādena akkante yāva pāde udakalekhā na vippasīdati, na saṃsīdati, na vūpasammatī”ti evamettha atthaṃ vadanti. Te panete kiriyābhedena vuttā kālavisesā, na aññamaññaṃ samasamā, ūnādhikabhāgavantova daṭṭhabbā. Dve tayo javanavārā kāmāvacarajavanavasena veditabbā, na itarajavanavasena. Na hi te parimitakālā, anantarā pavattabhavaṅgādayopi tadantogadhāva daṭṭhabbā. Tadubhayanti rūpārūpasantatidvayaṃ.

On the shore, the 'water-line made by treading' is a line of water near the shore that has become turbid. The phrase 'as long as it does not become clear' means: as long as it has not become clear through the departure of turbidity. Some teachers, however, state the meaning here thus: 'When a dry shore is trodden upon with a wet foot, as long as the water-line on the foot or in the footprint does not become clear, does not subside, and does not cease.' Furthermore, these specific periods of time are stated with a distinction in action; they are not mutually equal but are to be seen as having lesser and greater parts. Two or three series of impulsion are to be known by way of sense-sphere impulsion, not by way of other impulsions. For indeed, those others are not of a limited duration. Even the life-continuum, etc., that occur immediately after are to be seen as included within that. The term 'both of those' refers to the pair of continuities: the continuity of materiality and the continuity of mentality.

Ekabhavaparicchinnanti paṭisandhicutiparicchinnaṃ. Ekabhavapariyāpannaṃ dhammajātaṃ etarahīti vattabbaṃ addhāpaccuppannaṃ nāma. Manoti sasampayuttaṃ viññāṇamāha. Dhammāti ārammaṇadhammā. Manoti vā manāyatanaṃ. Dhammāti vedanādayo [M 2.0066] arūpakkhandhā. Ubhayametaṃ paccuppannanti addhāpaccuppannaṃ hontaṃ etaṃ ubhayaṃ hotīti attho. Viññāṇanti nikantiviññāṇaṃ. Tañhi tasmiṃ paccuppanne chandarāgavasena paṭibaddhaṃ hoti. Abhinandatīti taṇhādiṭṭhābhinandanāhi abhinandati. Tathābhūto ca vatthupariññāya abhāvato tesu paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati taṇhādiṭṭhīhi ākaḍḍhīyati. Ettha ca dvādasāyatanānaṃ “etaṃ paccuppanna”nti (ma. ni. 3.284) āgatattā tattha pavatto chandarāgo addhāpaccuppannārammaṇo, na khaṇapaccuppannārammaṇoti viññāyatīti dassento “yaṃ sandhāya bhaddekarattasutte…pe… saṃhīratīti vutta”nti āha. “Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassatī”ti (ma. ni. 3.272, 285) etthāpi vipassanācittaṃ khaṇapaccuppannaṃ, vipassitabbadhammā addhāpaccuppannāti gahetabbaṃ. Aññathā vipassanāva na sambhaveyya. “Khaṇapaccuppannaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āgata”nti na vuttaṃ tassa vasena ārammaṇakaraṇassa aṭṭhakathāyaṃ anāgatattā.

“Limited to a single existence” means bounded by rebirth-linking and death. The collection of phenomena that pertains to a single existence is to be called the ‘present-in-terms-of-duration.’ “Mind” refers to consciousness along with its associated factors. “Phenomena” refers to object-phenomena. Alternatively, “mind” means the mind-base, and “phenomena” refers to the formless aggregates such as feeling. Both of these, being present, are the present-in-terms-of-duration; this is the meaning. “Consciousness” means consciousness associated with clinging. For it is bound to that present by way of desire and lust. “Delights” means it delights by means of the delight of craving and wrong view. Being thus, due to the non-comprehension of the basis, one is drawn in and dragged by craving and wrong views toward these present phenomena. And here, because it is stated regarding the twelve sense-bases, “This is present,” it is understood that the desire and lust that arise in relation to them have the present-in-terms-of-duration as their object, not the momentary-present. Showing this, he said: “With reference to which it was said in the Bhaddekaratta Sutta… ‘one is drawn in’.” Also, in the verse, “And one who contemplates the present phenomenon, wherever it arises,” it should be understood that the insight-consciousness is the momentary-present, while the phenomena to be contemplated by insight are the present-in-terms-of-duration. Otherwise, insight itself would not be possible. It is not said, “The momentary-present is mentioned in the Pāḷi,” because the taking of an object based on it is not mentioned in the commentary.

Kecīti abhayagirivāsino. Ekakkhaṇe cittaṃ uppajjatīti iddhicittassa uppattisamakālameva paracittassapi uppattisambhavatoti yuttidassanaṃ. Yathā ākāsetiādi sadisūdāharaṇaṃ. Taṃ pana tesaṃ vacanaṃ ayuttaṃ. Kasmā? Maggaphalavīthito aññattha aniṭṭhe ṭhāne āvajjanajavanānaṃ nānārammaṇabhāvappattidosatoti yuttivacanaṃ.

“Some” refers to the Abhayagirivāsins. “Consciousness arises in a single moment”—this is a presentation of reasoning, because the arising of another’s consciousness is possible at the very same time as the arising of the consciousness of psychic power. The phrase beginning with “Just as in space” is a similar example. But that statement of theirs is unfitting. Why? Because, apart from the path and fruition process, in an undesirable situation, there is the fault of the advertence and impulsion moments attaining the state of having different objects. This is the statement of the reason for its unfitness.

Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ cetopariyañāṇaṃ paccuppannārammaṇaṃ hotīti āha “santatipaccuppannaṃ panā”tiādi[V 2.0063]. Addhāpaccuppannaṃ pana javanavārena dīpetabbaṃ, na sakalena paccuppannaddhunāti adhippāyo.

If it is so, how does the knowledge of others’ minds (cetopariyañāṇa) have a present object? To this, he said, “But the continuum-present...” and so on. The present-in-terms-of-duration, however, should be explained by way of the javana-process, not by the entire present duration; this is the intended meaning.

Tatrāyaṃ dīpanātiādi javanavārassa addhāpaccuppannabhāvadīpanamukhena iddhicittassa pavattiākāradīpanaṃ. Itarānīti āvajjanaparikammacittāni. Ettha ca “kecī”ti yadipi abhayagirivāsino adhippetā, te pana cittassa ṭhitikkhaṇaṃ na icchantīti “ṭhitikkhaṇe vā paṭivijjhatī”ti na vattabbaṃ siyā. Tathā ye “iddhimassa ca parassa ca ekakkhaṇe cittaṃ uppajjatī”ti vadanti, tesaṃ “ṭhitikkhaṇe vā bhaṅgakkhaṇe vā paṭivijjhatī”ti vacanaṃ na sameti. Na hi tasmiṃ khaṇadvaye uppajjamānaṃ paracittena saha ekakkhaṇe uppajjati nāmāti. Ṭhitibhaṅgakkhaṇesu ca uppajjamānaṃ ekadesaṃ paccuppannārammaṇaṃ, ekadesaṃ atītārammaṇaṃ āpajjati. Yañca vuttaṃ “parassa cittaṃ jānissāmīti rāsivasena mahājanassa [M 2.0067] citte āvajjite”ti, ettha ca mahājano atthato pare anekapuggalāti “paresaṃ cittaṃ jānissāmī”ti āvajjanappavatti vattabbā siyā. Athāpi parassāti mahājanassāti attho sambhaveyya, tathāpi tassa ekapuggalasseva vā cittarāsiṃ āvajjitvā ekassa paṭivijjhanaṃ ayuttaṃ. Na hi rāsiāvajjanaṃ ekadesāvajjanaṃ hotīti, tasmā tehi “mahājanassa citte āvajjite”tiādi na vattabbaṃ.

Here, the statement beginning “this explanation...” is a description of the mode of occurrence of the mind of psychic power, by way of explaining the state of the javana-process as the present-in-terms-of-duration. “The others” refers to the advertence and preparatory minds. Here, although by “some” the Abhayagirivāsins are intended, they, however, do not accept the duration-moment of the mind; therefore, it would not be proper to say, “or penetrates at the duration-moment.” Similarly, for those who say, “The mind of the one with psychic power and of another person arises in a single moment,” their statement, “penetrates at the duration-moment or at the dissolution-moment,” is not consistent.
