'Endowed with faculties' means possessed of faculties such as the eye and so forth; by this, he shows the arising of the six sense bases. All this was said by way of showing that the holder of a speculative view becomes deluded by making the function of ignorance and so forth, which proceed according to conditions, his own activity. Like the unbreakable gems strung on an uncuttable thread mentioned in the Acchejjasutta, the determination of what occurs before and after is called 'necessity.' Or, by necessity; or, necessity itself is concurrence, a coming together; this is 'concurrence through necessity.' Through that, they are transformed in their states of existence, having attained the state of humans, devas, birds, and so forth; hence they are called 'those transformed by the state of concurrence through necessity.' And they also state the meaning thus: 'Transformed by necessity, by concurrence, and by the intrinsic nature called "existence," they attain various different states; hence they are called "those transformed by the state of concurrence through necessity".'

Etehi ca vikappanehi avijjā akusalaṃ cittaṃ katvā satte puññādīsu saṅkhāresu yattha katthaci pavattetīti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “so avijjāya andhīkato”tiādi. Paṭipajjatīti upasaṅkamati.

And showing this meaning, that by these speculations ignorance makes the mind unwholesome and causes beings to engage in formations of merit and so forth wherever they may be, he said: 'He, blinded by ignorance,' and so forth. 'Engages in' means 'approaches'.

Apariṇāyakoti arahattamaggasampaṭipādakakalyāṇamittarahito, arahattamaggañāṇāvasānaṃ vā ñāṇaṃ samavisamaṃ dassetvā satte nibbānaṃ nayatīti pariṇāyakaṃ, tena rahito apariṇāyako. Dhammaṃ ñatvāti sappurisūpassayena catusaccappakāsakaṃ suttādidhammaṃ ñatvā, maggañāṇeneva vā sabbadhammapavaraṃ nibbānadhammaṃ ñatvā. Taṃjānanāyattaṃ pana sesasaccattayābhisamayaṃ [V 2.0276] samānakālampi taṃ purimakālaṃ viya katvā vuttaṃ. Upasanto carissatīti aggamaggādhigamena sabbaso avijjūpasamā upasanto saupādisesanibbānadhātuyaṃ ṭhito yāva anupādisesanibbānadhātupatti, tāva sattānaṃ hitacariyāya attabhāvaṃ pavattento carissati, diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārehi viharissatīti attho.

'Without a guide' means devoid of a good friend who leads one to properly attain the path of Arahantship; or, a guide is so called because, by showing the even and the uneven, he leads beings to Nibbāna with knowledge that culminates in the knowledge of the Arahantship path; one devoid of that is 'without a guide.' 'Having known the Dhamma' means having known the Dhamma of the suttas and so forth, which explains the Four Truths, through reliance on a good person; or, having known the Dhamma of Nibbāna, which is supreme among all dhammas, only through the knowledge of the path. Furthermore, since the comprehension of the remaining three truths is dependent on knowing that Nibbāna, it is spoken of as if it were a prior event, although it is simultaneous. 'He will live at peace' means: having become pacified through the attainment of the supreme path due to the complete pacification of ignorance, he abides in the Nibbāna-element with residue; until the attainment of the Nibbāna-element without residue, for that long he will fare on, causing his existence to continue for the practice of the welfare of beings. The meaning is that he will abide with blissful abidings in this very life.

Saṅkhārapaccayāviññāṇapadavitthārakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Detailed Exposition of the Phrase 'Consciousness Conditioned by Formations'.

620. Yathāvuttasaṅkhārapaccayā uppajjamānaṃ taṃ kammanibbattameva bhavituṃ arahatīti “bāttiṃsa lokiyavipākaviññāṇāni saṅgahitānī”ti āha. Dhātukathāyaṃ pana vippayuttena saṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadaniddese “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇena ye dhammā, saḷāyatanapaccayā phassena ye dhammā, phassapaccayā vedanāya ye dhammā vippayuttā, te [M 2.0295] dhammā katihi khandhehi…pe… saṅgahitā? Te dhammā asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā ekena khandhena, ekādasahi āyatanehi, ekādasahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā. Katihi asaṅgahitā? Catūhi khandhehi, ekenāyatanena, sattahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā”ti (dhātu. 466) vacanato sabbaviññāṇaphassavedanāpariggaho kato. Yadi hi ettha viññāṇaphassavedanā sappadesā siyuṃ, “vipākā dhammā”ti (dha. sa. tikamātikā 3) imassa viya visajjanaṃ siyā. Tasmā tattha abhidhammabhājanīyavasena saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇādayo gahitāti adhippāyo veditabbo. Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāro ca abhidhammabhājanīye (vibha. 243) catubhūmakakusalasaṅkhāro, akusalasaṅkhāro ca vuttoti eso eva dhātukathāyaṃ gahitoti daṭṭhabbo. Bhavo pana dhātukathāyaṃ kammūpapattibhavavisesadassanatthaṃ na abhidhammabhājanīyavasena gahito, evañca katvā tattha “upādānapaccayā bhavo”ti anuddharitvā “kammabhavo”tiādinā (dhātu. 66) nayena bhavo uddhaṭo.

620. That which arises conditioned by formations as stated is fit to be only kamma-produced. Therefore, it is said, 'thirty-two mundane resultant consciousnesses are included.' However, in the Dhātukathā, in the exposition of terms included and excluded by dissociation, it is stated: 'Those phenomena that are dissociated from consciousness conditioned by formations, from contact conditioned by the six sense bases, and from feeling conditioned by contact—by how many aggregates are these phenomena included? …pe… These phenomena, setting aside the unconditioned from the aggregates, are included by one aggregate, by eleven sense bases, and by eleven elements. By how many are they excluded? They are excluded by four aggregates, by one sense base, and by seven elements.' (Dhātu. 466) By this statement, the comprehension of all consciousness, contact, and feeling is made. Indeed, if consciousness, contact, and feeling were here taken partially, there would be a response like that for 'resultant phenomena.' Therefore, the intention should be understood that in that context, consciousness and the rest conditioned by formations are taken according to the Abhidhamma exposition. And formation conditioned by ignorance, which in the Abhidhamma exposition (Vibhaṅga 243) is stated as the wholesome formation of the four planes and the unwholesome formation, is to be understood as this very one taken in the Dhātukathā. However, existence (bhava) in the Dhātukathā is not taken according to the Abhidhamma exposition, for the purpose of showing the distinction between kamma-existence and rebirth-existence. And for this reason, there, without extracting 'existence conditioned by clinging,' existence is extracted by the method of 'kamma-existence,' etc. (Dhātu. 66).

Lokiyavipākamanoviññāṇameva sandhāyāha “bāvīsatividhaṃ hotī”ti. Chahi viññāṇehīti yathāadhikatehi cakkhuviññāṇādīhi chahi viññāṇehi. Kasmā panettha lokiyavipākaviññāṇasseva gahaṇaṃ katanti āha “lokuttarāni pana vaṭṭakathāya na yujjantī”ti. Yadi evaṃ kasmā dhātukathāyaṃ “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇena ye dhammā vippayuttā”tiādīsu (dhātu. 362) lokuttaravipākānampi gahaṇaṃ katanti? Taṃ yathādhammasāsanattā abhidhammadesanāya vipākattike (dha. sa. tikamātikā 3) viya anavasesavipākadhammasaṅgaṇhanavasena [V 2.0277] vuttaṃ. Suttantadesanā pana yathānulomadesanāti tattha pavattinivattiyo asaṅkarato dassetabbā. Tasmā tadatthasaṃvaṇṇanāti katvā pavattikathāyaṃ lokiyavipākaviññāṇāniyeva gahitāni. Tenevāha “vaṭṭakathāya na yujjantīti na gahitānī”ti.

Referring to mundane resultant mind-consciousness alone, it is said, “it is of twenty-two kinds.” By the six consciousnesses is meant the six consciousnesses, such as eye-consciousness, etc., as they are respectively concerned. But why is only mundane resultant consciousness taken up here? It is said, “Because supramundane ones are not suitable for the discussion of the round of existence.” If so, why in the Dhātukathā, in such passages as, “those phenomena that are dissociated from consciousness conditioned by formations,” etc. (Dhātu. 362), are the supramundane resultants also taken? That was stated by way of comprehending all resultant phenomena without remainder, as in the resultant triad, because the Abhidhamma exposition is a teaching that accords with the phenomena as they are. The Suttanta exposition, however, is a teaching that follows a sequence, and therein occurrence and cessation must be shown without being mixed. Therefore, as an explanation of that meaning, in the discussion of occurrence, only mundane resultant consciousnesses are taken up. For that very reason, it is said: “Because they are not suitable for the discussion of the round of existence, they are not taken.”

Yathā kataṃ kammaṃ phaladāne samatthaṃ hoti, tathā kataṃ “upacita”nti vuccatīti vipākadānayogyameva saṅkhāraṃ gaṇhanto “upacitakammābhāve”ti āha. Hetu nāma byatirekappadhānanti abhāva-ggahaṇaṃ, tena kamme sati bhāvato, asati abhāvatoti ayamettha adhippāyo[M 2.0296]. Yathā panassa viññāṇassa saṅkhārapaccayatā na siddhā, na evaṃ vipākabhāvo. So pana siddhoti katvā āha “vipākaṃheta”nti. Tena viññāṇassa vipākabhāvena saṅkhārapaccayattaṃ sādheti. Tassa pana sādhanatthaṃ “upacitakammābhāve vipākābhāvato”ti vuttanti taṃ vivaranto “vipākañcā”tiādimāha. Yadi uppajjeyyāti yadi kammanirapekkho vipāko uppajjeyya. Sabbesaṃ sattānaṃ brahmattaṃ upagatānaṃ ghānādiviññāṇāni mahāvipākaviññāṇānīti tassa tassa vipākassa anokāse ṭhitānampi. Vipākānīti viññāṇāpekkhāya napuṃsakaniddeso, sabbavipākaviññāṇānīti attho.

In whatever way a deed done is capable of giving fruit, in that way a deed done is called 'accumulated.' Thus, taking only the formation that is suitable for giving a result, He said, 'in the absence of accumulated kamma.' A cause, by nature, has absence as its primary characteristic; therefore, the inclusion of 'absence' is made. By that, when kamma exists, there is presence, and when it does not exist, there is absence; this is the intention here. Furthermore, while for this consciousness the state of being conditioned by formations is not established, its nature as a result is not so. That nature as a result, however, is established. Having considered this, He said, 'because it is a result.' By that, through the consciousness's nature as a result, He establishes its state of being conditioned by formations. Furthermore, for the purpose of establishing that, it was said, 'because of the absence of result in the absence of accumulated kamma.' Therefore, wishing to explain that, He said, 'and the result...' etc. 'If it were to arise' means: if a result were to arise independent of kamma, then for all beings, even for those who have attained the state of a Brahmā and are abiding in a place that is not the occasion for this or that result, olfactory consciousness, etc., and great resultant consciousnesses would arise. The word 'vipākāni' is a neuter designation with reference to 'consciousness'; the meaning is 'all resultant consciousnesses'.

Saṅkhārā bahū ekūnatiṃsacetanābhedato, viññāṇāni ca bahūni bāttiṃsavidhattā, na ca sabbato sabbānīti āha “katarasaṅkhārapaccayā kataraviññāṇanti ce”ti. “Viññāṇa”nti ca idaṃ viññāṇasāmaññaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ. Kāmaṃ khandhaniddesepi (visuddhi. 2.451 ādayo) imāni viññāṇāni niddiṭṭhāni, taṃ pana atisaṃkhittaṃ, na ca tattha nesaṃ saṅkhārapaccayatā vibhāvitāti taṃ pavattiyaṃ, paṭisandhiyañca bhavādīsu pavattanākāravasena vitthārato dassetuṃ “kāmāvacarapuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Manoviññāṇeti niddhāraṇe bhūmmaṃ. Mahāvipākānīti viññāṇāpekkhāya napuṃsakaniddeso. Mahāvipākāti pana pāṭhe manoviññāṇadhātuyoti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ.

Formations are many, by way of the twenty-nine divisions of volition, and consciousnesses are also many, due to being of thirty-two kinds. And not all arise from all; therefore, He said, 'If the question is, “Which consciousnesses are conditioned by which formations?”' And this term 'consciousness' was stated taking consciousness in general. Although in the exposition of the aggregates these consciousnesses were specified, that, however, was very brief, and their state of being conditioned by formations was not explained there. Therefore, in order to show that in detail by way of its manner of occurrence during the course of life and at rebirth-linking in the various planes of existence, etc., the passage beginning 'Conditioned by meritorious formations of the sense-sphere...' was begun. In 'manoviññāṇe,' it is the locative case of specification. 'Mahāvipākāni' is a neuter designation with reference to 'consciousness.' However, in the reading 'mahāvipākā,' it should be connected by bringing in the term 'manoviññāṇadhātuyo' (mind-consciousness-elements).

621. Yaṃsaṅkhārapaccayāti yassa yassa saṅkhārassa paccayabhāvena. Yaṃ viññāṇanti “yaṃ yaṃ viññāṇa”nti evaṃ ubhayattha āmeḍitalopo daṭṭhabbo. “Hotī”ti iminā kāraṇabhāve viññāṇassa sabbhāvamattaṃ paveditaṃ, na pavattivisesoti taṃ dassento “evaṃ pavatti veditabbā”ti āha[V 2.0278]. Brahmānampi aniṭṭharūpādiāpāthagamane akusalavipākacakkhuviññāṇādīni kadāci uppajjantīti “imāni terasa…pe… pavattantī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ vokāro vitthāro etthāti pañcavokāro, so eva bhavo, etasmiṃ pañcavokārabhave. Hoti hi bhinnādhikaraṇānampi aññapadatthasamāso yathā “urasilomo”ti. Atha vā yathāpaccayaṃ pavattamānehi pañcahi khandhehi vokarīyatīti pañcavokāro, so eva bhavoti sabbaṃ pubbe viya.

621. “Yaṃsaṅkhārapaccayāti” means: because of the state of being a condition of whatever formation. “Yaṃ viññāṇanti” means “whatever consciousness”; thus, in both places, the elision of the repeated word should be understood. By the word “hoti,” it is declared that when there is a cause, there is merely the existence of consciousness; a specific mode of occurrence is not declared. Therefore, to show that specific mode of occurrence, he said, “Thus, the occurrence should be understood.” Even for Brahmās, when undesirable visible objects and so on come into range, unwholesome-resultant eye-consciousness and so on sometimes arise. Therefore, it was said, “These thirteen... occur.” Therein, “pañcavokāro” is so called because herein there is the “vokāra,” the expansion, of the five aggregates. That itself is “bhava,” existence; in this five-constituent existence. Indeed, there can be a relative compound (aññapadatthasamāso) even of terms with different referents, as in “urasilomo.” Alternatively, it is called “pañcavokāro” because it is diversified by the five aggregates occurring in accordance with conditions. That itself is “bhava,” existence. Everything is as before.

“Pavattiyaññeva [M 2.0297] pavattantī”ti saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ vivarituṃ “katha”ntiādi āraddhaṃ.

To elaborate on the meaning briefly stated as “they occur only in the course of an existence,” the section beginning with “How?” was commenced.

“Yebhuyyena lobhasampayuttajavanāvasāne”ti idaṃ paṭighavicikicchuddhaccasampayuttānantaraṃ somanassasahagatassa anuppajjanatoti keci, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. “Cakkhuṃ assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati…pe… vicikicchā uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, akusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjatī”ti vacanato. Iṭṭhaṃ ce ārammaṇaṃ, somanassatadārammaṇaṃ na na uppajjatīti. Javanena tadārammaṇaniyame somanassasahagatānantaraṃ somanassasahagatāneva sandhāya vuttanti apare, taṃ vicāretabbaṃ upekkhāsahagatakusalākusalajavanānantarampi somanassatadārammaṇassa icchitabbattā. Upekkhāsahagatakiriyājavanānantarameva hi somanassatadārammaṇaṃ na icchanti.

Regarding the statement, “Mostly at the end of greed-associated javanas,” some say this was stated because a joy-accompanied tadārammaṇa does not arise immediately after javanas associated with aversion, doubt, or restlessness. That should not be accepted. For it is said: “One savors the eye, delights in it; with that as basis, lust arises, wrong view arises… doubt arises, restlessness arises. When the unwholesome has ceased, the resultant arises as a tadārammaṇa.” If the object is desirable, a joy-accompanied tadārammaṇa does not fail to arise. Others say that in the rule concerning tadārammaṇa following javana, it was said with reference only to a joy-accompanied tadārammaṇa immediately after a joy-accompanied javana. That should be investigated, because a joy-accompanied tadārammaṇa is also desirable immediately after equanimity-accompanied wholesome and unwholesome javanas. Indeed, it is only immediately after an equanimity-accompanied functional javana that they do not desire a joy-accompanied tadārammaṇa.

Yasmā pana tihetukajavanāvasāne ca kadāci ahetukaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hoti, tasmā “yebhuyyenā”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā ekacittakkhaṇāyukaṃ javanārammaṇaṃ hoti, tadā tattha ekameva tadārammaṇaṃ hotīti katvā “sakiṃ vā”ti vuttanti keci. Apare pana tadārammaṇaṃ nāma javanārammaṇānubhavanakiccaṃ, taṃ ekacittakkhaṇike tathā āsannabhede ārammaṇe nuppajjati. Tasmā “sakiṃ vā”ti idaṃ dirattatirattādi viya vacanasiliṭṭhatāvasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ, dvikkhattumeva pana uppajjatīti. “Dirattatiratta”nti (pāci. 50) ettha hi vā-saddassa abhāvā vacanasiliṭṭhatāmattena dirattaggahaṇaṃ katanti yujjati. “Nirantaraṃ tirattadassanatthaṃ vā”ti idha pana vā-saddo vikappattho vuttoti sakiṃ eva ca kadāci pavattiṃ sandhāya “sakiṃ vā”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teneva hi sammohavinodaniyaṃ sakiṃ tadārammaṇappavattiyā vicāretabbataṃ dassentena “cittappavattigaṇanāyaṃ pana sabbadvāresu tadārammaṇe dve eva cittavārā āgatā”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 227) vuttaṃ.

Since, however, at the end of a triple-rooted impulsion, a rootless registration sometimes occurs, therefore it is said 'mostly.' Since, when the object of impulsion has a remaining lifespan of one mind-moment, then in that case only one registration occurs, some say that it is for this reason that 'or once' was stated. Others, however, say that registration has the function of experiencing the object of impulsion, and that it does not arise in an object that has a lifespan of one mind-moment and is thus close to perishing. Therefore, it should be understood that this phrase 'or once' is stated, like 'two or three nights,' for the sake of elegant expression; in fact, it arises only twice. Indeed, in 'two nights, three nights' (Pāc. 50), due to the absence of the word 'or', it is appropriate that the inclusion of 'two nights' is made merely for the sake of euphony, or for the purpose of showing three nights without interruption. Here, however, the word 'or' is stated in the sense of an alternative; therefore, it should be understood that 'or once' is stated with reference to the fact that it sometimes occurs just once. For that very reason, in the Sammohavinodanī, when showing that the occurrence of registration just once is a matter to be investigated, it is said: 'But in the counting of cognitive processes, in all doors, only two mind-moments of registration are mentioned' (Vibh-a. 227).

Tattha [V 2.0279] cittappavattigaṇanāyanti vipākakathāyaṃ balavarūpādiārammaṇe vuttaṃ cittappavattigaṇanaṃ sandhāyāha. Tattha hi dveva tadārammaṇuppattivārā vuttā[M 2.0298]. Tadeva hi sandhāya idhāpi vuttaṃ “abhidhammaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana tadārammaṇe dve cittavārā āgatā”ti. Abhidhammaṭṭhakathāyaṃ aniyatārammaṇaṭṭhānakiccā hutvā pavattantīti (vibha. aṭṭha. 227) dvāraṃ anāmasitvā eva vuttaṃ, taṃ anantaraṃ parato vuttasahetukavipākaviññāṇānaṃ sadisasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ kātukāmatādhippāyena vuttaṃ. Ahetukadvayādīnañhi bhavaṅgabhūtānaṃ sayameva dvārattā, cutipaṭisandhibhūtānañca bhavaṅgasaṅkhātena, aññena ca dvārena anuppattito niyataṃ, aniyataṃ vā dvāraṃ etesanti na sakkā vattunti.

Therein, by 'the counting of the cognitive process,' it is said in reference to the counting of the cognitive process mentioned in the discussion on resultants in the context of strong visible objects, etc. Indeed, therein only two occasions of the arising of registration were stated. Referring to that very statement, it is also stated here: 'However, in the Abhidhamma commentary, two cognitive series concerning registration have occurred.' In the Abhidhamma commentary, the statement 'they arise, having an indeterminate object, basis, and function' (VibhA 227) was made without touching upon the door; that was stated with the intention of wanting to give a similar description for the root-accompanied resultant consciousnesses mentioned immediately thereafter. Indeed, for the two rootless types, etc., which have become the life-continuum, it is because they themselves are the door; and for those which have become death and rebirth-linking, because they do not arise through another door designated as the life-continuum, nor through any other door, it is not possible to say of them that 'their door is fixed' or 'indeterminate'.

Ahetukadvayassa pana santīraṇatadārammaṇabhūtassa dvāraṃ labbhati, tañca aniyatanti tampi gaṇhanto “aniyatadvārārammaṇaṭṭhānakiccā hutvā pavattantī”ti āha. Teneva cettha mahāvipākānampi tadārammaṇabhūtānaṃ dvāraṃ labbhatīti tatthāpi dvāraggahaṇaṃ kataṃ.

However, for the pair of rootless resultants which have become investigating and registration consciousnesses, a door is obtained, and that is indeterminate. Including that also, he said, 'they arise, having an indeterminate door, object, basis, and function.' And for that very reason, here, because a door is obtained even for the great resultants which have become registration consciousnesses, there also the inclusion of 'door' was made.

Ekassa sattassa pavatto rūpāvacaravipāko pathavīkasiṇādīsu yasmiṃ ārammaṇe pavatto, tato aññasmiṃ tassa pavatti natthīti rūpāvacarānaṃ niyatārammaṇatā vuttā. Itarāni āruppavipākaviññāṇāni. Niyataṃ avatthukānīti niyatāvatthukāni. Kasiṇugghāṭimākāsādīsuyeva ārammaṇesu pavattanato niyatārammaṇāni. Tatrāti pavattiyaṃ. Assāti bāttiṃsavidhassa vipākaviññāṇassa. Te te saṅkhārāti yathāvuttā puññābhisaṅkhārādisaṅkhārā. Kammapaccayenāti nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena. Upanissayapaccayenāti pakatūpanissayapaccayena.

The fine-material sphere resultant consciousness that has arisen for a single being, in whichever object among the earth-kasiṇa, etc., it has arisen, does not arise in any other object apart from that; thus, for the fine-material sphere resultants, fixedness of object is stated. The others are the immaterial-sphere resultant consciousnesses. They are of fixed physical basis because they are fixedly without a physical basis. 'Therein' means in the course of an existence. 'Of this' means of the thirty-two-fold resultant consciousness. 'Those respective formations' means the formations such as the aforementioned meritorious formations, etc. 'By kamma condition' means by the differently-momented kamma condition. 'By support condition' means by natural support condition.

622. Evaṃ pavattiyaṃ viññāṇappavattiṃ dassetvā paṭisandhiyaṃ dassetuṃ “yaṃ pana vutta”ntiādimāha. Tattha anurūpāya paṭisandhiyāti anurūpena paṭisandhikiccena. Taṃ pana anurūpataṃ sayameva vakkhati. Bhavantarena bhavantarassa sandhānaṃ idha paṭisandhīti taṃ acittakampi atthevāti katvā “kati paṭisandhiyo”ti pucchaṃ katvāpi “kati paṭisandhicittānī”ti pucchā katā. “Kena katthā”ti kena cittena kasmiṃ bhave.

622. Having thus shown the occurrence of consciousness in the course of existence, in order to show it in rebirth-linking, he said, “Now, what was said…,” and so on. Therein, by ‘a suitable rebirth-linking’ is meant ‘by a suitable rebirth-linking function.’ He himself will explain that suitability. The linking of one existence to another is here rebirth-linking; considering that it can also be without consciousness, even after asking the question, “How many rebirth-linkings?”, the question, “How many rebirth-linking consciousnesses?” was asked. By ‘By what, where?’ is meant ‘By what consciousness, in what existence?’

Tatthāti tesu ekūnavīsatiyā paṭisandhicittesu. Kusalavipākāya ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyāti [V 2.0280] sambandho. Natthi devesu ahetukā paṭisandhīti “manussaloke”ti visesanaṃ. Napuṃsakādīnanti ādisaddena [M 2.0299] mammādīnaṃ saṅgaho. Keci pana ekacce ahetukapaṭisandhikā avikalindriyā hutvā thokaṃ vicāraṇapakatikāpi hontiyeva, tasmā tādisānampi idha ādisaddena saṅgahoti vadanti. Saṅkhepatoti samāsato, asukāya paṭisandhiyā asukaṃ ārammaṇanti vibhāgaṃ akatvāti attho.

Therein, means among those nineteen rebirth-linking consciousnesses. The connection is with the rootless mind-consciousness-element that is wholesome-resultant. Since there is no rootless rebirth-linking among the devas, the specification ‘in the human world’ is made. By the word ‘etc.’ in ‘neuter, etc.,’ there is the inclusion of the stammering, etc. Some, however, say: ‘Certain individuals with rootless rebirth-linking, having unimpaired faculties, are also by nature capable of a little investigation; therefore, even such individuals are included here by the word “etc.”’ By ‘in brief’ is meant summarily; that is, the meaning is without making the distinction that ‘for such-and-such a rebirth-linking, there is such-and-such an object.’

Sesānanti rūpāvacarā pañca, paṭhamatatiyāruppā dveti imāsaṃ vuttāvasesānaṃ sattannaṃ paṭisandhīnaṃ. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ cuticittaṃ nāma natthi paṭisandhiārammaṇe eva pavattanato. Dvīsu ārammaṇesūti atītanavattabbavasena dvīsu ārammaṇesu.

By ‘of the remaining’ is meant of these seven rebirth-linkings that remain from those already mentioned: the five form-sphere rebirth-linkings, and the two that are the first and third formless-sphere rebirth-linkings. There is no so-called death-consciousness that has a present object, because it proceeds only with the object of rebirth-linking. By ‘in two objects’ is meant in two objects by way of the past and the ineffable.

623. Tānīti pubbe katāni kammāni. Assāti āsannamaraṇassa puggalassa. Olambantīti sāyanhe mahantānaṃ pabbatakūṭānaṃ chāyā viya bhūmiyaṃ tassa citte avalambanti upatiṭṭhanti. Tasmiṃ niruddheti tasmiṃ cuticitte niruddhamatte tassa nirodhasamanantarameva. Tadevāti taṃyeva yathāvuttajavanavīthiyā ārammaṇabhūtaṃ. Avijjātaṇhādīsu kilesesu anupacchinnesveva kammādino upaṭṭhānaṃ, tañca ārabbha cittasantānassa bhavantaraninnapoṇapabbhāratā hotīti āha “anupacchinnakilesabalavināmita”nti. Santāne hi vināmite tadekadesabhūtaṃ paṭisandhicittañca vināmitameva hoti, na ca ekadesavināmitabhāvena vinā santānassa vināmitatā atthīti. Sabbattha pana duggatipaṭisandhininnāya cutiyā purimajavanāni akusalāni, itarāya ca kusalānīti nicchinanti. “Nimittassādagadhitaṃ vā, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ tiṭṭhati, anubyañjanassādagadhitaṃ vā, tasmiṃ ce samaye kālaṃ karoti, ṭhānametaṃ vijjati, yaṃ dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ upapajjeyya nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā”ti (saṃ. ni. 4.235) hi vuttaṃ, tasmā akusalaṃ duggatiyaṃ, kusalañca sugatiyaṃ paṭisandhiyā upanissayo hotīti. Arahato pana sabbaso kilesānaṃ upacchinnattā paṭippassaddhasabbabhavussukkatāya kammādinimittaṃ na upaṭṭhahati, tato vijjamānampi kammaṃ aladdhasahāyattā paṭisandhiṃ na janeti.

623. By 'those' (tāni) is meant 'actions previously done' (pubbe katāni kammāni). By 'his' (assa) is meant 'of the person near death' (āsannamaraṇassa puggalassa). By 'they hang' (olambanti) is meant 'they hang down upon his mind and appear, just as the shadows of great mountain peaks in the evening hang down upon the earth' (sāyanhe... upatiṭṭhanti). By 'when that ceases' (tasmiṃ niruddhe) is meant 'at the very moment that death-consciousness ceases; immediately after its cessation' (tasmiṃ cuticitte niruddhamatte tassa nirodhasamanantarameva). By 'that very one' (tadeva) is meant 'that very object of the impulsion-process as described' (taṃyeva yathāvuttajavanavīthiyā ārammaṇabhūtaṃ). Even while defilements such as ignorance and craving remain uncut, the appearance of kamma, etc., occurs, and based on that, the mental continuum has an inclination, tendency, and bent towards another existence; hence it is said, 'inclined by the power of uncut defilements' (anupacchinnakilesabalavināmitaṃ). For when the continuum is inclined, the rebirth-linking consciousness, being a part of that continuum, is also inclined; and there is no inclination of the continuum without the inclination of a part. In all cases, it is determined that for a death that inclines towards rebirth in a woeful state, the preceding impulsions are unwholesome, and for the other, they are wholesome. For it is said: 'Monks, when consciousness persists, it persists greedy for the delight in signs or greedy for the delight in secondary characteristics. If at that time one dies, it is possible that one may be reborn in one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm' (Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.235). Therefore, the unwholesome is a strong supporting condition for rebirth-linking in a woeful state, and the wholesome for rebirth-linking in a happy state. However, for an Arahant, because all defilements are completely cut off and all anxiety about existence has been pacified, the sign of kamma, etc., does not appear. Therefore, even existing kamma, because it has not obtained an associate, does not produce rebirth-linking.

Vuttappakārakammavasenāti pāpakammavasena, tadupaṭṭhāpitanti adhippāyo. “Narakādīsu aggijālavaṇṇādika”nti idaṃ taṃsadisatāvasena vuttaṃ. Na [M 2.0300] hi so eva nirayaggivaṇṇādi tadā tassa [V 2.0281] āpāthaṃ āgacchati. Tattha aggijālavaṇṇādikanti ādi-saddena vettaraṇīsimbaliasipattavanādivaṇṇaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Narakādīsūti pana ādi-saddena petatiracchānānaṃ nibaddhasañcaraṇaṭṭhānapariyāpannavaṇṇaṃ. Manodvāre āpāthamāgacchatīti kammabalena upaṭṭhāpitavaṇṇāyatanaṃ supinaṃ passantassa viya, dibbacakkhussa viya ca manodvāre eva gocarabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ekaṃ āvajjanaṃ, pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇānīti tīṇi vīthicittāni.

By 'by the power of kamma of the aforementioned kind' is meant 'by the power of evil kamma'; 'presented by that' is the intended meaning. The phrase 'the appearance of blazing fires, etc., in hells, etc.' is stated by way of similarity to that. For indeed, that very appearance of hellfire, etc., does not come into his field of perception at that time. Here, in 'the appearance of blazing fires, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes the appearance of the Vetaraṇī River, the silk-cotton tree forest, the sword-leaf forest, etc. And in 'in hells, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes the appearance pertaining to the fixed wandering places of petas and animals. By 'it comes into the range of the mind-door' is meant that the visual-form base, presented by the power of kamma, comes into the scope of the mind-door itself, just as for one seeing a dream or for one with the divine eye. One adverting, five impulsions, and two registrations—these are three kinds of process-consciousnesses.

Rāgādihetubhūtaṃ hīnamārammaṇanti akusalavipākassa ārammaṇaṃ bhavituṃ yuttaṃ aniṭṭhamārammaṇamāha. Tampi hi saṅkappanavasena rāgassāpi hetu hotīti. Akusalavipākajanakakammasahajātānaṃ vā taṃsadisāsannacutijavanacetanāsahajātānañca rāgādīnaṃ hetubhāvo eva hīnatā. Tañhi pacchānutāpajanakakammānamārammaṇaṃ kammavasena aniṭṭhaṃ akusalavipākassa ārammaṇaṃ bhaveyya. Aññathā ca iṭṭhārammaṇe pavattassa akusalakammassa vipāko akusalakammanimittārammaṇo na bhaveyya. Na hi akusalavipāko iṭṭhārammaṇo bhavituṃ arahatīti.

By 'an inferior object that is a cause of lust, etc.,' he states it is an undesirable object fit to be the object of an unwholesome resultant. For even that, by way of conception, can be a cause of lust. Or, the inferiority is precisely the state of being a cause for lust, etc., that are co-arisen with kamma that generates unwholesome results, and that are co-arisen with volitions of near-death impulsions similar to that. For that object of kamma that generates later remorse would, by the power of kamma, become an undesirable object for an unwholesome resultant. And otherwise, the result of unwholesome kamma that occurred with a desirable object would not have an unwholesome kamma-sign as its object. For an unwholesome result is not fit to have a desirable object.

Pañcadvāre ca āpāthaṃ āgacchantaṃ paccuppannaṃ kammanimittaṃ āsannakatakammārammaṇasantatiyaṃ uppannaṃ, taṃsadisañca daṭṭhabbaṃ. Aññathā tadeva paṭisandhiārammaṇūpaṭṭhāpakaṃ, tadeva ca paṭisandhijanakaṃ bhaveyya. Na ca paṭisandhiyā upacārabhūtāni viya, etasmiṃ tayā pavattitabbanti paṭisandhiyā ārammaṇaṃ anuppādentāni viya ca pavattāni cutiāsannāni javanāni paṭisandhijanakāni bhaveyyuṃ. “Katattā upacitattā”ti (dha. sa. 431) hi vuttaṃ. Tadā ca taṃsamānavīthiyaṃ viya pavattamānāni kathaṃ katūpacitāni siyuṃ? Tadā na assāditāni. Na ca lokiyāni lokuttarāni viya samānavīthiphalāni honti. “Pubbe vāssa taṃ kataṃ hoti pāpakammaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ, pacchā vāssa taṃ kataṃ hoti pāpakammaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ, maraṇakāle vāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi samattā hoti samādinnā. Tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjatī”tiādinā (ma. ni. 3.303) sutte maraṇakāle samattāya samādinnāya micchādiṭṭhiyā, sammādiṭṭhiyā ca sahajātacetanāya paṭisandhidānaṃ vuttaṃ, na ca dubbalehi pañcadvārikajavanehi micchādiṭṭhi, sammādiṭṭhi [M 2.0301] vā samattā hoti samādinnā. Tathā hi vuttaṃ sammohavinodaniyaṃ “sabbampi hetaṃ kusalākusaladhammapaṭivijānanādicavanapariyosānaṃ kiccaṃ manodvārikacitteneva hoti, na pañcadvārikenāti [V 2.0282] sabbassapetassa kiccassa karaṇe sahajavanakāni vīthicittāni paṭikkhittānī”ti (vibha. aṭṭha. 766).

And the present kamma-sign coming into focus at the five doors should be seen as that which has arisen in the continuity of the object of kamma done nearby, and as similar to that object of kamma. Otherwise, that very kamma would be the presenter of the rebirth-linking object and also the generator of rebirth-linking. Furthermore, the death-proximate javanas would not be generators of rebirth-linking, for they arise as if they were preliminary to rebirth-linking and as if not producing the object for rebirth-linking, with the thought, “In this you should proceed.” For it is said, “because of having been done and accumulated” (Dhs. §1296). And at that time, how could those javanas that arise as if in a cognitive process similar to that rebirth-linking be ‘done and accumulated’? At that time, they are not savored. And mundane javanas do not have their fruit in the same cognitive process, as do supramundane ones. In the sutta, by way of such passages as, “Either earlier he has done an evil deed to be experienced as painful, or later he has done an evil deed to be experienced as painful, or at the time of death he has wrong view completely adopted and firmly held. Due to that, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, the lower world, hell” (MN 136), it is stated that the giving of rebirth-linking is by the volition co-nascent with wrong view, or with right view, that is completed and undertaken at the time of death. And wrong view or right view is not completed and undertaken by the weak five-door javanas. For so it is said in the Sammohavinodanī: “All this function—from the discernment of wholesome and unwholesome states up to its end in passing away—is done only by mind-door consciousness, not by five-door consciousness. Therefore, in performing all this function, the cognitive-process-cittas of the five doors along with their javanas are rejected” (Vibh-a. 159).

Tattha hi na kiñci dhammaṃ paṭivijānātīti “manopubbaṅgamā dhammā”ti (dha. pa. 1-2) evaṃ vuttaṃ ekampi kusalaṃ vā akusalaṃ vā na paṭivijānātīti ca vuttaṃ. Yesaṃ paṭivibhāvanappavattiyā sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā anveti, tesaṃ sā pavatti pañcadvāre paṭikkhittā. Kusalākusalakammasamādānañca tādisamevāti. Tadārammaṇānantaraṃ pana cavanaṃ, tadanantarā ca upapatti manodvārikā eva hoti, na sahajavanakavīthicittapariyāpannāti iminā adhippāyena idha pañcadvārikatadārammaṇānantarā cuti, tadanantarā paṭisandhi ca vuttāti daṭṭhabbā. Tattha avasesapañcacittakkhaṇāyuke rūpādimhi uppannaṃ paṭisandhiṃ sandhāya “paccuppannārammaṇaṃ upapatticittaṃ paccuppannārammaṇassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti, avasesaekacittakkhaṇāyuke ca uppannaṃ paṭisandhiṃ sandhāya “paccuppannārammaṇaṃ upapatticittaṃ atītārammaṇassa bhavaṅgassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti ca vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Indeed, therein, regarding the statement 'one does not discern any state,' it is also stated that one does not discern even a single wholesome or unwholesome state, in accordance with the saying, 'Mind precedes all phenomena' (Dhp. 1-2). For those states whose clear manifestation is followed by either happiness or suffering, that manifestation is rejected at the five doors. And the undertaking of wholesome and unwholesome kamma is just the same. However, the decease immediately after the tadārammaṇa, and the rebirth-linking immediately after that, occur only at the mind-door; they are not included in the cognitive process of the five doors along with its javanas. With this intention, it should be understood that here, decease immediately after a five-door tadārammaṇa and the rebirth-linking immediately after that are spoken of. Therein, with reference to a rebirth-linking that has arisen taking as its object a visible form, etc., that has a lifespan of five remaining thought-moments, it should be known that it is said: 'The rebirth-linking consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum with a present object by way of the contiguity condition.' And with reference to a rebirth-linking that has arisen taking as its object one that has a lifespan of one remaining thought-moment, it is also said: 'The rebirth-linking consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum with a past object by way of the contiguity condition.'

624. Kaṇhapakkhe sukkapakkhaṃ ṭhapetvāti ettha yathā pubbe “pāpakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā”ti vutte kaṇhapakkhe “anavajjakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā”ti sukkapakkho vutto, evaṃ “duggatipariyāpannaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ, narakādīsu aggijālavaṇṇādikaṃ duggatinimitta”nti ca vutte kaṇhapakkhe “sugatipariyāpannaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ, manussaloke rattakambalasadisamātukucchivaṇṇasaṅkhātaṃ, devaloke vā uyyānavimānakapparukkhādivaṇṇasaṅkhātaṃ sugatinimitta”nti evaṃ sukkapakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā sesaṃ sabbaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Atītapaccuppannārammaṇāyāti kammakammanimittavasena atītārammaṇāya, mātukucchivaṇṇādisugatinimittavasena paccuppannārammaṇāya.

624. Regarding the phrase 'having set aside the bright side in the dark side': Here, just as previously, when 'evil kamma or kamma-sign' was stated as the dark side, 'blameless kamma or kamma-sign' was stated as the bright side. Similarly, when 'rebirth-linking consciousness included in a woeful destiny, and a sign of a woeful destiny such as the color of flames in the hells and so on' were stated as the dark side, then 'rebirth-linking consciousness included in a happy destiny, designated as the color of the mother's womb which is like a red blanket in the human world, or designated as the color of gardens, celestial mansions, wish-fulfilling trees and so on in the deva world, which is a sign of a happy destiny'—thus having established the bright side, all the rest should be understood by the previous method. Regarding 'having past and present objects': by way of kamma and kamma-sign, it has a past object; by way of a sign of a happy destiny such as the color of the mother's womb, it has a present object.

625. Tañca khoti yadetaṃ “anavajjakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā”ti aniyamanaṃ kataṃ, tañca kho. Kammanimittameva āpāthamāgacchati ekantato [M 2.0302] attano kammārammaṇatāya mahaggatavipākassa. Suddhāya vāti mahaggatakammanimittārammaṇāya javanavīthiyā, tadārammaṇarahitāyāti attho, sā pana javanavīthi mahaggatavipākassa upacāro viya daṭṭhabbā. Keci pana tañca vīthiṃ mahaggatāvasānaṃ vadanti. “Navattabbārammaṇā vā”ti idaṃ rūpāvacarapaṭisandhiṃ, āruppesu [V 2.0283] ca paṭhamaṃ, tatiyañca sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dutiyacatutthā pana atītārammaṇavacaneneva gahitā.

625. Regarding the statement 'And that indeed': that which was made unspecified as 'blameless kamma or kamma-sign'—that, indeed, comes into the field of consciousness as a kamma-sign only. This is because the exalted resultant consciousness exclusively has its own kamma as its object. As for the phrase 'or by the pure': the meaning is, of a javana-process that has an exalted kamma-sign as its object and is devoid of tadārammaṇa. But that javana-process should be regarded as if it were the proximity of the exalted resultant consciousness. Some, however, say that that javana-process culminates in the exalted. The phrase 'or having an object that cannot be asserted' is stated with reference to the fine-material rebirth-linking, and, among the immaterial states, the first and the third. The second and fourth, however, are included by the very statement about having a past object.

Mātukucchivaṇṇasaṅkhātantiādinā vaṇṇo eva gatinimittabhāvena āgato. Tattha saddo tāva anupādinnabhāvena sugatipariyāpannatāya gatinimittabhāvena aṭṭhakathāsu nāgatoti yuttametaṃ, gandhādīnaṃ pana anāgamane kāraṇaṃ vīmaṃsitabbaṃ.

By the phrase 'designated as the color of the mother's womb' and so on, it is color alone that is presented as a sign of destiny. In this regard, that sound, in the first place, does not appear in the commentaries as a sign of destiny—due to its nature of being non-appropriated and its inclusion in a happy destiny—is appropriate. However, the reason for the non-appearance of smell and the other sense objects should be investigated.

Ayaṃ tāta tavatthāya buddhapūjā karīyatītiādīsu pubbacetanāvasena puññaṃ hoti. Sabbantimajavane vattamānassāpīti vadanti.

In such phrases as, 'Dear son, this worship of the Buddha is performed for your benefit,' they say that merit arises by the power of prior volition, even for one existing in the very last javana.

626. “Etenānusārena āruppacutiyāpi anantarā paṭisandhi veditabbā”ti idaṃ kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu “pathavīkasiṇajjhānādivasena paṭiladdhamahaggatassa sugatiyaṃ ṭhitassā”ti evamādike eva naye ayampi paṭisandhi avaruddhāti? Na, tattha rūpāvacaracutianantarāya eva paṭisandhiyā vuttattā. Tattha hi “pathavīkasiṇādikaṃ vā nimittaṃ mahaggatacittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthaṃ āgacchati, cakkhusotānaṃ vā”tiādinā tena vacanena rūpāvacaracutiyā eva anantarā paṭisandhi vuttāti viññāyati. Athāpi yathāsambhavayojanāya ayampi paṭisandhi tattheva avaruddhā, arūpāvacaracutianantarā pana rūpāvacarapaṭisandhi natthi. Arūpāvacare ca uparūpari cutiyā anantarā heṭṭhimā heṭṭhimā paṭisandhi natthīti catutthāruppacutiyā navattabbārammaṇapaṭisandhi natthi. Tena tato tattheva atītārammaṇā, kāmāvacare ca atītapaccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi. Itarāhi ca yathāsambhavaṃ atītanavattabbārammaṇā āruppapaṭisandhi, atītapaccuppannārammaṇā ca kāmāvacarapaṭisandhi yojetabbāti imassa visesassa dassanatthaṃ visuṃ uddharaṇaṃ kataṃ.

626. “By this method, rebirth immediately after decease from the formless realms should also be understood.” Why was this said? Is it not so that this rebirth is also included in such a method as, ‘for one who has attained a sublime state by means of the earth kasiṇa jhāna, etc., and is established in a fortunate destiny’? No, because in that case, what is stated is only rebirth immediately after decease from the fine-material realm. For there, it is understood that by the statement beginning, ‘the earth kasiṇa or other sign, or a sublime mind, comes into the range of the mind-door, or of the eye and ear,’ only rebirth immediately after decease from the fine-material realm is stated. And yet, by applying it as is possible, this rebirth is also included there. However, there is no fine-material rebirth immediately after decease from the formless realm. And in the formless realm, there is no lower and lower rebirth immediately after decease from a higher and higher realm; therefore, after decease from the fourth formless attainment, there is no rebirth with an unstatable object. Therefore, after that, in that very realm, there is rebirth with a past object, and in the sense-sphere realm, there is rebirth with a past or present object. And from the other deceases, as is possible, formless rebirth with a past or unstatable object, and sense-sphere rebirth with a past or present object, should be connected. To show this distinction, a separate exposition was made.

627. Evaṃ ārammaṇavasena ekavidhāya kāmāvacarasugaticutiyā duvidhā duggatipaṭisandhi, duggaticutiyā duvidhā sugatipaṭisandhi, kāmāvacarasugaticutiyā dviekadvippakārānaṃ kāmarūpārūpānaṃ vasena pañcavidhā sugatipaṭisandhi[M 2.0303], rūpāvacaracutiyā tatheva pañcavidhā, duvidhāya āruppacutiyā paccekaṃ dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ kāmāruppānaṃ vasena aṭṭhavidhā ca paṭisandhi [V 2.0284] dassitā. Duggaticutiyā pana ekavidhāya duggatipaṭisandhi duvidhā na dassitā, taṃ dassetuṃ “duggatiyaṃ ṭhitassa panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yathā vuttā pana –

627. Thus, by way of the object, from one kind of decease in a fortunate sense-sphere destiny, two kinds of rebirth in a woeful destiny are shown; from decease in a woeful destiny, two kinds of rebirth in a fortunate destiny are shown; from decease in a fortunate sense-sphere destiny, five kinds of rebirth in a fortunate destiny are shown, by way of the sense-sphere, fine-material, and formless rebirths which have divisions of two, one, and two respectively; from decease in the fine-material sphere, five kinds are shown in the same way; and from two kinds of decease in the formless sphere, eight kinds of rebirth are shown, by way of two sense-sphere and two formless rebirths for each individually. However, from one kind of decease in a woeful destiny, two kinds of rebirth in a woeful destiny have not been shown; to show this, the passage beginning, “But for one established in a woeful destiny,” was stated. However, as stated:

Dve dve pañcātha pañcaṭṭha, dve bhavālambabhedato;

Cutiyā tādisāyetā, catuvīsati sandhiyo. (vibha. mūlaṭī. 227);

Two, two, five, then five, eight, and two—by the distinction of existence-objects; after such a passing away, these are the twenty-four rebirth-linkings.

628. “Kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā”tiādinā (dha. sa. 431) nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayabhāvo heṭṭhā dassitappakāroti upanissayabhāvameva dassento “vuttañheta”ntiādimāha.

628. By the text beginning with, “Because of the performance of wholesome kamma belonging to the sense-sphere,” the state of being a differently-timed kamma-condition is of the type that was shown below; therefore, showing only the state of being a decisive support condition, he says the text beginning with, “For it has been said.”

Nissayapaccayabhūtena rūpena sahapavattiyevettha viññāṇassa tena missitā, tadabhāvo amissitā. Yavanti ettha sattā ekajātisamanvayena aññamaññamissitā hontīti yoniyo. Sucaritaduccaritavasena gantabbā pāpuṇitabbāti gatiyo. Tiṭṭhati etthāti ṭhiti, viññāṇassa ṭhiti viññāṇaṭṭhiti. Nānattakāyanānattasaññītiādiāvāso eva sattehi āvasitabbato sattāvāso. Asaññasattāvāsassa idha asambhavato “sattāvāsavasena aṭṭhavidhaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ.

Herein, only the co-arising with materiality that has become a dependence-condition is the mixing of consciousness with that materiality; the absence of that is the unmixed. Insofar as beings here are mutually mixed by being endowed with a common birth, they are called 'wombs' (yoni). Because they are to be gone to, to be reached, by way of good and bad conduct, they are called 'destinations' (gati). 'It stands here,' thus it is a 'station' (ṭhiti); the station of consciousness is a 'station of consciousness' (viññāṇaṭṭhiti). The abode itself, beginning with 'diverse bodies and diverse perceptions,' is called an 'abode of beings' (sattāvāsa) because it is to be dwelled in by beings. Because the abode of non-percipient beings is impossible here, it is said, “It is eightfold by way of the abodes of beings.”

629. Aññatra jātipaṇḍakapaṭisandhiyāti ettha paṭhamakappikapaṭisandhiyāpīti vattabbaṃ. Sāpi hi bhāvena vināva uppajjatīti.

629. In the text, “Except for the rebirth-linking of a congenital eunuch,” it should also be said, “and the rebirth-linking of those at the beginning of the aeon.” For that too arises only without the faculty of sex.

Omatoti avamato, avakaṃsatoti attho. Ādināti “missaṃ amissa”nti etasmiṃ duke ādimhi vuttena missaviññāṇena. Omato dve vā tayo vā dasakā uppajjantīti gabbhaseyyakānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Aññattha pana aneke kalāpā saha uppajjanti. Brahmattabhāvepi hi anekagāvutappamāṇena aneke kalāpā saha uppajjantīti tiṃsato adhikāneva rūpāni honti. Tadahujātaeḷakassa lomaṃ jātiuṇṇāti keci. Himavantappadese jātimantaeḷakalomaṃ jātiuṇṇāti apare. Gabbhaṃ phāletvā gahitaeḷakalomaṃ jātiuṇṇāti aññe. Imāsu gatīsu imā yoniyo sambhavanti, imāsu na sambhavantīti evaṃ yonīnaṃ gativasena sambhavabhedo.

Omatoti means inferior (`avamato`), of a lower grade (`avakaṃsato`). Ādinā refers to the mixed consciousness stated at the beginning of the dyad 'mixed and unmixed.' The statement 'From an inferior origin, two or three decads arise' is made with reference to womb-born beings. Elsewhere, however, many groups arise together. For even in a Brahma-existence, many groups with a measure of many leagues arise together; thus, there are indeed more than thirty material phenomena. Some say that `jātiuṇṇā` is the wool of a lamb born on that very day. Others say that `jātiuṇṇā` is the wool of a thoroughbred lamb from the Himalayan region. Still others say that `jātiuṇṇā` is the wool of a lamb taken by splitting open the womb. The distinction of possibility for the modes of birth according to the destinations is as follows: 'In these destinations, these modes of birth are possible; in these, they are not possible.'

630. Bhummavajjesūti [M 2.0304] bhummadevānaṃ vajjanaṃ yonivibhāgaṃ pati tesaṃ manussasadisattā. Yoniyo [V 2.0285] tisso purimikā na hontīti yonittayapaṭikkhepena pacchimā yoni anuññātāti atthato āpannameva hoti. Gatittayeti manussapetatiracchānasaññite gatittaye. Tañhi ettha pubbe anāmaṭṭhaṃ.

630. Bhummavajjesu means the exclusion of the earth-devas with regard to the division of the modes of birth, because of their similarity to humans. The statement 'The three former modes of birth do not exist' means that by the rejection of the three modes of birth, the last mode of birth is permitted; this is indeed arrived at by way of the meaning. Gatittaye means in the three destinations designated as human, peta, and animal. For that was not previously touched upon here.

Ca-saddo avuttasamuccayatthoti dassetuṃ “ca-saddenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kasmā pana nijjhāmataṇhikapetesu purimikā tisso yoniyo na santīti? Asambhavato. Tāsañhi niccāturabhāvato kāmasevā natthīti na tā aṇḍajādayo honti. Kucchiyaṃ tāsaṃ gabbho nāvatiṭṭhati jālasabbhāvatoti keci. Aggijālāya santappamānasarīrā etā nibbattantīti allaṭṭhānesu, pupphādīsu ca sambhavābhāvato saṃsedajatāpi tāsaṃ natthevāti vadanti. Tenāha “opapātikā eva hi te hontī”ti.

To show that the word `ca` has the meaning of gathering what is unstated, the passage beginning with `ca-saddena` was stated. But why are the three former modes of birth not found among the `nijjhāmataṇhika` petas? Because of impossibility. For, since they are constantly afflicted, there is no sexual indulgence for them, and thus they are not egg-born and so on. Some say that a fetus does not remain in their womb because of the presence of flames. Because they are born with bodies tormented by a mass of fire, and because of the impossibility of their arising in moist places, or in flowers and so on, birth from moisture is also not possible for them, so they say. Therefore, he said: 'Indeed, they are only of spontaneous birth.'

Rūpībrahmesu tāva opapātikayonikesūti opapātikayonikehi rūpībrahme niddhāreti. Rūpībrahmesūti hi adhikaraṇe bhummaṃ, opapātikesūti niddhāraṇe. Tena “opapātikayonikesū”ti sāmaññato vuttarāsito “rūpībrahmesū”ti visesena tadekadesaṃ niddhāreti. Cakkhusotavatthudasakānaṃ, jīvitanavakassa cāti ettha keci “cakkhusotavatthusattakānaṃ, jīvitachakkassa cāti catunnaṃ kalāpānaṃ vasena rūpabhave paṭisandhiviññāṇena saha sattavīsati rūpāni uppajjanti, tattha gandharasāhārānaṃ paṭikkhittattā”ti kāraṇaṃ vatvā taṃ samatthentā “pāḷiyañhi ‘rūpadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe ṭhapetvā aññasattānaṃ devānaṃ pañcāyatanāni pātubhavanti, pañca dhātuyo pātubhavantī’ti (vibha. 1015-1016) vuttaṃ, tathā ‘rūpadhātuyā cha āyatanāni, nava dhātuyo’ti sabbasaṅgahakavasena tattha vijjamānāyatanadhātuyo dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Kathāvatthumhi ca ghānāyatanādīnaṃ viya gandhāyatanādīnañca tattha bhāvo paṭikkhitto ‘atthi tattha ghānāyatananti? Āmantā. Atthi tattha gandhāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe’tiādinā (kathā. 520). Na ca aphoṭṭhabbāyatanānaṃ pathavīdhātuādīnaṃ viya agandharasāyatanānaṃ gandharasānaṃ tattha bhāvo sakkā vattuṃ, phusituṃ sakkuṇeyyatāvinimuttassa pathavīādisabhāvassa viya gandharasāyatanabhāvavinimuttassa gandharasasabhāvassa [M 2.0305] abhāvā. Yadi ca ghānasamphassādīnaṃ kāraṇabhāvo natthīti ‘āyatanānī’ti te na vucceyyuṃ, dhātusaddo pana nissattanijjīvavācakoti ‘gandhadhātu rasadhātū’ti avacane kāraṇaṃ natthi, dhammabhāvo ca tesaṃ ekantena icchitabbo sabhāvadhāraṇādilakkhaṇato aññassa abhāvā. Dhammānañca āyatanabhāvo ekantiko [V 2.0286] yamake vutto ‘dhammo āyatananti? Āmantā’ti (yama. 1.āyatanayamaka.13). Tasmā tesaṃ gandharasāyatanabhāvābhāvepi koci āyatanabhāvo vattabbo. Yadi ca phoṭṭhabbabhāvato añño pathavīādibhāvo viya gandharasabhāvato añño tesaṃ koci sabhāvo siyā, tesaṃ dhammāyatanasaṅgaho. Gandharasabhāve pana āyatanabhāve ca sati ‘gandho ca so āyatanañca gandhāyatanaṃ, raso ca so āyatanañca rasāyatana’nti idamāpannamevāti gandharasāyatanabhāvo ca na sakkā nivāretuṃ. ‘Tayo āhārā’ti ca vacanato kabaḷīkārāhārassa tattha abhāvo viññāyati. Tasmā yathā pāḷiyā avirodho hoti, tathā rūpagaṇanā kātabbā. Evañhi dhammatā na vilomitā hotī”ti vadanti.

First, by the phrase 'among the form-sphere Brahmas, those of spontaneous birth,' one specifies the form-sphere Brahmas from among those of spontaneous birth. For 'among the form-sphere Brahmas' (rūpībrahmesu) is in the locative case, while 'among the spontaneously born' (opapātikesu) is for specification. Therefore, from the generally stated group 'of spontaneous birth,' a part thereof is specified as 'form-sphere Brahmas.'

Regarding the phrase 'of the decad of eye, ear, and heart-base, and of the ennead of life faculty,' here some say: 'By way of four groups—namely, the heptads of eye, ear, and heart-base, and the hexad of life—twenty-seven material phenomena arise together with the rebirth-linking consciousness in the form realm, because smell, taste, and nutriment are rejected there.' Stating this reason and seeking to establish it, they say: 'For in the Pāḷi it is said: "At the moment of arising in the form realm, setting aside the non-percipient devas, five sense bases appear, five elements appear" (Vibh. 1015-1016). Likewise, it is said: "In the form realm, there are six sense bases, nine elements," this being stated by way of comprehensive inclusion to show the sense bases and elements existing there. And in the Kathāvatthu, the existence there of the smell-base and so on is also rejected by the passage beginning: "Is there a nose-base there? Yes. Is there a smell-base there? It should not be said so" (Kathā. 520). And it is not possible to speak of the existence there of smells and tastes that are not the smell-base and taste-base, just as one cannot speak of the earth element, etc., that are not the tangible-base. This is because, just as there is no nature of earth, etc., that is devoid of the state of being touchable, there is no nature of smell and taste that is devoid of the state of being the smell-base and taste-base. And if they were not to be called "bases" because there is no causal state for nose-contact, etc., still, since the word "element" denotes what is non-sentient and lifeless, there is no reason for not saying "smell-element" and "taste-element." And their nature as phenomena must certainly be accepted, because there is no other reality apart from that which has the characteristic of bearing its own nature, etc. The nature of phenomena as a base is also stated as certain in the Yamaka: "Is a phenomenon a base? Yes" (Yam. 1, Āyatanayamaka, 13). Therefore, even in the absence of their nature as smell-base and taste-base, some nature as a base should be stated for them. And if, just as there might be a nature of earth, etc., other than the state of being tangible, there were for them some nature other than the nature of smell and taste, they would be included in the mind-object base. However, when the nature of smell and taste and the nature of a base exist, it is indeed arrived at that "it is smell and it is a base, thus smell-base; it is taste and it is a base, thus taste-base." Thus, the nature of being a smell-base and taste-base cannot be prevented. And from the Pāḷi text "three kinds of nutriment," the absence of physical nutriment there is understood. Therefore, the enumeration of material phenomena should be done in such a way that there is no contradiction with the Pāḷi text. For in this way, the natural order is not violated.' So they say.

Ettha vuccate – rūpāvacarasattānaṃ ghānajivhāyatanābhāvato vijjamānāpi gandharasā āyatanakiccaṃ na karontīti te anāmasitvā pāḷiyaṃ “pañcāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti (vibha. 1015), “cha āyatanānī”ti (vibha. 992) ca ādi vuttaṃ, “tayo āhārā”ti ca ajjhoharitabbassa āhārassa abhāvena ojaṭṭhamakarūpasamuṭṭhāpanasaṅkhātassa āhārakiccassa akaraṇato, na sabbena sabbaṃ gandharasānaṃ, ojāya ca abhāvato. Iti visayino, kiccassa ca abhāvena visayo, kiccavā ca dhammo na vutto. Yasmiñhi bhave visayī natthi, tasmiṃ taṃhetuko nippariyāyena visayassa āyatanabhāvo natthīti vijjamānassāpi avacanaṃ yathā tattheva rūpabhave pathavītejovāyodhātūnaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanabhāvena. Yassa pana yattha vacanaṃ, tassa tattha visayīsabbhāvahetuko nippariyāyena āyatanabhāvo vutto yathā tattheva rūpāyatanassa.

Herein it is said: For beings of the form realm, due to the absence of the nose-base and tongue-base, although smells and tastes exist, they do not perform the function of a base. Therefore, without referring to them, it is stated in the Pāḷi, 'five bases appear' (Vibh. 1015), and 'six bases' (Vibh. 992), and so on. And 'three nutriments' is stated due to the absence of nutriment to be ingested and due to the non-performance of the function of nutriment, which is designated as the production of the nutrient-octad of matter. This is not stated because of the complete absence of smells, tastes, and nutrient. Thus, due to the absence of the sense faculty and of the function, the object and the phenomenon possessing a function are not mentioned. For in whatever existence a sense faculty does not exist, in that existence, because of that, the status of the object as a base in the primary sense does not exist. Therefore, even though it exists, it is not mentioned, just as in that very form realm the earth, fire, and wind elements are not mentioned as the tangible base. But for whatever is mentioned in a certain existence, its status as a base in the primary sense is stated there because of the existence of the sense faculty, just as in that very same realm, the status of the form base is stated.

Yadi visayīsabbhāvahetuko visayassa nippariyāyena āyatanabhāvo, kathamasaññasattānaṃ dve āyatanāni pātubhavantīti, asaññasattānañhi [M 2.0306] cakkhāyatanaṃ natthi, acakkhāyatanabhāvena ca nesaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ aññesaṃ avisayoti? Nāyaṃ virodho. Yena adhippāyena rūpadhātuyaṃ saññīnaṃ gandhāyatanādīnaṃ avacanaṃ, tena rūpāyatanassāpi avacananti asaññīnaṃ ekaṃ āyatanaṃ vattabbaṃ. Yathāsakañhi indriyagocarabhāvāpekkhāya yesaṃ nippariyāyena āyatanabhāvo atthi, tesu niddisiyamānesu tadabhāvato rūpadhātuyaṃ saññīnaṃ gandhādike visuṃ āyatanabhāvena avatvā dhammasabhāvānativattanato, manoviññāṇassa ca visayabhāvūpagamanato dhammāyatanantogadhe katvā [V 2.0287] “pañcāyatanānī”ti pāḷiyaṃ (vibha. 1015) vuttaṃ. Etadatthañhi “dhammāyatana”nti sāmaññato nāmakaraṇaṃ, piṭṭhivaṭṭakāni vā tāni katvā “pañcāyatanānī”ti vuttaṃ.

If the unqualified status of an object as a sense-base is due to the existence of the corresponding sense faculty, how then is it said that 'two sense-bases appear for non-percipient beings'? For non-percipient beings lack the eye-base, and because they are without the eye-base, their form-base is not an object for others. This, however, is not a contradiction. For, by the same reasoning that the smell-base and so on are not mentioned for percipient beings in the form realm, the form-base also would not be mentioned; therefore, one sense-base should be stated for them. Indeed, with reference to the range of their respective faculties, when those things for which there is an unqualified sense-base status are being described, due to the absence of that status, smells and so on are not stated as separate sense-bases for percipient beings in the form realm. Rather, because the intrinsic nature of phenomena is not transgressed, and because they become objects of mind-consciousness, they are included within the mind-object base. Thus, in the Pāḷi text (Vibhaṅga 1015), it is said, 'five sense-bases.' Indeed, it is for this purpose that 'mind-object base' is given as a general name; or, treating those others as supplementary, it is said, 'five sense-bases'.

Yena ca pana adhippāyena asaññīnaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ vuttaṃ, tena saññīnampi gandhādīnaṃ visuṃ gahaṇaṃ kātabbanti imassa nayassa dassanatthaṃ “asaññasattānaṃ devānaṃ dve āyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti (vibha. 1017) vuttaṃ. Asatipi hi tattha attano indriye rūpassa vaṇṇāyatanasabhāvātikkamo natthevāti taṃ rūpāyatanantveva vuccati. Iminā ca nayadassanena gandhādīni tīṇi pakkhipitvā saññīnaṃ aṭṭha āyatanāni, asaññīnaṃ pañcāti ayamattho dassito hoti. Evañcetaṃ sampaṭicchitabbaṃ, aññathā rūpaloke phusituṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya pathavīādīnaṃ brahmānaṃ vacīghoso eva na siyā. Na hi paṭighaṭṭanānighaṃsamantarena saddappavatti atthi, na ca phusanasabhāvānaṃ katthaci aphusanabhāvatā sakkā viññātuṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanasaṅkhātassa ca bhūtattayassa abhāve rūpabhave rūpāyatanādīnampi sambhavo eva na siyā. Tasmā phusituṃ sakkuṇeyyatāyapi pathavīādīnaṃ tattha kāyindriyābhāvena tesaṃ phoṭṭhabbabhāvo na vutto. Evañca katvā rūpadhātuyaṃ tesaṃ sappaṭighavacanañca samatthitaṃ hoti. Vuttañhi “asaññasattānaṃ anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā”tiādi (paṭṭhā. 2.22.20).

And the intention with which the form-base is stated for non-percipient beings is to show this method: that for percipient beings also, odors and so forth should be taken separately. To demonstrate this method, it is said: “For non-percipient beings, two bases become manifest.” For even though their own faculty does not exist there, there is no transgression of the nature of form as the color-base; therefore, it is called simply the form-base. And by this demonstration of the method, the following meaning is shown: for percipient beings there are eight bases and for non-percipient beings five, when the three beginning with odor are included. And this should be accepted in this way; otherwise, because earth and so forth would be unable to be touched in the form realm, there would be no vocal sound of the Brahmās. For there is no production of sound without striking and friction, nor can a nature of non-contact be known anywhere in things that have a nature of contact. Moreover, in the absence of the triad of primary elements designated as the tangible-base, there would be no possibility even for the form-base and so forth in the form existence. Therefore, although earth and so forth are capable of being touched, their nature as tangible is not stated there due to the absence of the body-faculty. And having done so, the statement that they are 'with resistance' in the form realm is also established. For it is said: “For non-percipient beings, in dependence on one invisible and impingent great element, two great elements arise,” and so on.

Paṭigho ca nāma bhūtattayassa kāyappasādaṃ pati tannissayabhūtaghaṭṭanādvārena abhimukhabhāvo, idha pana taṃsabhāvatā. So ca phusituṃ asakkuṇeyyasabhāvassa ghaṭṭanāya abhāvato natthi. Yadi tattha asatipi visayini rūpāyatanaṃ gahetvā “dve āyatanānī”ti vuttaṃ, atha kasmā [M 2.0307] gandhāyatanādīni gahetvā “pañcāyatanānī”ti na vuttanti? Nayadassanavasena desanā pavattāti vuttovāyamattho. Atha vā tattha rūpāyatanasseva vacanaṃ kadāci aññabhūmikānaṃ pasādassa visayabhāvaṃ sandhāya, na pana itaresaṃ abhāvato, nāpi pariyāyenapi āyatanabhāvābhāvato. Asaññīnañhi rūpāyatanaṃ samānatalavāsīnaṃ vehapphalānaṃ, uparibhūmikānañca suddhāvāsānaṃ pasādassa visayabhāvaṃ gacchati, na pana gandharasāti tesaṃyeva tattha avacanaṃ yuttaṃ. Kathāvatthumhi ca nippariyāyena gandhāyatanādīnaṃ atthibhāvaṃ paṭijānantaṃ sandhāya paṭisedho kato.

And impingement is the state of confronting the sensitive body by the three primary elements, by means of striking the material phenomena which are its support; here, however, it is the state of having that nature of striking. And that confrontation does not exist, due to the absence of striking against that which has the nature of being unable to be touched. If, even when the sense faculty is not present there, the visible form base is taken and it is said, 'two bases,' then why, having taken the odor base and so on, is it not said, 'five bases'? The teaching proceeds by way of showing the method—this meaning has already been stated. Or else, the mention of only the visible form base there is sometimes with reference to its being an object for the sensitive matter of those in other planes, but not due to the absence of the others, nor due to the absence of their being bases even in a figurative sense. For the visible form base of the non-percipient beings becomes an object for the sensitive matter of the Vehapphala brahmās dwelling on the same plane and of the Suddhāvāsa beings in higher planes, but odors and tastes do not. Therefore, their non-mention there is appropriate. And in the Kathāvatthu, the refutation is made with reference to one who acknowledges the existence of the odor base and so on in a non-figurative sense.

Yadipi [V 2.0288] cetaṃ vacanaṃ tattha gandhāyatanādīnaṃ abhāvavibhāvanaṃ na hoti, atthibhāvadīpanampi pana aññavacanaṃ natthevāti? Nayidamevaṃ, aṭṭhakathāsu tattha nesaṃ atthibhāvassa niddhāretvā vuttattā. Yañhi aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ pāḷiyā na virujjhati, taṃ pāḷi viya pamāṇabhūtaṃ agarahitāya ācariyaparamparāya yāvajjatanā āgatattā. Tattha siyā – yaṃ pāḷiyā na virujjhati aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ, taṃ pamāṇaṃ, idaṃ pana virujjhatīti? Nayidamevaṃ, yathā na virujjhati, tathā paṭipāditattā. Cakkhādīnaṃ āyatanānaṃ, tannissayānañca viññāṇānaṃ sattasuññatāsandassanatthaṃ bhagavato dhātudesanāti āyatanabhāvena vuttānaṃyeva dhātubhāvadīpanato dhātubhāvassāpi tesaṃ avacanaṃ yujjati eva. Tasmā yathā pāḷiyā avirodho hoti, tathā cakkhudasakādivasena idha rūpagaṇanā katāti na ettha dhammatāvilomanāsaṅkāya okāsoti veditabbaṃ.

Even if this statement does not make clear the non-existence of the odor base, etc., there, is it not the case that there is also no other statement that makes clear their existence? No, it is not so, because in the commentaries their existence there has been ascertained and stated. For whatever commentary statement does not contradict the Pāḷi is authoritative—just like the Pāḷi—since it has come down through an unreproached lineage of teachers up to the present day. Here, there might be the objection: 'A commentary statement that does not contradict the Pāḷi is authoritative, but this one contradicts it.' No, it is not so, because it has been explained in a way that does not contradict it. The Blessed One's teaching of the elements is for the purpose of showing the voidness of a being with regard to the sense bases such as the eye, and the consciousnesses dependent on them. Therefore, since the nature as elements is shown only for those things spoken of in terms of their nature as sense bases, the non-statement of their nature as elements is indeed fitting. Therefore, it should be understood that the enumeration of form is done here by way of the eye-decad, etc., in such a way that there is no contradiction with the Pāḷi, and thus there is no room here for suspicion of a contradiction with the natural order.

Aññesu saṃsedajaopapātikayonikesūti rūpībrahme pana ṭhapetvā aññesu opapātikesu, saṃsedajesu cāti evamettha sambandho veditabbo. Opapātikavisesanañhettha aññaggahaṇaṃ, na saṃsedajavisesanaṃ asambhavato. Sati hi sambhave, byabhicāre ca visesanavisesitabbatā hoti. Kāmāvacaradevesu sabbakālaṃ paṭisandhipavattīsu yathāvuttāya santatiyā rūpānaṃ labbhanato vuttaṃ “tāni ca niccaṃ devesū”ti. Na hi te kadācipi vikalindriyā, abhāvakā ca hontīti. Cakkhu nesaṃ dasannaṃ pūraṇoti katvā cakkhudasako nāma, asādhāraṇena vā cakkhunā lakkhito dasako cakkhudasako. Evaṃ sesāti yathā cakkhudasako vutto, evaṃ sesāpi dasakā yojetvā veditabbā. “Saṃsedajūpapātayonīsu[M 2.0308], avakaṃsato tiṃsā”ti saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vivaranto “avakaṃsato panā”tiādimāha, taṃ panetaṃ pāḷiyā na sameti. Na hi pāḷiyaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ saṃsedajopapātikānaṃ aghānakānaṃ upapatti vuttā. Dhammahadayavibhaṅge hi “kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavanti, kassaci dasāyatanāni, kassaci aparāni dasāyatanāni, kassaci navāyatanāni, kassaci sattāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vuttaṃ, na vuttaṃ “aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti (vibha. 1007). Yadi hi aghānakassāpi upapatti siyā, tikkhattuṃ “dasāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vattabbaṃ siyā, tikkhattuñca “navāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti, na ca taṃ vuttaṃ.

In the phrase 'Among other beings born from moisture and spontaneous birth,' furthermore, having excluded the form-realm Brahmās, the connection here should be understood as referring to 'other spontaneously born beings and those born from moisture.' The term 'other' here qualifies 'spontaneously born,' not 'born from moisture,' because that is impossible. For when there is possibility and deviation, the state of being a qualifier and that which is to be qualified occurs. Regarding the deities of the sense sphere, because at all times—during rebirth-linking and during the course of existence—the continuity of forms as stated is obtainable, it is said, 'And those are always present among the deities.' For they are never deficient in faculties, nor are they ever without the sex-faculty. Because their eye is the completion of ten factors, it is called the 'eye-decad'; or, the decad characterized by the unique eye is the 'eye-decad.' Just as the eye-decad is explained, so too should the other decads be understood by applying the same logic. Desiring to explain the meaning stated in brief as 'Among those born from moisture and spontaneous birth, thirty are inferior,' he said, 'But as for the inferior ones...' and so on. However, this does not agree with the Pāḷi. For the Pāḷi does not state the rebirth of sense-sphere beings born from moisture or spontaneously who are without the smell-faculty. In the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga, it is stated: 'At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere, for some, eleven bases arise; for some, ten bases; for some, another ten bases; for some, nine bases; and for some, seven bases arise.' It is not stated, 'eight bases arise.' For if the rebirth of one without the smell-faculty were possible, the phrase 'ten bases arise' would have to be stated three times, and 'nine bases arise' also three times—but this is not stated.

Tattha upapattikkhaṇeti paṭisandhikkhaṇe. Ekādasāti paripuṇṇāyatanassa saddāyatanavajjāni ekādasa āyatanāni. Kassaci dasāyatanānīti andhassa cakkhāyatanavajjāni. Aparāni dasāyatanānīti [V 2.0289] badhirassa sotāyatanavajjāni. Navāyatanānīti andhabadhirassa cakkhusotāyatanavajjāni. Sattāyatanānīti gabbhaseyyakassa rūpagandharasakāyaphoṭṭhabbamanodhammāyatanavasena vuttaṃ. Yadi cakkhusotaghānavikalopi uppajjeyya, tassa aṭṭhevāyatanāni siyuṃ, na ca vuttaṃ “aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti. Tasmā nattheva cakkhusotaghānavikalo. Sati ca aghānakūpapattiyaṃ punapi “kassaci aparānipi dasāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vattabbaṃ siyā. Tathā ca sati yathā andhabadhirassa vasena “kassaci navāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti ekavāraṃ vuttaṃ, evaṃ andhāghānakassa, badhirāghānakassa ca vasena “kassaci aparāni navāyatanāni, kassaci aparānipi navāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vattabbaṃ siyāti attho. Evaṃ dhātupātubhāvādipañhānipi vattabbānīti vadanti. Ettha ca yathā “sattati ukkaṃsatotha rūpānī”ti padaṃ “saṃsedajūpapātayonīsū”ti ettha yonidvayavasena yojīyati, na evaṃ “avakaṃsato tiṃsā”ti idaṃ. Idaṃ pana saṃsedajayonivaseneva yojetabbaṃ. Ekayoganiddiṭṭhassāpi ekadeso sambandhaṃ labhatīti saṃsedajassa jaccandhabadhiraaghānakanapuṃsakassa jivhākāyavatthudasakānaṃ vasena tiṃsa rūpāni uppajjantīti vuttaṃ, na opapātikassāti ayamettha aṭṭhakathāyamadhippāyo.

Herein, 'at the moment of arising' means at the moment of relinking. 'Eleven' refers to the eleven bases, excluding the sound base, for one with complete bases. 'For some, ten bases' refers to the exclusion of the eye base for a blind person. 'Other ten bases' refers to the exclusion of the ear base for a deaf person. 'Nine bases' refers to the exclusion of the eye and ear bases for one who is blind and deaf. 'Seven bases' is stated for one lying in the womb, by way of the bases of form, odor, taste, body, tangible objects, mind, and mental objects. If one deficient in the eye, ear, and nose were to arise, there would be only eight bases for such a one, yet it is not stated, “eight bases appear.” Therefore, one deficient in the eye, ear, and nose does not exist. And if there were a rebirth deficient in the nose, it should also be said, “for some others, ten bases appear.” And that being so, just as it is stated once, “for some, nine bases appear,” by way of one who is blind and deaf, so too, by way of one who is blind and deficient in the nose, and one who is deaf and deficient in the nose, it should be said, “for some others, nine bases appear,” and “for still others, nine bases appear”—this is the meaning. In this way, they say, the questions concerning the manifestation of elements, and so forth, should also be stated. And here, just as the phrase 'seventy forms at the maximum' is connected in the context of 'in moisture-born and spontaneous births' by way of the two types of birth, this phrase 'thirty at the minimum' is not so connected. This latter, however, should be connected only by way of the moisture-born type of birth. Because even of something indicated by a single connection, a part may find its connection, it is stated that for a moisture-born being who is a congenitally blind, deaf, noseless eunuch, thirty forms arise by way of the decads of tongue, body, and heart-base—but not for a spontaneously born being. This is the intended meaning here in the commentary.

Ye [M 2.0309] pana “opapātikassa jaccandhabadhiraaghānakanapuṃsakassa jivhākāyavatthudasakānaṃ vasena tiṃsa rūpāni uppajjantīti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vutta”nti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. So hi pamādapāṭho. Evañca katvā āyatanayamakavaṇṇanāyaṃ “kāmadhātuyaṃ pana aghānako opapātiko natthi. Yadi bhaveyya, ‘kassaci aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī’ti vadeyyā”ti (yama. aṭṭha. āyatanayamaka 18-21) vuttaṃ. Apare panāhu “kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavantīti yāva ‘kassaci navāyatanānī’ti pāḷi opapātike sandhāya vuttā. Tasmā pubbenāparaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ avirodho siddho. Tathā ca yathāvuttapāḷiyā ayamatthavaṇṇanā aññadatthu saṃsandati sametiyevā”ti. Yaṃ paneke vadanti “opapātikaggahaṇena saṃsedajāpi saṅgayhanti. Tathā hi dhammahadayavibhaṅge ‘kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavantī’tiādīnaṃ (vibha. 1007) niddese ‘opapātikānaṃ petāna’ntiādinā (vibha. 1009) opapātikaggahaṇameva kataṃ, na saṃsedajaggahaṇa”nti, taṃ paripuṇṇāyatanānaṃyeva saṃsedajānaṃ opapātikesu saṅgahaṇavasena vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “saṃsedajayonikā paripuṇṇāyatanāparipuṇṇāyatanabhāvena opapātikasaṅgahaṃ katvā vuttā”ti, padhānāya [V 2.0290] vā yoniyā sabbaṃ paripuṇṇāyatanayoniṃ dassetuṃ “opapātikānanti vutta”nti ca, idha pana yonidvayaṃ sarūpeneva pakāsetuṃ, saṃsedajayonivaseneva ca avakaṃsato rūpapavattiṃ dassetuṃ opapātikayoniyā itaraṃ asaṅgahetvā “saṃsedajūpapātayonīsū”ti vuttaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ.

As for those who say, “In the Great Commentary, it is stated that for a spontaneously born being who is congenitally blind, deaf, noseless, and sexless, thirty forms arise by way of the decads of tongue, body, and heart-base,” that should not be accepted. For that is an erroneous reading due to carelessness. And for this reason, in the commentary on the Āyatanayamaka, it is said: “But in the sense-sphere realm, there is no spontaneously born being who is noseless. If there were, it would be said, ‘For some, eight bases appear.’” Others, however, say: “The Pāḷi passage from ‘For some, eleven bases appear’ up to ‘for some, nine bases arise’ is stated with reference to spontaneously born beings. Therefore, the non-contradiction between the earlier and later parts of the commentary is established. And so, this explanation of the meaning indeed accords and fits together with the aforesaid Pāḷi.” As for what some say: “By the term ‘spontaneously born,’ moisture-born beings are also included. For in the exposition of the Dhammahadayavibhaṅga, in the explanation of ‘At the moment of arising in the sense-sphere realm, for some, eleven bases appear,’ etc., only the term ‘spontaneously born’ is used, as in ‘of the spontaneously born spirits,’ etc., not the term ‘moisture-born,’”—this should be understood as having been stated by way of including among the spontaneously born only those moisture-born beings who have complete bases. For the commentary states: “Those of moisture-born origin are mentioned by including them within the category of the spontaneously born, by way of their having complete or incomplete bases.” Alternatively, to show all complete-base origins by way of the primary origin, it is said, “of the spontaneously born.” Here, however, to explain both types of origin in their own nature, and to show the arising of form at the minimum by way of the moisture-born origin alone, without including the other within the spontaneously born origin, it is said, “in moisture-born and spontaneous-birth origins.” All this should be investigated and then accepted.

Ukkaṃsāvakaṃsānaṃ pana antareti “sattati, tiṃsā”ti evaṃ vuttānaṃ rūpassa ukkaṃsāvakaṃsaparicchedānaṃ majjhe. Anurūpato vikappo veditabboti apāyesu andhassa cha cakkhudasakābhāvato, tathā badhirassa sotadasakābhāvato, andhabadhirassa pana pañca cakkhusotadasakābhāvatoti evamādinā nayena veditabbo. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ vuttamevāti.

However, between the maximum and minimum, that is, in the middle of the maximum and minimum divisions of form spoken of as 'seventy' and 'thirty,' a distinction should be understood according to suitability. This should be understood by the following method: in the planes of misery, for a blind person, there are six, due to the absence of the eye-decad; similarly for a deaf person, due to the absence of the ear-decad; and for a person who is blind and deaf, there are five, due to the absence of the eye- and ear-decads. Whatever is to be said here has already been said.

631. Cutipaṭisandhīnaṃ khandhādīhi aññamaññasamānatā abhedo. Asamānatā bhedo.

631. The similarity to one another of death and relinking, by way of the aggregates and so on, is non-difference. Dissimilarity is difference.

Ārammaṇatopi [M 2.0310] abhinnāti catūsu āruppesu tato tato cavitvā tattha tattheva upapajjantassa vasena vuttaṃ. Tatheva pana heṭṭhā, rūpabhave vā upapatti natthi. Arūpabhūmito cavitvā heṭṭhā upapatti nāma kāmabhave eva, tatthāpi tihetukapaṭisandhi eva. Rūpabhavato pana cuto duhetukopi hotīti vadanti. Amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā mahaggataajjhattārammaṇā dutiyacatutthāruppapaṭisandhi. Evaṃ nayamattassa dassitattā vuttaṃ, avuttañca sabbaṃ saṅgahetvā āha “ayaṃ tāva arūpabhūmīsuyeva nayo”ti. Rūpārūpāvacarānaṃ upacārassa balavatāya tato cavitvā duggatiyaṃ upapatti natthīti “ekaccasugaticutiyā”ti āha. Ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhīti ettha ekaccaggahaṇassa payojanaṃ maggitabbaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha adhippāyo siyā – nānattakāyanānattasaññīsu vuttā ekacce ca vinipātikā tihetukādipaṭisandhikā, tesaṃ paṭisandhiṃ vinipātikabhāvena “duggatipaṭisandhī”ti gahetvā sabbasugaticutiyā ca sā paṭisandhi hoti, na ekaccasugaticutiyā evāti tannivattanatthaṃ ekaccaduggatiggahaṇaṃ kataṃ.
