Apāyapaṭisandhi eva hi ekaccasugaticutiyā hoti, na sabbasugaticutiyāti. Atha vā duggatipaṭisandhi duvidhā ekaccasugaticutiyā anantarā, duggaticutiyā cāti. Tattha pacchimaṃ vajjetvā purimaṃyeva gahetuṃ vuttaṃ “ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhī”ti. Ahetukacutiyā sahetukapaṭisandhīti duhetukā ca tihetukā ca yojetabbā. Maṇḍūkadevaputtādīnaṃ viya hi ahetukacutiyā tihetukapaṭisandhipi hotīti.

The statement 'is not different even in terms of object' is said with reference to one who, having passed away from this or that of the four immaterial realms, is reborn in that very same realm. However, there is no rebirth below, or in the fine-material realm. When one passes away from the immaterial plane, rebirth below, so-called, occurs only in the sense-sphere realm, and even there, it is only a three-rooted rebirth-linking. But they say that one who has passed away from the fine-material realm can also be two-rooted. Immediately after a death-consciousness with a non-exalted, external object, the second and fourth immaterial rebirth-linking, which has an exalted, internal object, occurs. Since only a mere method has been shown thus, encompassing all that has been said and not said, he states, 'This, for now, is the method only in the immaterial planes.' Due to the strength of the access concentration of those in the fine-material and immaterial spheres, there is no rebirth in a woeful destination after passing away from there; therefore, he says, 'after the death of some in a happy destination.' Regarding 'some woeful rebirth-linking,' the purpose of taking up 'some' should be sought here. Herein, this might be the intention: some vinipātikas mentioned among those with 'diverse bodies and diverse perceptions' have three-rooted and other kinds of rebirth-linking. Taking their rebirth-linking as a 'woeful rebirth-linking' due to their state as vinipātikas, one might think that this rebirth-linking occurs after every death in a happy destination, and not only after the death of some. To prevent this, the term 'some woeful [rebirth-linking]' was used. For rebirth-linking in the plane of misery indeed occurs only after the death of some in a happy destination, not after every death in a happy destination. Alternatively, woeful rebirth-linking is twofold: that which is immediately after the death of some in a happy destination, and that which is after a death in a woeful destination. Therein, having excluded the latter, the term 'some woeful rebirth-linking' is said in order to take up only the former. Regarding the phrase 'after a rootless death, a rebirth-linking with roots,' both two-rooted and three-rooted rebirth-linkings should be applied. For, like the deity Maṇḍūka and others, even after a rootless death, a three-rooted rebirth-linking also occurs.

Tassa [V 2.0291] tassa viparītato ca yathāyogaṃ yojetabbanti “ekaccasugaticutiyā ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhī”tiādīsu bhedavisesesu “ekaccaduggaticutiyā ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhī”tiādinā yaṃ yaṃ yujjati, taṃ taṃ yojetabbanti attho. Yujjamānamattāpekkhanavasena napuṃsakaniddeso kato. Yojetabbanti vā bhāvatthatā daṭṭhabbā. “Amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya mahaggataajjhattārammaṇā”tiādīsu pana viparītayojanā na kātabbā. Na hi mahaggataajjhattārammaṇāya cutiyā arūpabhūmīsu amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇā paṭisandhi atthi. “Catukkhandhāya āruppacutiyā anantarā pañcakkhandhā kāmāvacarapaṭisandhī”ti etassa vipariyāyo sayameva yojito. “Atītārammaṇāya cutiyā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhī”ti [M 2.0311] etassa ca vipariyāyo natthi eva. Bhedaviseso eva ca evaṃ vitthārena dassito, abhedaviseso pana ekekasmiṃ bhede tattha tattheva cutipaṭisandhiyojanāvasena veditabbo “pañcakkhandhāya kāmāvacaracutiyā pañcakkhandhā kāmāvacarā…pe… avitakkaavicārāya avitakkāvicārā”ti. Catukkhandhāya pana catukkhandhā sayameva yojitā. Eteneva nayena sakkā viññātunti pañcakkhandhādīsu abhedaviseso na dassitoti.

The meaning of 'And in each case of reversal, it should be applied as is appropriate' is as follows: in specific distinctions such as 'for some, from passing away in a happy destination, there is rebirth-linking in a woeful destination,' whatever is suitable, such as 'for some, from passing away in a woeful destination, there is rebirth-linking in a woeful destination,' that very thing should be applied. The indication in the neuter gender was made by way of considering only the matter being applied. Alternatively, for the word 'yojetabbaṃ' (should be applied), its abstract sense should be understood. However, in cases such as 'after a death with a non-exalted, external object, a rebirth-linking with an exalted, internal object,' the reverse application should not be made. For after a passing away with an exalted, internal object in the formless realms, there is no rebirth-linking with a non-exalted, external object. The reverse of 'from a passing away in the formless plane with four aggregates, there is, immediately after, a rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere with five aggregates' has been applied by himself. And for 'from a passing away with a past object, there is a rebirth-linking with a present object,' a reverse simply does not exist. And thus only the specific distinction has been shown in detail. But the non-distinction should be understood in each case by way of applying the passing away and rebirth-linking in that very same state, such as: 'from a passing away in the sense-sphere with five aggregates, [there is] a sense-sphere [rebirth-linking] with five aggregates... from [a passing away] without initial thought and sustained thought, [there is a rebirth-linking] without initial thought and sustained thought.' However, for [the passing away with] four aggregates, [the rebirth-linking with] four aggregates has been applied by himself. Because it can be understood by this very method, the non-distinction in cases of the five aggregates, etc., was not shown.

632. Itīti evaṃ vuttappakārena. Etaṃ viññāṇaṃ avijjādisahakārikāraṇasahitassa saṅkhārassa vasena laddhappaccayaṃ. Bāhirakakappitassa adhipatiṭṭhanakassa abhāvato rūpārūpadhammamattaṃ. Tenāha “na satto na jīvo”ti. Upetīti vuccati tathāvohāramattaṃ, atthato pana paccayasāmaggiyā bhavantarabhāvena uppajjanamattanti adhippāyo. Tenāha “tassa cā”tiādi. Tato hetuṃ vināti tattha hetuṃ vinā. Manussacutipaṭisandhikkamenāti manussacutito manussapaṭisandhikkamena. Evañhi pākaṭaggahaṇaṃ ubhayavisesanaṃ hoti. Pākaṭatā cettha tadāsannakkhandhavasena veditabbā “cavamāne upapajjamāne”tiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.247) viya. Manussacutipaṭisandhikkamenāti vā manussacutito yassa kassaci paṭisandhikkamena. Tathā hi vakkhati “nissayaṃ assādayamānaṃ vā anāssādayamānaṃ vā”ti (visuddhi. 2.632).

632. Thus, it is said in the manner stated. This consciousness is conditioned by formations accompanied by auxiliary causes such as ignorance. Since there is no controlling entity imagined by outsiders, it is merely phenomena of form and formlessness. Therefore, he says, “There is no being, no soul.” The phrase “it comes to be” is merely a conventional expression; in reality, however, the meaning is merely arising as another state of existence due to the assemblage of conditions. Hence, he says, “and for that,” etc. The phrase “without that cause” means “without a cause there.” The phrase “by way of the sequence of a human’s passing away and rebirth-linking” means by way of the sequence from a human’s passing away to a human’s rebirth-linking. For in this way, the term “manifest” becomes a qualifier for both. And the manifestness here should be understood by way of the aggregates proximate to that, as in such phrases as “while passing away and being reborn,” etc. Or, the phrase “by way of the sequence of a human’s passing away and rebirth-linking” means by way of the sequence from a human’s passing away to the rebirth-linking of anyone whatsoever. For so he will say, “either delighting in a support or not delighting in a support.”

Sarasenāti sabhāvena, parikkhīṇāyusaṅkhāratāyāti attho. Upakkamenāti attanā, parena vā katena sīsacchedanādiupakkamena. Sabbesaṃ aṅgapaccaṅgasandhīnaṃ bandhanāni sabbaṅgapaccaṅgasandhibandhanāni, tesaṃ chedakānaṃ. Sannipātanti patanaṃ pavatti. Hadayappadesopi anukkamena [V 2.0292] sussitvā appāvaseso hoti, pageva kāyoti āha “kamena upasussamāne sarīre”ti. Tenevāha “taṅkhaṇāvasesahadayavatthusannissita”nti. “Niruddhesu cakkhādīsū”ti idaṃ gabbhaseyyakānaṃ āyatanānaṃ anupubbuppatti viya nirodhopi anupubbato hotīti adhippāyena vuttaṃ, atimandabhāvūpagamanataṃ vā sandhāya “niruddhesū”ti vuttaṃ, na anavasesanirodhaṃ. Pañcadvārikaviññāṇānantarampi hi pubbe cuti dassitā. Yamake ca “yassa cakkhāyatanaṃ nirujjhati, tassa manāyatanaṃ nirujjhatīti? Āmantā. Yassa [M 2.0312] vā pana manāyatanaṃ nirujjhati, tassa cakkhāyatanaṃ nirujjhatīti? Sacittakānaṃ acakkhukānaṃ cavantānaṃ tesaṃ manāyatanaṃ nirujjhati, no ca tesaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ nirujjhati. Sacakkhukānaṃ cavantānaṃ tesaṃ manāyatanañca nirujjhati, cakkhāyatanañca nirujjhatī”tiādinā (yama. 1.āyatanayamaka.120) cakkhāyatanādīnaṃ cuticittena saha nirodho vuttoti.

The term 'sarasena' means 'by its own nature'; the meaning is 'by the state of having the life-formation completely exhausted'. 'Upakkamena' refers to an assault, such as beheading and so on, committed either by oneself or by another. The term 'sabbaṅgapaccaṅgasandhibandhanāni' refers to the bonds of all major and minor limb joints; 'tesaṃ chedakānaṃ' means 'of those that sever them.' 'Sannipātanti' means falling or occurrence. Even the heart region gradually dries up and has little remaining; how much more so the body! Therefore, it is said: "as the body gradually dries up." For that very reason, it is said: "dependent on the heart-base that remains only for that moment." The phrase "when the eye, etc., have ceased" is said with the intention that, just as the sense bases of beings in the womb arise sequentially, so too their cessation occurs sequentially. Or, "have ceased" is said in reference to their having reached a state of extreme weakness, not in reference to cessation without remainder. For indeed, death was previously shown to occur even immediately after the five-door consciousness. And in the Yamaka, by the text beginning, "For one for whom the eye-base is ceasing, for him is the mind-base ceasing? Yes. Or again, for one for whom the mind-base is ceasing, for him is the eye-base ceasing? For those with mind but without eyes who are passing away, for them the mind-base is ceasing, but their eye-base is not ceasing. For those with eyes who are passing away, for them both the mind-base is ceasing and the eye-base is ceasing," the cessation of the eye-base and so on, together with the death-consciousness, is stated.

Hadayavatthumatteti hadayavatthupadesamatte. Na hi hadayavatthuṃ nissāya kāyindriyaṃ pavattati. Hadayavatthupi tadā ātape pakkhittaharitatālapaṇṇaṃ viya appāvasesaṃ hotīti “taṅkhaṇāvasesahadayavatthusannissita”nti vuttanti vadanti. Itaravatthūnaṃ pana sakiccāsamatthatāya kevalaṃ hadayavatthusannissitameva, tadā viññāṇaṃ hotīti vuttaṃ “taṅkhaṇāvasesahadayavatthusannissita”nti. Mātughātādi, mahaggatamaññaṃ vā tādisaṃ garukaṃ nāma. Samāsevitaṃ abhiṇhaso kataṃ. Āsannaṃ maraṇakāle kataṃ, yadā tadā vā katampi paribyattaṃ hutvā anussaritaṃ. Pubbakataṃ aparāpariyāyavedanīyaṃ. Laddho avaseso avijjādiko viññāṇassa paccayo etenāti laddhāvasesapaccayo, saṅkhāro. Etena vipaccituṃ katokāsaṃ yathūpacitaṃ kusalākusalacetanamāha. Kammanimittaṃ nāma yaṃ vatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā āyūhanakāle kammaṃ āyūhati, taṃ. Atīte kappakoṭisatasahassamatthakepi hi kamme kate vipaccanakāle āgantvā kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā upatiṭṭhati. Gatinimittaṃ nāma nibbattanakaokāse eko vaṇṇo. So ca niraye nibbattanārahassa “aggijālavaṇṇādiko”tiādinā heṭṭhā vuttoyeva. Avijjāpaṭicchāditādīnave tasmiṃ kammādivisaye paṭisandhiviññāṇassa ārammaṇabhāvena uppattiṭṭhānabhūte.

The term 'hadayavatthumatta' means 'merely in the location of the heart-base.' For indeed, the body faculty does not function dependent on the heart-base. At that time, the heart-base also becomes one with little remainder, like a fresh green palm leaf thrown into the sun's heat—thus it is said, 'dependent on the heart-base remaining for that moment,' so they say. However, because the other bases are incapable of performing their own functions, consciousness at that time is solely dependent on the heart-base; for this reason, it is stated, 'dependent on the heart-base remaining for that moment.' 'Grave' (garuka) is the name for matricide and the like, or sublime kamma (mahaggataṃ), or another such weighty deed. 'Frequently practiced' means repeatedly done. 'Proximate' means done at the time of death, or, though done at any time, that which, having become clear, is recollected. 'Previously done' means to be experienced in another turn. The formation (saṅkhāro) is called laddhāvasesapaccayo because by it the remaining conditions for consciousness, such as ignorance and so on, have been acquired. By this, it refers to the wholesome or unwholesome volition, accumulated accordingly, which has been given the opportunity to ripen. 'Kamma-nimitta' is that very object which, having been taken as the objective field, one exerts kamma upon at the time of exertion. Indeed, even when kamma was done over a hundred thousand crores of eons ago in the past, at the time of ripening, it comes and presents itself either as kamma or as a kamma-nimitta. 'Gati-nimitta' is a single visual form in the place of rebirth. And for one fit to be reborn in hell, this has already been spoken of below with the words 'the appearance of a mass of flames, etc.' In that objective sphere of kamma and so forth, which has the danger of being concealed by ignorance and has become the objective field and place of arising for the rebirth-linking consciousness.

Taṇhāya appahīnattā eva, purimuppannāya ca santatiyā tathāpariṇatattā paṭisandhiṭṭhānābhimukhaṃ viññāṇaṃ ninnapoṇapabbhāraṃ hutvā pavattatīti āha “taṇhā nāmetī”ti. Sahajātasaṅkhārāti [V 2.0293] cutiāsannajavanaviññāṇasahajātā cetanā, sabbepi vā phassādayo. Tasmiṃ paṭisandhiṭṭhāne kammādivisaye viññāṇaṃ khipanti. Khipantā viya tasmiṃ visaye paṭisandhivasena viññāṇapatiṭṭhānassa hetubhāvena pavattantīti attho. Tanti taṃ viññāṇaṃ. Cutipaṭisandhitadāsannaviññāṇānaṃ santativasena viññāṇanti upanītekattaṃ[M 2.0313]. Taṇhāya nāmiyamānaṃ…pe… pavattatīti namanakhipanapurimanissayajahanaaparanissayassādananissayarahitapavattanāni santativasena tassevekassa viññāṇassa honti, na aññassāti dasseti. Santativasenāti ca vadanto “tadevidaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anañña”nti (ma. ni. 1.396) imañca micchāgāhaṃ paṭikkhipati. Sati hi nānattanaye santativasena ekattanayo hotīti. Ettha ca orimatīrarukkhavinibaddharajju viya purimabhavattabhāvavinibaddhaṃ kammādiārammaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, puriso viya viññāṇaṃ, tassa mātikātikkamanicchā viya taṇhā, atikkamanapayogo viya khipanakasaṅkhārā, yathā ca so puriso paratīre patiṭṭhahamāno paratīrarukkhavinibaddhaṃ kiñci assādayamāno vā anassādayamāno vā kevalaṃ pathaviyaṃ sakabalapayogeheva patiṭṭhāti, evamidampi bhavantarattabhāvavinibaddhaṃ hadayavatthusaṅkhātaṃ nissayaṃ pañcavokārabhave assādayamānaṃ, catuvokārabhave anassādayamānaṃ vā kevalaṃ ārammaṇasampayuttakammeheva pavattati. Tattha assādayamānanti pāpuṇantaṃ, paṭilabhamānanti attho.

Because of the very non-abandonment of craving, and because of the previously arisen continuity having matured in such a way, consciousness, having become inclined, bent, and sloped towards the site of rebirth-linking, proceeds. Therefore, he said, 'craving leads it.' Co-nascent formations are the volitions co-arisen with the death-proximate impulsion consciousnesses, or all the mental factors beginning with contact. They cast consciousness into that object, such as kamma, at the site of rebirth-linking. The meaning is: as if casting it, they proceed in that object by way of rebirth-linking, by being the cause for the establishment of consciousness. That is that consciousness. By way of continuity, the consciousnesses of death, rebirth-linking, and those proximate to them are brought to a state of oneness as 'consciousness.' By the text 'Being led by craving... it proceeds,' he shows that the acts of bending, casting, abandoning the former support, obtaining the subsequent support, and proceeding without a support belong, by way of continuity, to that very single consciousness, and not to another. And by saying 'by way of continuity,' he also rejects this wrong view: 'This very consciousness runs on, transmigrates, it is not another.' For when the method of diversity exists, there is the method of oneness by way of continuity. And here, the object, such as kamma, bound to the state of existence in a previous life, should be seen like a rope tied to a tree on the near shore; consciousness like the man; craving like his desire to cross the channel; and the propelling formations like the effort to cross over. And just as that man, while establishing himself on the far shore, establishes himself merely on the ground by his own strength and effort, whether obtaining or not obtaining something tied to a tree on the far shore, so too this consciousness proceeds merely by means of kamma associated with its object, whether obtaining the support called the heart-base, which is bound to the state of existence in the next life, in the five-constituent existence, or not obtaining it in the four-constituent existence. Therein, 'obtaining' means reaching, attaining; this is the meaning.

Bhavantarādipaṭisandhānatoti bhavantarassa aññabhavassa ādipaṭisandhānabhāvato. Bhavantarādayo vā bhavayonigativiññāṇaṭṭhitisattāvāsantarāni, tesaṃ paṭisandhānatoti attho. Tadetaṃ viññāṇaṃ nāpi idhāgataṃ imasmiṃyeva bhave uppannattā. Kammanti paṭisandhijanakaṃ kammaṃ. Saṅkhārāti cutiāsannajavanaviññāṇasahagatā khipanakasaṅkhārā. Natīti namanavasena pavattataṇhā. Visayo kammādi.

The term 'bhavantarādipaṭisandhānato' means 'because of being the initial connection to another existence,' that is, to a different existence. Alternatively, 'bhavantarādayo' (another existence and so on) refers to another existence, another womb, another destiny, another consciousness-station, and another abode of beings; 'tesaṃ paṭisandhānato' means 'because of their connection.' That consciousness has not come here, for it has arisen right within this very existence. 'Kamma' refers to the kamma that generates rebirth-linking. 'Saṅkhārā' are the propelling formations accompanied by the death-proximate impulsion consciousness. 'Nati' refers to craving that proceeds by way of inclination. The 'object' refers to kamma and so on.

633. Saddapaṭighosādīnaṃ satipi paccayapaccayuppannabhāve santānabandho na pākaṭoti tesaṃ ekattanānattabhāvaṃ anāmasitvā anāgamanātītahetusamuppādameva dassento “ettha cā”tiādimāha. Saddādihetukāti ettha paṭighoso saddahetuko. Padīpo padīpantarādihetuko. Muddā lañchanahetukā. Chāyā ādāsādiabhimukhamukhādihetukā. Honti aññatra agantvāti saddādipaccayadesaṃ anupagantvā saddādihetukā honti tato pubbe abhāvā. Evaṃ idampi paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ na hetudesaṃ gantvā taṃhetukaṃ hoti tato pubbe abhāvā. Tasmā na idaṃ hetudesato [V 2.0294] purimabhavato idhāgataṃ paṭighosādayo viya saddādidesato, nāpi tattha hetunā vinā uppannaṃ saddādīhi vinā [M 2.0314] paṭighosādayo viyāti attho. Atha vā honti aññatra agantvāti pubbe paccayadese sannihitā hutvā tato aññatra gantvā tappaccayā na honti uppattito pubbe abhāvā, nāpi saddādipaccayā na honti, evaṃ idampīti vuttanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.

633. Although for sound, echoes, and so on, the state of being condition and conditioned exists, their binding into a continuum is not evident. Therefore, without considering their state of being one or different, and showing only dependent origination from a past cause that does not involve coming, he said, 'Here also...' and so on. In the phrase 'caused by sound, etc.': here, an echo is caused by a sound. A lamp is caused by another lamp, etc. A seal is caused by a stamp. A reflection is caused by a face, etc., facing a mirror, etc. 'They arise without going elsewhere' means that without approaching the place of the cause, such as sound, they are caused by sound, etc., because they did not exist before that. Similarly, this rebirth-linking consciousness does not become caused by that cause by going to the place of the cause, because it did not exist before that. Therefore, this consciousness has not come here from the place of the cause—the previous existence—just as echoes, etc., do not come from the place of sound, etc.; nor has it arisen there without a cause, just as echoes, etc., do not arise without sound, etc. This is the meaning. Alternatively, 'they arise without going elsewhere' means: having been previously present in the place of the cause, they do not then go from there to another place and become caused by that, because they did not exist before their arising; nor are they without causes such as sound, etc. Similarly, this too should be connected in the way already stated.

Natthi ekatā ekasantānekattepi aññasseva viññāṇassa pātubhavanato. Nāpi nānatā santānabandhato padīpo viya. Khaṇikāya hi padīpajālāya santānekattaṃ upādāya so evāti vuccati, atthakiccañca sādheti, evamidhāpi daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Yadi hī”tiādinā santānabandhe ekantaṃ ekatāya, nānatāya ca aggahetabbataṃ, gahaṇe ca dosaṃ dasseti. Esa nayoti atidesena bījaṅkurādīsu sabbahetuhetusamuppannesu yathāsambhavaṃ yojanā kātabbāti dasseti. Idhāpi hi hetuhetusamuppannaviññāṇānaṃ ekantamekatte sati na manussagatito devagati sambhūtā siyā. Ekantanānatte na kammavato phalaṃ siyā, tato “rattassa bījaṃ rattassa phala”ntiādikassa viya “bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, rohitasso nāma isi ahosi”ntiādikassa (saṃ. ni. 1.107) vohārassa lopo siyā, tasmā ettha santānabandhesu hetuhetusamuppannesu na ekantamekatā vā nānatā vā upagantabbā na gahetabbā. Ettha ca ekantaekatāpaṭisedhena “sayaṃkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkha”nti (vibha. mūlaṭī. 227) imaṃ diṭṭhiṃ nivāreti, ekantanānatāpaṭisedhena “paraṃkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkha”nti (vibha. mūlaṭī. 227), hetuhetusamuppannatāvacanena “adhiccasamuppanna”nti (vibha. mūlaṭī. 227) imaṃ diṭṭhiṃ nivāreti.

There is no oneness, for even in the oneness of a single continuum, another consciousness appears. Nor is there diversity, like a lamp, due to the binding of the continuum. For in the momentary flame of a lamp, by assuming the oneness of the continuum, it is called 'the same,' and it fulfills its purpose; so too should this be understood here. By the phrase 'If indeed,' etc., it is shown that in the binding of a continuum, absolute oneness or diversity should not be grasped, and that grasping either leads to fault. 'This is the method' indicates that by way of analogy, this should be applied as appropriate to seeds, sprouts, etc., in all cases of phenomena arisen from cause and condition. Here too, if consciousnesses arisen from cause and condition were absolutely one, then a divine destiny could not arise from a human destiny. If they were absolutely diverse, there would be no fruit for the doer of kamma. Then, expressions such as 'A red seed, a red fruit' or 'Venerable sir, formerly I was a sage named Rohitassa' would cease to exist. Therefore, in these continuums bound by cause and condition, neither absolute oneness nor absolute diversity should be adopted or grasped. Here, by refuting absolute oneness, the view 'Pleasure and pain are self-made' is eliminated. By refuting absolute diversity, the view 'Pleasure and pain are made by another' is eliminated. And by stating that they arise from cause and condition, the view 'They arise without cause' is eliminated.

634. Tatthāti phaluppattiṭṭhāne. Aññassāti yena taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ, tato aññassa. Aññatoti yaṃ taṃ kammaṃ nibbattitaṃ, tato aññato. “Dhammamattaṃ bhavantaramupetī”ti (visuddhi. 2.632; vibha. aṭṭha. 227; mahāni. aṭṭha. 27; paṭi. ma. aṭṭha. 1.1.105) vuttattā phalassa upabhuñjake ca asati kassa taṃ phalaṃ siyāti anuyuñjeti. Tatrāti tasmiṃ yathāvutte anuyoge.

634. 'Therein' refers to the place where the fruit arises. 'Of another' means of someone other than the one by whom that kamma was done. 'From another' means from a cause other than that kamma which was produced. Because it is said, 'A mere phenomenon passes on to another existence,' and since there is no experiencer of the fruit, he questions: 'To whom would that fruit belong?' 'Therein' refers to that aforementioned question.

Tatthāti ekasantāne. Yasmiṃ dhammapuñje kammaṃ nibbattaṃ, tasseva santāneti attho. Etassa atthassāti hetuphalānaṃ atthato aññattepi teneva [M 2.0315] hetuphalabhāvena sambandhattā taṃ phalaṃ “aññassa, aññato”ti vā na vattabbanti etassa atthassa. Catumadhuraalattakarasādibhāvanā ambamātuluṅgādibījānaṃ [V 2.0295] abhisaṅkhāro. Ettha ca abhisaṅkhataṃ bījaṃ viya kammavā satto, abhisaṅkhāro viya kammaṃ, bījassa aṅkurādippabandho viya sattassa paṭisandhiviññāṇādippabandho. Tatthuppannassa madhurassa rattakesarassa vā phalassa vā tasseva bījassa, tato eva ca abhisaṅkhārato bhāvo viya kammakārakasseva sattassa, taṃkammato eva ca phalassa bhāvo veditabbo. Bālasarīre kataṃ vijjāpariyāpuṇanaṃ, sippasikkhanaṃ, osadhappayogo ca na vuḍḍhasarīraṃ gacchanti. Atha ca tannimittaṃ vijjāpāṭavaṃ sippajānanaṃ, anāmayatā ca vuḍḍhasarīre honti, na ca tāni aññassa honti taṃsantatipariyāpanne eva vuḍḍhasarīre uppajjanato, na ca yathāpayuttena vijjāpariyāpuṇanādinā vinā tāni aññato honti tadabhāve abhāvato, evaṃ idhāpi santāne yaṃ phalaṃ, etaṃ nāññassa. Na ca aññatoti yojetabbaṃ. Etena ca saṅkhārābhāve phalābhāvameva dasseti, na aññapaccayanivāraṇaṃ karoti.

‘Therein’ means in a single continuum. The meaning is: in whichever aggregate of phenomena the kamma is produced, it is in that very continuum. For the purpose of this meaning: even when cause and fruit are distinct in essence, because they are connected by that very nature of cause and fruit, that fruit cannot be said to belong to ‘another’ or to arise ‘from another’. The infusion with the four sweets, lac-dye juice, and so forth, is the preparation of the seeds of mango, citron, and so on. And here, the being who has kamma is like the prepared seed, kamma is like the preparation, and the continuity of the rebirth-linking consciousness and so on of the being is like the continuity of the sprout and so on of the seed. Just as the sweet or red-filamented fruit that arises therein belongs to that very seed and arises from that very preparation, so too should the fruit be understood as belonging to the very being who is the doer of the kamma and arising from that very kamma. The learning of knowledge, the training in crafts, and the application of medicine done in a child’s body do not pass over to the adult body. And yet, due to that cause, sharpness of knowledge, skill in crafts, and freedom from illness arise in the adult body. And these do not belong to another, because they arise in the adult body that is included in that very continuum. Nor do they come from another, for without the previously applied learning of knowledge and so forth, they would not exist, due to their absence in the absence of that cause. Similarly, here too, whatever fruit is in the continuum, it is not of another. And it should be construed as not from another. And by this, it shows only the absence of fruit in the absence of formations; it does not negate other conditions.

Yampi vuttaṃ, tattha vadāmāti vacanaseso. Tattha vā upabhuñjake asati siddhā bhuñjakasammutīti sambandho. Phalatīti sammuti phalatisammuti.

As to that which was said, ‘therein we shall reply’ is the remaining part of the statement. Or, the connection is this: when there is no experiencer, the designation ‘experiencer’ is established. The designation ‘it bears fruit’ is the designation-of-bearing-fruit.

Rukkhasaṅkhātānaṃ dhammānanti rukkhapaññattiyā upādānabhūtānaṃ bhūtupādāyadhammānaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā yathā khandhasantāne kusalākusalacetanuppattiyaṃ “puññaṃ karoti, pāpaṃ karotī”ti kattuvohāro, evaṃ tassa phaluppattiyaṃ “sukhaṃ anubhavati, dukkhaṃ anubhavatī”ti upabhuñjakavohāro, tasmā na ettha khandhavinimuttena aññena upabhuñjakena nāma koci attho atthīti.

The phenomena designated as 'trees' are the primary and derived material phenomena that serve as the basis for the designation 'tree'. Therefore, just as in the continuity of the aggregates, when wholesome or unwholesome volition arises, the conventional expression 'one does merit, one does evil' is used for a doer, so too, when its fruit arises, the conventional expression 'one experiences happiness, one experiences suffering' is used for an experiencer. Therefore, herein, there is no need for any so-called experiencer apart from the aggregates.

635. Evaṃ santepīti asaṅkantipātubhāve tattha ca yathāvuttadosapariharaṇe sati, siddheti attho. Pavattikkhaṇeyevāti saṅkhārānaṃ pavattamānakkhaṇe eva. Pavattito pubbeti kammāyūhanakkhaṇato pubbe, avijjamānatāya samānattā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Pacchā cāti vipaccanappapattito pacchā ca.

635. Even so: the meaning is that it is established when there is the appearance of non-transference and, in that regard, the avoidance of the aforementioned faults. 'At the very moment of occurrence' means: precisely at the moment formations are occurring. 'Before the occurrence' means: before the moment of kamma-accumulation; it is said thus because of the similarity in being non-existent. 'And after' means: and after its attainment of ripening.

Avipakkavipākā katattā ce paccayā, vipakkavipākānampi katattaṃ samānanti tesampi phalāvahatā siyāti āsaṅkānivattanatthaṃ āha “na ca niccaṃ phalāvahā”ti.

To dispel the doubt that might arise—'If formations whose results have not yet ripened are conditions because they have been done, and since the state of having been done is also the same for formations whose results have ripened, might those too be fruit-bearing?'—it is said, 'Nor are they always fruit-bearing'.

“Na [M 2.0316][V 2.0296] vijjamānattā avijjamānattā vā”ti etena vijjamānattaṃ, avijjamānattañca nissāya vuttadose pariharati. Tassā pāṭibhogakiriyāya, bhaṇḍakīṇanakiriyāya, iṇaggahaṇakiriyāya vā karaṇamattaṃ taṃkiriyākaraṇamattaṃ, tadeva tadatthaniyyātane paṭibhaṇḍadāne, iṇadāne ca paccayo hoti, aphalitaniyyātanādiphalanti attho.

'Not due to existence or non-existence'—by this, he avoids the stated faults that depend on existence and non-existence. Merely the doing of that action—be it the act of guaranteeing, the act of buying goods, or the act of taking a loan—that very act of doing is the condition for the handing over for that purpose, for the payment for the goods, and for the payment of the debt. The meaning is: it has as its result the handing over, etc., which has not yet come to fruition.

636. Sammohavighātatthanti bāttiṃsāya viññāṇesu yathāvuttasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ, pavattiyañca paccayabhāve vibhajja avibhāvite pavattanakasammohassa apanayanatthaṃ.

636. For the purpose of dispelling confusion means: for the purpose of removing the potential confusion that would arise if the state of the aforesaid formations as a condition for the thirty-two types of consciousness—both at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence—were not analyzed and clearly shown.

Puññābhisaṅkhāreti niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Avisesenāti “tihetuko tihetukassā”tiādikaṃ bhedaṃ akatvā sāmaññato, piṇḍavasenāti attho. Sabbattha upanissayapaccayo balavakammassa vasena yojetabbo. “Dubbalañhi kammaṃ upanissayapaccayo na hotī”ti paṭṭhānasaṃvaṇṇanāya dassitametaṃ. Rūpāvacarapañcakusalacetanābhedoti “ṭhapetvā abhiññāppatta”nti visesetvā vattabbaṃ, na vā vattabbaṃ vipākassa paccayabhāvakathāya avipākārahassa pasaṅgābhāvato. Abhiññācetanāya hi avipākatā heṭṭhā vibhāvitā eva. Avisesena panāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Pañcannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānanti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ.

In `puññābhisaṅkhāreti` (meritorious formation), the locative case is used for determination. `Avisesena` (without distinction) means without making a distinction such as 'a tri-rooted [meritorious formation] for a tri-rooted [resultant consciousness],' but generally, by way of a collection; this is the meaning. Everywhere, the decisive support condition should be connected by means of strong kamma. For it was shown in the commentary on the Paṭṭhāna: 'Weak kamma does not become a decisive support condition.' Regarding the fivefold division of wholesome volitions of the form realm, it should be specified by saying 'excluding the volition that has attained supernormal knowledge,' or it need not be specified, because in the discussion of the conditionality for a result, there is no involvement of a formation incapable of yielding a result. For the non-resultant nature of the volition associated with supernormal knowledge has already been explained below. In the phrase `avisesena pana` (but without distinction) also, this is the same method. It should be connected by supplying the phrase 'for the five resultant consciousnesses'.

Pañcannanti cakkhusotaviññāṇānaṃ, sampaṭicchanamanodhātuyā, dvinnaṃ santīraṇamanoviññāṇadhātūnañcāti etesaṃ pañcannaṃ. Tathevāti dvedhā eva. Kathaṃ pana iṭṭhārammaṇeyeva pavattanakāni kusalavipākaviññāṇāni duggatiyaṃ pavattantīti āha “niraye mahāmoggallānattherassā”tiādi. Thero hi tattha iddhiyā vassaṃ nimminitvā katipayaṃ velaṃ nirayaggiṃ vūpasametvā tesaṃ dhammaṃ deseti.

`Pañcannaṃ` (for the five) refers to these five: the eye- and ear-consciousnesses, the receiving mind-element, and the two investigating mind-consciousness elements. `Tatheva` (similarly) means in a twofold manner only. But how do wholesome resultant consciousnesses, which arise only in relation to desirable objects, occur in a woeful state? He says, 'in hell, of the Elder Mahāmoggallāna,' etc. For the Elder, there, having created rain by psychic power and having pacified the hell-fire for some time, teaches the Dhamma to them.

Sveva kāmāvacaro puññābhisaṅkhāro. Avisesena pana puññābhisaṅkhāroti kāmāvacaraṃ, rūpāvacarañcāti duvidhampi puññābhisaṅkhāraṃ ekajjhaṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

That very meritorious formation is of the sense sphere. The phrase `avisesena pana puññābhisaṅkhāro` (but meritorious formation without distinction), however, collectively includes both kinds of meritorious formation: that of the sense sphere and that of the form sphere.

Dvādasākusalacetanābhedoti ettha uddhaccasahagatacetanāya gahaṇe kāraṇaṃ na dissati, vicāretabbametaṃ. Ekassa viññāṇassa tatheva [M 2.0317] paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatteti ekasseva paccayabhāvaniyamo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatte. Pavatte hi sattannampi paccayoti adhippāyo.

Here, regarding the twelvefold division of unwholesome volitions, the reason for including volition accompanied by restlessness is not apparent; this should be investigated. The determination of being a condition for only one consciousness is at rebirth-linking, not in the course of existence. For in the course of existence, it is a condition for all seven. This is the intention.

Rūpabhave [V 2.0297] catunnanti akusalavipākānaṃ cakkhusotaviññāṇasampaṭicchanasantīraṇānaṃ. Tāni pana ekantato aniṭṭhārammaṇāni, rūpabhave ca kathaṃ aniṭṭhārammaṇasamāyogoti āha “so ca kho”tiādi. “Tathā kāmāvacaradevalokepi aniṭṭharūpādayo natthī”ti idaṃ yebhuyyavasena vuttaṃ. Bahulañhi tesaṃ iṭṭhā eva rūpādayo upaṭṭhahanti, kadāci aniṭṭhaṃ. Devānañhi kesañcideva pubbanimittapātubhāvakālādīsu milātamālādianiṭṭhārammaṇasamāyogo hotīti.

In the form realm, 'of the four' means of the unwholesome-resultant eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, receiving-consciousness, and investigating-consciousness. These, however, have exclusively undesirable objects. But how can there be an association with undesirable objects in the form realm? Therefore, he said what begins with 'so ca kho'. The statement, 'Similarly, in the sense-sphere heavenly realms, undesirable forms, etc., do not exist,' was said for the most part. For, indeed, mostly only desirable forms, etc., appear to them; the undesirable appears only sometimes. Indeed, for only some devas, at times such as the appearance of the preliminary sign [of death], does the association with undesirable objects such as withered garlands occur.

637. Yattha vitthārappakāsanaṃ kataṃ, tato bhavato paṭṭhāya mukhamattappakāsanaṃ kātukāmo āha “ādito paṭṭhāyā”ti. Teneva “dvīsu bhavesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Manussāpi keci aṇḍajā, saṃsedajā ca hontīti tadapekkhāya “catūsu yonīsū”ti vuttaṃ. Ekattakāyaekattasaññitāsāmaññena catutthajhānabhūmikāpi asaññāruppavajjā catutthiṃyeva viññāṇaṭṭhitiṃ bhajanti. Esa puññābhisaṅkhāro. Vuttanayenevāti “nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena ceva upanissayapaccayena cā”ti vuttanayeneva. Yathāsambhavanti ekavīsatikāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalavipākesu cuddasannaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ, pavatte ca, sattannaṃ pavatte evāti ayaṃ yathāsambhavo.

637. Where a detailed explanation has been given, from there onward, desiring to provide a mere summary indication, he says, 'from the beginning.' For that very reason, 'in two existences,' etc., was stated. Some humans are also egg-born and moisture-born; with reference to them, 'in four kinds of birth' was stated. By the commonality of having a single body and single perception, even those of the fourth jhāna plane, excluding the non-percipient and formless beings, resort only to the fourth station of consciousness. This is the meritorious formation. 'In the way stated' means in the way stated as 'by way of the condition of kamma of different moments and by way of the dependence condition.' 'As is possible' means: among the twenty-one wholesome-resultants of the sense-sphere and form-sphere, for fourteen at rebirth-linking and in the course of life, and for seven only in the course of life—this is the meaning of 'as is possible'.

Tādiseyevāti nānattakāyaekattasaññīsaṅkhāteyeva.

'In such a way indeed' means indeed in what is designated as 'diverse in body, one in perception'.

Catunnaṃ viññāṇānanti bhavādayo apekkhitvā vuttaṃ. Catūsu antogadhānaṃ pana tiṇṇaṃ viññāṇānaṃ tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu paccayabhāvo yojetabbo. Aviññāṇake sattāvāse saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇe alabbhamānepi tassa saṅkhārahetukattaṃ labbhateva. Tathā hi tattha puññābhisaṅkhāro kaṭattārūpānaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena paccayo hoti. Etasmiñca mukhamattappakāsane puññābhisaṅkhārādīnaṃ duggatiādīsu pavattiyaṃ kusalavipākādiviññāṇānaṃ paccayabhāvo bhavesu vuttanayeneva viññāyatīti na vuttoti veditabbo.

The phrase 'Of the four consciousnesses' is stated with reference to existences and so on. However, the state of the three consciousnesses included within the four being a condition in the three stations of consciousness should be connected. Even though in the non-conscious abode of beings, consciousness conditioned by formations is not obtained, its state of having formations as a cause is indeed obtained. For indeed, there the meritorious formation is a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of the condition of kamma at different moments. And in this mere introductory explanation, the state of meritorious formations, etc., being a condition for wholesome-resultant consciousness, etc., in their occurrence in woeful states, etc., is to be understood by the very method stated in regard to the existences; therefore, it should be understood that it is not stated here.

Viññāṇapaccayānāmarūpapadavitthārakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Detailed Exposition of the Term 'Name-and-Form Conditioned by Consciousness'.

638. Vibhāgā [M 2.0318] nāmarūpānanti nāmassa, rūpassa ca pabhedato.

638. "The classification of name-and-form" means by way of the distinction of name and of form.

Tattha nāmassa tāva pabhedaṃ dassentena kāmaṃ viññāṇampi nāmameva, paccayapaccayuppanne pana asaṅkarato [V 2.0298] dassetuṃ “ārammaṇābhimukhaṃ namanato vedanādayo tayo khandhā”ti vuttaṃ. Nibbānassa panettha pavattikathāyaṃ appaccayattā, namanaṭṭhābhāvato ca pasaṅgo eva natthi. Nāmanaṭṭhena hi taṃ nāmaṃ, na namanaṭṭhena. Tesaṃ nāmarūpānaṃ sukhādivasena, pathavīādivasena ca vibhāgo.

Therein, firstly, by one wishing to show the distinction of name: although consciousness is indeed also just name, yet in order to show the condition and the conditioned without confusion, it is stated: 'the three aggregates, feeling, etc., from bending towards an object.' Furthermore, for Nibbāna, in this discussion on the occurrence of the round of existence, there is no occasion whatsoever, both because it is not a condition and because of the absence of the meaning of bending. For that (Nibbāna) is 'nāma' (name) in the sense of causing (mind) to incline, not in the sense of bending. The classification of those name-and-form is by way of pleasure, etc., and by way of earth, etc.

Ekaṃ sattāvāsanti asaññasattāvāsaṃ. Purimesu catūsu, asaññasattāvāse cāti pañcasu.

"One abode of beings" refers to the abode of non-percipient beings. In the four preceding ones, and in the abode of non-percipient beings, thus in five.

Gabbhaseyyaggahaṇena jalābujā gahitāti “aṇḍajānañcā”ti vuttaṃ. Aṇḍajānañca abhāvakānanti yojetabbaṃ. Santatisīsānīti kalāpasantānamūlāni. Yadipi vikārarūpāni paṭisandhikkhaṇe na santi, lakkhaṇaparicchedarūpāni pana santīti tāni paramatthato aparinipphannānīti vajjento āha “rūparūpato”ti. Phassādike saṅkhārakkhandhabhāvena ekattaṃ netvā “tevīsati dhammā”ti vuttaṃ. Apanetvāti kalāpantaragate pathavīādike samānalakkhaṇatāya aggahetvā.

By the taking of 'womb-lying', the womb-born are included; therefore, 'and the egg-born' is stated separately. 'And of the egg-born who are without faculty-materiality'—thus it should be connected. 'The heads of continuity' are the roots of the continuity of material groups. Although the materialities of alteration are not present at the moment of rebirth-linking, the materialities of characteristic and limitation are present; therefore, wishing to exclude those which are not ultimately produced, he says, 'from material materiality'. Having brought contact, etc., to a state of oneness by way of being the aggregate of formations, it is stated, 'twenty-three phenomena'. 'Having removed' means not taking the earth element, etc., located in another material group, because of having a common characteristic.

Tesanti brahmakāyikādīnaṃ. Vitthārenāti catūsupi santatisīsesu rūpānaṃ asaṅkhipanena.

"Theirs" (tesaṃ) refers to the Brahmakāyika beings and so on. "In detail" (vitthārena) means by not condensing the materialities in all four starting points of continuity.

Kāmabhave pana yasmā sesaopapātikānanti ettha kiñcāpi kāmabhave opapātikā vuttā na santi, yena sesaggahaṇaṃ sātthakaṃ bhaveyya, aṇḍajagabbhaseyyakehi pana opapātikasaṃsedajā sesā hontīti sesaggahaṇaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. Atha vā brahmakāyikādikehi opapātikehi vuttehi sese sandhāya “sesaopapātikāna”nti āha. Te pana arūpinopi santīti “kāmabhave”ti vuttaṃ. Aparipuṇṇāyatanānaṃ pana nāmarūpaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ rūpamissakaviññāṇaniddese vuttanayena sakkā dhammagaṇanato viññātunti na vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the passage "in the sense-sphere existence... the remaining spontaneously arisen beings," although in the sense-sphere existence spontaneously arisen beings have not been mentioned, by which the inclusion of "the remaining" would be meaningful, it should be understood that the inclusion of "the remaining" is made because the spontaneously arisen and moisture-born are the remainder from the egg-born and womb-born. Alternatively, referring to the remaining ones from the spontaneously arisen beings who have been mentioned, such as the Brahmakāyika beings, he said, "the remaining spontaneously arisen beings." But since those remaining ones are also formless beings, "in the sense-sphere existence" was said. However, regarding those with incomplete sense bases, their mentality-materiality can be known according to the method stated in the exposition of consciousness mixed with materiality, by way of enumerating the dhammas as is appropriate; therefore, it should be understood that it is not stated here.

Paṭisandhicittena saha pavattaututoti paṭisandhicittena saha uppannarūpesu tejodhātuto. Hadayavatthuno taṅkhaṇuppannattā paṭisandhicittassa vatthudubbalatā. Tesaṃ ajjhoharitāhārena anugate sarīre [M 2.0319] āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ suṭṭhaddhakanti sambandho. Naroti teneva mātukucchigatabhāvena tirokkho. Avakaṃsato dve aṭṭhakāneva utucittasamuṭṭhānāni hontīti sasaddakālaṃ sandhāya “ukkaṃsato dvinnaṃ navakāna”nti vuttaṃ. Pubbeti yaṃ pubbe santatidvayādikaṃ sattakapariyosānaṃ rūpaṃ idha vuttaṃ, taṃ ekekassa [V 2.0299] cittassa tīsu tīsu khaṇesu uppajjamānameva vuttanti katvā āha “pubbe…pe… sattatividha”nti. Duvidhampi tanti utusamuṭṭhānaṃ, cittasamuṭṭhānañcāti duvidhampi taṃ saddaṃ.

"The temperature that proceeds together with the rebirth-linking consciousness" means: from the heat element among the kamma-born materialities that have arisen together with the rebirth-linking consciousness. Because the heart-base arises at that very moment, the rebirth-linking consciousness has a weak physical base. The connection is: for those womb-born beings, in the body sustained by ingested food, the nutriment-originated pure octad arises. "Concealed" (tiro) means: concealed precisely because of being in the mother's womb. At a minimum, there are only two octads, originated by temperature and consciousness; therefore, referring to a time when there is sound, it was said, "at a maximum, two nonads." "Previously" means: because the materiality which was previously mentioned here—beginning with the two continuities and ending with the septad—was said to be arising in the three moments of each and every consciousness, he said, "previously... sevenfold." "That which is also twofold" means: that sound which is twofold, namely, temperature-originated and consciousness-originated.

Saṇṭhātunti addhaniyabhāvena ṭhātuṃ, attano pana khaṇamattaṃ tiṭṭhateva. Catuddisā vavatthāpitāti aññamaññaṃ saṃsaṭṭhasīsā mūlena catūsu disāsu vavatthāpitā. Aññamaññaṃ āliṅgetvā ṭhitā bhinnavāhanikā viya ca.

"To stand firm" (saṇṭhātuṃ) means to stand in a lasting way; but on its own, it stands for only a moment. "Established in the four directions" means: with their tips mixed with one another, they are well established in the four directions by their base. And they stand embracing one another, like broken boats.

639. Pañcavokārabhave ca pavattiyanti rūpājanakakammajapañcaviññāṇappavattikālaṃ, sahajātaviññāṇapaccayañca sandhāyāha. Tadā hi tato nāmameva hotīti. Kammaviññāṇapaccayā pana tadāpi ubhayaṃ hotīti sakkā vattuṃ, pacchājātaviññāṇapaccayā ca rūpaṃ upatthaddhaṃ hotīti. Asaññesūtiādi kammaviññāṇapaccayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pañcavokārabhave ca pavattiyanti bhavaṅgādijanakakammato aññena rūpuppattikālaṃ, nirodhasamāpattikālaṃ, bhavaṅgādiuppattikālato aññakālañca sandhāya vuttanti yuttaṃ. Bhavaṅgādiuppattikāle hi taṃjanakena kammunā uppajjamānaṃ rūpaṃ, so ca vipāko kammaviññāṇapaccayo hotīti sakkā vattuṃ. Sahajātaviññāṇapaccayānapekkhampi hi pavattiyaṃ kammena pavattamānaṃ rūpaṃ, nāmañca na kammaviññāṇānapekkhaṃ hotīti. Sabbatthāti paṭisandhiyaṃ, pavatte ca. Sahajātaviññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, kammaviññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpañca yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Nāmañca rūpañca nāmarūpañcāti ettha nāmarūpasaddo attano ekadesena nāmasaddena nāmasaddassa sarūpo, rūpasaddena ca rūpasaddassa, tasmā sarūpānaṃ ekasesoti ekadesasarūpekaseso, nāmarūpasaddassa ṭhānaṃ itaresañca nāmarūpasaddānaṃ adassananti attho.

639. And in the five-constituent existence, during the course of existence, he speaks with reference to the time of the occurrence of the five consciousnesses born of kamma that does not generate materiality, and to consciousness as a co-nascence condition. For at that time, indeed, only mentality exists from that. However, it can be said that even at that time both exist due to kamma-consciousness as a condition, and that materiality is supported by consciousness as a post-nascence condition. The phrase 'in the unconscious beings, etc.' is said with reference to kamma-consciousness as a condition. And the phrase 'in the five-constituent existence, during the course of existence' is said with reference to the time of the arising of materiality by kamma other than that which generates the life-continuum, etc., the time of the attainment of cessation, and a time other than the time of the arising of the life-continuum, etc.; thus it is appropriate. For at the time of the arising of the life-continuum, etc., it can be said that the materiality arising from the kamma that generates it, and that resultant consciousness, have kamma-consciousness as their condition. Indeed, materiality and mentality that occur due to kamma in the course of existence, even while not depending on consciousness as a co-nascence condition, are not independent of kamma-consciousness. 'In all cases' means at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence. Mentality-materiality due to consciousness as a co-nascence condition, and mentality-materiality due to kamma-consciousness as a condition, should be connected as is possible. Here, in the phrase 'mentality and materiality and mentality-materiality,' the word 'mentality-materiality' (nāmarūpa), by one of its parts, the word 'mentality' (nāma), has the form of the word 'mentality,' and by the word 'materiality' (rūpa), has the form of the word 'materiality.' Therefore, 'ellipsis of identical forms' (sarūpānaṃ ekaseso) means 'ellipsis of one part of an identical form' (ekadesasarūpekaseso). The meaning is the standing of the word 'mentality-materiality' and the non-appearance of the other words 'mentality' and 'materiality'.

Vipākato aññaṃ avipākaṃ. Yato dvidhā mataṃ, tato yuttameva idanti yojetabbaṃ.

Other than resultant [consciousness] is non-resultant. Because it is understood in two ways, therefore this is indeed appropriate; thus it should be connected.

Kusalādicittakkhaṇeti [M 2.0320] ādi-saddena akusalakiriyacittakkhaṇe viya vipākacittakkhaṇepi vipākājanakakammasamuṭṭhānaṃ saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ. Vipākacittakkhaṇe pana abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇapaccayā pubbe vuttanayena ubhayañca labbhatīti tādisavipākacittakkhaṇavajjanatthaṃ “kusalādicittakkhaṇe”ti vuttaṃ.

In the phrase 'at the moment of wholesome consciousness, etc.,' it should be understood that by the word 'etc.,' just as at the moments of unwholesome and functional consciousness, also at the moment of resultant consciousness, materiality arisen from kamma that does not generate a resultant is included. However, since at the moment of resultant consciousness both are obtained due to volitional-formation consciousness as a condition, in the manner previously stated, the phrase 'at the moment of wholesome consciousness, etc.' was said for the purpose of excluding such a moment of resultant consciousness.

640. Suttantikapariyāyatoti [V 2.0300] paṭṭhāne rūpānaṃ upanissayapaccayassa avuttattā vuttaṃ. Suttante pana yasmiṃ sati yaṃ hoti, asati ca na hoti, so tassa upanissayo nidānaṃ hetu pabhavoti katvā “viññāṇūpanisaṃ nāmarūpa”nti rūpassa ca viññāṇūpanissayatā vuttā. Vanapatthapariyāye ca vanapatthagāmanigamanagarajanapadapuggalūpanissayo iriyāpathavihāro, tato ca cīvarādīnaṃ jīvitaparikkhārānaṃ kasirena, appakasirena ca samudāgamanaṃ vuttaṃ, na ca vanapatthādayo ārammaṇūpanissayādibhāvaṃ iriyāpathānaṃ, cīvarādisamudāgamanassa ca bhajanti. Tasmā vinā abhāvo eva suttantikapariyāyato upanissayabhāvo daṭṭhabbo. Nāmassa abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇaṃ kammārammaṇapaṭisandhiādikāle ārammaṇapaccayova hotīti vattabbameva natthīti rūpasseva suttantikapariyāyato ekadhāva paccayabhāvo vutto. Sasaṃsayassa hi rūpassetaṃ paccayo hotīti vutte nāmassa hotīti vattabbameva natthīti.

640. The phrase 'by the Suttanta method' is used because the conditioning by dependence condition for material forms is not mentioned in the Paṭṭhāna. However, in the Suttas, based on the principle that 'when this exists, that is; when this does not exist, that is not; that is its support, source, cause, and origin,' it is stated, 'mentality-materiality has consciousness as its support,' and thus the state of material form having consciousness as its dependence condition is stated. And in the Vanapattha discourse, the dwelling in a certain posture has a forest thicket, village, town, city, district, or person as its support; and from that, the arising of life-requisites such as robes, with or without difficulty, is stated. And forest thickets and so on do not attain the state of being an object-dependence condition, etc., for the postures or for the arising of robes and so on. Therefore, by the Suttanta method, the state of being a dependence condition should be understood as simply the non-existence of an effect in the absence of its cause. For mentality, since volitional consciousness at the time of rebirth-linking with a kamma-object, etc., is only an object condition, there is nothing to be said about it being another type of condition. Thus, the state of being a condition is stated in one way only for material form by the Suttanta method. Indeed, when it is said, 'This is a condition for material form, which is subject to doubt,' there is nothing to be said that it is a condition for mentality.

Pavattassa pākaṭattā apākaṭaṃ paṭisandhiṃ gahetvā pucchati “kathaṃ paneta”ntiādinā. Suttato nāmaṃ, yuttito rūpaṃ viññāṇapaccayā hotīti jānitabbaṃ.

Because the course of existence is manifest, taking up the unmanifest rebirth-linking, he asks with the words, 'But how is this?' and so on. It should be known that mentality is conditioned by consciousness based on the Sutta, and material form is conditioned by consciousness based on reasoning.

Yuttito sādhetvā suttena taṃ daḷhaṃ karonto “kammasamuṭṭhānassāpi hī”tiādimāha. Cittasamuṭṭhānassevāti cittasamuṭṭhānassa viya. Ettha ca “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa”nti (ma. ni. 3.126; saṃ. ni. 2.1, 39; mahāva. 1; udā. 1) bhāsamānena bhagavatā yasmā upaparikkhamānānaṃ paṇḍitānaṃ paramatthato nāmarūpamattameva pavattamānaṃ dissati, na satto, na jīvo, tasmā kenaci appaṭivattiyaṃ anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ hoti. Suññatappakāsanañhi dhammacakkappavattananti. Atha vā nāmarūpamattatāvacanena pavattiyā dukkhasaccamattatā vuttā. Dukkhasaccappakāsanena ca tassa samudayo, tassa ca nirodho, nirodhagāminipaṭipadā ca [M 2.0321] pakāsitā eva hoti. Ahetukassa dukkhassa, hetunirodhā anirujjhanakassa ca abhāvā, nirodhassa ca upāyena vinā anadhigantabbattāti catusaccappakāsanaṃ dhammacakkappavattanaṃ niddhāretabbaṃ.

Having established it by reasoning, and wishing to make that statement firm with the Sutta, he said the passage beginning with 'kammasamuṭṭhānassāpi hi'. 'Cittasamuṭṭhānasseva' means 'like that which has arisen from mind'. And here, since the Blessed One said, 'With consciousness as condition, there is mentality-materiality,' for the wise who investigate closely, in the ultimate sense only mere mentality-materiality is seen occurring—not a being, not a soul. Therefore, an unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma, which cannot be turned back by anyone, has been set rolling. Indeed, the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma is the very exposition of the state of being void of a being or a soul. Or alternatively, by the statement of the state of being mere mentality-materiality, the mere state of the truth of suffering of the process is stated. And by the exposition of the truth of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation are indeed revealed. Because there is no causeless suffering, and no suffering that does not cease with the cessation of its cause, and because cessation cannot be attained without a means, the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma should be determined as the exposition of the Four Truths.

Nāmarūpapaccayāsaḷāyatanapadavitthārakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Detailed Exposition of the Term 'the Six Sense Bases as Conditioned by Mentality-Materiality'

641. Tanti [V 2.0301] nāmarūpaṃ. Tassāti saḷāyatanassa. Tādisassevāti katekasesasseva.

641. 'Taṃ' means mentality-materiality. 'Tassa' means 'of the six sense bases'. 'Tādisassa eva' means 'of that very thing for which a single remainder has been made'.

Idhāpi nāmanti khandhattayasseva gahaṇe kāraṇaṃ vuttanayameva. Niyamatoti idañca catunnaṃ bhūtānaṃ, channaṃ vatthūnaṃ, jīvitassa ca yathāsambhavaṃ sahajātanissayapurejātaindriyādinā saḷāyatanassa pavattamānassa ekantena paccayabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Rūpāyatanādīnaṃ pana sahajātanissayānupālanabhāvo natthīti aggahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Ārammaṇārammaṇapurejātādibhāvo ca tesaṃ na sasantatipariyāpannānameva, na ca cakkhādīnaṃ viya ekappahārenevāti aniyamato paccayabhāvo. Niyamato…pe… jīvitindriyanti evanti ettha evaṃ-saddena vā rūpāyatanādīnampi saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatananti ettha yadipi chaṭṭhāyatanasaḷāyatanasaddānaṃ saddato sarūpatā natthi, atthato pana saḷāyatanekadesova chaṭṭhāyatananti ekadesasarūpatā atthīti ekadesasarūpekaseso katoti veditabbo. Atthatopi hi sarūpānaṃ ekadesasarūpekasesaṃ icchanti “vaṅko ca kuṭilo ca kuṭilā”ti. Tasmā atthato ekadesasarūpānañca ekasesena bhavitabbanti.

Here also, the reason for taking only the three aggregates by the term 'nāma' is just as has been stated. And this term 'niyamato' (necessarily) is stated with reference to the fact that the four great elements, the six bases, and the life faculty are invariably a condition for the occurring six sense-bases, as is appropriate, by way of co-nascence, dependence, pre-existence, faculty, and so on. However, it should be understood that the form-base and so on are not taken here, because they do not have the state of co-nascent dependence and sustenance. And their state of being an object, pre-nascent, and so on, is not only for those included in one's own continuity, nor is it in one and the same way like the eye-base and so on; therefore, their state of being a condition is not fixed. In the text 'Niyamato…pe… jīvitindriyaṃ', the inclusion of the form-base and so on should also be seen, or alternatively, it is included by the word 'evaṃ' (thus). Here, in 'chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatanaṃ', although the words 'sixth sense-base' and 'six sense-bases' are not identical in sound, in meaning, however, the sixth sense-base is only a part of the six sense-bases. Therefore, because there is a partial identity in meaning, it should be understood that a single remainder of partial identity has been made. For grammarians desire a single remainder of partial identity even for things that are identical in meaning, as in 'vaṅko ca kuṭilo ca kuṭilā' ('crooked' and 'bent' become 'the bent ones'). Therefore, there should also be a single remainder for things that are partially identical in meaning.

Atha vā chaṭṭhāyatanañca manāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatananti vā manāyatananti vā chaṭṭhāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatanañca chaṭṭhāyatananti vā manāyatanañca manāyatanañca manāyatananti vā ekasesaṃ katvā cakkhādīhi saddhiṃ “saḷāyatana”nti vuttanti tameva ekasesaṃ nāmamattapaccayassa, nāmarūpapaccayassa ca manāyatanassa vasena kataṃ atthato dassento āha “chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañca saḷāyatananti evaṃ katekasesassā”ti. Yathāvuttopi hi ekaseso atthato chaṭṭhāyatanañca saḷāyatanañcāti evaṃ kato nāma [M 2.0322] hotīti. Sabbattha ca ekasese kate ekavacananiddeso katekasesānaṃ saḷāyatanādisaddavacanīyatāsāmaññavasena katoti daṭṭhabbo.

Alternatively, having made a single remainder of 'the sixth sense-base and the mind-base' as 'the sixth sense-base' or 'the mind-base,' or of 'the sixth sense-base and the sixth sense-base' as 'the sixth sense-base,' or of 'the mind-base and the mind-base' as 'the mind-base,' it is called 'the six sense-bases' together with the eye-base, etc. To show in terms of meaning that very single remainder—made with respect to the mind-base that is conditioned by name-only and conditioned by name-and-form—he says, 'chaṭṭhāyatanañca…pe…sesassā’ti.' For even the single remainder as stated is, in meaning, indeed made thus: 'the sixth sense-base and the six sense-bases.' And it should be understood that everywhere, when a single remainder is made, the singular designation is made on the basis of the commonality of the single remainders being expressible by terms like 'the six sense-bases,' etc.

“Na aññathā”ti etena tassa tassa nāmassa, rūpassa ca abhāve taṃ taṃ āyatanaṃ na hotīti byatirekaṃ vibhāveti.

By this phrase, 'Not otherwise,' it clarifies the negative concomitance: that in the absence of such and such name and form, such and such a sense-base does not come to be.

Yanti [V 2.0302] yaṃ yaṃ nāmaṃ, rūpañca. Yassāti yassa yassa āyatanassa. Yathāti sahajātādinā yena yena pakārena. Neyyanti ñeyyaṃ.

'Yanti' means whatever name and form. 'Yassāti' means of whichever sense-base. 'Yathāti' means in whatever way, such as by way of co-nascence, etc. 'Neyyanti' means what is to be known.

Tassa vasenāti tassa hetuādipaccayassa vasena. Ukkaṃsāvakaṃsoti ettha sattadhā paccayabhāvato ukkaṃso aṭṭhadhā paccayabhāvo, tato navadhā, tato dasadhāti ayaṃ ukkaṃso. Avakaṃso pana dasadhā paccayabhāvato navadhā paccayabhāvo, tato aṭṭhadhā, tato sattadhāti evaṃ veditabbo, na pana sattadhā paccayabhāvato eva dvepi ukkaṃsāvakaṃsā yojetabbā, tato avakaṃsābhāvatoti.

'By its power' means by the power of its condition, such as cause. Regarding 'superiority and inferiority,' here, from the state of being a condition in seven ways, superiority is the state of being a condition in eight ways, from that in nine ways, and from that in ten ways—this is superiority. Inferiority, however, should be understood thus: from the state of being a condition in ten ways, it is the state of being a condition in nine ways, from that in eight ways, and from that in seven ways. However, both superiority and inferiority should not be applied from the sevenfold state of being a condition alone, because from that there is no inferiority.

Vipākaṃ nāmanti sambandho. Vuttanayenevāti sahajātādivasena, sattadhā, hetuādivasena ca. Itaranti avipākaṃ nāmaṃ.

The connection is 'resultant name.' 'By the method already stated' means by way of co-nascence, etc., in seven ways, and by way of cause, etc. 'The other' means non-resultant name.

“Hadayavatthuno sahāyaṃ hutvā”ti etena arūpe viya asahāyaṃ nāmaṃ na hoti, hadayavatthu ca nāmena saha chaṭṭhāyatanassa paccayo hotīti ettakameva dasseti, na pana yathā hadayavatthu paccayo hoti, tathā nāmampīti ayamattho adhippeto. Vatthu hi nāmassa vippayuttapaccayo hoti, na nāmaṃ. Nāmañca vipākahetādipaccayo hoti, na vatthūti. Pavatte arūpadhammā kammajarūpassa ṭhitippattasseva paccayā honti, na uppajjamānassāti vippayuttaatthiavigatā ca pacchājātavippayuttādayo eva cakkhādīnaṃ yojetabbā.

By 'having become a companion to the heart-base,' this shows that, unlike in the formless realm, name is not without a companion, and the heart-base, together with name, is a condition for the sixth sense-base. This much alone is indicated, and not that the intended meaning is that name is also a condition in the same way as the heart-base. For the base is a dissociated condition for name, but name is not. And name is a condition such as result, cause, etc., but the base is not. In the course of existence, immaterial phenomena are conditions only for kamma-born matter that has reached the state of presence, not for that which is arising. Thus, for the eye-base, etc., the dissociated, presence, and non-disappearance conditions should be applied only as post-nascence dissociated and the like.

“Tatthevā”ti iminā “pavatte”ti idaṃ paccāmaṭṭhanti āha “tattheva hi pavatte”ti. “Pañcavokārabhave”ti pana idaṃ “pañcanna”nti iminā dīpitamevāti. Pavattiyaṃ cakkhāyatanādikassa nāmaṃ vipākapaccayo na hoti, attanā janitarūpasseva hoti. Paṭisandhiyaṃ pana kammasamuṭṭhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānasadisaṃ, tasmā vatthunopi vipākapaccayo hotiyeva.

By 'right there,' it refers back to 'in the course of existence,' hence it says, 'right there indeed in the course of existence.' But 'in the five-constituent existence' is already explained by 'of the five.' In the course of existence, name is not a resultant condition for the eye-base, etc.; it is so only for the matter generated by itself. At rebirth-linking, however, kamma-originated matter is like mind-originated matter; therefore, for the base also, it is indeed a resultant condition.

Rūpatoti [M 2.0323] rūpesu. Yaṃ yaṃ āyatanaṃ uppajjatīti paṭisandhiyaṃ aṇḍajajalābujānaṃ pañcasu āyatanesu kāyāyatanameva uppajjati. Itaresaṃ yathārahaṃ itarānipi.

'From material form' means among material forms. As for 'whatever sense-base arises,' at rebirth-linking, for the egg-born and the womb-born, only the body-base arises among the five sense-bases. For the others, the other sense-bases also arise as appropriate.

Avasesamanāyatanassāti ettha “pañcakkhandhabhave panā”ti etassa anuvattamānattā pañcavokārabhave [V 2.0303] eva pavattamānaṃ pañcaviññāṇehi avasesaṃ manāyatanaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nāmarūpassa sahajātādisādhāraṇapaccayabhāvo, sampayuttādiasādhāraṇapaccayabhāvo ca yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbo. “Rūpapaccayā pañcāyatanānī”ti ayampi nayo labbhati nirodhasamāpannānaṃ vasena, so pana apacurabhāvato yebhuyyena ca paṭisandhiyaṃ paccayabhūtasseva nāmarūpassa pavattiyaṃ paccayabhāvo vibhāvitoti na dassitoti veditabbaṃ.

Here, in 'for the remaining mind-base,' since 'but in the five-aggregate existence' is carried over, it should be understood that what is spoken of is the mind-base remaining from the five consciousnesses, which occurs only in the five-constituent existence. The state of name-and-form as a common condition, such as co-nascence, and its state as an uncommon condition, such as association, should be applied as is possible. The method 'the five sense-bases are conditioned by material form' is also obtained by way of those who have attained cessation attainment; however, it should be known that this is not shown, because it is infrequent, and because for the most part, the state as a condition in the course of existence of that very name-and-form which was a condition at rebirth-linking has been explained.

Saḷāyatanapaccayāphassapadavitthārakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Extensive Exposition of the Term 'Contact Conditioned by the Six Sense-Bases'

642. Bāvīsatiyā lokiyavipākaviññāṇehi sampayuttā bāvīsatilokiyaviññāṇasampayuttā. Tato eva bāvīsati.

642. 'Associated with the twenty-two mundane consciousnesses' means associated with the twenty-two mundane resultant consciousnesses. Therefore, there are twenty-two.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ saḷāyatane, tesu chasu āyatanesūti attho. Ajjhattanti sasantatipariyāpannameva gaṇhāti. Tañhi sasantatipariyāpannakammanibbattaṃ tādisassa phassassa paccayo hoti. Rūpādīni, pana bahiddhā anupādinnāni ca phassassa ārammaṇaṃ honti, na tāni cakkhādīni viya sasantatipariyāpannakammakilesanimittappavattibhāvena phassassa paccayā hontīti paṭhamācariyavāde na gahitāni, dutiyācariyavāde pana yathā tathā vā paccayabhāve sati na sakkā vajjetunti gahitāni.

“Therein” means in that sixfold sense-base, that is, in those six sense-bases. By the term “internal,” it takes only that which is included in one's own continuum. For that, being included in one's own continuum and produced by kamma, is a condition for such contact. Forms, etc., on the other hand, being external and unappropriated, are objects for contact; they are not conditions for contact in the way that the eye, etc., are—by way of their occurrence as included in one's own continuum and caused by kamma and defilements. Therefore, in the view of the first teachers, they are not taken. In the view of the second teachers, however, they are taken because it is not possible to exclude them when they are conditions in some way or other.

Tatthāti saḷāyatanapaccayā phassapade. Ye tāva ācariyā mahāvihāravāsinova yathā viññāṇaṃ, evaṃ nāmarūpaṃ, saḷāyatanaṃ, phassaṃ, vedanañca paccayaṃ, paccayuppannañca sasantatipariyāpannaṃ dīpentā vipākameva icchanti. “Chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti abhidhammabhājanīyapāḷi (vibha. 243) āruppaṃ sandhāya vuttāti “chaṭṭhāyatanapaccayā phassoti pāḷianusārato”ti vuttaṃ.

“Therein” refers to the phrase 'contact conditioned by the six sense-bases'. Firstly, those teachers who are residents of the Mahāvihāra, while explaining that just as consciousness, so too name-and-form, the six sense-bases, contact, and feeling—both as condition and as conditioned—are included in one's own continuum, intend only the resultant. The Abhidhamma-bhājanīya Pāḷi, “Contact is conditioned by the sixth sense-base” (Vibhaṅga 243), is said with reference to the formless realm. Therefore, it is said, “according to the Pāḷi, ‘contact is conditioned by the sixth sense-base.’”

Sabbe phassā na sambhontīti yojanā. Yadi sabbāyatanehi eko phasso sambhaveyya, “saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso”ti ekassa vacanaṃ yujjeyya[M 2.0324], athāpi ekamhā āyatanā sabbe phassā sambhaveyyuṃ, tathāpi sabbāyatanehi sabbaphassasambhavato āyatanabhedena phassabhedo natthīti tadabhedavasena ekassa vacanaṃ yujjeyya, tathā pana asambhavato na yuttanti codeti “na sabbāyatanehī”tiādinā[V 2.0304]. Aññassāpi vā asambhavantassa vidhānassa bodhanatthametaṃ vuttaṃ “nāpi ekamhā āyatanā sabbe phassā”ti. “Na sabbāyatanehi eko phasso sambhotī”ti idameva pana ekaphassavacanassāyuttattadīpakaṃ kāraṇanti veditabbaṃ. Nidassanavasena vā etaṃ vuttaṃ. Nāpi ekamhā āyatanā sabbe phassā sambhonti, evaṃ na sabbāyatanehi eko phasso sambhoti. Tasmā ekassa vacanaṃ ayuttanti. Parihāraṃ pana anekāyatanehi ekaphassassa sambhavatoti dassento “tatridaṃ vissajjana”ntiādimāha. Avasesasampayuttadhammāyatanā phassavajjitā taṃsampayuttacetasikā dhammā.

The construction is: 'All contacts do not arise.' If one contact were to arise from all bases, the statement in the singular, 'contact is conditioned by the six sense-bases,' would be appropriate. Furthermore, if all contacts were to arise from one base, even so, because all contacts arise from all bases, there is no distinction of contact by the distinction of bases; therefore, by way of that non-distinction, the statement in the singular would be appropriate. However, since that is not possible, it is not suitable; thus, the objection is made with the words beginning 'not from all bases...' Alternatively, this was said to make known another impossible arrangement: 'nor from one base do all contacts arise.' However, it should be known that this very statement, 'One contact does not arise from all bases,' is the reason demonstrating the unsuitability of the statement in the singular. Alternatively, this was said by way of example: just as all contacts do not arise from one base, so too one contact does not arise from all bases. Therefore, the statement in the singular is unsuitable. However, showing the solution—that one contact arises from many bases—He said the words beginning, 'Herein, this is the explanation...' The remaining associated mental-object bases are the mental factors associated with it, with contact excluded.

Ekopi anekāyatanappabhavo ekopanekāyatanappabhavo.

The term `ekopanekāyatanappabhavo` is a euphonic combination for `ekopi anekāyatanappabhavo`, meaning: even a single contact is produced from many bases, or has many bases as its origin.

Chadhā paccayatte pañca vibhāvaye, ekaṃ navadhā paccayatte, bāhirāni cha āyatanāni ārammaṇādinā yathāsambhavaṃ paccayatte vibhāvayeti sambandho.

One should elucidate the five bases in their state as a condition in six ways, and the one resultant mind-base in its state as a condition in nine ways. The six external bases should be elucidated in their state as a condition by way of object-condition and so on, as is appropriate. This is the connection.

Anekabhedassāti kusalavipākādipañcadvārādivasena anekavidhassa dvipañcaviññāṇasampayuttavajjassa vipākaphassassa. Tāni cāti rūpāyatanādīni. “Mano ca nesaṃ gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhotī”ti (ma. ni. 1.455) hi vuttaṃ. Tathā cāti paccuppannāni rūpādīni paccuppannañca dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ rūparūpaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ārammaṇapaccayamattenāti taṃ sabbaṃ apaccuppannaṃ, aññañca dhammāyatanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

The phrase 'of many kinds' (`anekabhedassa`) refers to resultant contact, which is of various kinds by way of wholesome resultant contact, etc., and the five sense-doors, etc., excluding that associated with the two sets of five consciousnesses. The phrase 'and those' (`tāni ca`) refers to the form base and so on. For it is said, “And the mind experiences their object and sphere” (Majjhima Nikāya 1.455). The phrase 'and thus' (`tathā ca`) is said in reference to present forms, etc., and the present subtle form included in the mental-object base. The phrase 'merely as object condition' (`ārammaṇapaccayamattena`) is said in reference to all that which is not present, and to the other mental-object base.

Phassapaccayāvedanāpadavitthārakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Extensive Exposition of the Section 'Feeling Conditioned by Contact'

643. Dvārato saḷevāti pabhavasāmaññato ekavidhāpi uppattidvārato cha eva hontīti chaḷeva vedanā vuttā.

643. The phrase 'from the door, just six' (`dvārato saḷeva`) is stated because, although feelings are of one kind in terms of their general nature of arising, they are just six by way of the doors of arising. Thus, six feelings are stated.

Cittabhedena ekūnanavutividhāpi idhādhippetā eva dassetuṃ “vedanāsu panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. “Sesāna”nti ettha sampaṭicchanasampayuttāya cakkhusamphassādayo pañca yadipi anantarādīhi paccayā honti, anantarādīnaṃ pana [M 2.0325] upanissaye antogadhattā santīraṇatadārammaṇānañca sādhāraṇassa tassa vasena “ekadhā”ti vuttaṃ. Ekekasmiṃ dvāre hi cakkhudvārādīsu uppannacakkhuviññāṇādīhi [V 2.0305] sahajātā phassā sakasakavīthīsu sampaṭicchanādīhi sampayuttavedanānaṃ, manodvāre tadārammaṇavaseneva pavattānaṃ tebhūmakavipākavedanānampi sahajātamanosamphassasaṅkhāto so phasso aṭṭhadhā paccayo hotīti yojetabbaṃ.

To show that even the eighty-nine kinds of feeling by way of the division of consciousness are intended here, the phrase 'among feelings, however,' etc., is stated. Here, regarding the phrase 'for the rest' (`sesānaṃ`), although the five contacts beginning with eye-contact are conditions by way of immediacy, etc., for the feeling associated with receiving consciousness, it is said 'in one way' (`ekadhā`) because immediacy, etc., are included in decisive support, and by way of that decisive support which is common to investigating and registering consciousnesses. Indeed, in each of the doors, such as the eye-door, the contacts that have arisen together with eye-consciousness, etc., in their respective cognitive processes, are conditions for the feelings associated with receiving, etc. In the mind-door, for the feelings that proceed only by way of registering, and also for the resultant feelings of the three planes, that contact known as co-nascent mind-contact is a condition in eight ways. Thus it should be connected.

Rūpārūpāvacaravipākavedanā paṭisandhiādivaseneva pavattanti, kāmāvacarāpi ekaccāti “tebhūmakavipākavedanānampī”ti vuttaṃ. Tāsampi hi sahajātamanosamphasso aṭṭhadhāva paccayo hoti. Paccayaṃ anupādinnampi keci icchantīti “yā panā”tiādinā manodvārāvajjanasampayuttaphassassa paccayabhāvo vutto. Tañca mukhamattadassanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etena nayena sabbassa anantarassa, anānantarassa ca phassassa tassā tassā vipākavedanāya upanissayatā yojetabbāti.

Resultant feelings of the form and formless spheres arise only by way of rebirth-linking, etc.; and some sense-sphere resultant feelings also arise thus. Therefore, it is said, 'of the resultant feelings of the three planes also.' Indeed, for these too, co-nascent mind-contact is a condition in eight ways. Because some desire a condition even if it is not appropriated, the state of contact associated with mind-door adverting as a condition is stated by the phrase beginning with 'yā pana.' And that should be seen as a mere introductory indication. By this method, the nature of all contiguous and non-contiguous contact as a decisive support condition for each respective resultant feeling should be connected.

Vedanāpaccayātaṇhāpadavitthārakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Extensive Exposition of the Section 'Craving Conditioned by Feeling'

644. Idhāti imasmiṃ loke, imasmiṃ vā sāsane cha taṇhā dīpitā. Idhāti vā imasmiṃ vedanāpaccayā taṇhāpade. Tatthāti tāsu chasu taṇhāsu.

644. “Herein” means in this world, or in this Dispensation, where six cravings are shown. Or, “herein” means in this section on 'craving conditioned by feeling.' “Therein” means among those six cravings.

Ekekāya sassatadiṭṭhisahagatāya, ucchedadiṭṭhisahagatāya ca taṇhāya tadabhinandanānuguṇo rūpādīsu pavattiākāro, kevalaṃ kāmassādavasena pavattiyā visiṭṭhākārattā vuttappavattiākārato taṇhāya tividhatā.

For each craving associated with eternalist view and with annihilationist view, the mode of its occurrence regarding forms, etc., is in accordance with delighting in that view. Because its mode is distinct from an occurrence merely by way of enjoying sensual pleasure, the threefold nature of craving is stated in terms of its mode of occurrence.

Mamattenāti sampiyāyanena, assādanataṇhāya icceva vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha putto viya vedanā daṭṭhabbā, khīrādayo viya vedanāya paccayabhūtā rūpādayo, khīrādidāyikā dhāti viya rūpādichaḷārammaṇadāyakā cittakārādayo cha. Tattha sukhasamphassavatthadāyako tantavāyo, vejjo rasāyatanojāvasena, tadupatthambhitajīvitavasena ca dhammārammaṇassa dāyakoti daṭṭhabbo. Sabbāpesā aṭṭhasatappabhedāpi.

'With possessiveness' means with great affection; it is said to mean 'with craving for enjoyment.' In that simile, feeling should be seen as like a son; forms, etc., which are conditions for feeling, as like milk, etc.; and the six providers of the six sense-objects such as form, like painters and so on, should be seen as like a wet-nurse who gives milk, etc. Among them, the weaver is a provider of cloth that has a pleasant touch; the physician, by the power of the nutritive essence of an elixir and by the power of the life sustained by it, should be seen as a provider of the mind-object. All this craving, too, has one hundred and eight divisions.

Ārammaṇapaccayo uppajjamānāya ārammaṇamattameva hoti, na upanissayo viya uppādakoti uppādakassa upanissayasseva vasena “ekadhāvā”ti [M 2.0326] vuttaṃ. Upanissayena vā ārammaṇūpanissayo [V 2.0306] saṅgahito. Tena ca ārammaṇabhāvena taṃsabhāgo aññopi ārammaṇapaccayabhāvo dīpito hotīti upanissayavaseneva paccayabhāvo vuttoti veditabbo.

The object-condition is merely the object for the arising craving; it is not a producer like a decisive support condition. Therefore, it is said, 'in one way,' by way of the producing decisive support condition only. Alternatively, by the decisive support condition, the object-as-decisive-support condition is included. And by that state of being an object, another state of being an object-condition, which is of a similar nature, is also elucidated. Therefore, it should be understood that the state of being a condition is stated only by way of the decisive support condition.

“Yasmā vā”tiādinā na kevalaṃ vipākasukhavedanā eva, tissopi pana vedanā vipākā visesena taṇhāya upanissayapaccayo, avisesena itarā cāti dasseti. Upekkhā pana santattā, sukhamicceva bhāsitāti tasmā sāpi bhiyyo icchanavasena taṇhāya upanissayoti adhippāyo. Upekkhā pana akusalavipākabhūtā aniṭṭhattā dukkhe avarodhetabbā, itarā iṭṭhattā sukheti sā dukkhaṃ viya, sukhaṃ viya ca upanissayapaccayo hotīti sakkā vattuṃ. “Vedanāpaccayā taṇhā”ti vacanena sabbassa vedanāvato paccayassa atthitāya taṇhuppattippasaṅge tannivāraṇatthamāha “vedanāpaccayā cāpī”tiādi.

By the words beginning with 'Because...', it is shown that not only resultant pleasant feeling, but indeed the three feelings that are resultant are specifically a decisive support condition for craving, and the other feelings are so generally. But as for equanimity, because of its tranquil nature, it is spoken of only as pleasant; therefore, the meaning is that it too, by way of stronger desire, is a decisive support for craving. However, equanimity that is the result of unwholesome kamma, because it is undesirable, should be included in suffering; the other, because it is desirable, in happiness. Thus, it can be said that it is a decisive support condition like suffering and like happiness.
