Or else, having abandoned the fear that is the knowledge arising by way of the appearance of danger, and the delight, called joy, that arises by way of comprehension. For when emptiness has been seen in all respects, there is no occasion for fear and delight; rather, equanimity alone is established. Hence he said: 'He is indifferent toward formations.' Herein, to show the absence of that wrong grasp by which there might be non-indifference, he said: 'He does not grasp "I" or "mine."' Now, to show a simile for this indifference, he said: 'like a man who has divorced his wife,' and so on.

Tattha [V 2.0432] anudāsīnatāpubbikā udāsīnatā vuccamānā idha opammatthaṃ pharatīti dassetuṃ “iṭṭhā kantā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ativiya naṃ mamāyeyya itthīnaṃ sāṭheyyakūṭeyyavaṅkeyyādīnaṃ ajānanato. Muñcitukāmo hutvāti muñcitukāmova hutvā, taṃ vissajjeyya nirapekkhatāya vasenevāti adhippāyo. Ayaṃ yogāvacaro. Muñcitukāmatāya uddhaṃ yāva saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ na uppajjati, tāva pavattā vipassanā paṭisaṅkhānupassanā evāti āha “paṭisaṅkhānupassanāya saṅkhāre pariggaṇhanto”ti.

Here, to show that the equanimity being spoken of, which is preceded by non-indifference, serves the purpose of a simile, the words 'charming and beloved,' and so on, were stated. Because of not knowing the deceit, fraudulence, crookedness, and so on of women, he would be extremely possessive of her. 'Desiring to be free' means: having become desirous of being free, he would give her up with complete detachment—this is the meaning. This meditator. From the desire for freedom upwards, as long as the knowledge of equanimity towards formations has not arisen, the insight that proceeds is precisely the contemplation of reflection; therefore, he said: 'comprehending formations with the contemplation of reflection.'

Patilīyatīti ekapassena nilīyati nilīnaṃ viya hoti. Patikuṭatīti saṅkucati. Paṭivaṭṭatīti vivaṭṭati. Na sampasāriyatīti na visarati, abhirativasena na pakkhandatīti attho.

'It shrinks back' means it hides on one side, it is as if hidden. 'It recoils' means it contracts. 'It turns back' means it turns away. 'It does not stretch out' means it does not spread; the meaning is that it does not leap forward out of delight.

Iccassāti iti evaṃ assa yogino.

'Thus for him' means: thus, in this way, for this meditator.

767. Tikkhavisadasūrabhāvena saṅkhāresu ajjhupekkhane sijjhamāne taṃ panetaṃ saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ anekavāraṃ pavattamānaṃ paripākagamanena anulomañāṇassa paccayabhāvaṃ gacchantaṃ nibbānaṃ santato passati nāma. Tathābhūtañca sabbaṃ saṅkhārappavattaṃ vissajjetvā nibbānameva pakkhandati nāma. Tayidaṃ idha ñāṇaṃ anulomagotrabhuñāṇehi saddhiṃ ekattaṃ netvā vuttaṃ ekattanayavasena[M 2.0460]. No ce nibbānaṃ santato passatīti tāva saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇassa aparipakkatamevāha. Samuddaṃ tarantīti sāmuddikā, saṃyattikā. Disājānanako kāko disākāko, lakkhaṇamattañcetaṃ yo koci tādiso sakunto veditabbo. Videsanti adesaṃ samudde aparicitaṭṭhānaṃ. Anugantvāti anu anu gantvā.

767. When equanimity towards formations is being accomplished with sharpness, clarity, and courage, that knowledge of equanimity towards formations, proceeding many times and going to maturity, becomes a condition for conformity knowledge and is said to see Nibbāna as peaceful. And such a knowledge, having relinquished the entire process of formations, is said to leap into Nibbāna itself. Here this knowledge has been spoken of by way of a single method, having been brought to oneness with conformity knowledge and change-of-lineage knowledge. The phrase 'If it does not see Nibbāna as peaceful' states that up to that point, the knowledge of equanimity towards formations is simply immature. 'Those who cross the ocean' are seafarers, mariners. 'A direction-knowing crow' is a disākāka; and this is merely a designation, for any such bird should be understood. 'A foreign land' means a place one has not been to, an unfamiliar location in the ocean. 'Having followed' means having gone again and again.

Tayidaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ. Piṭṭhaṃ vaṭṭayamānaṃ viyāti thūlathūlato vivecanavasena nipphoṭiyamānaṃ saṇhaṃ saṇhaṃ piṭṭhacuṇṇaṃ viya. Nibbaṭṭitakappāsanti nibbaṭṭitabījaṃ kappāsaṃ. Vihanamānaṃ viyāti dhanukena vihaññamānaṃ viya. Upamādvayenapi punappunaṃ sammasanena vipassanāñāṇassa sukhumatarabhāvāpattimāha. Yathā yathā hi vipassanābhāvanābalena tikkhā, visadā, sūrā ca hoti, tathā tathā sukhumatarāpi hotīti. Saṅkhāravicinaneti pavicayassa sikhāppattatāya saṅkhāresu viya tesaṃ vicinanepi udāsīnaṃ hutvā tividhānupassanāvasena tiṭṭhati pakārantarassa abhāvato. [V 2.0433] “Sattadhā aṭṭhārasadhā”tiādinā vibhattāpi hi anupassanāpakārā aniccānupassanādīsveva tīsu antogadhāti matthakappattā vipassanā tāsaṃ eva vasena tiṭṭhati.

This is insight knowledge. 'Like flour being ground' means like very fine flour-dust being threshed by way of separating out the coarse parts. 'Ginned cotton' means cotton with the seeds removed. 'Like being carded' means like being struck with a carding bow. By these two similes as well, he indicates the attainment of an increasingly subtle state by insight knowledge through repeated comprehension. For just as insight becomes sharp, clear, and courageous through the power of the development of insight, so too it becomes more and more subtle. 'Scrutinizing formations' means that because investigation has reached its peak, having become indifferent towards the scrutinizing of formations just as towards the formations themselves, one abides by way of the threefold contemplation, as there is no other mode. For although the modes of contemplation are divided as 'sevenfold, eighteenfold,' and so on, they are included within just these three—contemplation of impermanence, and so on. Thus insight, having reached the summit, abides by way of these very same contemplations.

768. Tatrāti tasmiṃ vimokkhamukhabhāvāpajjane, ariyapuggalavibhāgapaccayatthe ca. Idaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ indriyānanti saddhindriyasamādhindriyapaññindriyānaṃ. Ādhipateyyavasenāti sampayuttadhammānaṃ adhipatibhāvavasena. Aniccānupassanābahulassa hi saddhindriyaṃ balavaṃ hoti, dukkhānupassanābahulassa samādhindriyaṃ, anattānupassanābahulassa paññindriyanti tissannaṃ anupassanānaṃ vasena balavatarabhāvaṃ pattāni imāni tīṇi indriyāni vimokkhamukhabhāvaṃ āpādentīti āha “tividhānupassanā…pe… āpajjati nāmā”ti. Tividhavimokkhamukhabhāvanti ettha ke pana tayo vimokkhā, kāni vā tīṇi vimokkhamukhānīti antolīne anuyoge vimokkhamukhādhīnattā vimokkhādhigamassa vimokkhamukhāni tāva dassento “tisso hi…pe… vuccantī”ti vatvā ayañca attho pāḷito eva viññāyatīti dassento “yathāhā”tiādimāha.

768. 'Therein' means in that attainment of the state of being a door to deliverance, and in the state of being a condition for the distinction among noble persons. This is insight knowledge. 'Of the three faculties' means of the faculties of faith, concentration, and wisdom. 'By way of dominance' means by way of being dominant over associated states. For one who cultivates the contemplation of impermanence, the faith faculty becomes strong; for one who cultivates the contemplation of suffering, the concentration faculty becomes strong; for one who cultivates the contemplation of not-self, the wisdom faculty becomes strong. Thus he said, 'by way of the threefold contemplation... pe... it is said to attain,' because these three faculties, having attained a more powerful state by way of the three contemplations, produce the state of being a door to deliverance. Regarding 'the state of being a threefold door to deliverance,' in response to the implicit question, 'What are the three deliverances, and what are the three doors to deliverance?'—since the attainment of deliverance is dependent on the doors to deliverance, first showing the doors to deliverance, he said, 'For three... pe... are called,' and then, to show that this meaning is known from the Pāli text itself, he said, 'As it is said,' and so on.

Lokaniyyānāyāti [M 2.0461] lokato nikkhamanāya, sattalokassa vā vaṭṭadukkhato nikkhamanāya. Paricchedaparivaṭumatoti udayabbayavasena paricchedato ceva parivaṭumato ca. Samanupassanatāyāti sammadeva anu anu passanāya saṃvattantīti sambandho. Aniccānupassanā hi saṅkhāre ādito udayena, antato vayena paricchinne passati. Ādiantavantatāya hi te aniccāti. Animittāya ca dhātuyāti sabbasaṅkhāranimittavirahato “animittā”ti laddhanāmāya asaṅkhatāya dhātuyā. Cittasampakkhandanatāyāti paricchinditvā anulomañāṇādibhāvena sammadeva adhicittassa anupavisanatthāya. Appaṇihitāyāti rāgapaṇidhiādīnaṃ abhāvena “appaṇihitā”ti laddhanāmāya. Suññatāyāti attasuññatāya “suññatā”ti laddhanāmāya.

'For leading out of the world' means for exiting from the world, or for exiting from the round of suffering of the world of beings. 'Because of being delimited and circumscribed' means because of being both delimited and circumscribed by way of arising and passing away. 'Because of contemplation' means it conduces to seeing correctly again and again; this is the connection. For the contemplation of impermanence sees formations as delimited at the beginning by arising and at the end by passing away. Indeed, because they have a beginning and an end, they are impermanent. 'And for the signless element' means for the unconditioned element that has obtained the name 'signless' because of the absence of all signs of formations. 'For the leaping of the mind' means for the sake of the higher mind's proper entry by way of conformity knowledge and so on, after having delimited. 'For the desireless' means for that which has obtained the name 'desireless' because of the absence of aspirations such as the aspiration of lust. 'For emptiness' means for that which has obtained the name 'emptiness' because of its being empty of a self.

Gatinti nibbattiṃ. Saṅkhārānaṃ sabhāvavibhāvanena saṃvejiyamānaṃ cittaṃ sammāpaṭipattiyaṃ samuttejitaṃ nāma hotīti āha “manosamuttejanatāyāti cittasaṃvejanatāyā”ti. Mamaṃkārena attaniyasaññitassa vatthuno sāmibhūto attā paṭhamaṃ parāmasīyati, tato attaniyanti āha “nāhaṃ, na mamāti evaṃ anattato samanupassanatāyā”ti. Tīṇi padānīti paricchedaparivaṭuma, manosamuttejana, samanupassanapadānīti vadanti, “sabbasaṅkhāre”tiādīni pana tīṇi vākyāni tīṇi [V 2.0434] padānīti veditabbāni. Tenevāti aniccānupassanādīnaṃ vasena tesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ padānaṃ vuttattā eva. Pañhavissajjaneti “aniccato manasi karoto kathaṃ saṅkhārā upaṭṭhahantī”ti pañhassa vissajjane.

Destination means arising. The mind, stirred by the discernment of the inherent nature of formations, is said to be stimulated towards right practice; hence it is said, ‘by mental stimulation means by stirring of the mind.’ Through the making of ‘mine,’ the self as the owner of an object perceived as ‘what is mine’ is first grasped; then, ‘what is mine’ is grasped. Thus it is said: ‘by contemplating as not-self thus: “This is not I, this is not mine.”’ They say the three terms are delimitation and circumscription, mental stimulation, and contemplation. However, the three sentences beginning with ‘all formations’ should be understood as the three terms. Therefore, it is because these three terms have been stated by way of the contemplation of impermanence, etc. In the answering of the question: in the answer to the question, ‘For one who attends to [them] as impermanent, how do formations appear?’

769. Evaṃ vimokkhamukhāni dassetvā idāni vimokkhe dassetuṃ “katame panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Aniccato manasi karontoti aniccānupassanaṃ anuyuñjanto. Adhimokkhabahuloti saddhindriyabahulo. Yassa visesato aniccānupassanā tikkhā sūrā hoti, tassa saddhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti. “Aniccā saṅkhārā”ti hi ādito saddhāmattakena paṭipajjitvā vipassanāya ukkaṃsagatāya tarupallavādīsu viya maṇikanakādīsupi tesaṃ aniccataṃ sātisayaṃ paccakkhato passato “sammāsambuddho vata so bhagavā”ti satthari saddhā balavatī pavattatīti so adhimokkhabahulo, adhimattasaddho ca hoti. Tassa aniccānupassanābahulatāya aniccākārato [M 2.0462] vuṭṭhānaṃ hotīti so “animittaṃ vimokkhaṃ paṭilabhatī”ti vuttaṃ. Passaddhibahuloti dukkhānupassanaṃ anuyuñjanto “dukkhā saṅkhārā, tappaṭipakkhato sukho nirodho”ti ca manasikāravasena nibbānassa santapaṇītasukhabhāvaṃ adhimuccanto abhiṇhaṃ pītipāmojjasamāyogato passaddhibahulo hoti. Tato ca adhimattasamādhindriyapaṭilābhena rāgapaṇidhiyā dūrībhāvato appaṇihitavimokkhasamadhigamo hotīti vuttaṃ “dukkhato…pe… paṭilabhatī”ti. Vedabahuloti anattānupassanaṃ anuyuñjanto attasuññatāya nipuṇañāṇavisayattā ñāṇabahulo hoti. Tato ca adhimattapaññindriyapaṭilābhena mohassa dūrībhāvato suññatavimokkhasamadhigamo hotīti āha “anattato…pe… paṭilabhatī”ti.

769. Having thus shown the doors to liberation, now, in order to show the liberations, the passage beginning ‘But what are they?’ was stated. ‘One who attends to impermanence’ means a yogi who engages in the contemplation of impermanence. ‘Abundant in resolution’ means abundant in the faculty of faith. For the person for whom the contemplation of impermanence is especially sharp and keen, for that person the faculty of faith becomes exceedingly strong. Indeed, for one who, having initially practiced with mere faith that ‘formations are impermanent,’ when insight becomes elevated, sees directly and exceedingly their impermanence even in jewels, gold, and so on, just as in tender sprouts and so on, strong faith in the Teacher arises: ‘Truly, that Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One!’ Thus, that yogi is abundant in resolution and possessed of exceedingly strong faith. For that yogi, due to the abundance of contemplation of impermanence, emergence occurs from the aspect of impermanence; thus it is said, ‘he attains the signless liberation.’ ‘Abundant in tranquility’ means a yogi who engages in the contemplation of suffering. By way of attention that ‘formations are suffering, and cessation, its opposite, is happiness,’ being resolved upon the state of Nibbāna as peaceful and sublime happiness, he becomes abundant in tranquility through the frequent, proper association with rapture and joy. And from that, through the attainment of the exceedingly strong faculty of concentration, due to the removal of the aspiration which is lust, the attainment of the desireless liberation occurs. Thus it is said: ‘From suffering…pe… he attains.’ ‘Abundant in knowledge’ means a yogi who engages in the contemplation of not-self. Because the emptiness of self is the domain of subtle knowledge, he becomes abundant in knowledge. And from that, through the attainment of the exceedingly strong faculty of wisdom, due to the removal of delusion, the attainment of the emptiness liberation occurs. Thus it is said: ‘From not-self…pe… he attains.’

Yo aniccānupassanāya nimittavasena saṅkhāre pariggahetvā vipassanaṃ anuyuñjanto yattha idaṃ saṅkhāranimittaṃ sabbaso natthi, taṃ “animittaṃ nibbāna”nti animittākārena adhimuccanto vuṭṭhānagāminimaggena ghaṭeti. Tassa maggo animittato nibbānaṃ sacchikarotīti vuccatīti āha “animittākārena nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavatto ariyamaggo”ti. Svāyaṃ nibbānassa animittākāro neva maggena kato, na vipassanāya, atha kho sabhāvasiddho. Tadārammaṇatāya ca maggo animittoti vuccatīti dassento āha “animittāya dhātuyā uppannattā animitto”ti. Yo dukkhānupassanāvasena paṇidhiyā dūrībhāvakaraṇena appaṇihitaṃ adhimuccanto[V 2.0435], yo anattānupassanāvasena attūpaladdhiyā dūrībhāvakaraṇena suññataṃ adhimuccantoti ca ādinā yojetabbaṃ. Tenāha “eteneva nayenā”tiādi.

A person who, having grasped formations by way of their sign through the contemplation of impermanence and practicing insight, becomes resolved in its signless aspect upon that wherein this sign of formations is entirely absent—that is, 'the signless Nibbāna'—and strives by means of the path leading to emergence. For that person, it is said that the path realizes Nibbāna as signless. Therefore, he said: ‘The noble path that has occurred having taken Nibbāna in its signless aspect as its object.’ This signless aspect of Nibbāna is made neither by the path nor by insight, but is indeed established by its own nature. And, to show that the path is called ‘signless’ because it has that as its object, he said: ‘Because it has arisen in relation to the signless element, it is signless.’ It should be connected in this way and so on: a person who, by means of the contemplation of suffering, is resolved upon the desireless by causing the removal of aspiration; and a person who, by means of the contemplation of not-self, is resolved upon emptiness by causing the removal of the apprehension of self. Therefore, he said: ‘By this same method,’ and so on.

770. Yadi ariyamaggo tividhampi vimokkhanāmaṃ labhati, atha kasmā abhidhamme vimokkhadvayameva āgatanti codanaṃ sandhāyāha “yaṃ panā”tiādi. Tattha tanti abhidhamme vimokkhadvayavacanaṃ. Nippariyāyato vipassanāgamanaṃ sandhāyāti ujukameva vipassanato maggassa nāmāgamanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kasmā? Animittavipassanā āgamanīyaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā attano maggassa nāmaṃ dātuṃ na sakkoti. Kāmaṃ sutte “animittañca bhāvehi, mānānusayamujjahā”ti (su. ni. 344) animittavipassanā kathitā, sā pana niccanimittadhuvanimittaattanimittāni [M 2.0463] ugghāṭentīpi sayaṃ nimittadhammesu eva caratīti sanimittāva hotīti. Apica abhidhammo nāma paramatthadesanā, animittamaggassa ca paramatthato hetuvekallameva. Aniccānupassanāvasena hi animittavimokkho kathito. Tattha ca saddhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti, taṃ ariyamagge ekaṅgampi na hoti, amaggaṅgattā attano maggassa nāmaṃ dātuṃ na sakkoti. Itaresu dukkhānupassanāya vasena appaṇihitavimokkho, anattānupassanāya vasena suññatavimokkho.

770. In reference to the objection, ‘If the noble path obtains the name of liberation in three ways, then why in the Abhidhamma has only a pair of liberations been mentioned?’ the passage beginning ‘But as to that…’ was stated. Therein, the text refers to the statement in the Abhidhamma about the pair of liberations. This is said with reference to the non-figurative approach from insight, that is, it is said with reference to the name coming to the path directly from insight. Why? Because signless insight, though standing in the position of being the approach, cannot give its name to its own path. Although in the Suttas signless insight is spoken of—‘Develop the signless and abandon the underlying tendency to conceit’ (Snp 4.10)—and although it eradicates the signs of permanence, stability, and self, it itself operates on things that possess signs, so it is itself with a sign. Moreover, the Abhidhamma is the teaching on ultimate reality, and for the signless path, in an ultimate sense, there is a deficiency of a cause. For the signless liberation is spoken of by way of the contemplation of impermanence. And there the faculty of faith is predominant, but that is not even a single factor of the noble path. Since it is not a path factor, it cannot give its name to its own path. In the other cases, the desireless liberation is by way of the contemplation of suffering, and the emptiness liberation is by way of the contemplation of not-self.

Tesu appaṇihitavimokkhena samādhindriyaṃ, suññatavimokkhena paññindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hotīti tāni ariyamaggassa aṅgattā attano maggassa nāmaṃ dātuṃ sakkonti, na animittamaggo tadabhāvatoti keci. Ye pana vadanti “animittamaggo āgamanato nāmaṃ alabhantopi saguṇato ca ārammaṇato ca nāmaṃ labhatī”ti, tesaṃ matena appaṇihitasuññatamaggāpi saguṇato eva, ārammaṇato eva ca nāmaṃ labheyyunti? Taṃ ayuttaṃ. Kasmā? Maggo hi dvīhi kāraṇehi nāmaṃ labhati sarasato ca paccanīkato cāti, sabhāvato ca paṭipakkhato cāti attho. Appaṇihitamaggo hi rāgapaṇidhiādīhi vimutto, suññatamaggo rāgādīhi suñño evāti te sarasato nāmaṃ labhanti. Tathā appaṇihitamaggo paṇidhissa paṭipakkho, suññatamaggo attābhinivesassa evāti te paccanīkato nāmaṃ labhanti, animittamaggo pana rāgādinimittānaṃ, niccanimittādīnaṃ vā abhāvena sarasato eva nāmaṃ labhati, no paccanīkato. Na hi so saṅkhāranimittārammaṇāya aniccānupassanāya paṭipakkho, sā [V 2.0436] panassa anulomabhāve ṭhitāti sabbathāpi abhidhammapariyāyena animittamaggo na labbhati. Tena vuttaṃ “taṃ nippariyāyato vipassanāgamanaṃ sandhāyā”ti.

Among these, with the desireless liberation the faculty of concentration is predominant, and with the emptiness liberation the faculty of wisdom is predominant. Since these are factors of the noble path, they can give their names to their own path, but the signless path cannot, due to the absence of such a factor, some say. But as to those who say, ‘Although the signless path does not obtain a name from its approach, it does obtain a name from its own quality and from its object’—according to their view, would the desireless and emptiness paths also obtain names only from their qualities and only from their objects? That is not proper. Why? The path obtains its name for two reasons: from its own essence and from its opposition—that is, from its own nature and from being an antidote. For the desireless path is liberated from aspirations for lust, etc., and the emptiness path is empty of lust, etc.; thus they obtain their names from their own essence. Similarly, the desireless path is the antidote to aspiration, and the emptiness path is the antidote to clinging to self; thus they obtain their names from opposition. The signless path, however, obtains its name only from its own essence—due to the absence of the signs of lust, etc., or the signs of permanence, etc.—but not from opposition. For it is not the antidote to the contemplation of impermanence, which takes the sign of formations as its object; rather, that contemplation stands in conformity with it. Therefore, in every way, the signless path is not obtained according to the Abhidhamma exposition. Hence it was said: ‘That is said with reference to the non-figurative approach from insight.’

Yasmā suttantapariyāyena animittamaggo labbhati. Vuṭṭhānagāminī hi vipassanā yaṃ yaṃ sammasantī vuṭṭhānaṃ gacchati, tassa tassa vasena āgamanīyaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā attano maggassa nāmaṃ deti, tattha aniccato vuṭṭhahantassa maggo animitto hoti, dukkhato vuṭṭhahantassa appaṇihito, anattato vuṭṭhahantassa suññato, tasmā suttantasaṃvaṇṇanā esāti katvā idha tayopi vimokkhā uddhaṭā. Yaṃ pana paṭisambhidāmagge abhinivesanimittapaṇidhimuñcanaṃ upādāya tissannampi anupassanānaṃ tadāgamanavasena tadanvayassa maggassa ca suññatavimokkhādibhāvo niddiṭṭho, tassa pariyāyabhāve [M 2.0464] vattabbameva natthīti dassetuṃ “vipassanāñāṇaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vipassanāñāṇaṃ paṭisambhidāmagge “appaṇihito, vimokkho”ti ca kiñcāpi vuttanti sambandho.

Because the signless path is obtained by the Suttanta method. For insight leading to emergence gives its name to its own path by standing in the position of being the approach, based on whatever it emerges from contemplating. Therein, for one emerging from impermanence, the path is signless; for one emerging from suffering, it is desireless; for one emerging from not-self, it is empty. Therefore, having considered that this is the Suttanta explanation, all three liberations have been cited here. But as to the fact that in the Paṭisambhidāmagga, on account of relinquishing adherence, the sign, and aspiration, the state of being the emptiness liberation, etc., has been indicated for all three contemplations based on the cause of their arising and for the path that follows from them—to show that there is nothing to be said about this being a figurative expression, the passage beginning ‘For insight knowledge…’ was stated. The connection is: Although in the Paṭisambhidāmagga insight knowledge is also called ‘desireless’ and ‘liberation’...

Aniccānupassanāñāṇanti “aniccā saṅkhārā”ti anupassanāvasena pavattañāṇaṃ. Niccato abhinivesaṃ muñcatīti “te niccā”ti niccākārato pavattamicchābhinivesaviddhaṃsanavasena, tadanvayaṃ pana maggañāṇaṃ samucchedavasena muñcati. Itīti tasmā. Aniccābhinivesato rittatāya, vimuttatāya ca suññato vimokkho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.

Knowledge of the contemplation of impermanence is the knowledge that proceeds by way of contemplating ‘formations are impermanent.’ It releases adherence to permanence means: by way of destroying the wrong adherence that proceeds in the aspect of permanence as ‘they are permanent’; but the path knowledge that follows from that releases it by way of eradication. Therefore, because of being empty of and liberated from adherence to permanence, it is the emptiness liberation. This same method applies to the remaining passages.

Tanti tividhaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ. Tattha yassa pariyāyato, yassa ca nippariyāyato nāmalābho, taṃ dassetuṃ “saṅkhāranimittassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Na nippariyāyena, atha kho pariyāyenāti attho. Tasmāti nippariyāyakathābhāvato. Vimokkhadvayameva vuttaṃ abhidhammeti adhippāyo. Etthāti etasmiṃ vipassanādhikāre. “Tividhavimokkhamukhabhāvaṃ āpajjitvā”ti etasmiṃ vā uddesavacane.

That insight knowledge is threefold. Herein, to show which of them obtains a name figuratively and which obtains it non-figuratively, the passage beginning ‘of the sign of formations…’ was stated. The meaning is: not non-figuratively, but rather figuratively. Therefore, because it is a non-figurative account, the intention is that only two liberations are mentioned in the Abhidhamma. Herein—that is, in this section on insight, or in this summary statement: ‘having arrived at the state of being an entrance to the threefold liberation.’

771. Tesaṃ vibhāgāyāti tesaṃ yathāvuttānaṃ sattannaṃ ariyapuggalānaṃ saddhānusāriādibhāvena vibhattasabhāvatāya.

771. For their distinction: that is, for the sake of the distinguished state of those seven aforementioned noble individuals, by way of being a faith-follower and so on.

772. Saddhindriyaṃ paṭilabhatīti saddhānusāribhāvitākāraṇabhūtaṃ adhimattaṃ saddhindriyaṃ paṭilabhati. Adhimokkhabahulatāya, saddhindriyādhimattatāya ca kāraṇaṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Apica ayamettha [V 2.0437] saṅkhepattho – aniccākārasallakkhaṇassa saddhābhibuddhiyā upanissayabhāvato tadanvaye magge saddhā tikkhatarā hoti, tena aṭṭhamako saddhānusārī nāma hoti. Sesesu sattasu ṭhānesūti paṭhamaphalato paṭṭhāya yāva aggaphalā sattasu ṭhānesu. “Sattasu ṭhānesū”ti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu sesesu chasu ṭhānesu saddhāvimutto, aggaphale pana sacāyaṃ arūpajjhānalābhī, ubhatobhāgavimutto hoti, no ce arūpajjhānalābhī, paññāvimutto, na saddhāvimutto. Abhidhamme hi –

772. One attains the faculty of faith: this means one attains the intensified faculty of faith, which is the cause for the developed state of being a faith-follower. The reason for the abundance of resolution and for the predominance of the faculty of faith has already been stated before. Moreover, the concise meaning here is this: because the contemplation of the characteristic of impermanence is a decisive support for the growth of faith, faith becomes sharper in the path that follows from that. Thus, the eighth individual is called a faith-follower. In the remaining seven instances: that is, in the seven instances from the first fruition up to the highest fruition. Why is it said, 'in seven instances'? Is it not that in the remaining six instances one is liberated by faith, while at the highest fruition, if one has obtained the formless jhānas, one is liberated in both ways, and if one has not obtained them, one is liberated by wisdom, not liberated by faith? For in the Abhidhamma:

“Katamo ca puggalo saddhāvimutto? Idhekacco puggalo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tathāgatappaveditā cassa dhammā paññāya diṭṭhā [M 2.0465] honti, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā honti, no ca kho yathādiṭṭhippattassa. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo saddhāvimutto”ti (pu. pa. 208) –

And what kind of person is one liberated by faith? Here, a certain person understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’; ‘This is the origin of suffering’; ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ The teachings declared by the Tathāgata have been seen by them with wisdom, and having seen them with wisdom, some of their taints are destroyed, but not to the same extent as for one attained to view. This person is called one liberated by faith.

Ekaccāsavaparikkhayavacanato saddhāvimuttassa sekkhabhāvo viññāyati, na asekkhabhāvo. Aṭṭhakathāyañca “dve dhurāni, dve abhinivesā, dve sīsānī”ti vacanato natthi arahato saddhāvimuttatāti? Saccametaṃ nippariyāyato. Nippariyāyakathā hi abhidhammo, idha pana pariyāyena evaṃ vuttaṃ. Yadi pariyāyato arahato saddhāvimuttatā, ko pana so pariyāyo? Saddhāvimuttanvayatā. Yo hi aggamaggakkhaṇe saddhāvimutto hoti, so aggaphalakkhaṇepi tadanvayatāya saddhāvimuttoti paṭisambhidāmagge pariyāyena vuttoti idhāpi tatheva vuttaṃ. Atha vā saddhāvimuttasadisatāya arahā saddhāvimutto. Kā panettha sadisatā? Yathā saddhāvimuttassa sekkhassa kilesakkhayo kuṇṭhena asinā kadalicchedasadiso “no ca kho yathādiṭṭhippattassā”ti vacanato, evaṃ tadanvayassāpi arahatoti ayamettha sadisatā. Kiṃ pana nesaṃ kilesapahāne nānattaṃ atthīti? Natthi. Atha kasmā saddhāvimutto diṭṭhippattaṃ na pāpuṇātīti? Āgamanīyanānattena. Diṭṭhippatto hi āgamanamhi kilese vikkhambhento appakasirena akilamanto vikkhambhetuṃ sakkoti, saddhāvimutto kicchena kasirena vikkhambhetuṃ sakkoti. Apica paññāyapi nesaṃ vemattatā. Sā ca yāvatikā labbhatevāti vadanti. Evañca katvā paṭhamamaggādīsu satipi indriyasamatte saddhādīnaṃ tikkhatāvacanampi samatthitaṃ hoti.

From the statement 'some of their taints are destroyed,' it is understood that the one liberated by faith is a trainee, not a non-trainee. And in the commentary, from the statement 'two yokes, two resolves, two heads,' does it follow that there is no arahant who is liberated by faith? This is true non-figuratively. For the Abhidhamma is a non-figurative account, but here this is stated figuratively. If an arahant is liberated by faith figuratively, what then is that figurative sense? It is being in the lineage of one liberated by faith. For one who is liberated by faith at the moment of the supreme path is, at the moment of the supreme fruit, also called 'liberated by faith' figuratively in the Paṭisambhidāmagga on account of being in that lineage; and here, too, it is stated in the same way. Or else, an arahant is 'liberated by faith' because of similarity to one liberated by faith. What is the similarity here? Just as for the trainee liberated by faith the destruction of defilements is like cutting a plantain trunk with a blunt sword—in accordance with the words 'but not as for one attained to view'—so too is it for the arahant who is in that lineage. This is the similarity here. But is there any difference in their abandoning of defilements? There is not. Then why does one liberated by faith not attain to the state of one attained to view? Because of the difference in their path of approach. For one attained to view, while suppressing the defilements on the path of approach, is able to suppress them with little trouble and without fatigue; but one liberated by faith is able to suppress them only with difficulty and trouble. Moreover, there is also a difference in their wisdom. And they say that this difference is just as much as can be obtained. And for this reason, even in the first path and so on, despite the balance of the faculties, the statement about the sharpness of faith and other faculties is also justified.

773. Soti [V 2.0438] dukkhato vuṭṭhito. Sabbatthāti aṭṭhasupi ṭhānesu. Nanu ca aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “dve dhurānī”ti niyamitattā paṭhamamaggakkhaṇe saddhānusārī vā siyā, dhammānusārī vā? Idha na saddhānusārī yutto, kāyasakkhitāpi arahato natthi. Abhidhamme hi –

773. 'He': that is, one who has emerged from suffering. 'In all': that is, in all eight instances. But is it not so that in the commentary, because it is determined by 'two yokes,' at the moment of the first path one might be either a faith-follower or a Dhamma-follower? Here, a faith-follower is not appropriate, and the state of a body-witness also does not exist for an arahant. For in the Abhidhamma:

“Katamo ca puggalo kāyasakkhī? Idhekacco puggalo aṭṭha vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo kāyasakkhī”ti (pu. pa. 208) –

And what person is a body-witness? Here, a certain person dwells having touched the eight liberations with the body, and for them, having seen with wisdom, some taints are destroyed. This person is called a body-witness.

Ekaccāsavaparikkhayavacanato [M 2.0466] kāyasakkhino sekkhabhāvova viññāyatīti? Saccametaṃ nippariyāyato, idha pana pariyāyena vuttaṃ. Ko pana so pariyāyoti? Kāyasakkhisadisatā. Upacārarūpajjhānasamādhito hi sātisayaṃ arūpasamādhisamphassaṃ laddhā nibbattīti ekaccāsavaparikkhayaṃ upādāya “kāyasakkhī”ti vattabbapuggalena sātisayasamādhisamphassatadadhiṭṭhānāsavaparikkhayasāmaññaṃ apekkhitvā kāyasakkhī viya kāyasakkhīti arahā paṭisambhidāmagge vuttoti idhāpi tameva nayaṃ gahetvā arahatopi kāyasakkhitā vuttā. Suttantasaṃvaṇṇanā hesāti. Nippariyāyena pana paṭhamaphalato paṭṭhāya chasu ṭhānesu kāyasakkhī nāma hoti, so ca kho aṭṭhasamāpattilābhī, na vipassanāyāniko sukkhavipassako, upacāramattalābhī, rūpajjhānamattalābhī vā. Passaddhibahuloti ca passaddhisīsena samādhi vuttoti sātisayasamādhilābhī samathayānikova adhippeto, samathayānikasseva ca kāyasakkhibhāvo heṭṭhā vutto. Arūpajjhānanti catubbidhaṃ arūpajjhānaṃ. Tattha pana ekampi laddhā arahattaṃ patto ubhatobhāgavimutto eva hotīti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “arūpajjhāna”micceva vuttaṃ, na “cattāri arūpajjhānānī”ti. Tenāyaṃ catunnaṃ arūpasamāpattīnaṃ, nirodhasamāpattiyā ca vasena pañcavidho hoti. Esa nayo kāyasakkhimhipi. Dvīhi bhāgehi dve vāre vimuttoti ubhatobhāgavimutto.

From the statement 'some taints are destroyed,' is it not understood that the state of a body-witness is exclusively that of a trainee? This is true non-figuratively, but here it is stated figuratively. What then is that figurative sense? Similarity to a body-witness. For in the Paṭisambhidāmagga an Arahant is called a 'body-witness' in the sense of being like a body-witness, with reference to a commonality with a person who is to be called a 'body-witness'—one who, on account of the destruction of some taints, has obtained contact with a superior formless concentration that surpasses the concentration of access and of the form jhānas. This commonality consists in the contact with superior concentration and the destruction of taints based upon it. Therefore, here too, having adopted that same method, the state of a body-witness is ascribed even to an Arahant. For this is a commentary on the Suttantas. Non-figuratively, however, the name 'body-witness' applies in the six instances starting from the first fruition. And that person is an obtainer of the eight attainments, not a practitioner of the insight vehicle, a dry-insight practitioner, one who has obtained only access concentration, or one who has obtained only form jhāna. And by 'abounding in tranquility,' concentration is meant with tranquility as its head; thus a practitioner of the serenity vehicle who has obtained superior concentration is intended, and the state of a body-witness has been stated before only for a practitioner of the serenity vehicle. 'Formless jhāna' means the fourfold formless jhāna. But here, to show this meaning—that one who has attained Arahantship after obtaining even one of them is one liberated in both ways—it is just said 'formless jhāna,' not 'the four formless jhānas.' Thus this person is fivefold by way of the four formless attainments and the attainment of cessation. This same method applies also to the body-witness. 'Liberated by two parts' or 'on two occasions,' thus 'liberated in both ways.'

774. Paññavato nipuṇatarā, gambhīrā ca atthā pākaṭā hutvā upaṭṭhahantīti anattato manasi karoto vedabahulatā, paññindriyapaṭilābho ca vutto. Dhammānusārī hoti paññindriyassa adhimattattā. Paññā hi idha “dhammo”ti adhippetā “saccaṃ dhammo dhiti cāgo”tiādīsu viya (jā. 1.1.57).

774. Because for a person of great wisdom, meanings that are especially subtle and profound become manifest and present themselves, for one who attends by way of not-self, an abundance of wisdom and the attainment of the faculty of wisdom are stated. One is a Dhamma-follower due to the predominance of the faculty of wisdom. Indeed, here 'Dhamma' is intended as wisdom, as in passages such as: 'Truth, Dhamma, fortitude, and generosity…' (Ja 1.1.57).

775. Yassā [V 2.0439] pāḷiyā vasena idha ariyapuggalassa saddhāvimuttādibhāvo vutto, taṃ pāḷiṃ dassetuṃ “vuttaṃ heta”ntiādi āraddhaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva.

775. To show the Pāḷi text by means of which the state of a noble person as one liberated-by-faith and so on is stated here, the passage beginning 'For this was said…' was introduced. That is indeed easy to understand.

776. “Saddhindriyassa adhimattattā saddhāvimutto”ti evamādiatthassa sādhakaṃ aparampi vuttaṃ. “Saddahanto vimutto”ti etena sabbathā avimuttassa [M 2.0467] saddhāmattena vimuttabhāvadassanena saddhāvimuttassa sekkhabhāvameva vibhāveti. Saddhāvimuttoti vā saddhāya adhimuttoti attho.

776. Something further has been said that establishes the meaning of such statements as: 'One is liberated-by-faith because of the predominance of the faculty of faith.' By this text, 'Liberated while having faith,' it clarifies only the state of being a trainee for one who is liberated-by-faith, by showing a state of liberation through mere faith for one who is not at all liberated. Or, 'liberated-by-faith' means one who is resolved by faith.

Phuṭṭhantaṃ sacchikatoti phuṭṭhānaṃ anantaraṃ phuṭṭhanto, phuṭṭhānaṃ arūpajjhānānaṃ anantaro kāloti adhippāyo, accantasaṃyoge cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ, phuṭṭhānantarakālameva sacchikaraṇūpāyena sacchikātabbaṃ sacchākāsīti vuttaṃ hoti. Bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ vā etaṃ yathā “ekamanta”nti (pārā. 2). Yo hi arūpajjhānena rūpakāyato, nāmakāyekadesato ca vikkhambhanavimokkhena vimutto, tena nirodhasaṅkhāto vimokkho ālocito pakāsito viya hoti, na pana kāyena sacchikato, nirodhaṃ pana ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaccesu āsavesu khepitesu tena so sacchikatova hoti. Tasmā so sacchikātabbaṃ yathāālocitaṃ nāmakāyena sacchākāsīti kāyasakkhīti vuccati, na tu vimutto ekaccānaṃ āsavānaṃ aparikkhīṇattā. Diṭṭhantaṃ pattoti dassanasaṅkhātassa sotāpattimaggañāṇassa anantaraṃ pattoti vuttaṃ hoti. Paṭhamaphalato paṭṭhāya hi yāva aggamaggā diṭṭhippattoti. “Diṭṭhiyā patto”ti vā pāṭho, catusaccadassanasaṅkhātāya diṭṭhiyā nirodhaṃ pattoti attho. Ime ca saddhāvimuttādayo tayo paramatthato apariyositañāṇakiccāti taṃ nayaṃ dassetuṃ “saddahanto vimuccatī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Jhānaphassanti sātisayaṃ jhānaphassaṃ. Tena arūpajjhānaphasso saṅgahito hoti.

‘He has realized the end of what has been touched’ means the end of what has been touched, [realized] immediately after what has been touched. The intention is that this is the time immediately after what has been touched, that is, the formless jhānas. This is an accusative of continuous connection. It is said that he has realized what is to be realized by the means of realization at the very time immediately after what has been touched. Or this is a neuter noun of state, like ‘ekamantaṃ’ (Pārā. 2). For one who is liberated from the material body and from a part of the mental body by the liberation-by-suppression of the formless jhānas, for him the liberation called cessation is as if considered and revealed, but not realized with the (mental) body. But when, having made cessation the object, some taints have been destroyed, by him it is indeed realized. Therefore, because he has realized with the mental body what is to be realized as it was considered, he is called a ‘body-witness,’ but he is not liberated because some taints are not yet destroyed. ‘Attained-to-view’ means it is said that he has attained it immediately after the knowledge of the path of stream-entry, which is designated as ‘seeing.’ For from the first fruition up to the highest path, he is called ‘attained-to-view.’ Or the reading is ‘attained by view’; the meaning is that he has attained cessation by the view designated as the seeing of the Four Noble Truths. And these three—the faith-liberated one and others—in the ultimate sense have an uncompleted task of knowledge. To show this method, it is said, ‘Believing, one is liberated,’ and so on. ‘Jhāna-contact’ means superior jhāna-contact. By this, the contact of the formless jhānas is included.

“Dukkhā saṅkhārāti ñātaṃ hotī”ti iminā dukkhasaccapaṭivedhamāha, “sukho nirodhoti ñātaṃ hotī”ti iminā nirodhasaccapaṭivedhaṃ. Tadubhayena ca samudayamaggasaccapaṭivedhaṃ nānantariyakabhāvato. “Ñātaṃ hotī”ti iminā dutiyamaggakiccaṃ, “diṭṭhaṃ hotī”ti iminā tatiyamaggakiccaṃ, “viditaṃ hotī”ti iminā catutthamaggakiccaṃ, “sacchikata”nti iminā paṭhamaphalakiccaṃ, “phusita”nti iminā sesaphaladvayakiccaṃ. Iti diṭṭhippattassa maggaphalañāṇabyāpāradassanāni imāni padānīti vadanti.

‘Formations are suffering—this is known’: by this, he states the penetration of the truth of suffering. ‘Cessation is bliss—this is known’: by this, he states the penetration of the truth of cessation. And by both of these, he states the penetration of the truth of the origin and the path, because of their inseparable nature. By ‘this is known,’ the function of the second path is stated; by ‘this is seen,’ the function of the third path; by ‘this is cognized,’ the function of the fourth path; by ‘realized,’ the function of the first fruition; by ‘touched,’ the function of the remaining two fruitions. Thus, they say, these terms are demonstrations of the operations of the path and fruition knowledges for one who is attained-to-view.

777. Itaresūti [V 2.0440] saddhānusāriādipadesu. Saddhaṃ anusaratīti āgamanīyaṭṭhāne ṭhitaṃ saddhaṃ anugacchati. Yathā sā tikkhā sūrā ahosi[M 2.0468], maggakkhaṇepi tadanurūpameva pavattetīti attho. Saddhāya vā anusaratīti saddhāya kāraṇabhūtāya saccapaṭivedhassa anurūpaṃ sarati gacchati, paṭipajjatīti attho. Dvīhipi atthavikappehi saddhāya adhimattataṃyeva vibhāveti. Dhammānusārīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Ubhatobhāgavimuttoti dvīhi bhāgehi dve vāre vimutto, rūpakāyato ca nāmakāyato ca vikkhambhanavasena, samucchedavasena ca vimuttoti attho. Arūpajjhānena rūpakāyato ca nāmakāyekadesato ca vimutto, ariyamaggena nāmakāyato vimuttoti ubhohi bhāgehi dve vāre vimuttattā ubhatobhāgavimutto. Pajānanto vimuttoti paṭhamajjhānaphassena vinā parijānanādippakārehi cattāri ariyasaccāni jānanto paṭivijjhanto tesaṃ kiccānaṃ matthakappattiyā niṭṭhitakiccatāya visesena muttoti vimutto.

777. ‘In the others’ refers to the terms such as faith-follower, etc. ‘He follows faith’ means he follows after the faith that is established in a trustworthy position. The meaning is that just as that faith was sharp and heroic, so too at the moment of the path he makes it proceed in a corresponding way. Or, ‘he follows by means of faith’ means that with faith as the cause, he goes or practices in conformity with the penetration of the truths. By both alternative meanings, it clarifies the predominance of faith. In the case of the Dhamma-follower, too, the method is the same. ‘Liberated in both respects’ means liberated on two occasions by two parts: liberated from the material body and the mental body by way of suppression and by way of eradication. He is liberated from the material body and from a part of the mental body by means of the formless jhānas, and liberated from the mental body by the noble path; thus, because he is liberated on two occasions by both parts, he is ‘liberated in both respects.’ ‘Liberated by wisdom’ means that, without the contact of the first jhāna, by such means as fully understanding, he knows and penetrates the four noble truths. By reaching the culmination of those functions, having completed the task, he is specially freed, thus ‘liberated’.

Ayaṃ panettha nippariyāyato saṅkhepakathā – yassa aniccākārato vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, so adhimokkhabahulo saddhindriyassa tikkhabhāvena paṭhamamaggakkhaṇe saddhānusārī nāma hoti, majjhe chasu ṭhānesu saddhāvimutto. Aggaphalakkhaṇe paññāvimutto nāma hoti. Tathā yassa dukkhākārato vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, tassa passaddhibahulatāya samādhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti dukkhupanisāya saddhāyapi tibbatarattā, dhuraniyamato ca. Sopi paṭhamamaggakkhaṇe saddhānusārī eva hoti, majjhe chasu ṭhānesu saddhāvimutto, ante paññāvimutto ca hoti. Yassa pana anattākārato vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, so vedabahulo paññindriyassa tikkhabhāvena paṭhamamaggakkhaṇe dhammānusārī eva hoti, majjhe chasu ṭhānesu diṭṭhippatto, ante paññāvimutto eva hoti. Ime pana na aṭṭhavimokkhalābhino, aṭṭhavimokkhalābhī pana paṭhamamaggakkhaṇe saddhānusārī vā dhammānusārī vā siyā. Majjhe chasu ṭhānesu kāyasakkhī, pariyosāne ubhatobhāgavimuttoti.

This, however, is the concise explanation here in a direct sense: One whose emergence is through the aspect of impermanence is abundant in resolution; due to the sharpness of the faith faculty, at the moment of the first path, he is called a faith-follower; in the middle, in the six stages, a faith-liberated one. At the moment of the highest fruition, he is called a wisdom-liberated one. Similarly, one whose emergence is through the aspect of suffering has an abundance of tranquility, and the concentration faculty is predominant, because suffering is a supporting condition, because of the extreme sharpness of faith, and because of the fixed rule of the seven. He too, at the moment of the first path, is indeed a faith-follower; in the middle, in the six stages, a faith-liberated one, and in the end, a wisdom-liberated one. But one whose emergence is through the aspect of non-self is abundant in knowledge; due to the sharpness of the wisdom faculty, at the moment of the first path, he is indeed a Dhamma-follower; in the middle, in the six stages, one attained-to-view; and in the end, indeed a wisdom-liberated one. These, however, are not attainers of the eight liberations. But an attainer of the eight liberations might be a faith-follower or a Dhamma-follower at the moment of the first path. In the middle, in the six stages, he is a body-witness; at the end, one liberated in both respects.

Saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ.

The knowledge of equanimity towards formations.

778. Yaṃ taṃ vimokkhamukhabhāvaṃ āpajjitvā sattaariyapuggalavibhāgāya ca paccayo hotīti vuttaṃ, taṃ panetaṃ saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ. Purimena ñāṇadvayenāti muñcitukamyatāpaṭisaṅkhānupassanāñāṇadvayena atthato [M 2.0469] ekaṃ, pavattiākārabhedato nānanti adhippāyo. Yathāvuttamatthaṃ aṭṭhakathāya, pāḷiyā ca sādhetuṃ “tenāhū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Muñcitukamyatāmuñcanupāyakaraṇañāṇānipi saṅkhāresu udāsīnabhāveneva pavattanato saṅkhārupekkhāsamaññāneva hontīti [V 2.0441] vuttaṃ “idaṃ saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ ekameva tīṇi nāmāni labhatī”ti. Tena saṅkhārupekkhāvohāro muñcitukamyatādiñāṇasamudāyavisayoti dasseti.

778. That which was said to be a condition for the division of the seven noble persons by having reached the state of being a gateway to liberation, that is this knowledge of equanimity towards formations. 'By the previous pair of knowledges' refers to the two knowledges of desire for deliverance and contemplation of reflection. The intention is that they are one in essence but different in their mode of occurrence. To establish the aforesaid meaning by means of the commentary and the Pāḷi, it was stated, 'Therefore they said,' and so on. The knowledges of the desire for deliverance and of making the means for deliverance also receive the designation 'equanimity towards formations' because they proceed towards formations only with an attitude of indifference. Thus it was said: 'This knowledge of equanimity towards formations, though one, obtains three names.' Thereby he shows that the term 'equanimity towards formations' has as its object the collection of the knowledges beginning with the desire for deliverance.

780. Uppādādīnīti uppādapavattādiapadesena vutte saṅkhāre. Pariccajitukāmatāti tappaṭibandhachandarāgappahānena vissajjitukāmatā. Paṭisaṅkhānanti punappunaṃ tīraṇaṃ. Muñcitvāti nirālayabhāvāpattiyā apekkhāvissajjanavasena vissajjitvā. Avasāneti tathākaraṇassa uttarakālaṃ. Yāva nibbānasampakkhandanā na ijjhati, tāva vicinanepi udāsīnatāya ñāṇassa santānavasena pavattiṃ sandhāyāha “ajjhupekkhanaṃ santiṭṭhanā”ti. Evanti ajjhupekkhanākārasāmaññato “muñcitukamyatā ca sā santiṭṭhanā cā”ti vuttākārena.

780. ‘Arising, etc.’ refers to the formations spoken of under the headings of arising, occurrence, and so on. ‘Desire to abandon’ is the desire to relinquish by abandoning the desire and lust that are connected to it. ‘Reflection’ is repeated scrutiny. ‘Having relinquished’ means having relinquished by way of abandoning expectation through the attainment of a state without longing. ‘At the end’ means the time subsequent to having done so. With reference to the proceeding of knowledge by way of a continuum with equanimity even while investigating, for as long as the plunging into Nibbāna is not accomplished, he says, ‘equanimous observation and stability.’ ‘Thus’ means because of the similarity in the mode of equanimous observation, in the way stated as ‘it is both the desire for deliverance and that stability.’

781. Ime dhammāti ime ñāṇasaṅkhātā dhammā, ñāṇapariyāyo vā idha dhamma-saddo, tasmā imāni ñāṇānīti attho. Ekattāti ekasabhāvā.

781. ‘These dhammas’ means these dhammas designated as knowledges, or here the word ‘dhamma’ is a synonym for knowledge; therefore the meaning is ‘these knowledges.’ ‘Oneness’ means having a single nature.

782. Vuṭṭhānagāminī hoti vuṭṭhānagamanato. Saṅkhārupekkhādiñāṇattayassāti saṅkhārupekkhānulomagotrabhusaññitassa ñāṇattayassa. Kiccavasena pavattiṭṭhānavasenapi lokiyañāṇānaṃ upari ṭhitattā vuttaṃ “uttamabhāvaṃ pattattā”ti. Nimittabhūtatoti vipassanāya ārammaṇabhūtato khandhapañcakato. Tenāha “abhiniviṭṭhavatthuto”ti. Tañhi vipassanāya gocarakaraṇasaṅkhātena abhinivesena abhiniviṭṭhavatthunti pavuccati. Taṃ panetaṃ sasantatipariyāpannampi parato diṭṭhitāya “bahiddhā”ti vuttaṃ. Tadeva hi “bahiddhā sabbanimittānī”ti tattha tattha vuccati. Ajjhattapavattatoti sasantāne micchādiṭṭhipavattanaādito, tadanuvattakakilesakkhandhehi ca. Tañhi sasantatiyaṃ kilesappavattabhāvato, tannimittaṃ asati maggabhāvanāya uppajjanakaupādinnakkhandhapavattabhāvato ca tathā vuttaṃ. Vuṭṭhahanañca nesaṃ ārammaṇākaraṇaṃ, āyatiṃ anuppattidhammatāpādanañca. Ghaṭiyati attano anantarameva maggasamuppattito.

782. It is emergence-leading because it goes to emergence. This refers to the triad of knowledges designated as equanimity towards formations, conformity, and change-of-lineage. Because it stands above the mundane knowledges by way of function and its state of occurrence, it is said ‘because it has attained the supreme state.’ ‘From what has become the sign’ means from the five aggregates that have become the object of insight. Hence he says, ‘from the object of adherence.’ For it is called ‘the object of adherence’ because of the adherence designated as making it the resort of insight. But this, though included in one's own continuity, is called ‘external’ because it is seen as other. For that same thing is called in various places ‘all external signs.’ ‘From what occurs internally’ means from the occurrence of wrong view, etc., in one's own continuity, and from the accompanying aggregates of defilements. For it is so called because of the occurrence of defilements in one's own continuity, and because of the occurrence of the clung-to aggregates which have that as their cause and which arise in the absence of the development of the path. And emergence from them is the not-making them an object and the bringing them to a state of non-arising in the future. It connects, because of the arising of the path immediately after itself.

783. Tatrāti [M 2.0470] tasmiṃ “abhiniviṭṭhavatthuto vuṭṭhahanato”ti saṅkhepavacane. Ajjhattabahiddhā rūpārūpapapañcakkhandhalakkhaṇattayavasena ayaṃ mātikā uddeso. Ajjhattaṃ abhinivisitvāti sasantatipariyāpannesu khandhesu vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā. “Ajjhattā vuṭṭhātī”ti idaṃ [V 2.0442] vuṭṭhānagāminiyā ajjhattadhammārammaṇattā pariyāyato vuttaṃ, nippariyāyato pana maggo sabbatopi vuṭṭhāti. Bahiddhā vuṭṭhātītiādīsupi eseva nayo. Ekappahārenāti ekajjhaṃ, taṃ pana ajjhattādivibhāgaṃ akatvā “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti (dī. ni. 1.298; saṃ. ni. 5.1081; mahāva. 16; paṭi. ma. 2.30) avibhāgena vuṭṭhānagāminiyā pavattivasena veditabbaṃ, tayidaṃ satthu sammukhā desanānusārena ñāṇaṃ pesentassa ñāṇuttarassa sambhavatīti vadanti.

783. Herein refers to that concise statement, ‘from emerging from the basis of adherence.’ This is the outline of the matrix by way of the internal and external, form and formless, the five aggregates, and the three characteristics. Having adhered internally means having established insight into the aggregates included in one's own continuity. ‘One emerges internally’ is said figuratively because the insight leading to emergence has internal phenomena as its object; but in a non-figurative sense, the path emerges from all phenomena. The same method applies to ‘one emerges externally,’ and so on. With a single stroke means all at once. This should be understood as occurring by way of the proceeding of the insight leading to emergence, without making a division into internal, etc., and without distinction, as: ‘Whatever is a phenomenon subject to origination, all that is a phenomenon subject to cessation.’ They say that this is possible for one who is superior in knowledge, who directs their knowledge in accordance with the teaching in the Teacher's presence.

784. Suddhaajjhattadassanamatteneva maggavuṭṭhānaṃ na hoti mamaṃkāravatthunopi pariññeyyattā maggasaṅkhātaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ, maggena vā vuṭṭhānaṃ maggavuṭṭhānaṃ.

784. The emergence of the path does not occur merely through insight into the purely internal, because the basis for ‘making mine’ must also be fully understood. The emergence designated as the path, or emergence by means of the path, is the emergence of the path.

785. Rāsiṃ katvāti bhūtupādāyavasena duvidhaṃ antarabhedavasena anekabhedampi “ruppanaṭṭhena rūpa”nti piṇḍato gahetvā. Yathā rūpe vipassanābhiniveso yebhuyyena vipassanāyānikassa, evaṃ arūpe vipassanābhiniveso yebhuyyena samathayānikassa hoti. Abhinivesoti ca vipassanāya pubbabhāge kattabbanāmarūpaparicchedo veditabbo. Tasmā paṭhamaṃ rūpapariggaṇhanaṃ rūpe abhiniveso. Esa nayo sesesupi.

785. Having made a heap means having grasped concisely as ‘form in the sense of being afflicted’ that which is twofold by way of primary elements and derived matter, and also of many kinds by way of internal divisions. Just as adherence to insight regarding form is generally for one who follows the vehicle of insight, so adherence to insight regarding the formless is generally for one who follows the vehicle of serenity. And adherence should be understood as the determination of name-and-form that is to be done in the preliminary stage of insight. Therefore, the initial grasping of form is adherence to form. This same method applies to the others as well.

786. Yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti kāmaṃ udayabbayapariggaṇhanaṃ abhinivesoti dassitaṃ, yathāupaṭṭhite pana rūpārūpadhamme, tesañca paccaye pariggahetvā saṅkhepeneva vipassanāñāṇaṃ cārento ñāṇuttaro yathānisinnova ñāṇapaṭipāṭiyā khippameva saccāni paṭivijjhanto ekappahārena pañcahi khandhehi vuṭṭhāti nāma. Aññathā ekeneva lokiyacittena pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ pariggahaparijānanādīnaṃ asambhavato. Na hi sanidassanasappaṭighādiṃ ekajjhaṃ ārammaṇaṃ kātuṃ sakkā. Yassa pana ekavāraṃ ñāṇena phassitaṃ, puna taṃ phassitabbameva, tādisassa vasena vuttanti vadanti.

786. Although it is shown by the statement, ‘Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation,’ that the grasping of arising and passing away is adherence, still, a person with superior knowledge, having grasped the form and formless phenomena as they have appeared and their conditions, by exercising insight-knowledge only briefly, just as he is seated, quickly penetrates the truths in the order of the knowledges and is said to emerge from the five aggregates with a single stroke. Otherwise, it would be impossible for a single mundane insight consciousness to perform the grasping, full understanding, etc., of the five aggregates. For indeed, it is not possible to take as a single object simultaneously things that are visible and resistant, etc. But they say this was stated with reference to such a one for whom what has been touched once by knowledge is not to be touched again.

788. Ettha [M 2.0471] ca abhiniveso akāraṇaṃ vuṭṭhānameva pamāṇaṃ, tasmā heṭṭhā vuttavimokkhaariyapuggalavibhāgāpi vuṭṭhānavasena sambhavantīti dassetuṃ “ettha ca yopī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha tayopi janāti vuṭṭhānavasena bhede asatipi abhinivesavaseneva laddhaṃ bhedaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ.

788. And here, adherence is not the principal cause; emergence alone is the standard. Therefore, to show that even the divisions of liberation and noble persons mentioned below are possible by way of emergence, the passage beginning, ‘And here, whoever…’ was introduced. Therein, the statement about the three persons is made by taking the distinction obtained only by way of adherence, even though there is no distinction based on emergence.

789. Saddhiṃ [V 2.0443] purimapacchimañāṇehīti bhayatupaṭṭhānādipurimañāṇehi ceva gotrabhuādipacchimañāṇehi ca saha. Uddānanti uddeso.

789. Together with the preceding and subsequent knowledges means together with the preceding knowledges, such as the knowledge of the appearance of terror, and with the subsequent knowledges, such as change-of-lineage knowledge. Summary means enumeration.

Yattha katthaci…pe… vaṭṭeyyuṃ taṃtaṃñāṇaṭṭhāniyassa upamāvatthuno labbhanato. Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāneti imasmiṃ vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanāpadese. Sabbanti sabbaṃ ñāṇaṃ, sabbaṃ vā ñāṇakiccaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti vemajjhe ṭhatvā vibhāviyamānattā. Vuttā visuddhikathāyaṃ.

Wherever... and so on... they might occur, because a basis for a simile is found for each respective stage of knowledge. But in this place means in this section on the insight leading to emergence. All means all knowledge, or all functions of knowledge, becomes manifest, being made clear while standing in the middle. This was stated in the talk on purification.

790. Nilīyitvāti upavisitvā. Parāmasitvāti vīmaṃsitvā.

790. Having concealed oneself means having settled down. Having handled means having investigated.

Gayhupagaṃ adisvāti gahaṇayoggaṃ niccasārādiṃ adisvā. Cittassa vaṅkabhāvakarānaṃ māyādīnaṃ suṭṭhu vikkhambhanena anulomassa ujukasākhāsadisatā. Nibbānālocanato gotrabhuñāṇassa uddhaṃ ullokanasadisatā. Appatiṭṭhe nibbāne patiṭṭhitattā maggañāṇassa ākāse uppatanasadisatā.

Not seeing anything to be grasped means not seeing anything suitable for grasping, such as permanence, essence, etc. Because of the thorough suppression of things that make the mind crooked, such as deceit, conformity knowledge is like a straight branch. Because it looks towards Nibbāna, change-of-lineage knowledge is like looking upwards. Because it is established in the unestablished Nibbāna, path knowledge is like flying up into the sky.

791. Sappavissajjanaṃ viya gotrabhuñāṇaṃ sabbasaṅkhāragataṃ vissajjitvā nibbānassa ālambanato. Āgatamaggaṃ olokentassa ṭhānaṃ viya maggañāṇaṃ asammohapaṭivedhavasena attanopi dassanato. Abhayaṭṭhāne ṭhānanti abhayaṭṭhānaṃ sampattamāha, na tassa pāpuṇapaṭipattiṃ.

791. Change-of-lineage knowledge is like the releasing of a snake, because it releases all formations and takes Nibbāna as its object. Path knowledge is like the standing of one looking at the path that has been traversed, because of penetration by means of non-delusion and because of seeing itself. 'Standing in the place of safety' speaks of having reached the place of safety, not the practice for reaching it.

792. Attatthādīnaṃ anavabujjhanato “ahaṃ, mamā”ti gahaṇassa niddokkamanasadisatā. Muñcitukamyatāggahaṇeneva paṭisaṅkhā santiṭṭhanāpi gahitā. Tissannampi tāsaṃ saṃsārato nikkhamanādhimuttatāya nikkhamanamaggolokanasadisatā. Magge diṭṭhe maggapaṭipatti viya anulome siddhe maggo siddho evāti anulomassa maggadassanasadisatā. Saṅkhāranimittato nikkhantattā ādittagharato nikkhamanaṃ viya gotrabhuñāṇaṃ. Vegena gamanaṃ [M 2.0472] viya maggañāṇaṃ vissajjetabbagahetabbapadesesu sādhanakiccavisesayogato.

792. Because of not understanding one's own benefit, etc., the grasping of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ is like falling asleep. By the very grasping of the desire for deliverance, reflection and equipoise are also included. Because of being intent on escaping from saṃsāra in regard to all three of them, it is like looking for the path of escape. Just as the practice of the path is accomplished when the path is seen, so when conformity is accomplished the path is surely accomplished; thus, conformity knowledge is like seeing the path. Because it has escaped from the sign of formations, change-of-lineage knowledge is like escaping from a burning house. Path knowledge is like moving with speed, because of its connection with the special task of accomplishment in the sections of what is to be relinquished and what is to be grasped.

793. Parato na mamāyitabbato ca passitabbānaṃ khandhānaṃ “ahaṃ, mamā”ti gahaṇassa rājagoṇānaṃ sakagahaṇasadisatā vuttā.

793. Because the aggregates that are to be seen are other and not to be cherished as ‘mine,’ the grasping of them as ‘I’ and ‘mine’ is said to be like taking the king's cattle as one's own.

794. Sabhaye [V 2.0444] abhayadassanahetutāya khandhānaṃ “ahaṃ, mamā”ti gahaṇassa yakkhiniyā saṃvāsasadisatā. Susānavijahanaṃ viya saṅkhārasusānaṃ vijahitvā nibbānārammaṇavasena pavattaṃ gotrabhu.

794. Because it is a cause for seeing fearlessness in what is fearful, the grasping of the aggregates as ‘I’ and ‘mine’ is like cohabiting with a yakkhiṇī. Like abandoning a charnel ground, change-of-lineage knowledge proceeds by way of Nibbāna as its object, having abandoned the charnel ground of formations.

795. Puttagiddhinīti puttavacchalā. Ottappamānāti sārajjayamānā. Oḷārikaoḷārikalobhakkhandhādivikkhambhanena saṅkhārapariccajanato anulomassa tattheva dārakoropanasadisatā.

795. ‘One fond of her son’ means one affectionate toward her son. ‘Feeling a sense of shame’ means becoming bashful. Because of abandoning formations through the suppression of the grosser aggregates of greed and so on, conformity knowledge is like setting down the child right there.

796. Vuṭṭhānagāminiyā…pe… dassanatthaṃ vuttā, na purimāsu viya bhayatupaṭṭhānādīsu ṭhitassa bhāyanādiākāradassanatthanti adhippāyo. Aparāparuppattito, cirānubandhato, dussahato ca vaṭṭadukkhasadisaṃ jighacchādukkhanti āha “saṃsāravaṭṭajighacchāyā”ti. Kāyagatāsati eva bhojanaṃ kāyagatāsatibhojanaṃ. Sā panettha maggasampayuttā sammāsati kāyānupassanādikiccasādhanavasena amatarasaparibhogatāya ca “amatarasaṃ kāyagatāsatibhojana”nti vuttā. Tenāha bhagavā “amataṃ te, bhikkhave, paribhuñjanti, ye kāyagatāsatiṃ paribhuñjantī”tiādi (a. ni. 1.600).

796. The meaning is that this was stated for the purpose of showing the insight leading to emergence... and so on, not, as in the previous examples, for the purpose of showing the mode of fearing, etc., of a yogi who abides in the knowledge of the appearance of terror, etc. Because of its repeated arising, its long persistence, and its unbearableness, the suffering of hunger is like the suffering of the round; thus he says, ‘by the hunger of the round of saṃsāra.’ Mindfulness directed to the body itself is food; hence ‘the food of mindfulness directed to the body.’ Herein, that right mindfulness associated with the path is called ‘the food of mindfulness directed to the body, which is the deathless taste’ because it accomplishes the task of contemplation of the body, etc., and because of partaking of the deathless taste. Therefore the Blessed One said: ‘Bhikkhus, they partake of the deathless who partake of mindfulness directed to the body,’ and so on.

Phalarasāmalakasiṅgīveramuggamāsādi anekaṅgasambhāraṃ.

Comprised of a collection of many ingredients, such as fruit juice, emblic myrobalan, ginger, mung beans, and black gram.

Kapaṇāseribhāvādikaraṇena taṇhāsinehassa sītasadisatā. Maggatejanti ariyamaggasaṅkhātaṃ indaggiṃ.

Because it causes a state of wretchedness, of not being one's own master, etc., the attachment of craving has a likeness to cold. The heat of the path means the sovereign fire called the noble path.

Rāgaggiādayo ekādasaggī vūpasamanti etthāti ekādasaggivūpasamaṃ, nibbānaṃ.

The eleven fires, beginning with the fire of lust, are extinguished herein; thus, the extinguishing of the eleven fires is Nibbāna.

Andhakāraparetoti caturaṅgasamannāgatena andhakārena kiñci attatthaṃ vā paratthaṃ vā kātuṃ asakkuṇeyyabhāvena abhibhūto. Ñāṇamayo āloko etissāti ñāṇālokā, maggabhāvanā.

‘Engulfed by darkness’ means being overcome by the four-factored darkness, in the sense of being unable to do anything for one's own welfare or for the welfare of others. Because this development of the path has a light consisting of knowledge, it is called ‘the light of knowledge’; this refers to the development of the path.

Amatabhūtaṃ[M 2.0473], amatabhāvasādhakaṃ vā osadhaṃ amatosadhaṃ, nibbānaṃ. Heṭṭhā attanā vuttameva saṅkhārupekkhābyāpāraṃ nigamanavasena dassento “tena vutta”ntiādimāha.

The medicine that has become the deathless, or that accomplishes the deathless state, is the deathless medicine: Nibbāna. Showing by way of conclusion the function of equanimity towards formations, which he himself has already stated below, he said, ‘Therefore it was said,’ and so on.

797. Nirālayatāya [V 2.0445] taṇhāvasena bhavādīsu avisaṭajjhāsayo hutvā tato saṅkucitacitto patilīnabhāvena carati pavattatīti patilīnacaro, tassa patilīnacarassa. Saṃsāre bhayassa ikkhanatāya bhikkhuno kāyacittavivekasiddhiyā vivittamāsanaṃ bhajamānassa. Sāmaggiyanti yuttaṃ, patirūpanti attho. Bhavaneti kāmabhavādike tividhepi bhave. So hi idha bhavanaṭṭhena bhavanti vutto. Na dassayeti anuppajjanavasena na dasseyya. Tassa taṃ adassanaṃ sāmaggiyanti buddhādayo ariyā āhūti yojanā.

797. Because of being without attachment, his disposition is not diffused through craving in regard to states of existence, etc.; having become one with a contracted mind from those states of existence, he fares and proceeds in a withdrawn way; thus he is one of withdrawn conduct. Of that one of withdrawn conduct: of the bhikkhu who, because of seeing the danger in saṃsāra, resorts to a secluded seat for the accomplishment of bodily and mental seclusion. 'Harmonious' means suitable; the meaning is 'fitting.' 'In existence' means in the threefold existence, such as sensual existence, etc. For that threefold existence is here called 'bhavana' (existence) in the sense of becoming. 'He does not show' means he would not show it, in the sense of non-arising. The construction is: The noble ones, such as the Buddhas, declare that non-showing of his to be 'harmonious.'

Niyametvāti niyataṃ ekaṃsikaṃ katvā. Bojjhaṅgavisesaṃ, maggaṅgavisesaṃ, jhānaṅgavisesaṃ, paṭipadāvisesaṃ, vimokkhavisesanti visesasaddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Visesanti chasattabhāvo sattaṭṭhabhāvo pañcādibhāvoti imaṃ yathākkamaṃ bojjhaṅgādīnaṃ ariyamagge labbhamānabhedaṃ. Pādakajjhānanti maggassa āsannavuṭṭhānagāminiyā vipassanāya padaṭṭhānabhūtaṃ jhānaṃ. Vipassanāya ārammaṇabhūtāti maggāsannāya eva vuṭṭhānagāminiyā vipassanāya gocarabhūtā vipassitā. Puggalajjhāsayoti ubhinnaṃ bhede sati vipassakassa ajjhāsayo. Ettha ca paṭhamaṃ kecīti vutto tipiṭakacūḷanāgatthero. Dutiyaṃ kecīti vutto moravāpīvāsimahādattatthero. Tatiyaṃ kecīti vutto tipiṭakacūḷābhayatthero.

Having determined means having made it certain and definite. The word 'distinction' should be connected individually with: distinction of enlightenment factors, distinction of path factors, distinction of jhāna factors, distinction of modes of practice, and distinction of liberations. 'Distinction' means the state of being sixfold or sevenfold, sevenfold or eightfold, or having five parts, etc.; this is the variety of enlightenment factors and so on obtainable in the noble path, in due order. 'Jhāna as basis' means the jhāna that is the foundation for the insight leading to emergence proximate to the path. 'Become the object of insight' means having become the resort of the insight leading to emergence proximate to the path, which has been contemplated. 'Individual inclination' means the inclination of the insight meditator when there is a difference between the two, namely, the jhāna as basis and the jhāna as object of insight. Here, the first 'some' refers to the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷanāga. The second 'some' refers to the Elder Mahādatta, the resident of Moravāpī. The third 'some' refers to the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷābhaya.

Tesampi vādesu ayaṃ pubbabhāgavuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā niyametiyevāti veditabbā. Kasmā? Vipassanāniyameneva hi paṭhamattheravādepi apādakapaṭhamajjhānapādakamaggā paṭhamajjhānikāva honti, itare ca dutiyajjhānikādimaggā pādakajjhānavipassanāniyamehi taṃtaṃjhānikāva tato tato dutiyādipādakajjhānato uppannassa saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇassa pādakajjhānātikkantānaṃ aṅgānaṃ asamāpajjitukāmatāvirāgabhāvanābhāvato, itarassa ca atabbhāvato. Yathā hi maggāsannāya vipassanāya somanassasahagatatte maggassa paṭhamādijhānikatā ca upekkhāsahagatatte pañcamajjhānikatā eva ca hoti, tato ca bojjhaṅgādīnaṃ [M 2.0474] visesoti tesaṃ niyamane āsannakāraṇaṃ, padhānakāraṇañca vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā, na evaṃ pādakajjhānādayo. Yasmā pana pādakajjhānena vinā vipassanāva imaṃ yathāvuttavisesaṃ niyametuṃ na sakkoti, vuttanayena pana padhānakāraṇaṃ hotiyeva, tasmā “vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanāva niyametī”ti avatvā “vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā niyametiyevā”ti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ sesavādesupi vipassanāniyamo yathāsambhavaṃ yojetabbo. Yathā hi pādakajjhānātikkantānaṃ aṅgānaṃ asamāpajjitukāmatāvirāgabhāvanābhūtā [V 2.0446] vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā adhiṭṭhānabhūtena pādakajjhānena āhitavisesā maggassa bojjhaṅgādivisesaniyāmikā hoti, evaṃ ārammaṇabhūtasammasitajjhānātikkantānaṃ aṅgānaṃ jigucchanākāravirāgabhāvanābhūtā sammasitajjhānena āhitavisesā, ubhayasabbhāve ajjhāsayavasena tato aññatarena āhitavisesā ca vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā maggassa bojjhaṅgādivisesaṃ niyametīti.

In their theories too, it should be understood that this preliminary insight leading to emergence is what invariably determines. Why? Because it is solely through the determination by insight that, even in the theory of the first elder, paths without a basis-jhāna and paths with the first jhāna as basis are only of the first jhāna; and the other paths—of the second jhāna and so on—are of their respective jhānas only, due to the determination by the jhāna as basis and by insight. This is because, for the knowledge of equanimity towards formations that has arisen from that respective second, etc., basis-jhāna, there is the absence of the cultivation of dispassion that is the desire not to attain the factors that transcend the basis-jhāna, and for the other [knowledge], because of the absence of such [a cultivation of dispassion]. For just as when insight proximate to the path is accompanied by joy, the path becomes one of the first jhānas, etc., and when it is accompanied by equanimity, it becomes one of the fifth jhāna only, and from that there is a distinction of enlightenment factors, etc., so insight leading to emergence is the proximate cause and the principal cause in their determination, not the basis-jhāna and so on. However, since insight alone, without the basis-jhāna, cannot determine this aforesaid distinction, but it is indeed the principal cause in the way stated, therefore, without saying 'insight leading to emergence alone determines,' it is said 'insight leading to emergence invariably determines.' Thus, in the remaining theories too, the determination by insight should be applied as is appropriate. For just as insight leading to emergence—which is the cultivation of dispassion that is the desire not to attain the factors that transcend the basis-jhāna, and which has its distinction effected by the basis-jhāna which is its foundation—is the determiner of the path's distinction of enlightenment factors, etc.; so too insight leading to emergence—which is the cultivation of dispassion in the form of revulsion towards the factors that transcend the contemplated jhāna which is its object, and which has its distinction effected by the contemplated jhāna; and which, when both are present, has its distinction effected by one or the other of them according to inclination—determines the path's distinction of enlightenment factors, etc.

798. Tatra tasmiṃ bojjhaṅgādivisesaniyamane. Ajhānalābhī suddhavipassanāyānikova sukkhavipassako. So hi jhānasinehena vipassanāya asiniddhabhāvato sukkhā lūkhā vipassanā etassāti sukkhavipassakoti vuccati. Pakiṇṇakasaṅkhāreti pādakajjhānato aññe saṅkhāre. Tena pādakajjhānasaṅkhāresu sammasitesu vattabbameva natthīti dasseti. “Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā”ti hi vuttaṃ. Ettha ca sukkhavipassakādiggahaṇaṃ vipassanāniyamassa ekantikabhāvadassanatthaṃ. Na hi vuṭṭhānagāminiṃ vinā kevalaṃ pādakajjhānādayo niyamahetū diṭṭhā, vuṭṭhānagāminī pana pādakajjhānādīnaṃ abhāvepi sukkhavipassakādīnaṃ maggassa paṭhamajjhānikabhāvahetu, tasmā sā bojjhaṅgādivisesaniyamane ekantikahetūti. Idāni yathāvuttamatthaṃ pākaṭataraṃ kātuṃ “tesaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ visesoti ayaṃ jhānādīnaṃ caturaṅgikādiviseso, na pubbe viya vipassanāniyameneva, atha kho pādakajjhānaniyamena ceva vipassanāniyamena ca. Tesampīti pañcakanaye dutiyatatiyacatutthajjhānāni pādakāni katvā uppāditamaggānampi. “Āsannapadese”ti iminā vipassakena antarantarā paviṭṭhasamāpattiyā vasena ayaṃ viseso natthīti dasseti.

798. Therein: in that determination of the distinction of enlightenment factors, etc. One who has not attained jhāna is a bare-insight practitioner, a dry-insight meditator. For since his insight is not moistened by the 'oil' of jhāna, his insight is dry and rough; thus he is called a 'dry-insight meditator.' 'Miscellaneous formations' means formations other than those of the jhāna as basis. He thereby shows that there is nothing to be said when the formations of the jhāna as basis are contemplated. For it was said: 'Having made the first jhāna the basis.' Here, the inclusion of the dry-insight meditator, etc., is for the purpose of showing the conclusive nature of the determination by insight. For without insight leading to emergence, the mere jhāna as basis, etc., are not seen as causes of determination. But insight leading to emergence, even in the absence of the jhāna as basis, etc., is the cause for the path of the dry-insight meditator, etc., to be of the first jhāna. Therefore, it is the conclusive cause in the determination of the distinction of enlightenment factors, etc. Now, to make the aforesaid meaning clearer, the passage beginning 'For them...' was stated. 'This distinction' means this four-factored distinction, etc., of the jhānas, etc., is not, as before, by the determination of insight alone, but by the determination of both the jhāna as basis and insight. 'Even for them' means even for the paths produced after making the second, third, and fourth jhānas the basis in the fivefold system. By 'in the proximate region,' he shows that this distinction does not exist on account of the attainment entered into from time to time by the insight meditator.

799. Tatrāpi [M 2.0475] cāti dutiyattheravādepi. Taṃtaṃsamāpattisadisatā taṃtaṃsammasitasaṅkhāravipassanāniyamehi hoti. Tatrāpi hi vipassanā taṃtaṃvirāgāvirāgabhāvanābhāvena somanassasahagatā, upekkhāsahagatā ca hutvā jhānaṅgādiniyamaṃ maggassa karotīti evaṃ vipassanāniyamo vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

799. 'And there too' means in the theory of the second elder too. The similarity to this or that attainment occurs through the determinations of this or that contemplated formation and of insight. For there too, insight, through being the cultivation of dispassion or non-dispassion for this or that, becomes accompanied by joy or accompanied by equanimity and effects the determination of the jhāna factors, etc., for the path. Thus the determination by insight should be understood in the way already stated.

800. Tanti taṃtaṃjhānasadisabhavaṃ. Svāyamattho pādakajjhānasammasitajjhānupanissayehi vinā ajjhāsayamattena asijjhanaṃ upanissayena vinā saṅkappamattena sakadāgāmiphalādīnaṃ asijjhanadīpakena nandakovādena dīpetabbo. Tattha hi yathā sotāpannāyapi paripuṇṇasaṅkappataṃ vadantena [V 2.0447] bhagavatā “yassa yassa upanissayo atthi, tassa tasseva ajjhāsayo niyāmako, nāññassā”ti tena tena paripuṇṇasaṅkappatā hoti, na tato paraṃ, saṅkappasabbhāve satipi asijjhanatoti ayamattho dīpito, evamidhāpi yassa yassa dutiyādijhānikassa maggassa yathāvutto upanissayo atthi, tassa tasseva ajjhāsayo niyāmako, nāññassa satipi tasmiṃ asijjhanato. Imasmiṃ pana vāde pādakasammasitajjhānupanissayasabbhāve ajjhāsayo ekantena hoti taṃtaṃphalūpanissayasabbhāve taṃtaṃsaṅkappo viyāti tadabhāvābhāvato “ajjhāsayo niyametī”ti vuttaṃ. Etthāpīti tatiyattheravādepi. Vuttanayenevāti “yato yato samāpattito vuṭṭhāyā”tiādinā vuttanayena. Tasmā “tatrāpi hi vipassanā”tiādinā idha vuttanayena tadattho veditabbo.

800. That is, the state of being similar to this or that jhāna. This meaning—namely, the non-accomplishment by mere inclination without the supports of the basic jhāna and the contemplated jhāna—should be illustrated by the Nandakovāda Sutta, which illuminates the non-accomplishment of the fruit of once-returning, etc., by mere resolve without a support. For in that Sutta, this meaning was illuminated: just as the Blessed One, speaking of the completeness of resolve even for a stream-entering nun, said, 'For whichever fruit there is a support, for that very one the inclination is the determiner, not for another'; thus, with respect to that very fruit there is completeness of resolve, not beyond that, because of non-accomplishment even when resolve is present. So too here, for whichever path associated with the second jhāna, etc., there is the aforesaid support, for that very one the inclination is the determiner, not for another, because of non-accomplishment even when that inclination is present. But in this view, when there is the presence of the supports of the basic jhāna and the contemplated jhāna, the inclination certainly arises—just as when there is the support for this or that fruit, this or that resolve arises. Therefore, because of the absence of its non-existence, it is said, 'the inclination determines.' 'Here too' means in the view of the third elder too. 'In the way stated' means in the way stated beginning, 'Having emerged from whatever attainment…' Therefore, its meaning should be understood in the way stated here beginning, 'For there too, insight…'

801. Evaṃ vipassanāya bojjhaṅgādiniyāmikataṃ dassetvā idāni paṭipadādiniyāmikataṃ dassento “sace panāya”ntiādimāha. Tattha ayanti saṅkhārupekkhā vuttā. Sāpi hi kāmaṃ “imaṃ vāraṃ rocesu”nti ettha kalāpasammasanāvasāne udayabbayānupassanāya pavattamānāya uppannassa vipassanupakkilesassa tikkhattuṃ vikkhambhanena kicchatāvāraṃ dukkhāpaṭipadāti rocesunti vadanti, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “vipassanāñāṇe tikkhe sūre pasanne vahante uppannaṃ vipassanānikantiṃ dukkhena kasirena kilamanto pariyādiyatī”ti vuttattā pubbabhāge muñcitukamyatādibhāvena pavattamānā [M 2.0476] saṅkhārupekkhā attano paṭipakkhe kicchena kasirena vikkhambhentī dukkhāpaṭipadāpakkheyeva tiṭṭhatīti. Tenāha “ādito kilese vikkhambhayamānā”tiādi. Keci pana “yena ñāṇena vipassanupakkilesā vikkhambhitā, tena saddhiṃ idaṃ ñāṇaṃ ekattanayavasena ekaṃ katvā ‘ādito kilese vikkhambhayamānā’ti vutta”nti vadanti. Sappayogenāti cittappayogasaṅkhātena saussāhanena. Sasaṅkhārenāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Ubhayenāpi vikkhambhanassa kicchasiddhimeva vadati. Vipariyāyenāti adukkhena appayogena asaṅkhārena. Maggasaññitaṃ icchitaṭṭhānaṃ anugantvā parivasati vippavasati etthāti parivāso, vipassanā parivāso etassa atthīti vipassanāparivāso, maggapātubhāvo, taṃ pana sīghaṃ kurumānā khippābhiññā nāma hotīti vuttaṃ “saṇika”nti.
