Kurumānā ayaṃ saṅkhārupekkhāti yojanā. Yato maggo āgacchati, taṃ āgamanīyaṭṭhānaṃ, tasmiṃ āgamanīyaṭṭhāne. Maggassa pabhavaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā nāmaṃ detīti sambandho. Dukkhāpaṭipadādandhābhiññādivipassanānayo añño, añño eva maggoti āha “attano attano maggassā”ti. Tena āgamanato laddhanāmena “dukkhāpaṭipadā [V 2.0448] dandhābhiññā”tiādīni cattāri nāmāni labhati. Na hi maggassa sarasato edisaṃ nāmaṃ atthi.

801. Having thus shown the determinative nature of insight regarding the enlightenment factors, etc., now, showing its determinative nature regarding the modes of practice, etc., he says, 'But if this…' Herein, by 'this' is meant equanimity towards formations. For although some say, 'They approved this turn,' this refers to the fact that at the end of the comprehension of groups, while the contemplation of arising and passing away is proceeding, they approved of the difficult turn—which is the threefold suppression of the arisen defilement of insight—as 'painful practice'. But in the commentary, it is said: 'When the knowledge of insight is sharp, keen, clear, and exerting itself, one exhausts the arisen delight in insight with difficulty, toil, and weariness.' Therefore, in the preliminary stage, equanimity towards formations, proceeding with the state of desire for deliverance, etc., while suppressing its opponents with difficulty and toil, stands only in the faction of the painful practice. Hence he says, 'Suppressing the defilements from the beginning,' etc. Some, however, say: 'The knowledge by which the defilements of insight were suppressed—this knowledge, together with that, having been made one by way of the single-meaning method, is what is meant when it is said, "Suppressing the defilements from the beginning."' 'With effort' means with exertion, which is designated as mental application. 'With preparation' is a synonym for that very thing. By both, it speaks only of the difficult accomplishment of the suppression. 'By the opposite' means without difficulty, without effort, without preparation. Not yet having approached the desired place designated as the path, one dwells around (parivasati), one dwells apart (vippavasati) therein (ettha); hence, it is a 'dwelling' (parivāso); it is the manifestation of the path. But when making that happen quickly, it is called 'quick direct-knowledge'; thus, the word 'slowly' is stated. The connection is: this equanimity towards formations, while making [it happen]. From where the path comes, that is the 'place of arrival'. In that place of arrival, at the source-place of the path, standing, it gives the name—this is the connection. The method of insight, such as painful practice with slow direct-knowledge, is one thing, and the path is another thing entirely. Hence he says, 'of its own respective path.' Therefore, by the name obtained from its place of arrival, it receives the four names, such as 'painful practice with slow direct-knowledge.' For the path by its own nature does not have such a name.

Sā panāyaṃ vuttappabhedā paṭipadā. Nānā hotīti visuṃ visuṃ hoti. Ekassa bhikkhuno catūsupi maggesu ekāva hotīti niyamo natthi calanato. Ahesunti vuttaṃ, amhākaṃ bhagavantaṃ sandhāya hontīti pana vattabbaṃ. Sabbesampi hi sammāsambuddhānaṃ cattāropi maggā sukhāpaṭipadā khippābhiññāva hontīti. Paṭipadāpasaṅgena adhipatimpi dassetuṃ “yathā cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Adhipatayoti chandādiadhipatayo. Pubbābhisaṅkhārānurūpañhi maggo paccekaṃ chandādhipateyyo vā hoti vīriyādīsu aññatarādhipateyyo vā, na kassaci niyamo atthi. Tenāha “kassaci bhikkhuno”tiādi.

Now, this practice with its aforementioned distinctions is various; that is, it is distinct in each case. There is no fixed rule that for a single bhikkhu it is just one kind of practice for all four paths, because it fluctuates. It is said, 'They were'; but with reference to our Blessed One, it should, however, be said, 'They are.' For indeed, in the case of all Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, all four paths are only of pleasant practice with quick direct-knowledge. To show the predominances as well in connection with the practice, the passage beginning with 'And as…' was stated. 'Predominances' means the predominances such as desire, etc. For indeed, in accordance with prior volitional formations, the path is individually dominated either by desire or by one of the others, such as energy; there is no fixed rule for anyone. Therefore, he said the passage beginning with 'for a certain bhikkhu…'.

802. Pubbe vuttappakārato sātisayaṃ katvā anavasesato maggassa nāmalābhe kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sarasenāti sabhāvena attano pavattivisesena. Paccanīkenāti paṭipakkhavasena. Saguṇenāti attano guṇavasena.

802. To show the reason for the path's acquisition of names in a complete way that surpasses the manner previously stated, the passage beginning with 'Moreover…' was stated. Therein, 'by its own nature' (sarasena) means by its intrinsic nature, by its own distinctive mode of occurring. 'By way of the opponent' (paccanīkena) means by way of opposition. 'By way of its quality' (saguṇena) means by way of its own quality.

Kāmañcettha [M 2.0477] yathā āgamanena vinā saguṇena, ārammaṇena ca maggassa nāmalābho avavatthito, evaṃ paccanīkena vinā saraseneva nāmalābho, tathāpi sarasādayo paccekaṃ nāmalābhassa kāraṇamevāti dassetuṃ “sarasena vā”tiādinā sabbattha aniyamattho vā-saddo vutto. Te ca asaṅkarato dassetuṃ “sace hī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha sammasitvāti sammasanahetu. Hetuattho hi ayaṃ tvā-saddo “ghataṃ pivitvā balaṃ hoti, sīhaṃ disvā bhayaṃ hotī”tiādīsu viya, maggakattukāya vuṭṭhānakiriyāya ekantikahetubhūtā saṅkhārupekkhā phalūpacārena “vuṭṭhātī”ti vuttā. Yasmā vā saṅkhārupekkhāti vuṭṭhānagāminiyā etaṃ upalakkhaṇaṃ, tadantogadhañca gotrabhuñāṇaṃ nimittato vuṭṭhāti, tasmā vuttaṃ ekattanayena “sammasitvā vuṭṭhātī”ti. Animittavimokkhena vimuccatīti animittasaññitena vimuccanena vimuccati, “maggo”ti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Vimuccatīti vā taṃsamaṅgī ariyapuggalo. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Idaṃ sarasato nāmaṃ nāmāti idaṃ nimittādivirahato animittaṃ appaṇihitaṃ suññatanti tividhampi maggassa sabhāvato siddhanāmaṃ nāma.

Although here, just as the path's acquisition of a name is not determined by its own quality and object without its mode of arrival, so too its acquisition of a name is not determined by its own nature alone without the opponent; nevertheless, to show that its own nature and so on are each a cause for the acquisition of a name, the word 'or' (vā), which signifies non-fixity, is used everywhere in the phrase 'by its own nature, or…' and so on. And to show these without confusion, the passage beginning 'If…' is introduced. Herein, 'having contemplated' means 'because of contemplation.' For this suffix '-tvā' has the sense of cause, as in such examples as 'by drinking ghee one becomes strong' and 'by seeing a lion fear arises.' Equanimity towards formations, being the decisive cause for the act of emergence performed by the path, is called 'emerges' by a figure of speech based on the fruit. Or, since this 'equanimity towards formations' is a characteristic of the insight leading to emergence, and the change-of-lineage knowledge included within it emerges from the sign, it is therefore said by the method of unity, 'having contemplated, it emerges.' 'Is liberated by the signless liberation' means is liberated by the liberation called the signless; 'the path' should be supplied and connected. Or, 'is liberated' refers to the noble person endowed with it. The same method applies to the other two cases. This is called 'the name from its own nature.' That is, this threefold name of the path—the signless, the desireless, and emptiness—is the name established by its own nature due to the absence of the sign and so on.

Esāti [V 2.0449] maggo. So ca kho pubbabhāgamaggena saddhiṃ ekaṃ katvā vutto ekattanayena. Idaṃ paccanīkato nāmaṃ nāmāti idaṃ niccanimittādīnaṃ paṇidhiyā, attasaññāya ca pahānavasena laddhaṃ maggassa animittādināmattayaṃ paṭipakkhato siddhanāmaṃ nāma.

This is the path. And it is spoken of as one with the preliminary-part path by the method of unity. This is called 'the name from the opponent.' That is, this threefold name of the path—the signless and so on—obtained by way of abandoning the sign of permanence and so on, aspiration, and the perception of self, is the name established from the opponent.

Suññattāti vivittattā. Na hi magge rāgādayo santi. Rūpanimittādīnanti rūpanimittavedanānimittādīnaṃ gahetabbānanti adhippāyo. Rāganimittādīnanti etthāpi eseva nayo. Saviggahānaṃ viya upaṭṭhānañhettha nimittanti adhippetaṃ. Idamassa saguṇato nāmanti idaṃ rāgādivivittattā rūpanimittādipaṇidhiādiabhāvavasena assa maggassa saguṇato siddhaṃ nāmaṃ.

‘Emptiness’ means because of being secluded. For on the path there are no lust and other defilements. ‘Signs of form, etc.’ means that signs of form, signs of feeling, etc., are to be understood; this is the meaning. The same method applies here also in ‘signs of lust, etc.’ Here ‘sign’ is intended as the presence of things as if they were substantial. ‘This is its name from its quality’ means: this is the name of this path, established from its own quality, by way of its being secluded from lust, etc., and by way of the absence of the sign of form, etc., and of aspiration, etc.

Svāyanti so ayaṃ maggo. Suññatanti sabbasaṅkhārasuññato, attasuññato ca suññataṃ. Sabbasaṅkhāranimittābhāvato animittaṃ. Taṇhāpaṇidhiādīnaṃ abhāvena appaṇihitaṃ. Idamassa ārammaṇato nāmanti yathā sukhārammaṇaṃ rūpaṃ “sukha”nti vuccati, evaṃ suññatādināmassa nibbānassa [M 2.0478] ārammaṇakaraṇato idaṃ assa maggassa suññatādibhedaṃ ārammaṇato siddhaṃ nāmaṃ.

This is that path. ‘Emptiness’ means it is empty because it is empty of all formations and empty of self. It is ‘signless’ because of the absence of the sign of all formations. It is ‘desireless’ because of the absence of craving, aspiration, etc. ‘This is its name from its object’ means: just as a form that is a pleasant object is called ‘pleasant,’ so too, because this path takes as its object Nibbāna, which is named ‘emptiness,’ etc., this name of the path, with its divisions such as emptiness, is a name established from its object.

803. Anattānupassanā attasuññatāya diṭṭhattā sarasato suññatā nāma. Tassā suññatāvipassanāya maggo vipassanāgamanena suññato. Animittā nāma niccanimittādīnaṃ ugghāṭanato. Idaṃ pana maggassa animittanāmaṃ na abhidhammapariyāyena labbhati. Kiṃ kāraṇaṃ? Abhidhamme sarasaṃ anāmasitvā paccanīkato nāmalābhato. Yo hi saguṇārammaṇehi nāmalābho, so sarasappadhāno hoti, saraseneva ca nāmalābhe sabbamaggānaṃ suññatādibhāvoti vavatthānaṃ na siyā. Tasmā abhidhamme satipi dvīhipi kāraṇehi animittanāmalābhe paccanīkatova nāmavavatthānakaraṇaṃ gayhatīti tadabhāvā na labbhati. Atha vā na labbhatīti aññanirapekkhehi saguṇārammaṇehi na labbhati. Kiṃ kāraṇaṃ? Abhidhamme sarasapaccanīkehi sahitehi nāmalābhato. Paccanīkañhi vavatthānakaraṇaṃ anapekkhitvā kevalassa sarasassa nāmahetubhāvo abhidhamme natthi, avavatthānāpattito. Tasmā attābhinivesapaṇidhipaṭipakkhavipassanānulomā maggā satipi sarasantare paccanīkasahitena sarasena nāmaṃ labhanti. Animittamaggassa pana vipassanā nimittapaṭipakkhā na hoti, sayaṃ nimittaggahaṇato nimittaggahaṇānivāraṇāti tadanulomo maggopi na nimittassa paṭipakkho. Yadi siyā, nimittagatavipassanāyapi paṭipakkho siyā, tasmā vijjamānopi saraso vavatthānakarapaccanīkābhāvā abhidhamme animittanāmadāyako [V 2.0450] na gayhatīti. Yadi evaṃ, aniccānupassanānulomo maggo abhidhamme asaṅgahito siyāti? Na, suddhikapaṭipadānaye tassa saṅgahitattā. Tasmā eva hi so vutto. Suttante pana pariyāyadesanattā saguṇārammaṇamattenapi nāmaṃ gayhatīti āha “suttantapariyāyena labbhatī”ti. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva. Āgamanavasenapi maggassa animittanāmaṃ labbhatiyevāti dassetuṃ “tatrā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Āgamanīyaṭṭhāneti āgamanapaṭipadāṭhāne. Sesaṃ vuttanayattā uttānamevāti.

803. The contemplation of non-self is called emptiness by its own nature because it has seen the emptiness of self. The path of that insight into emptiness is called empty by the approach of insight. It is called signless because it removes the signs of permanence and so on. However, this name 'signless' for the path is not obtained by way of the Abhidhamma. What is the reason? Because in the Abhidhamma, a name is obtained from its opponent, without considering its own nature. For whatever obtaining of a name there is through its own quality and object, that has its own nature as primary; and if a name were obtained only by its own nature, there would be no distinction of all paths as having the state of emptiness, and so on. Therefore, in the Abhidhamma, although a name may be obtained by both causes, the making of a distinction between names is accepted only from the opponent; thus, due to the absence of that opponent as a distinguishing factor, it is not obtained. Or, 'it is not obtained' means it is not obtained through its own quality and object independent of others. What is the reason? Because in the Abhidhamma, a name is obtained from its own nature and its opponent combined. For, without regard to the opponent which makes the distinction, the status of being a cause for a name for the mere own nature does not exist in the Abhidhamma, because it would lead to a lack of distinction. Therefore, paths that are in conformity with insight that is the counterpart to clinging to self and aspiration obtain a name by their own nature together with its opponent, even when another own nature is present. But the insight of the signless path is not the counterpart to the sign, because it itself grasps the sign; thus, the path in conformity with it is also not the counterpart to the sign. If it were, it would also be the counterpart to insight directed towards the sign. Therefore, even though its own nature is present, due to the absence of an opponent that makes a distinction, it is not accepted in the Abhidhamma as a giver of the name 'signless'. If so, would the path in conformity with the contemplation of impermanence be unincluded in the Abhidhamma? No, because it is included in the method of the path of purification. For that very reason, it is stated. In the Suttanta, however, because the teaching is indirect, a name is accepted even by its mere own quality and object; thus he said, 'it is obtained by way of the Suttanta.' Whatever should be said here has already been said below. To show that the name 'signless' for the path is indeed obtained also by way of the approach, 'For there...' and so on was said. `Āgamanīyaṭṭhāne` means: in the place of the practice of the approach. The remainder is clear, because the method has been stated.

Saṅkhārupekkhāñāṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Knowledge of Equanimity Towards Formations is Concluded.

Anulomañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Elucidation of the Discourse on the Knowledge of Conformity.

804. Adhimokkhasaddhāti [M 2.0479] pasādabhūto vatthugato nicchayo adhimokkho. Tasmā tathābhūtā bhāvanāvisesena kiccato adhimattatāya balavatarā nibbattati. Supaggahitanti suṭṭhu paggahitaṃ. Asallīnaṃ paṭutarabhāvena paṭipakkhavidhamanasamatthaṃ vīriyaṃ hoti. Sūpaṭṭhitāti tikkhataratāya ārammaṇābhimukhabhāvena suṭṭhu upaṭṭhitā sati hoti. Susamāhitanti passaddhisukhānaṃ sātisayatāya suṭṭhu samāhitaṃ ārammaṇe sammadeva ṭhapitaṃ appitaṃ viya hoti. Tikkhatarāti anulomañāṇuppattiyā paccayo bhavituṃ samatthabhāvena sātisayaṃ tikkhā sūrā. Saṅkhārānaṃ vicinanepi majjhattabhūtasaṅkhārupekkhā paññā uppajjati. Aniccāti vā…pe… sammasitvā bhavaṅgaṃ otaratīti aniccādīsu ekenākārena sammasantī sattakkhattuṃ pavattitvā bhijjantī bhavaṅgaṃ otiṇṇā nāma hoti tato paraṃ bhavaṅgassa vāroti katvā. Saṅkhārupekkhāya katanayenevāti aniccādinā ālambanakaraṇanayeneva, na sammasitanayena. Tenāha “ārammaṇaṃ kurumāna”nti. Āvaṭṭetvāti nivattetvā cittassa bhavaṅgavasena vattituṃ adatvā. Visadisacittapavattisaṅkhātāya vīciyā abhāvena avīcikā, cittasantati. Kiriyamanodhātuyā hi bhavaṅge āvaṭṭite kiriyamayacittapavattivipākacittuppattiyā savīcikā santarā, na evaṃ manodvārāvajjanenāti vuttaṃ “avīcikaṃ cittasantatiṃ anuppabandhamāna”nti. Tathevāti yathā atītāsu dvattiṃsajavanavīthīsu saṅkhārupekkhā “aniccā”ti vā “dukkhā”ti vā “anattā”ti vā saṅkhāre ārammaṇamakāsi, tatheva. Parikammanti vuccati maggassa parikammattā paṭisaṅkhārakattā[V 2.0451]. Upacāranti vuccati maggassa āsannattā, samīpacārikattā vā. Anulomattaṃ sayameva vadati.

804. Faith as determination means that determination is a conviction established in its object, having become serene. Therefore, such faith, through special cultivation, becomes especially strong in terms of its function due to its intensity, and arises. ‘Well-exerted’ means well-uplifted. It is energy that is unsluggish, and through its special keenness, is capable of destroying opposing factors. ‘Well-established’ means that mindfulness is well-established due to being especially sharp and through facing the object. ‘Well-concentrated’ means that due to the excellence of tranquility and bliss, it is well-concentrated, rightly placed on the object, as if absorbed. ‘Sharper’ means exceedingly sharp and valiant, through its capability to be a condition for the arising of conformity-knowledge. Even in investigating formations, the wisdom that is equanimity towards formations, having become neutral, arises. ‘Having contemplated “impermanent,” etc., it descends into the bhavaṅga’ means: contemplating in one aspect among impermanence and so on, having occurred seven times, when it breaks, it is said to have descended into the bhavaṅga, because after that, it is the turn of the bhavaṅga. ‘By the very same method as was done by equanimity towards formations’ means: only by the method of making impermanence, etc., the object, not by the method of contemplation. Therefore, he said, ‘making it the object’. ‘Having adverted’ means having turned back, not allowing the mind to proceed by way of the bhavaṅga. Due to the absence of an interval, which is described as the occurrence of a dissimilar consciousness, the continuity of consciousness is uninterrupted. For when the bhavaṅga is adverted to by the functional mind-element, the continuity of functional consciousness has an interval due to the arising of resultant consciousness; it is not so with mind-door adverting. Therefore, it was said, ‘maintaining an uninterrupted continuity of consciousness’. ‘Just so’ means: just as in the past two or three javana-processes, equanimity towards formations made the formations its object as ‘impermanent,’ or ‘suffering,’ or ‘non-self,’ just so here. It is called ‘preparation’ because it is the preparation for the path and the act of reconsideration. It is called ‘access’ because of its nearness to the path, or because it occurs in the vicinity. He himself states what is meant by conformity.

Ayañca nayo kāmaṃ maggavīthiyaṃ paṭhamajavanassa paṭisaṅkharaṇaṭṭho, dutiyassa tato āsannaṭṭho, tatiyassa heṭṭhimuparimānaṃ anulomaṭṭho ca yuttoti vutto, tathāpi sabbesampi imā samaññā sambhavantīti dassetuṃ “avisesena panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha āsevananti ādarena sevanaṃ. Purimabhāgapacchimabhāgānanti heṭṭhimānaṃ, uparimānañca dhammakoṭṭhāsānaṃ. Aṭṭhannanti udayabbayañāṇādīnaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ. Sabbāpi vipassanā lakkhaṇattayasammasanakiccāva[M 2.0480], idampi tathevāti vuttaṃ “tathakiccatāyā”ti. Uparīti magge. Bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ tathakiccatāya anulometi sammosādipaṭipakkhavidhamanato. Idāni anulomañāṇassa tadubhayakiccānulomaṃ vitthārato dassetuṃ “tañhī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha anulomañāṇaṃ saccapaṭicchādakamohakkhandhādīnaṃ sātisayaṃ vidhamanena lokiyañāṇesu ukkaṃsapariyantagataṃ, tato eva heṭṭhā nibbattitaudayabbayañāṇādīnampi kiccaṃ paṭipakkhadūrībhāvena atthato sādhentameva hutvā pavattati, tathāpavattamānañca tesaṃ kiccaṃ anulomentaṃ viya hotīti āha “udayabbayavantānaṃ…pe… tathakiccatāya anulometī”ti. Tattha “bhayato upaṭṭhita”nti imināpi ārammaṇasīsena ñāṇabyāpārameva vadati sappaṭibhayānaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ yathāsabhāvadassanadīpanato. Sesesu pana sattasupi ṭhānesu ñāṇabyāpārova dassito. Yasmā etaṃ anulomañāṇaṃ aniccādīsu aññataralakkhaṇavaseneva saṅkhāre ārabbha pavattati, tasmā vuttaṃ “aniccalakkhaṇādivasena saṅkhāre ārabbha pavattattā”ti. Tāya paṭipattiyāti yā sā anulomañāṇassa thūlathūlasaccapaṭicchādakasaṃkilesavikkhambhanapaṭipatti, tāya. Na hi anulomañāṇe tathā anuppanne gotrabhuñāṇaṃ nibbānaṃ ālambituṃ sakkoti, gotrabhuñāṇe vā anuppanne maggañāṇaṃ uppajjatīti.

Although this method is said to be suitable—that in the path process, for the first javana there is the meaning of preparation, for the second the meaning of being nearer than that, and for the third the meaning of conforming to the states below and above—nevertheless, to show that these designations are possible for all of them, the passage beginning with 'But without distinction...' was stated. Therein, 'repetition' (āsevana) means associating with respect. 'To the earlier and later parts' means to the portions of Dhamma that are lower and higher. 'Of the eight' means of the eight beginning with the knowledge of rise and fall. All insight has the function of contemplating the three characteristics, and this knowledge of conformity is also just like that; therefore, it was said, 'by having that same function.' 'Higher' means in the path. It conforms to the factors of enlightenment having the correct function because it dispels opposing factors such as confusion. Now, in order to show in detail the conformity of the knowledge of conformity to the function of both of those, the passage beginning with 'For that...' was stated. Therein, the knowledge of conformity, by powerfully dispelling the mass of delusion, etc., that conceals the truths, has reached the highest limit among worldly knowledges. For that very reason, by being far from opposing factors, it proceeds, in effect, accomplishing the function of the knowledges of rise and fall, etc., that have arisen below. And while proceeding in such a way, it is as if conforming to their function; therefore, he said, 'It conforms to those possessing rise and fall... by having that same function.' Therein, also by this phrase 'appeared as fearful,' he speaks only of the operation of knowledge by making the object primary, because it shows the seeing of perilous formations as they really are. But in the remaining seven instances, only the operation of knowledge is shown. Because this knowledge of conformity proceeds taking formations as its object by way of one or another characteristic among impermanence, etc., therefore it was said, 'because it proceeds taking formations as its object by way of the characteristic of impermanence, etc.' 'By that practice' means: by that practice of the knowledge of conformity which is the suppression of the grosser defilements that conceal the truths. For if the knowledge of conformity has not arisen in such a way, change-of-lineage knowledge is not able to take Nibbāna as its object; or if change-of-lineage knowledge has not arisen, path knowledge does not arise.

Vuttamatthaṃ opammena pākaṭataraṃ kātuṃ “yathā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha aṭṭhannaṃ vohārikamahāmattānaṃ agatigamanaṃ pahāya taṃtaṃvinicchayakaraṇaṃ viya aṭṭhannaṃ ñāṇānaṃ yathāsakaṃ paṭipakkhaṃ pahāya saṅkhāresu udayabbayādipaṭipatti, rañño majjhattabhāvo viya anulomañāṇassa purimapacchimadhammakoṭṭhāsassa anukūlatā. Tenevāti heṭṭhimañāṇānaṃ anulomanamukhena uparibodhipakkhiyānaṃ anulomanatoyeva. Saccānulomikanti vuccati maggasaccassa anulomikattā.

To make the meaning that has been stated clearer by a simile, the words 'Just as...' and so on were said. Therein, just as the eight great judicial ministers, having abandoned the wrong course, make their respective judgments, so the eight knowledges, having abandoned their respective opposing factors, practice the understanding of the rise and fall, etc., in formations. The impartiality of the king is like the suitability of the conformity-knowledge for the earlier and later portions of the Dhamma. For this very reason, it is so called precisely because it conforms to the higher factors of enlightenment by way of conforming to the lower knowledges. It is called 'conformity to the truths' because of its conformity to the truth of the path.

Anulomañāṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Knowledge of Conformity is Concluded.

Vuṭṭhānagāminīvipassanākathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of Insight Leading to Emergence

805. Kiñci [M 2.0481][V 2.0452] asaṅkhatārammaṇampi ñāṇaṃ vuṭṭhānagāminiyā ekasaṅgahanti katvā “saṅkhārārammaṇāyā”ti visesanaṃ kataṃ. Tañhi visesato vuṭṭhānaṃ ariyamaggaṃ gacchati upetīti vuṭṭhānagāminīti vattabbataṃ labhati. Tenāha “sabbena sabba”ntiādi. Asammohatthanti tattha tattha sutte pariyāyantarehi āgatāya sammohābhāvatthaṃ. Suttasaṃsandanāti suttānaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ suttapadānaṃ anusandānaṃ.

805. Thinking, 'Even a certain knowledge that has the unconditioned as its object is included as one with insight leading to emergence,' the qualification 'having formations as its object' was made. For it is specifically that which goes to or approaches the noble path of emergence that obtains the designation 'leading to emergence.' Therefore, he said, 'in every way,' etc. 'For the purpose of non-delusion' means for the purpose of the absence of delusion regarding the insight leading to emergence that is described in various suttas under different expressions. 'Comparison with the suttas' means the connection of the suttas, of those various sutta passages.

Ye lokiye saṅkhāre ārabbha anulomapariyosānā vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā pavattati, taṃsannissitā tappaṭibaddhā taṇhā tehi vinā appavattanato tammayā nāma, tammayāva tammayatā, tammayā vā taṇhāsampayuttā khandhā, tesaṃ bhāvo tammayatā, sā eva taṇhā. Tappaṭipakkhā vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā atammayatā. Tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “tammayatā nāma taṇhā, tassā pariyādiyanato vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanā atammayatāti vuccatī”ti (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 3.310). Nissāyāti taṃ atammayataṃ nissayaṃ katvā, bhāvetvāti attho. Ekattāti ettha ayaṃ pāḷi “atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā rūpesu…pe… phoṭṭhabbesu, ayaṃ, bhikkhave, upekkhā nānattā nānattasitā”ti (ma. ni. 3.310), sayampi nānāsabhāvā, nānārammaṇanissitā cāti attho. Sā pana samādhisampayuttā vipassanupekkhā veditabbā. “Atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā ākāsānañcāyatananissitā…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatananissitā, ayaṃ, bhikkhave, upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā”ti (ma. ni. 3.310). Yā hi taṃtaṃarūpacittuppādapariyāpannā upekkhā, sā ekasabhāvattā, ekārammaṇattā ca ekattā, ekattasitā cāti vuccati, sā pana taṃtaṃjhānasahagatavedanupekkhā ca tadārammaṇavipassanupekkhā cāti vadanti. Taṃ pajahathāti tadārammaṇakilesapahānena pajahatha. Tenāha “taṃ samatikkamathā”ti.

Regarding the worldly formations, when insight leading to emergence culminating in conformity arises, the craving dependent on them, connected to them, is called 'identification with them' because it does not arise without them. That very identification is the state of 'being identified with them'; or, the aggregates associated with craving are 'identified with them,' and their state is 'being identified with them,' which is simply craving. The insight leading to emergence that counteracts it is 'non-identification with them.' Therefore, it is said in the commentary: 'Craving is called "identification with them"; because insight leading to emergence exhausts it, it is called "non-identification with them."' 'Dependent on' means having made that non-identification the basis, that is, having developed it. Regarding 'oneness,' here the Pāḷi text states: 'There is, bhikkhus, equanimity regarding forms… tangible objects. This, bhikkhus, is equanimity based on diversity, supported by diversity,' meaning it is itself of diverse nature and depends on diverse objects. However, that should be understood as insight-equanimity connected with concentration. 'There is, bhikkhus, equanimity dependent on the base of infinite space… the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This, bhikkhus, is equanimity based on oneness, supported by oneness.' Indeed, the equanimity included in the arising of consciousness pertaining to those particular formless attainments is called 'oneness' and 'supported by oneness' because it has a single nature and a single object. They say this refers to the equanimity of feeling associated with the respective jhāna and the equanimity of insight regarding that object. 'Abandon that' means abandon it by abandoning the defilements connected to that object. Hence, He said: 'Transcend that.'

Nibbidāti vuṭṭhānagāminī. Tattha hi sutte virajjatīti maggakiccamāha, vimuccatīti phalakiccaṃ.

Disenchantment (nibbidā) is insight leading to emergence. For in that sutta, 'becomes dispassionate' refers to the function of the path, and 'is liberated' refers to the function of the fruit.

Susimasuttaṃ [M 2.0482][V 2.0453] nidānavagge. Tattha dhammaṭṭhitiñāṇaṃ vuṭṭhānagāminīti vuttā dhammaṭṭhitiyaṃ paṭiccasamuppāde asammuyhanavasena pavattanato. Nibbāne ñāṇanti maggañāṇamāha.

The Susima Sutta is in the Nidāna Vagga. There, the knowledge of the stability of phenomena is said to be 'insight leading to emergence' because it operates without confusion regarding dependent origination, which is the stability of phenomena. 'Knowledge of Nibbāna' refers to the knowledge of the path.

Saññā kho, poṭṭhapādāti ettha kāmaṃ “saññā”icceva vuccati, pubbe pana “saññaggaṃ phusatī”ti vuttattā āha “saññagganti vuttā”ti.

'Perception, Poṭṭhapāda' – here, although it is simply called 'perception,' because it was previously said 'one touches the peak of perception,' therefore it is said 'the peak of perception.'

Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhīti tadekadesabhūtā vuṭṭhānagāminī vuttā. Samudāyesu hi pavattā vohārā avayavesupi pavattantīti. Pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅganti pārisuddhiyā padhānakāraṇaṃ.

'The purification of knowledge and vision of the path' is said to be the insight leading to emergence, being a part of it. For usages that prevail with reference to wholes also prevail with reference to their parts. 'An auxiliary to complete purity' means a principal cause for purity.

Tīhi nāmehīti anulomagotrabhuvodānasaṅkhātehi tīhi nāmehi.

'By three names' means by the three names designated as conformity, change-of-lineage, and purification.

Kittitāti thomitā ariyamaggādhiṭṭhānatāya. Mahantānaṃ sīlakkhandhādīnaṃ esanaṭṭhena mahesinā sammāsambuddhena. Santakilesatāya santā. Yoganti bhāvanaṃ, bhāvanābhiyogaṃ vā.

'Praised' means extolled because of being the basis for the Noble Path. By the Great Seer, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in the sense of seeking great qualities such as the aggregates of virtue. 'Peaceful' because of the pacification of defilements. 'Yoga' means development, or application to development.

Paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Purification of Knowledge and Vision of the Path is concluded.

Iti ekavīsatimaparicchedavaṇṇanā.

Thus concludes the Commentary on the Twenty-first Chapter.

22. Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā

22. Commentary on the Exposition of the Purification of Knowledge and Vision

Paṭhamamaggañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the First Path Knowledge

806. Idāni [M 2.0483][V 2.0454] ñāṇadassanavisuddhiyā niddese anuppatte sā yassa ñāṇassa anantaraṃ uppajjati, taṃ tāva dassento “ito paraṃ gotrabhuñāṇaṃ hotī”ti āha. Ito paranti ito anulomañāṇato upari. Tanti gotrabhuñāṇaṃ. Neva paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ bhajati aniccādivasena saṅkhārānaṃ aggahaṇato. Na ñāṇadassanavisuddhiṃ bhajati satipi nibbānārammaṇatte kilesānaṃ akhepanato. Tato evetaṃ viññāṇadhātūnaṃ visayaṃ uddesantaṃ dassanakiccaṃ karontaṃ kiriyamanodhātu viya maggassa āvajjanaṭṭhāniyaṃ vuccati. Antarāti chaṭṭhasattamavisuddhīnaṃ vemajjhe. Abbohārikameva hoti ubhayavisuddhilakkhaṇatābhāvato. Tathāpi vuṭṭhānagāminiyā pariyosānatāya vipassanāpakkhikaṃ. Tenevassa taṃsotapatitatā. Tenāha “vipassanāsote…pe… saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti. Etenassa paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhibhajanaṃ dasseti. Sotassa ariyassaādito pajjanaṃ sotāpatti, so eva maggo, sotaṃ vā ariyaṃ ādito pajjati adhigacchatīti sotāpatti, paṭhamako. Tassa maggo sotāpattimaggo. Paṭisandhivasena sakideva imaṃ manussalokaṃ āgacchatīti sakadāgāmī, tassa maggo sakadāgāmimaggo. Paṭisandhivasena kāmabhavaṃ na āgacchatīti anāgāmī, tassa maggo anāgāmimaggo. Kilesādīnaṃ hananādinā arahaṃ, aggamaggaṭṭho. Tassa bhāvo arahattaṃ, so eva maggoti arahattamaggo. Catūsu maggesu ñāṇaṃ ekajjhaṃ gahetvā ñāṇadassanavisuddhi nāma.

806. Now, when the exposition of the purification by knowledge and vision has been reached in due course, first showing that knowledge immediately after which it arises, he said: 'Beyond this is the change-of-lineage knowledge.' 'Beyond this' means above this conformity knowledge. That is the change-of-lineage knowledge. It does not partake in the purification of knowledge and vision of the path because it does not grasp formations by way of impermanence, etc. It does not partake in the purification by knowledge and vision because, even though it has Nibbāna as its object, it does not destroy the defilements. For that very reason, this is said to be in the position of adverting for the path, like the functional mind-element that, indicating the object for the consciousness-elements, performs the function of seeing. 'In between' means in the middle of the sixth and seventh purifications. It is simply not designated as a purification because it lacks the characteristics of both purifications. Nevertheless, because it is the culmination of the insight that leads to emergence, it belongs to the side of insight. For that very reason, it has fallen into that stream. Therefore he said: 'it is reckoned in the stream of insight... etc.' By this, its participation in the purification of knowledge and vision of the path is shown. Entering the noble stream at the beginning is stream-entry (sotāpatti); that itself is the path. Or, because one enters or attains the noble stream at the beginning, it is called stream-entry; it is the first. The path of that one is the path of stream-entry. Because one comes to this human world only once by way of rebirth-linking, one is called a once-returner (sakadāgāmī); the path of that one is the path of the once-returner. Because one does not come to the sense-sphere existence by way of rebirth-linking, one is called a non-returner (anāgāmī); the path of that one is the path of the non-returner. Because of having destroyed the enemies that are the defilements, one is an Arahant, one established in the highest path. The state of that one is Arahantship; that itself is the path, thus it is the path of Arahantship. The knowledge in the four paths, taken collectively, is called the purification by knowledge and vision.

Tehi tīhipīti heṭṭhā tiṇṇaṃ anulomañāṇānaṃ vuttattā vuttaṃ, tīsu vā dvinnaṃ antogadhattā. Tīhipīti vā vikappantarasampiṇḍanattho pi-saddo, tena tīhipi dvīhipīti vuttaṃ hoti. Attano balānurūpenāti attano attano ānubhāvānukūlaṃ. Paṭhamañhi anulomañāṇaṃ sabboḷārikaṃ, dutiyaṃ tato nātioḷārikaṃ, tatiyaṃ tato nātioḷārikaṃ tamaṃ antaradhāpeti. Atha vā balānurūpenāti heṭṭhā [V 2.0455] saṅkhārupekkhāya āhitabalānurūpena[M 2.0484]. Pubbābhisaṅkhāravasena hi anulomañāṇassāpi maggañāṇassa viya saddhāvimuttadiṭṭhippattānaṃ pavattiākārasiddho attheva mudutikkhatāviseso. Palibodhato upaṭṭhāti palibodhabhāvapaṭicchādakassa tamassa antaradhāpitattā. “Āsevanante”ti iminā dutiyassa vā tatiyassa vā anulomañāṇassa anantaraṃ gotrabhuñāṇuppatti, na paṭhamassāti dasseti tassa anāsevanattā. Na hi aladdhāsevanaṃ gotrabhuñāṇaṃ uppādetuṃ sakkoti. Nimittādivirahato, tabbidhurato ca “animitta”ntiādinā nibbānaṃ visesitaṃ. Puthujjanagottanti ariyehi asammissaṃ puthujjanasamaññaṃ. Gottanti hi ekavaṃsajānaṃ samānā samaññā, evaṃ idhāpīti. Puthujjanasaṅkhanti tasseva vevacanaṃ, puthujjanabhūminti puthujjanavatthuṃ. Ekantikatāya ekavārameva ca uppajjanato apunarāvaṭṭakaṃ.

'By these three' is said because the three conformity knowledges have been mentioned below, or because the two are included within the three. Or, in the phrase `tīhipi`, the particle `pi` has the meaning of combining another alternative; therefore, it is said to mean 'by three' and 'by two'. 'According to one's own strength' means in accordance with one's own respective power. For the first conformity knowledge dispels the most coarse darkness; the second dispels the darkness that is not too coarse compared to that; the third dispels the darkness that is not too coarse compared to that. Alternatively, 'according to strength' means in accordance with the strength instilled by the equanimity towards formations mentioned below. For, due to the power of previous volitional formations, even for the conformity knowledge—just as for the path knowledge—there certainly exists a distinction of softness and sharpness, established by the mode of its occurrence for those liberated by faith and those who have attained the view. It appears as an obstruction because the darkness that conceals the state of being an obstruction has been dispelled. By 'at the end of repetition', it is shown that the change-of-lineage knowledge arises immediately after the second or third conformity knowledge, not after the first, because the latter lacks repetition. For a conformity knowledge that has not obtained repetition is not able to produce the change-of-lineage knowledge. Nibbāna is specified by 'signless', etc., due to the absence of signs and so on, and due to being devoid of them. 'The lineage of ordinary people' means the designation 'ordinary person', unmixed with the noble ones. For 'lineage' is a common designation for those born of one lineage; so it is here too. 'The term "ordinary person"' is a synonym for that very thing. 'The plane of an ordinary person' means the basis of an ordinary person. Due to its definitiveness and because it arises only once, it does not recur.

Bahiddhā vuṭṭhānavivaṭṭaneti asaṅkhatadhātuyā bahibhāvato bahiddhāsaññitā saṅkhāragatā vuṭṭhānabhūte vivaṭṭane nipphajjamāne paññā. Abhibhuyyatīti abhibhavati. Pakkhandatīti anupavisati. Ettha ca “uppādaṃ abhibhuyyatī”tiādinā puthujjanagottābhibhavanaṃ tadatikkamanamāha. “Anuppādaṃ pakkhandatī”tiādinā ariyagottabhāvanaṃ tadubhayabhāvato.

'Emergence and turning away from the external' is the wisdom that arises while the turning away—which is an emergence from the aggregate of formations called 'external' due to being external to the unconditioned element—is being accomplished. 'Is overcome' means it overcomes. 'Enters' means it enters into. And here, by the phrase 'overcoming arising', etc., it states the overcoming of the ordinary person's lineage, its transcendence. By the phrase 'entering non-arising', etc., it states the causing to be of the noble lineage, or the reaching of the noble lineage, because of approaching it.

807. Ekāvajjanānaṃ nānāvīthitā natthīti na taṃnisedhanāya ekavīthiggahaṇaṃ, atha kho nānārammaṇānampi ekāvajjanānaṃ nānāvīthitā natthīti dassanatthanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Mahāmātikanti mahantaṃ udakavāhakaṃ. Laṅghitvāti anotaranto eva atikkamitvā. Ullaṅghitvāti uparibhāgeneva laṅghitvā. Ninnapoṇapabbhāratā uttaruttaravisiṭṭhā ninnatāva.

807. The taking up of the term 'single process' is not for the purpose of negating the diversity of processes for minds of a single advertence; rather, it should be understood as being for the purpose of showing that even for minds with different objects but a single advertence, there is no diversity of process. 'A great channel' means a large water-carrying channel. 'Having crossed over' means having passed over without descending into it. 'Having leaped over' means having leaped over only by way of the upper part. The state of being inclined, bent, and sloped is just an inclination that is successively more distinct.

Aṭṭhahi ñāṇehi anukkamena āhitavisesaṃ anulomañāṇaṃ nibbānārammaṇassa ñāṇassa paccayo bhavituṃ samatthaṃ jātanti āha “udayabbayānupassanādinā vegena dhāvitvā”ti. Rūpaṃ anekasantatisambandhatāya anekavaṭṭaracitā rajju viya hotīti vuttaṃ “rūparajjuṃ vā”ti. Attabhāvassa rukkhaṭṭhāniyatāya vuttattā taṃsambandhadaṇḍaṭṭhāniyatā vedanādīsu ekasseva yuttā, na vedanādisamudāyassāti vuttaṃ “vedanādīsu aññataradaṇḍaṃ vā”ti. Anulomāvajjanenāti anulomassa āvajjanena. Yena āvajjanena anulomañāṇaṃ uppajjati, tena taṃ ārammaṇaṃ. “Paṭhamena anulomacittena ullaṅghitvā”ti idaṃ sakkāyatīrassa tassa atikkamanārambhatāya [M 2.0485] vuttaṃ. “Dutiyena nibbānaninnapoṇapabbhāramānaso”ti idaṃ tassa sabbasaṅkhārato sātisayaṃ alaggaṃ hutvā [V 2.0456] visaṅkhāre allīnabhāvato vuttaṃ. Nibbāne ārammaṇakaraṇavasena patati yogāvacaro. Ekārammaṇeti ekavāraṃyeva ālambite ārammaṇe. Tenāha “aladdhāsevanatāyā”ti. Tena ekārammaṇe āsevanā upakāravatī, na tathā nānārammaṇeti dasseti.

Conformity knowledge, which has its distinction brought about successively by the eight knowledges, has become capable of being a condition for the knowledge that has Nibbāna as its object; therefore, he said, 'having run with the speed of the contemplation of rise and fall, etc.' Because form, due to its connection with many continuities, is like a rope made of many strands, it is said, 'or the rope of form.' Because the individual existence is said to be in the position of a tree, the state of being in the position of a stick connected to it is suitable for only one among feelings, etc., not for the aggregate of feelings, etc.; therefore, it is said, 'or a certain stick among feelings, etc.' By 'with the advertence of conformity' is meant by the advertence for conformity. By whichever advertence conformity knowledge arises, by that advertence that object is taken up. The phrase 'having leaped over with the first conformity consciousness' is said because of its being the initial undertaking of transcending. The phrase 'with the second, the mind is inclined, bent, and sloped towards Nibbāna' is said because of its state of adhering to the unconditioned, having become exceedingly unattached from all formations. The yogī falls into Nibbāna by way of making it the object. By 'on a single object' is meant on an object apprehended only once. Therefore, he said, 'because of not having obtained repetition.' Thereby he shows that repetition on a single object is beneficial, but not so on different objects.

808. Tatrāti anulomagotrabhūnaṃ itarītarakiccākaraṇe. Nakkhattayoganti nakkhattena candassa yogaṃ, nakkhattayogavibhāvaniyaṃ vā kālaṃ, divasanti attho.

808. By 'therein' is meant in the context of the non-performance of each other's function by conformity and change-of-lineage. By 'conjunction of a constellation' is meant the conjunction of the moon with a constellation, or the time to be made known by the conjunction of a constellation; the meaning is 'the day'.

Tatthātiādi upamāsaṃsandanaṃ.

The words beginning with 'therein' are for the comparison of the similes.

Evaṃ nibbattāhīti anulomañāṇāni viya saṅkhāre anālambitvā ahaṃ viya nibbānārammaṇe vattāhīti maggassa gotrabhunā dinnasaññāmuñcanaṃ, anubandhanañca nibbānārammaṇakaraṇameva sandhāya vuttaṃ.

The non-abandoning of the perception given to the path by the change-of-lineage knowledge, and the following of it, are spoken of with reference to simply making Nibbāna the object. The perception is: 'Do not take formations as an object as the conformity-knowledges do; rather, like me, you should function with Nibbāna as your object.'

809. Tatrāti tasmiṃ gotrabhunā dinnasaññaṃ amuñcitvā viya tena gahitārammaṇeyeva vattitvā maggassa lobhakkhandhādinibbijjhane. Usuṃ asati khippatīti issāso, dhanuggaho. Saragocaraṭṭhānaṃ nāma aṭṭhausabhamattaṃ. Tañca kho dūre pātino majjhimapurisassa vasena catuhatthāya yaṭṭhiyā vīsatiyaṭṭhi usabhaṃ, tena aṭṭhausabhamatte padese hatthavasena cattārīsādhikachasatahatthe padese. Phalakasatanti asanasāramayaṃ phalakasataṃ. Kumbhakāracakkasadise cakkayante. Āvijjhitvāti bhametvā. Daṇḍakaghaṭṭanāya uppādetabbasaddo daṇḍakasaññā. Phalakasatavinivijjhanassa paccayabhūtā daṇḍakasaññā viya gotrabhuñāṇaṃ lobhakkhandhādinibbijjhanassa maggañāṇassa paccayabhāvato. Issāso viya maggañāṇaṃ nibbijjhitabbanivijjhanato.

809. By 'therein' is meant the path's piercing of the aggregates of greed, etc., by functioning as if not abandoning the perception given by that change-of-lineage knowledge and continuing with the object apprehended by it. Because he shoots an arrow, he is an archer, a bowman. The range of an arrow is said to be about eight usabhas. And that, for a middling man who shoots far, is calculated thus: an usabha is twenty rods, with each rod being four cubits. Thus, in a region of eight usabhas, in terms of cubits, it is a region of six hundred and forty cubits. By 'a hundred planks' is meant a hundred planks made of asana heartwood on a wheel-machine similar to a potter's wheel. The sound to be produced by the striking of the rod is the 'perception of the rod.' Just as the perception of the rod is the condition for piercing the hundred planks, so the change-of-lineage knowledge should be understood, because it is the condition for the path-knowledge's piercing of the aggregates of greed, etc. Like the archer, the path-knowledge should be understood, because it pierces what is to be pierced.

810. Aṭṭhamabhavato paṭṭhāya nibbattanakaṃ anamataggasaṃsāravaṭṭadukkhasamuddaṃ soseti. Saddhādhanaṃ sīladhanaṃ hiridhanaṃ ottappadhanaṃ sutadhanaṃ cāgadhanaṃ paññādhananti imesaṃ sattannaṃ ariyadhanānaṃ. Sammukhībhāvanti paccakkhasiddhiṃ. Pāṇātipātādipañcaverāni [M 2.0486] ceva pañcavīsatimahābhayāni cāti sabbaverabhayāni. Aññesañca ratanattaye niviṭṭhasaddhādīnaṃ. Samudāye pavatto sotāpattimaggasaddo tadekadesepi pavattatīti āha “sotāpattimaggena sampayuttaṃ ñāṇa”nti.

810. Starting from the eighth existence, it dries up the ocean of suffering in the beginningless round of saṃsāra that is to arise. Of these seven noble treasures: the treasure of faith, the treasure of virtue, the treasure of moral shame, the treasure of moral dread, the treasure of learning, the treasure of generosity, and the treasure of wisdom. By 'direct presence' is meant direct accomplishment. The five enmities beginning with the destruction of life, and the twenty-five great fears—these are all the enmities and fears. And of others, such as faith, etc., established in the Triple Gem. The term 'stream-entry path,' which applies to the whole, also applies to a part of it; therefore, he said, 'knowledge associated with the stream-entry path.'

Paṭhamamaggañāṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The knowledge of the first path is concluded.

Sotāpannapuggalakathāvaṇṇanā

Elucidation of the Discourse on the Stream-Enterer Person

811. Tasseva [V 2.0457] sotāpattimaggacittassa. Kāmañcettha nātitikkhapaññassa dve, tikkhapaññassa tīṇi phalacittāni honti, avisesato pana gahitassa maggassa vasena “dve, tīṇi vā”ti vuttaṃ. Samādhimānantarikaññamāhūti yaṃ attano pavattisamanantaraṃ niyameneva phalappadānato ānantarikasamādhīti āhūti attho. Anantarameva pavattanakaṃ phalaṃ anantaraṃ, tattha niyutto, taṃ vā payojanaṃ etassāti ānantariko, maggo.

811. Of that very stream-entry path-consciousness. Although here, for one of not very keen wisdom, two fruition-consciousnesses arise, and for one of keen wisdom, three fruition-consciousnesses arise, it is said 'two or three' generally, by way of the path that has been taken. By 'they call it immediate concentration' (samādhimānantarikaññamāhu) is meant that because it inevitably yields fruition immediately after its own occurrence, they call it 'concentration with immediate result' (ānantarikasamādhi). The fruition that occurs immediately after is 'immediate' (anantaraṃ); that which is connected with it, or that for which it is the purpose, is 'immediate' (ānantariko), namely, the path.

Āsevananteti āsevanato ante, āsevanalābhino anulomañāṇassa anantaranti attho. Laddhāsevanameva anulomaṃ gotrabhuṃ uppādeti. Upari pana cha, satta vā javanāni pavattanti, tasmā cattāri phalacittāni hontīti vadeyyāti āha “sattacittaparamā ca ekāvajjanavīthī”ti.

By 'at the end of repetition' (āsevanante) is meant: at the end of, that is, immediately after the conformity-knowledge that has obtained the repetition condition. Only the conformity that has obtained the repetition condition produces the change-of-lineage. In case one might say, 'But further on, six or seven impulsions occur, therefore four fruition-consciousnesses arise,' he said, 'a cognitive process with a single adverting has a maximum of seven consciousness-moments.'

Taṃ pana na sārato paccetabbanti yojanā. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva.

But that, however, should not be accepted as the essential point; this is the connection. Whatever should be said here has already been said below.

812. Ettāvatāti paṭhamamaggānantaraṃ phalassa uppattimakkena. Bhusaṃ pamattopīti devarajjacakkavattirajjādipamādaṭṭhānaṃ āgamma bhusaṃ pamattopi. Yesaṃ yathāvuttaāvajjanajavanacittānaṃ uppattiyā esa sotāpanno paccavekkhati nāmāti adhippāyo.

812. By 'by this much' (ettāvatā) is meant: merely by the arising of the fruition immediately after the first path. By 'even if greatly heedless' (bhusaṃ pamattopi) is meant: even if greatly heedless, having come to a basis for heedlessness such as the state of a king of the gods or a universal monarch. The intention is: it is due to the arising of which aforementioned adverting and impulsion consciousnesses that this stream-enterer is said to review.

Eteneva pasaṅgena sesānaṃ ariyānaṃ paccavekkhaṇāni dassetuṃ “yathā cā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

In this very connection, in order to show the reviewings of the remaining noble ones, the passage beginning with 'and just as' (yathā ca) was stated.

Ukkaṭṭhaparicchedoyeva [M 2.0487] ceso, yadidaṃ pañcannaṃ, catunnañca paccavekkhaṇānaṃ dassananti attho. “Abhāvenevā”ti etena pahīnāvasiṭṭhakilesapaccavekkhaṇasamatthatā kassaci hoti, kassaci na hotīti dasseti. Lobho eva lobhadhammo.

And this is only a supreme distinction, meaning, the showing of the five and four reviewings. By this phrase, 'by the very absence' (abhāveneva), it shows that for some the ability to review the abandoned and the remaining defilements exists, while for some it does not. Greed itself is the state of greed.

Dutiyamaggañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Second Path-Knowledge

813. Kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ tanubhāvāyāti etesaṃ kilesānaṃ tanubhāvatthaṃ. Tattha dvīhi kāraṇehi tanubhāvo adhiccuppattiyā, pariyuṭṭhānamandatāya ca. Sakadāgāmissa hi vaṭṭānusārimahājanassa [V 2.0458] viya kilesā abhiṇhaṃ na uppajjanti, kadāci kadāci viraḷākārā hutvā uppajjanti. Tathā uppajjantāpi maddantā chādentā andhakāraṃ karontā na uppajjanti, dvīhi pana maggehi pahīnattā mandamandā tanukākārā hutvā uppajjanti. Keci pana “sakadāgāmissāpi kilesā cirena uppajjanti, uppajjantāpi bahalāva uppajjanti. Tathā hissa puttadhītaro dissantī”ti, taṃ akāraṇaṃ vatthupaṭisevanena vināpi gabbhaggahaṇasabbhāvato. Tasmā vuttanayeneva dvīhi kāraṇehi tesaṃ tanubhāvo veditabbo. Dutiyāyāti gaṇanavasenapi dutiyāya, uppattivasenapi dutiyāya bhūmiyā. Pattiyāti sāmaññaphalassa paṭilābhāya. Tañhi sampayuttānaṃ nissayabhāvato te dhammā bhavanti etthāti bhūmi. Yasmā vā samānepi lokuttarabhāve sayampi bhavati uppajjati, na nibbānaṃ viya apātubhūtaṃ, tasmāpi “bhūmī”ti vuccati. Yogaṃ karotīti vipassanābhiyogaṃ karoti. “Navahākārehi indriyāni tikkhāni bhavantī”tiādinā (visuddhi. 2.699) vuttanayeneva yadaggena indriyānaṃ tikkhataṃ sampādeti, tadaggena balāni, bojjhaṅgāni ca paṭutarabhāvaṃ āpādento indriyabalabojjhaṅgāni samodhānetvā lakkhaṇattayatīraṇavasena ñāṇena parimaddati. Tattha aparāparaṃ ñāṇaṃ cārento parivatteti. Tenāha “vipassanāvīthiṃ ogāhatī”ti. Vuttanayenevāti udayabbayañāṇādīnaṃ uppādane vuttanayena. Gotrabhuanantaranti ettha gotrabhu viya gotrabhu. Paṭhamamaggapurecārikañāṇañhi puthujjanagottābhibhavanato, ariyagottabhavanato ca nippariyāyato gotrabhūti vuccati, idaṃ pana taṃsadisatāya pariyāyato gotrabhu. Ekaccasaṃkilesavisuddhiyā[M 2.0488], pana accantavisuddhiyā ārammaṇakaraṇato ca vodānanti vuccati. Tenāha paṭṭhāne “anulomaṃ vodānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā 1.1.417). Yasmā pana paṭisambhidāmagge uppādādiabhibhavanatthaṃ upādāya “aṭṭha gotrabhudhammā samādhivasena uppajjanti, dasa gotrabhudhammā vipassanāvasena uppajjantī”tiādīsu (paṭi. ma. 1.60) gotrabhunāmenevetaṃ āgataṃ, tasmā idhāpi “gotrabhuanantara”nti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

813. `For the attenuation of sensual desire and ill will` means for the purpose of attenuating these defilements. Herein, attenuation occurs for two reasons: due to infrequent arising and due to the sluggishness of obsession. For a once-returner, unlike the great mass of people who follow the round of existence, defilements do not arise constantly; they arise only occasionally in a sparse manner. Even when they do arise, they do not arise crushing, covering, or creating darkness; but rather, because they have been abandoned by the two paths, they arise very sluggishly and in an attenuated form. Some, however, say: 'For a once-returner too, defilements arise after a long time, and when they arise, they arise thickly. Indeed, his sons and daughters are seen.' But that is not a valid reason, since the existence of conception is possible even without engaging in the physical act. Therefore, their attenuation should be understood by the two reasons in the way stated. `To the second` means to the second plane, both by way of counting and by way of arising. `For attainment` means for the attainment of the fruit of recluseship. Indeed, because it is a support for associated states, those states exist in it; for this reason, it is called a plane (`bhūmi`). Or, because, although it is similar in being supramundane, it itself comes to be, it arises—it is not unmanifested like Nibbāna—therefore it is also called a 'plane.' `Makes an effort` means he makes the effort of insight. In the way stated by 'The faculties become sharp in nine ways,' etc., to the extent that one accomplishes the sharpness of the faculties, to that extent, causing the powers and the enlightenment factors to reach a state of greater acuity, and having unified the faculties, powers, and enlightenment factors, one thoroughly masters them with knowledge by way of investigating the three characteristics. Therein, causing knowledge to proceed successively, one makes it revolve. Therefore, it is said, 'He enters the course of insight.' `In the way stated` means in the way stated for the arising of the knowledge of rise and fall, etc. `Immediately after change-of-lineage`: here, that which is like the change-of-lineage knowledge is called `gotrabhu`. Indeed, the knowledge that precedes the first path is called `gotrabhu` (change-of-lineage) in a direct sense because it overcomes the lineage of the common person and brings about the noble lineage. This knowledge, however, is called `gotrabhu` in a figurative sense because of its similarity to that. But it is called `vodāna` (purification) because of purification from some defilements and because of taking as its object that which is utterly pure. Therefore, it is said in the Paṭṭhāna, 'Conformity is a condition for purification by proximity condition.' However, because in the Paṭisambhidāmagga, with reference to the meaning of overcoming arising, etc., in such passages as, 'Eight change-of-lineage states arise by way of concentration; ten change-of-lineage states arise by way of insight,' etc., this knowledge is presented only by the name 'change-of-lineage' (`gotrabhu`), it should be understood that here too it is said, 'immediately after change-of-lineage' (`gotrabhuanantaram`).

Dutiyañāṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Knowledge is Concluded.

Tatiyamaggañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Third Path-Knowledge

814. Sakidevāti [V 2.0459] ekavāraṃyeva. “Imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā”ti iminā pañcasu sakadāgāmīsu cattāro vajjetvā ekova gahito. Ekacco idha sakadāgāmiphalaṃ patvā idheva loke parinibbāti, ekacco idha patvā devaloke parinibbāti, ekacco devaloke patvā tattheva parinibbāti, ekacco devaloke patvā idhūpapajjitvā parinibbāti. Ime cattāropi idha na gahitā. Yo pana idha patvā devaloke yāvatāyukaṃ vasitvā puna idhūpapajjitvā parinibbāti, ayaṃ ekova idha gahitoti veditabbo.

814. “Only once” means just one time. By this phrase, “having come to this world,” among the five types of once-returners, four are excluded and only one is taken. A certain one, having attained the fruit of a once-returner here, attains parinibbāna right here in this world. A certain one, having attained it here, attains parinibbāna in the deva world. A certain one, having attained it in the deva world, attains parinibbāna right there. A certain one, having attained it in the deva world, having arisen here, attains parinibbāna. These four are not taken here. But as for the one who, having attained it here, having lived in the deva world for the full extent of their lifespan, and having arisen here again, attains parinibbāna—this one alone is taken here. Thus it should be understood.

Kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ anavasesappahānāyāti tesaṃyeva sakadāgāmimaggena tanukatānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ niravasesappahānāya. Paṭisandhivasena kāmabhavassa anāgamanato anāgāmī.

“For the remainderless abandoning of sensual lust and ill will” means for the remainderless abandoning of those same fetters that were made thin by the path of the once-returner. Because of not returning to the sensual existence by way of rebirth-linking, one is a non-returner.

Tatiyañāṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Third Knowledge is Concluded.

Catutthamaggañāṇakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Fourth Path-Knowledge

815. Opapātikoti upapātayoniko. Imināssa gabbhaseyyā paṭikkhittā. Tattha parinibbāyīti tattha suddhāvāse parinibbāyitā. Anāvattidhammo tasmā lokāti paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena tasmā lokā idha [M 2.0489] anāvattanasabhāvo, buddhadassanadhammassavanānaṃ panatthāya āgamanaṃ hotiyeva.

815. “One of spontaneous birth” means one who has a spontaneous birth. By this, womb-birth is rejected for this person. “Attaining parinibbāna there” means having the nature of attaining parinibbāna there in the Pure Abodes. “Of a nature not to return from that world” means having the nature of not returning from that world to here by way of taking up a new rebirth-linking; however, a coming for the sake of seeing the Buddha or hearing the Dhamma certainly does exist.

Rūparāgaarūparāgamānauddhaccaavijjānaṃ anavasesappahānāyāti etesaṃ pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyasaṃyojanānaṃ nissesappajahanatthāya. Tattha rūpabhave chandarāgo rūparāgo. Arūpabhave chandarāgo arūparāgo. Māno arahattamaggavajjhamāno. Tathā uddhaccāvijjā.

“For the remainderless abandoning of lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance” means for the sake of the complete abandoning of these five higher fetters. Among these, desire and lust in the form existence is lust for form. Desire and lust in the formless existence is lust for the formless. Conceit is the conceit that is to be struck down by the path of Arahantship. Restlessness and ignorance are likewise.

Catutthañāṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fourth Knowledge is Concluded.

Arahantapuggalakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Arahant Individual

816. Mahākhīṇāsavoti [V 2.0460] mahānubhāvatānibandhanaṃ pūjāvacanametaṃ, na upādāyavacanaṃ yathā “mahāmoggallāno”ti. Na hi cūḷakhīṇāsavo nāma atthi. Antimadehaṃ dhāretīti antimadehadhārī. Khandhakilesābhisaṅkhārabhārānaṃ ohitattā oropitattā ohitabhāro. Anuppatto sadatthaṃ sakatthanti anuppattasadattho. Sadatthoti ca arahattaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañhi attupanibandhanaṭṭhena, attānaṃ avijahanaṭṭhena, attano paramatthaṭṭhena ca attano atthattā sakatthoti vuccati. Parikkhīṇāni dasapi bhavasaṃyojanāni etassāti parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano. Khandhādiatthaṃ sammā aññāya vimuttoti sammadaññāvimutto. Aggo ca so dakkhiṇeyyo ca, aggadakkhiṇaṃ vā arahatīti aggadakkhiṇeyyo.

816. The name 'Mahākhīṇāsava' is a term of praise and veneration that is a basis for recognizing great power; it is not a comparative term, as in 'Mahāmoggallāna'. Indeed, there is no such thing as a 'minor one with destroyed taints'. Because he bears the final body, he is called `antimadehadhārī`. Because the burdens of the aggregates, defilements, and formations have been laid down, he is called `ohitabhāro`. Because he has attained his own welfare, he is called `anuppattasadattho`. And 'his own welfare' should be understood as Arahantship. Indeed, that Arahantship is called `sakattha` (one's own welfare) because it is one's own welfare, due to its meaning of being connected to oneself, its meaning of not abandoning oneself, and its meaning of being one's own ultimate good. Because the ten fetters of becoming are destroyed for this person, he is called `parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano`. Because he is liberated by rightly understanding the meaning of the aggregates and so on, he is called `sammadaññāvimutto`. He is foremost and worthy of offerings; or, because he is worthy of the foremost offering, he is called `aggadakkhiṇeyyo`.

Bodhipakkhiyakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Factors of Enlightenment

817. Catunnaṃ maggañāṇānaṃ vasena catuñāṇāya. Ānubhāvavijānanatthanti satipaṭṭhānapāripūriādikassa ānubhāvassa bodhanatthaṃ.

817. `Catuñāṇāya` (for one with four knowledges) is explained as: by means of the four path-knowledges. `Ānubhāvavijānanatthaṃ` (for the purpose of understanding the power) means: for the purpose of knowing the power of such things as the complete fulfillment of the foundations of mindfulness.

Paripuṇṇā bodhipakkhiyā etassāti paripuṇṇabodhipakkhiyo, maggo. Tassa bhāvo paripuṇṇabodhipakkhiyabhāvo. Vuṭṭhānabalehi sampayuttatāva vuṭṭhānabalasamāyogo, ye saṃyojanādayo yena paṭhamamaggādinā pahātabbā.

The path for which the factors of enlightenment are fulfilled is `paripuṇṇabodhipakkhiyo`. The state of that is `paripuṇṇabodhipakkhiyabhāvo`. `Vuṭṭhānabalasamāyogo` is the combination of emergence and association with the powers. By this path, beginning with the first path, the fetters and so on are to be abandoned.

818. Bujjhanaṭṭhena [M 2.0490] vā bodho, maggacittuppādo. Tassa bujjhanakiriyāya anuguṇabhāvato pakkhe bhavāti bodhipakkhiyā.

818. Alternatively, `bodhi` (enlightenment) is so called because of the meaning of awakening; this refers to the arising of the path-consciousness. Because they are suitable for that act of awakening and are on its side, they are called `bodhipakkhiyā`.

819. Tesu bodhipakkhiyesu. Ārammaṇesūti kāyādiārammaṇesu. Okkhanditvāti anupavisitvā. Pakkhanditvāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Upaṭṭhānatoti asubhākārādiggahaṇavasena upagantvā avaṭṭhānato. Kāyādīsu asubhākārādiggahaṇaṃ pubbabhāgasatipaṭṭhānavasena subhasaññādipahānakiccasādhanaṃ maggasatipaṭṭhānavasena veditabbaṃ. Tattha hi ekāva sati catukiccasādhanavasena pavattati.

819. Among those factors of enlightenment. The word `ārammaṇesu` (in the objects) means: in objects such as the body. The word `okkhantitvā` (having plunged into) means: having entered into. The word `pakkhanditvā` (having rushed into) is a synonym for that very word. The word `upaṭṭhānato` (by attending) means: because of approaching and being established by way of grasping the aspect of foulness and so on. The grasping of the aspect of foulness and so on in the body and so on is to be understood by way of the preliminary-stage foundation of mindfulness. Accomplishing the task of abandoning the perception of beauty and so on is to be understood by way of the path-stage foundation of mindfulness. Indeed, in that path, a single mindfulness proceeds by way of accomplishing four functions.

820. Padahantīti [V 2.0461] vāyamanti, kāyacittāni paggaṇhanti vā. Asobhāhetūnaṃ saṃkilesadhammānaṃ pajahanena, sobhāhetūnañca vodānadhammānaṃ bhāvanena sobhanaṃ, sundaranti attho. Seṭṭhabhāvāvahanatoti pāsaṃsatamabhāvasādhanato. Padhānabhāvakāraṇatoti uttamabhāvahetuto.

820. “They strive” means they exert themselves, or they lift up their body and mind. By abandoning defiling qualities that are causes of ugliness, and by developing pure qualities that are causes of beauty, it is beautiful and lovely; this is the meaning. “Because it brings about the highest state” means because it accomplishes the most praiseworthy state. “Because it is a cause of the principal state” means because it is a cause for the highest state.

821. Pubbe vuttenāti iddhividhañāṇaniddese (visuddhi. 2.369) vuttena. Ijjhanaṭṭho nipphajjanaṭṭho, paṭilābhasampadā vā, yena vā ijjhanti iddhā vuddhā ukkaṃsagatā honti, taṃ ijjhanaṃ. Samādhipadhānasaṅkhārapamukhā maggadhammā idha “iddhī”ti adhippetā. Pubbaṅgamaṭṭho adhipatipaccayabhāvo. Tasmā sotāpattimaggo ijjhatīti iddhi, tasmā sampayuttā chandādayo pubbaṅgamaṭṭhena pādo. Tassā eva phalabhūtāya vuṭṭhānagāminiyā chandādayo pubbabhāgakāraṇaṭṭhena pādo. Soti iddhipādo. Ime lokuttarāvāti ime yathāvuttā chandādayo uttaracūḷabhājanīye āgatanayena lokuttarā veditabbā. Chandādiadhipativasena paṭiladdhadhammāpi phassādayo iddhipādā hontīti attho. Kāmañcettha iddhipādo no adhipati, adhipati vā no iddhipādo nāma natthi, yathā pana ekasmiṃ rajje rajjārahesu catūsu rājakumāresu ekasmiṃ kāle ekova rajjamanusāsati, na sabbe, evaṃ ekamekasmiṃ cittuppāde ekova adhipati, iddhipādo ca hotīti veditabbo.

821. “As previously stated” refers to what was said in the Exposition of the Knowledge of the Kinds of Spiritual Power. The meaning of 'success' (ijjhana) is accomplishment or the perfection of attainment; or, that by which one succeeds, prospers, and reaches excellence is 'success'. Here, the path-factors headed by concentration and striving-formations are intended by 'spiritual power' (iddhi). The meaning of 'forerunner' is the state of being a dominant condition. Therefore, the stream-entry path succeeds, thus it is 'spiritual power'; therefore, the associated factors such as zeal are a 'basis' by the meaning of 'forerunner'. Of that very resultant spiritual power leading to emergence, the factors such as zeal are a 'basis' by the meaning of being a cause of the preliminary part. Thus, it is a basis of spiritual power. “These are supramundane” means these factors such as zeal, as described, should be understood as supramundane according to the method that comes in the Uttaracūḷabhājanīya. The meaning is that even the factors such as contact, attained through the power of the dominants such as zeal, are bases of spiritual power. And while it is true that in this context there is no basis of spiritual power that is not a dominant, nor any dominant that is not a basis of spiritual power, still, just as in one kingdom, among four princes worthy of kingship, only one rules at a time, not all, so too in each and every mind-moment, only one is dominant and is a basis of spiritual power; this should be understood.

822. Assaddhiyaṃ [M 2.0491] saddhāpaṭipakkhā akusalā dhammā, avatthugato pasādapatirūpako micchādhimokkho vā. Kosajjaṃ thinamiddhapadhāno akusalacittuppādo. Pamādo satisammoso tathāpavattā akusalā khandhā. Abhibhavanasaṅkhātena adhipatiyaṭṭhenāti assaddhiyādīnaṃ abhibhavanato abhibhavananti vattabbena adhimokkhapaggahaupaṭṭhānaavikkhepapajānanassa ekalakkhaṇena sampayuttadhammesu adhipatiyaṭṭhena. Assaddhiyādīhi cāti ca-saddo samuccayattho aṭṭhānappayutto, tasmā akampiyaṭṭhena ca sampayuttadhammesu thirabhāvena ca balanti evamettha adhippāyo veditabbo.

822. “Faithlessness” are unwholesome states that are the opposite of faith, or it is wrong resolve, which is a semblance of confidence based on an unworthy object. “Laziness” is an unwholesome arising of consciousness in which sloth and torpor are predominant. “Heedlessness” is a lapse of mindfulness and the unwholesome aggregates that have arisen in such a way. “By the meaning of predominance which is designated as ‘overcoming’”: This is because of overcoming faithlessness and so forth, which is called ‘overcoming,’ and because of the meaning of predominance over associated states through a single characteristic among resolve, exertion, establishment, non-distraction, and understanding. In the phrase “and by faithlessness, etc.,” the word ‘ca’ has a conjunctive meaning and is inappropriately used. Therefore, the intention here should be understood thus: it is ‘strength’ (bala) because of the meaning of being unshakeable and because of the state of firmness among associated states.

823. Bujjhanakasattassāti catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ paṭivijjhanakasattassa. Yo heso lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe uppajjamānāya satiādidhammasāmaggiyā karaṇabhūtāya bujjhati kilesasantānaniddāya uṭṭhahati, cattāri vā ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhati, nibbānameva vā sacchikarotīti [V 2.0462] bodhīti vuccati ariyasāvako, tassa bodhissa bujjhanakasattassa aṅgāti bojjhaṅgā. Niyyānikaṭṭhenāti vaṭṭato nissaraṇaṭṭhena.

823. “Of a being who awakens” means of a being who penetrates the four noble truths. For that noble disciple who, at the moment of the supramundane path, by the assemblage of states beginning with mindfulness which is arising and has become the instrument, awakens, or rises from the sleep that is the continuum of defilements, or penetrates the four noble truths, or realizes Nibbāna itself, is for that reason called ‘bodhi’ (awakening). The factors of that ‘bodhi,’ of that being who awakens, are the ‘enlightenment factors’ (bojjhaṅgā). “By the meaning of leading out” means by the meaning of escape from the round of existence.

824. Pubbabhāge nānācittesu labbhantīti sambandho. Cuddasavidhenāti ānāpānairiyāpathacatusampajaññapaṭikkūlamanasikāradhātumanasikārapabbāni, nava sivathikapabbāni cāti evaṃ cuddasavidhena. Kāyaṃ pariggaṇhato ca kāyānupassanāsatipaṭṭhānaṃ labbhati, na vedanādayo pariggaṇhato. Esa nayo sesesupi. “Sukhaṃ vedana”ntiādināti vā “sāmisa”ntiādināti vā “nirāmisa”ntiādināti vā evaṃ navavidhena. Sarāgadosamohasaṃkhittamahaggatasamāhitasauttaravimuttapadānaṃ sapaṭipakkhānaṃ vasena soḷasavidhena. Nīvaraṇupādānakkhandhāyatanabojjhaṅgasaccapabbānaṃ vasena pañcavidhena. Imasmiṃ attabhāveti paccuppanne attabhāve. Anuppannapubbanti attano abhūtapubbaṃ. Parassa uppannaṃ akusalaṃ disvā tannimittañca vadhabandhārahādīnīti adhippāyo. Tassāti tādisassa. Bhavati hi taṃsadisepi tabbohāro yathā “tāniyeva osadhānī”ti. Tassa pahānāyāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Jhānavipassanā ito aññasmiṃ attabhāve uppannapubbāpi siyunti vuttaṃ “imasmiṃ attabhāve anuppannapubba”nti, chandiddhipādasammāvācānaṃyeva gahaṇaṃ. Tesu vuttesu sesiddhipādasesaviratiyo atthato [M 2.0492] vuttāva hontīti lakkhaṇahāravasena ayamattho veditabbo. Evaṃ nānācittesu labbhanti pubbabhāge ete satipaṭṭhānasammappadhānaiddhipādā. Catunnaṃ ñāṇānanti catunnaṃ ariyamaggañāṇānaṃ. Kāmaṃ sabbepi bodhipakkhiyadhammā maggacittuppādapariyāpannāva, tathāpi sātisayo sammappadhānabyāpāro maggakkhaṇeti vuttaṃ “phalakkhaṇe ṭhapetvā cattāro sammappadhāne”ti. Avasesā tettiṃsa labbhanti, te ca kho pariyāyato, na nippariyāyatoti adhippāyo.

824. In the initial stage, they are obtained in various states of mind—this is the connection. The fourteenfold method refers to the sections on mindfulness of breathing, postures, clear comprehension, contemplation of the repulsive, and reflection on the elements, and the nine charnel ground contemplations; thus, by the fourteenfold method. By encompassing the body, one attains the establishment of mindfulness as contemplation of the body, but not by encompassing feelings and the rest. This same principle applies to the others. Or, by the text beginning with ‘pleasant feeling,’ etc., or ‘worldly,’ etc., or ‘unworldly,’ etc.—thus, it is ninefold. By means of the terms—with lust, with hate, with delusion, contracted, expanded, concentrated, surpassable, and liberated—along with their opposites, it is sixteenfold. By means of the sections on the hindrances, clinging aggregates, sense bases, enlightenment factors, and truths, it is fivefold. ‘In this existence’ means in the present existence. ‘Not arisen before’ means not having occurred before for oneself. The intention is: seeing an unwholesome state that has arisen in another, and as its consequence, killing, binding, reviling, and so on. ‘Of that’ means of such a kind. For that designation is used even for something similar to that, just as in the expression ‘those very medicines.’ In ‘for the abandoning of that’ also, this is the very same principle. Jhāna and vipassanā might have arisen before in another existence than this one; therefore, it is said ‘not arisen before in this existence.’ Only the basis of spiritual power of zeal and right speech are to be taken. When these are mentioned, the remaining bases of spiritual power and the remaining abstinences are, in terms of meaning, already stated. This meaning should be understood by way of the method of characteristic inference. Thus, in the initial stage, these establishments of mindfulness, right strivings, and bases of spiritual power are obtained in various states of mind. ‘Of the four knowledges’ means of the four noble path knowledges. Indeed, all factors of enlightenment are included in the arising of path-consciousness. Nevertheless, the function of the right strivings is pre-eminent at the moment of the path; therefore, it is said, ‘setting aside the four right strivings at the moment of fruition.’ The remaining thirty-three are obtained, but figuratively, not literally—this is the intention.

825. Sesesu panāti iddhipādādīsu pañcasu koṭṭhāsesu. Yathā sativīriyesu “satipaṭṭhānaṃ sammappadhāna”nti saṅkhipanavasena hāpanaṃ, “kāyānupassanā”tiādivibhāgadassanavasena vaḍḍhanaṃ atthi, īdisaṃ hāpanavaḍḍhanaṃ natthīti attho.

825. As for the remaining ones—in the five categories such as the bases of spiritual power—just as in mindfulness and energy there is reduction by way of abbreviation, saying, “establishment of mindfulness, right striving,” and increase by way of showing distinctions, such as “contemplation of the body,” etc., there is no such reduction and increase. This is the meaning.

826. Idāni sabbesu eva yathārahaṃ labbhamānavibhāgadassanatthaṃ “apicā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha tesūti sattatiṃsāya bodhipakkhiyadhammesu. Chaddhāti ekadhā dvedhā catudhā pañcadhā aṭṭhadhā navadhāti evaṃ chappakārena te bhavanti.

826. Now, for the purpose of showing the obtainable distinctions in all of them appropriately, the passage beginning “Moreover…” is introduced. Therein, “among them” refers to the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment. “Sixfold” means they are in six ways: onefold, twofold, fourfold, fivefold, eightfold, and ninefold.

Chandiddhipādādivasenāti [V 2.0463] chando chandiddhipādavaseneva, cittaṃ cittiddhipādavaseneva, pītipassaddhiupekkhā bojjhaṅgavaseneva, saṅkappādayo maggavasenevāti evaṃ nava ekavidhāva honti.

By way of the basis of spiritual power of zeal, etc.: zeal is only by way of the basis of spiritual power of zeal; mind is only by way of the basis of spiritual power of mind; joy, tranquility, and equanimity are only by way of the enlightenment factors; and thought and so forth are only by way of the path factors. Thus, these nine are onefold.

Cuddaseva asambhinnāti sati vīriyaṃ chando cittaṃ paññā saddhā samādhi pīti passaddhi upekkhā sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvoti ime asambhinnā padantarasambhedena vinā aggahitaggahaṇena gayhamānā cuddaseva ca sabhāvadhammā. Cuddasāti ca ukkaṃsaparicchedena vuttaṃ. Tañca kho paṭhamajjhānikamaggacittuppādavasena, dutiyajjhānike pana sammāsaṅkappābhāvato terasa, tatiyacatutthapañcamajjhānikesu pītisambojjhaṅgābhāvato dvādasa honti. “Sattatiṃsappabhedato”ti idampi ukkaṃsavaseneva vuttaṃ, avakaṃsato pana vuttanayena ekasmiṃ khaṇe chattiṃsa, pañcatiṃsa honti, catunnaṃ adhipatīnaṃ ekajjhaṃ anuppajjanato ekasmiṃ khaṇe ekasseva iddhipādassa sambhavoti dvattiṃsa ca hontīti veditabbaṃ.

Fourteen are unmixed: mindfulness, energy, zeal, mind, wisdom, faith, concentration, joy, tranquility, equanimity, right thought, right speech, right action, and right livelihood. These, being unmixed—when reckoned by taking up what has not been taken before, without being mixed with another term—are indeed just fourteen intrinsic phenomena. And the number fourteen is stated by way of the maximum limit. This, in turn, is by way of the arising of the first jhānic path-consciousness. In the second jhānic path-consciousness, however, due to the absence of right thought, there are thirteen. In the third, fourth, and fifth jhānic path-consciousnesses, due to the absence of the joy enlightenment factor, there are twelve. The phrase “from the thirty-seven divisions” is also stated only by way of the maximum. But by way of the minimum, according to the method already stated, in one moment there are thirty-six or thirty-five. And because the four dominances do not arise simultaneously, in one moment there is the possibility of only one basis of spiritual power; thus there are also thirty-two. This should be understood.

Sattatiṃsapabhedato [M 2.0493] kathanti āha “sakiccanipphādanato”tiādi, ekaccassa sabhāvato ekassāpi attano ānubhāvānurūpakāyānupassanāditaṃtaṃkiccasādhanatoti attho. Sarūpena ca vuttitoti abhedassa cittiddhipādādikassa sarūpeneva pavattanato ca.

To the question, ‘How are there thirty-seven by way of division?’ he said, “By the accomplishment of their respective functions,” and so on. The meaning is this: because a certain state, although being one by its intrinsic nature, accomplishes those respective functions, such as the contemplation of the body, in accordance with its own power. And it is stated ‘by its own nature’ because that which is undivided, such as the basis of spiritual power of mind and so forth, proceeds by its own nature alone.

Etthāti ñāṇadassanavisuddhiyaṃ. Kasmā pana bodhipakkhiyesu jhānakoṭṭhāso na gahito, nanu jhānarahito ariyamaggo natthīti? Saccaṃ natthi, tato eva na kho panetaṃ evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ “bodhipakkhiyesu jhānaṃ na gahita”nti lakkhaṇūpanijjhānalakkhaṇassa jhānassa maggaggahaṇeneva gahitattā. Tañhi sandhāya “yasmiṃ samaye lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāvetī”tiādi (dha. sa. 277, 343 ādayo) vuttaṃ. Ārammaṇūpanijjhānalakkhaṇassa panettha sambhavo eva natthi. Aparo nayo – kasmā pana bodhipakkhiyesu jhānakoṭṭhāso na gahito, nanu jhānarahito ariyamaggo natthi, na ca taṃ paṭipadā viya ekantapubbabhāgiyaṃ, nāpi ekaccapaṭisambhidā viya magganissando, atha kho maggacittuppādapariyāpanno, yato “lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāvetī”ti (dha. sa. 277, 343 ādayo) vuttaṃ, maggamaggaparivāradhammā ca bodhipakkhiyadhammāti? Vuccate – yaṃ tāva vuttaṃ jhānarahito ariyamaggo natthī”ti, tattha na ariyamaggasampayogamattena jhānassa bodhipakkhiyatā [V 2.0464] labbhati atippasaṅgato. Āhārādīnampi hi bodhipakkhiyatā āpajjeyyāti. Etena maggacittuppādapariyāpannatā bodhipakkhiyabhāvassa akāraṇanti dassitaṃ hoti.

Here, in the purification of knowledge and vision. But why is the jhāna-component not included among the factors of enlightenment? Is it not true that there is no Noble Path without jhāna? Truly, there is not. However, it should not be seen thus: “Jhāna is not included among the factors of enlightenment,” because jhāna which has the characteristic of absorption into the characteristics (lakkhaṇūpanijjhāna) is included by the very inclusion of the path. For it is with reference to this that it is said, “At the time when one develops the supramundane jhāna,” and so on. But here, there is no possibility at all for jhāna which has the characteristic of absorption into an object (ārammaṇūpanijjhāna). Another explanation: Why then is the jhāna-component not included among the factors of enlightenment? Is it not true that there is no Noble Path without jhāna; that it is not something exclusively preliminary like the path of practice, nor a result of the path like some analytical insights, but rather is encompassed within the arising of the path-consciousness, since it is said, “One develops the supramundane jhāna”; and that the path and the dhammas of its retinue are factors of enlightenment? It is said: As to what was first said, “there is no Noble Path without jhāna,” in that regard, jhāna does not obtain the status of a factor of enlightenment merely by its association with the Noble Path, due to over-extension.
