Of the perception of permanence: of the grasping of the state of stability.

Sārādānābhinivesassāti [M 2.0510] asāresu sāragahaṇābhinivesassa.

Of the insistence on taking the essential: of the insistence on grasping the essential in the unessential.

Saṃsayamicchāñāṇānaṃ vasena sammuyhanaṃ sammoho, so eva abhinivesoti sammohābhiniveso. Saṅkhāresu leṇatāṇabhāvaggahaṇaṃ ālayābhiniveso, atthato bhavanikanti.

Confusion by way of doubt and wrong knowledge is delusion. That very [delusion] is adherence; thus, it is delusion-adherence. The grasping of the state of formations as a shelter and a protector is the insistence on attachment, which in essence is the craving for becoming.

Yathā [V 2.0480] cittaṃ saṅkhāre muñcitvā vivaṭṭaṃ nibbānaṃ pakkhandati, tathā pavattanato saṅkhārupekkhā ca anulomañca “vivaṭṭānupassanā”ti vuttaṃ. Niviṭṭhabhāvena ogāḷhabhāvena pavattasaṃyojanādikilesā eva kilesābhiniveso. Nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ samādhinti vipassanāsamādhimāha.

Just as the mind, having released the formations, rushes toward Nibbāna, the turning away [from the round], so too, because of occurring in that manner, both equanimity towards formations and conformity [knowledge] are called 'contemplation leading to the turning away.' The defilements, such as the fetters, that have arisen by way of being established and immersed, are themselves the insistence on defilements. By 'the concentration pertaining to penetration,' it refers to insight concentration.

851. Asanivicakkaṃ asanimaṇḍalaṃ. Evaṃ pahānanti anuppattidhammatāpādanamāha. Kammakilesānaṃ, sabbesampi vā saṅkhārānaṃ khayaṃ nirodhaṃ gacchatīti khayagāmī, ariyamaggo. Lokuttaraggahaṇeneva siddhepi khayagāmiggahaṇaṃ vaṇṇabhaṇanatthaṃ. Samucchedappahānamevāti avadhāraṇaṃ nippariyāyataṃ upādāya. Tadatthānevāti samucchedappahānatthāneva. Tena vikkhambhanatadaṅgappahānānaṃ maggasambhāratamāha tehi vinā asijjhanato. Atha vā tadatthānevāti maggatthāneva. Tena tadatthatāya tesaṃ taṃkiccataṃ dasseti. Tenāha “tasmā”tiādi. Tamevatthaṃ upamāya dassetuṃ “paṭirājānaṃ vadhitvā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Yampi tato pubbe katanti yaṃ tatorajjappattito pubbe kataṃ paccantasādhanaduggaviddhaṃsanādi. Yathā idañcidañca raññā katantiyeva vuccati, evaṃ lokiyañāṇena sādhitānipi vikkhambhanatadaṅgappahānāni samucchedappahānavasena pavattassa maggassa kiccabhāvena vuccanti, tadatthatāya, tesaṃ taṃsantatipatitatāya ca maggassāti veditabbā.

851. The wheel of lightning is the circle of lightning. Thus, by 'abandonment,' he speaks of bringing about the state of having the nature of non-re-arising. The noble path goes to the destruction and cessation of kamma and defilements, or of all formations; therefore, it is 'leading to destruction.' Even though the meaning is established by the inclusion of 'supramundane,' the inclusion of 'leading to destruction' is for the purpose of speaking praise. The emphasis in 'by way of eradication-abandonment alone' is taken as non-figurative. 'For that purpose' means solely for the purpose of eradication-abandonment. By that, it indicates that abandonments by suppression and by substitution of opposites are requisites for the path, since it cannot be accomplished without them. Or, 'for that purpose' means for the sake of the path. By that, it shows their function for that path, because they are for that purpose. Therefore, he says, 'Therefore,' etc. To illustrate that very meaning by a simile, it is stated, 'Having slain the opposing king,' etc. And whatever was done before that means whatever was done before attaining kingship, such as conquering border regions and destroying strongholds. Just as it is said, 'This and that were done by the king,' so too, the abandonments by suppression and by substitution of opposites, although accomplished by mundane knowledge, are spoken of as a function of the path that proceeds by way of eradication-abandonment, because they are for the purpose of that path, and because of the path's falling into their continuity. Thus it should be understood.

852. Lokiyassa, lokiyā vā sacchikiriyā lokiyasacchikiriyā. Evaṃ lokuttarasacchikiriyā veditabbā. Lābhīmhīti lābhī amhi. Tathā vasīmhīti etthāpi. Paccakkhato ñāṇaphassenāti paccakkhato ārammaṇakaraṇasaṅkhātena ñāṇaphassanena. “Paccakkhato”ti ca iminā anumānato ārammaṇakaraṇaṃ nivatteti, “īdisamida”nti paccavekkhaṇavasena paccakkhato jānanaṃ hettha “ñāṇaphasso”ti adhippeto. Phassitāti ñāṇena phuṭṭhā.

852. Worldly realization is the realization of the worldly, or a worldly realization. Similarly, supramundane realization should be understood. 'I have gained' means 'I am a gainer.' Likewise, the same applies to 'I have mastery.' 'Through direct knowledge-contact' means by knowledge-contact that is reckoned as making an object direct. And by this term 'directly,' it excludes making an object by way of inference; here, knowing directly by way of reviewing 'it is of such a nature' is intended as 'knowledge-contact.' 'Contacted' means touched by knowledge.

Jhānamaggaphalāni [M 2.0511] viya attano santāne anuppādetvāpi tappaṭicchādakasammohaviddhaṃsanavasena tathāviddhaṃsanapavattañāṇaṃ aparappaccayañāṇaṃ.

Like the jhāna, path, and fruition states, even without producing them in one's own continuity, knowledge that proceeds by way of destroying the delusion that conceals them, and by way of such destruction, is knowledge independent of others.

Passanto paccakkhato jānanto. Amatogadhanti amatapariyāpannaṃ, amatasaṅkhātanti attho.

Seeing, knowing directly. 'Immersed in the Deathless' means included in the Deathless, reckoned as the Deathless; this is the meaning.

Sotāpattimaggo paṭhamaṃ nibbānadassanato dassanaṃ, tena dassanena sacchikiriyā dassanasacchikiriyā. Kiñcāpi gotrabhuñāṇaṃ tato paṭhamataraṃ nibbānaṃ passati, ālambanakaraṇato [V 2.0481] disvā kattabbakiccākaraṇato pana na dassananti vuccati. Sā duvidhāpīti sā dassanabhāvanāvasena duvidhāpi sacchikiriyā. Dassanabhāvanāvasenāti dassanamaggabhāvanāmaggavasena. Tena amaggavasena pavattanibbānassa paccavekkhaṇasacchikiriyaṃ nivatteti. Nibbānassāti pana iminā maggaphalesu paccavekkhaṇasacchikiriyaṃ. Imassa ñāṇassāti imassa yathādhigatassa lokuttarañāṇassa.

The stream-entry path is called 'seeing' because it is the first seeing of Nibbāna; the realization by that seeing is 'seeing-realization.' Although the change-of-lineage knowledge sees Nibbāna even before that, it is not called 'seeing' because, though it sees by taking it as an object, it does not perform the function that should be performed. The phrase 'That is also twofold' means: that realization is also twofold by way of seeing and development. 'By way of seeing and development' means by way of the path of seeing and the path of development. By that, it excludes the realization-by-reviewing of Nibbāna that occurs by way of what is not the path. But by this word 'of Nibbāna,' it excludes the realization-by-reviewing of the paths and fruits. 'Of this knowledge' means of this supramundane knowledge as it has been attained.

853. Abhimatāti adhippetā. Bhāvanā nāma uppādanā, santānaparibhāvanā cāti tadubhayaṃ dassento “lokiyāna”ntiādimāha. Yadaggena hi lokiyā kusalādayo uppāditā, vaḍḍhitā ca, tadaggenassa sīlabhāvanā, kāyabhāvanā, cittabhāvanā, paññābhāvanā ca lokiyā nipphāditā hoti, tāya ca santānopi paribhāvitoti. Tāsu lokiyalokuttarabhāvanāsu idha ñāṇadassanavisuddhikathāyaṃ lokuttarabhāvanā adhippetā, na itarā tassā sambhārabhāvato. Catubbidhampetaṃ ñāṇanti etaṃ catubbidhampi ariyamaggañāṇaṃ lokuttarāni sammāvācādibhedāni sīlādīni uppādeti. Kathaṃ? Sahajātādipaccayatāya. Sīlādīnīti ettha ādi-saddena samādhissa gahaṇaṃ, na paññāya. Na hi tadeva taṃ uppādeti, maggacittuppādo pana uppādeti. Tadantogadhabhāvā sammāsaṅkappo. So hi pañcakkhandhasaṅgahitoti vadanti. Sīlādīnīti vā phalasīlādīnampi gahaṇanti paññāyapi gahaṇaṃ yujjatiyeva. Sahajātapaccayāditāyāti ettha ādi-saddena anantarapaccayāditāyapi saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Tehi ca santānaṃ vāsetīti tehi samucchindanapaṭipassambhanavasena pavattehi lokuttarehi sīlādīhi ariyapuggalo attano santānaṃ paribhāveti. Yaṃ nissāya parāvuttīti vadanti. Yathā pariññattayampi [M 2.0512] pahānattayampi maggañāṇassa kiccanti vuttaṃ pariyāyena, na evamidha. Idha pana lokuttarabhāvanāva assa maggañāṇassa kiccaṃ. Na hettha bhāvanāya pariyāyo labbhatīti avadhāraṇaṃ. Tena lokiyabhāvanaṃ nivatteti.

853. 'Abhimatā' means intended. 'Bhāvanā' is both production and perfuming the continuum, and to show both of these, the text says, “worldly,” etc. For to the extent that worldly wholesome qualities, etc., are produced and developed, to that extent the worldly cultivation of morality, cultivation of the body, cultivation of the mind, and cultivation of wisdom are accomplished for that person, and by that, the continuum is also perfumed. Among these worldly and supramundane cultivations, here in the discussion on the purification of knowledge and vision, supramundane cultivation is intended, not the other, because it serves as a prerequisite. This fourfold knowledge—that is, this fourfold knowledge of the Noble Path—produces supramundane morality, etc., which are differentiated as Right Speech, etc. How? By way of the co-nascence condition, etc. Here, in 'morality, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes concentration, but not wisdom. For that knowledge itself does not produce it, wisdom; however, the arising of the path-consciousness produces it. Because of its inclusion within that, Right Intention produces it, for they say it is included in the wisdom aggregate. Alternatively, by 'morality, etc.,' the inclusion of the morality, etc., of the fruit is also meant; therefore, the inclusion of wisdom is indeed appropriate. Here in 'by way of the co-nascence condition, etc.,' the word 'etc.' should be understood to also include being a contiguity condition, etc. And by “by these it perfumes the continuum,” it is meant that by these supramundane instances of morality, etc., which proceed by way of eradication and tranquilization, the noble person perfumes their own continuum. They say that, depending on this, there is a turning back. Just as it was said figuratively that the threefold full understanding and the threefold abandoning are functions of the Path Knowledge, it is not so here. Here, however, only supramundane cultivation is the function of this Path Knowledge. The emphasis is made because here no figurative meaning for 'cultivation' is found. By that emphasis, it excludes worldly cultivation.

Evaṃ sarūpeneva āgatāyāti “cittaṃ bhāvaya”nti samādhi viya cittasīsena anāgantvā “paññaṃ bhāvaya”nti evaṃ sarūpeneva āgatāya paññāya. Yaṃ vuttaṃ uddesavasena. Ettāvatā taṃ vitthāritaṃ hoti. Ayañca pañho vissajjito hotīti sambandho.

Thus, 'by that which has come in its own form' means: by wisdom that has come in its own form as 'develop wisdom,' not having come under the heading of 'mind' in the way that concentration does, which is expressed as 'develop the mind.' What was stated by way of summary has, by this much, been expanded. And this question has been answered—such is the connection.

Ñāṇadassanavisuddhiniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Exposition of the Purification of Knowledge and Vision is completed.

Iti bāvīsatimaparicchedavaṇṇanā.

Thus, the commentary on the twenty-second chapter.

23. Paññābhāvanānisaṃsaniddesavaṇṇanā

23. Commentary on the Exposition of the Benefits of the Development of Wisdom

Ānisaṃsapakāsanāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Elucidation of the Benefits

854. Anekasatānisaṃsā [M 2.0513][V 2.0482] sāvakabodhiādivipulodātaguṇavisesāvahattā. Vitthāratoti nayadassanaṃ akatvā “ayampi paññābhāvanāya ānisaṃso, ayampī”ti anupadadassanavasena vitthārato pakāsetuṃ na sukaraṃ atibahubhāvato. Assāti paññābhāvanāya. Nānākilesaviddhaṃsananti sakkāyadiṭṭhivicikicchādivasena nānāvidhānaṃ kilesadhammānaṃ tadaṅgādivasena pajahanaṃ. Ariyaphalarasānubhavananti sotāpattiphalādiphalasukhapaṭisaṃvedanaṃ.

854. The development of wisdom has many hundreds of benefits because it brings about special qualities that are vast and pure, beginning with the disciple's enlightenment. To elaborate: because they are so numerous, it is not easy to explain them in detail by way of showing them sequentially, saying, “This too is a benefit of the development of wisdom, and this too,” without presenting a methodology. 'Of this' means of the development of wisdom. 'The destruction of various defilements' is the abandoning, by way of temporary suppression and so forth, of various kinds of defilements, such as identity-view, doubt, and so on. 'The experience of the taste of the noble fruit' is the experiencing of the bliss of the fruits, beginning with the fruit of stream-entry.

Nānākilesaviddhaṃsanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Destruction of Various Defilements

855. “Ariyaphalarasānubhavana”nti eteneva kilesānaṃ paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ dīpīyatīti “ariyamaggakkhaṇe”ti visesavacanaṃ, tabbhāvabhāvato vā. Siddhe hi samucchedappahāne paṭippassaddhippahānaṃ siddhameva hotīti.

855. By this very phrase, 'the experience of the taste of the noble fruit,' the abandoning of defilements by pacification is shown. Therefore, the specific statement 'at the moment of the noble path' is made. Or, it is because of the existence of the latter state, pacification, due to the existence of the former, eradication. For when abandonment by eradication is accomplished, abandonment by pacification is indeed accomplished.

Bhīmavegānupatitāti sakalaṃ lokaṃ bhindantena viya bhīmena bhayānakena vegena sahasā patitā. Siluccayeti pabbate selaputhule. Satejujjalamaṇḍaloti saradakālasamiddhena attano tejasā samujjaladuddikkhamaṇḍalo. Vadhabandhanādiduggatiparipakkilesādijātiādisabbānatthavidhāyakaṃ. Sandiṭṭhikanti paccakkhabhūtaṃ. Jaññāti jāneyya. Idhāti imissaṃ paññābhāvanāyaṃ.

'Fallen with terrible velocity' means: fallen upon suddenly with a terrible, dreadful velocity, as if shattering the entire world. 'A great rock' means: large rocks on a mountain. 'With a radiant, blazing circle' means: having a circle that is intensely blazing and difficult to look at with its own radiance, perfected in the autumn season. 'That which is the producer of all non-benefit, such as killing, binding, etc.; affliction in bad destinations, etc.; birth, etc.' 'Directly visible' means: become manifest. 'One should know' means: one should know. 'Here' means: in this development of wisdom.

Phalasamāpattikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Attainment of Fruition

856. Ariyassa [V 2.0483] maggassa phalaṃ ariyaphalaṃ, ariyañca taṃ visuddhattā phalañcātipi ariyaphalaṃ, tassa raso, paṭippassaddhivimuttisukhaṃ, anubhavanaṃ nibbānārammaṇassa tassa paṭisevanaṃ. Tatrāti tesu dvīsu ākāresu. Assāti ariyaphalassa.

856. The fruit of the noble path is the noble fruit. And it is also the noble fruit because it is noble due to its purity, and it is a fruit. Its taste is the bliss of pacification and liberation. The experience is the partaking of that which has Nibbāna as its object. 'Therein' means: in those two aspects. 'Of this' means: of the noble fruit.

857. Saṃyojanesu [M 2.0514] pahīnesu sabbepi kilesā pahīnāyeva hontīti saṃyojanānaṃyeva gahaṇaṃ. Saṃyojanappahānamattameva ariyamaggassa phalaṃ nāma, na aññaṃ kiñci atthantaraṃ vipākabhūtanti adhippāyo. Tenāha “phalaṃ nāma na koci añño dhammo atthī”ti. Ke panetaṃ vadantīti? Andhakādayo. Te hi “arahattaṃ arahattanti, āvuso, vuccati…pe… mohakkhayo”ti (saṃ. ni. 4.315) suttapadassa atthaṃ aññathā gahetvā nippariyāyato “arahattaṃ nāma kiñci natthi, kilesappahānameva tathā voharīyatī”ti vadantā sesaphalepi paṭikkhipanti. Idaṃ suttampīti paṭisambhidāmaggapāḷimāha. Pakaṭṭho ukkaṭṭho yogoti payogo, ariyamaggo, payoganimittaṃ jātakilesānaṃ paṭippassaddhi payogapaṭippassaddhi. Yā pana ariyamaggassa bhāvitattā labbhamānāpi yassā vipākapaññāya nippajjamānāya nippajjati, sā paṭippassaddhiyaṃ nipphādetabbāyaṃ paññāti paṭippassaddhipaññāti vuttā. Sammādiṭṭhi micchādiṭṭhiyā vuṭṭhātīti sammādiṭṭhiyā ujuvipaccanīkadassanavasena vatvā tadaññatopi vuṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ “tadanuvattakakilesehī”ti vuttaṃ, tassā micchādiṭṭhiyā sampayogato, upanissayato ca anuvattakakilesehi. Tena tadekaṭṭhappahānamāha. Khandhehīti tadanuvattakakkhandhehi, tāya micchādiṭṭhiyā sampayuttakkhandhehi ceva tappaccayā āyatiṃ uppajjanakkhandhehi cāti attho. Bahiddhā ca sabbanimittehīti yathāvuttakilesakkhandhehi bahiddhābhūtehi vipassanāya gocarabhūtehi sabbasaṅkhāranimittehi.

857. When the fetters are abandoned, all defilements are indeed abandoned; thus, only the fetters are mentioned. The mere abandoning of the fetters is called the fruit of the noble path; there is no other distinct phenomenon which is a result. This is the intended meaning. Therefore, it is said: “There is no other phenomenon called fruit.” But who says this? The Andhakas and others. They, indeed, misinterpreting the meaning of the Sutta passage: “Arahantship, friends, is called… the destruction of delusion” (Saṃ. Ni. 4.315), saying that ultimately there is no such thing as Arahantship, but only the abandoning of defilements is conventionally spoken of in that way, and thus they reject the other fruits as well. By the words 'This Sutta also,' it refers to the Paṭisambhidāmagga Pāḷi. Payoga means excellent, supreme effort; it is the noble path. The pacification of arisen defilements on account of this application is 'pacification by application' (payogapaṭippassaddhi). But that pacification by application, though obtainable because the noble path has been developed, is produced when a certain resultant wisdom is being produced. That resultant wisdom is called 'wisdom of pacification' (paṭippassaddhipaññā) because it is the wisdom in the pacification that is to be produced. “Right view emerges from wrong view”—having stated it by way of showing the direct opposite, and to show emergence from other things as well, it is said, “from the defilements that follow it,” meaning, from the defilements that follow that wrong view by way of association and by way of supporting condition. By this, it speaks of abandoning those that have a common basis. “By the aggregates” means from the aggregates that follow it, that is, both from the aggregates associated with that wrong view and from the aggregates that will arise in the future on account of that as a condition; this is the meaning. “And by all external signs” means by all signs of formations which are external to the aforementioned defilements and aggregates and which are the objects of insight.

Evaṃ maggakiccaṃ dassetvā idāni tassa vasena phalaṃ dassetuṃ “tampayogapaṭippassaddhattā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tampayogapaṭippassaddhattāti tassa ajjhattabahiddhā vuṭṭhānādipayogassa paṭippassaddhattā. Maggo hi nimittato, pavattato ca vuṭṭhahanto kilese pajahatīti attano khaṇe taṃ payogaṃ karoti nāma, phalakkhaṇe panassa so payogo paṭippassaddho vūpasanto nāma hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “tampayogapaṭippassaddhattā”ti. Uppajjatīti maggānantaraṃ [V 2.0484] dvikkhattuṃ vā tikkhattuṃ vā uppajjati. Phalasamāpattikāle pana bahukkhattuṃ, nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa dvikkhattuṃ uppajjati. Sabbampi yathāvuttapayogapaṭippassaddhinimittaṃ uppajjanato “tampayogapaṭippassaddhattā uppajjatī”ti vuttaṃ. Maggassetaṃ phalanti yathāvuttā vipākā sammādiṭṭhi nāma, etaṃ ariyamaggassa [M 2.0515] phalanti veditabbaṃ. Vitthāretabbanti “sotāpattimaggakkhaṇe abhiniropanaṭṭhena sammāsaṅkappo micchāsaṅkappā”tiādinā (paṭi. ma. 1.63) saṅkappādivasena, sesamaggavasena ca vitthārato veditabbaṃ.

Having thus shown the function of the path, now, in order to show the fruit by means of it, the passage beginning with 'because of the pacification of that application' was stated. Therein, 'because of the pacification of that application' means because of the pacification of that application of emerging from the internal and external, and so forth. For the path, while emerging from the sign and from the process, abandons the defilements; thus, in its own moment, it is said to make that application. At the moment of fruition, however, that application of it is said to be pacified and calmed. Therefore, it was stated, 'because of the pacification of that application.' As for 'it arises': it arises two or three times immediately after the path. However, at the time of fruition attainment, it arises many times; for one emerging from cessation, it arises twice. Because it all arises on account of the pacification of the aforementioned application as its cause, it is stated, 'it arises because of the pacification of that application.' As for 'this is the fruit of the path': the aforementioned resultant right view is what is meant; this should be understood as the fruit of the noble path. As for 'it should be elaborated': it should be understood in detail by way of intention, etc., and by way of the remaining paths, according to the passage beginning with 'At the moment of the stream-entry path, right intention in the sense of directing [the mind] emerges from wrong intention,' etc. (Paṭis. I 63).

Cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, ime dhammā appamāṇārammaṇāti appamāṇārammaṇatāya maggehi nibbisesatāya. Tathā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaṅkhāto mahaggato dhammo nirodhato vuṭṭhānavelāyaṃ appamāṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayoti ariyaphalassa anantarapaccayatāya ca dīpanāti evamādīnipi ettha ariyaphalassa sabhāvadhammabhāvena atthitāya sādhakāni, na yathādassitapaṭisambhidāmaggapāḷiyevāti adhippāyo.

The passage 'And the four fruits of recluseship, these states have an immeasurable object' is cited because of the fruits' having an immeasurable object and being without distinction from the paths. Likewise, the declaration that 'the sublime state reckoned as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, at the time of emerging from cessation, is a condition for the immeasurable state by way of an immediate condition' is also made because of the noble fruit's being an immediate condition. Therefore, these and similar passages are, in this context, proofs for the existence of the noble fruit as an intrinsic state; it is not only the Paṭisambhidāmagga Pāḷi as shown that is a proof. This is the intention.

858. Phalasamāpattiyanti phalapavattisaṅkhātāya samāpattiyaṃ. Assāti ariyaphalassa. Sarūpakattukāraṇākāraṭṭhitivuṭṭhānānantaravasena idaṃ pañhākammaṃ.

858. “In the attainment of fruition” means in the attainment reckoned as the occurrence of fruition. “Of it” refers to the noble fruit. This question is posed by way of its intrinsic nature, agent, cause, mode, duration, emergence, and immediate succession.

859. Ariyaphalassa nirodhe appanāti ariyassa phalajhānassa nibbāne ārammaṇabhūte appanākārena pavatti.

859. “The absorption of the noble fruit in Cessation (Nibbāna)” means the continuous occurrence by way of absorption of the noble fruit-jhāna in Nibbāna, which has become its object.

860. Sabbepi puthujjanāti jhānasamāpattilābhinopi puthujjanā na samāpajjanti, pageva itare. Ariyā sabbepi phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjantīti kāmaṃ sāmaññajotanā, sā pana visesaniviṭṭhāyeva hoti. Adhigatattāti pana hetukittanaṃ. Uparimānampi heṭṭhimāya lokiyasamāpattiyā viya samāpajjanaṃ sādhentaṃ viya ṭhitanti taṃ nivattento “uparimā panā”tiādimāha. Tattha uparimāti sakadāgāmiādayo. Heṭṭhimanti sotāpattiphalādiṃ. Na samāpajjanti satipi adhigatatte. Kasmāti ce? Kāraṇamāha “puggalantarabhāvūpagamanena paṭippassaddhattā”ti. Etena uparimo ariyo heṭṭhimaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjati attanā adhigatattā, yathā taṃ lokiyasamāpattinti, evaṃ pavattaṃ hetuṃ byabhicāreti. Na hi lokiyajjhānesu puggalantarabhāvūpagamanaṃ nāma atthi visesābhāvato. Idha pana asamugghāṭitakammakilesanirodhanena [V 2.0485] puthujjanehi viya sotāpannassa, sotāpannādīhi sakadāgāmiādīnaṃ puggalantarabhāvūpagamanaṃ atthi. Yato heṭṭhimā heṭṭhimā phaladhammā uparūpari maggadhammehi [M 2.0516] nivattitā paṭipakkhehi viya abhibhūtā appavattidhammataṃyeva āpannā. Tenāha “paṭippassaddhattā”ti.

860. “Even all ordinary worldlings”—even ordinary worldlings who have obtained jhāna-attainment do not enter absorption, let alone others. “Noble ones all attain fruition-attainment”—this is indeed a general statement, but it is specifically qualified. “Because of having attained” is a statement of the reason. To refute the notion that the higher ones attain the lower fruition-attainment in the same way as a mundane attainment, he said, “but the higher ones…” and so forth. Herein, “higher ones” refers to once-returners and so on. “The lower” refers to the fruit of stream-entry and so on. They do not enter absorption, even though they have attained it. Why is that? The reason is given: “due to pacification by transitioning to another individual state.” By this, the argument that “a higher noble one attains the lower fruition-attainment because it has been attained by oneself, just as with a mundane attainment,” is refuted. For in mundane jhānas, there is no such thing as transitioning to another individual state, due to the absence of difference. Here, however, by means of the cessation of kamma and defilements that have not yet been uprooted, there is a transition to another individual state for the once-returners and so on from the stream-enterers and so on, just as there is for the stream-enterer from the worldlings. Since the lower and lower fruition states are reverted by the higher and higher path states, they are subdued as if by opposing forces and thus attain only a state of non-occurrence. Therefore, it is said, “due to pacification.”

Apica kusalakiriyapavatti nāma aññādisī, vipākapavatti ca aññādisī, anantaraphalattā ca lokuttarakusalānaṃ heṭṭhimato uparimo bhavantaragato viya hoti. Taṃtaṃphalavaseneva hi ariyānaṃ sotāpannādināmalābho. Te sace aññaphalasamaṅginopi honti, sotāpannādināmampi tesaṃ avaṭṭhitaṃ siyā, tena tena jhānena gahitapaṭisandhiko viyāti tassa tassa ariyassa taṃ taṃ phalaṃ bhavaṅgasadisanti na uparimassa heṭṭhimaphalasamaṅgitāya lesopi sambhavati, kuto tassa samāpajjananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Heṭṭhimā ca uparimanti heṭṭhimā ca sotāpannādayo ariyā uparimaṃ sakadāgāmiphalādiṃ na samāpajjantīti sambandho. Tattha kāraṇamāha “anadhigatattā”ti. Na hi anadhigatasamāpattiṃ samāpajjituṃ sakkā.

Furthermore, the occurrence of wholesome and functional actions is of one nature, and the occurrence of resultants is of another nature. And due to the immediate fruit of supramundane wholesome states, one in a higher stage from a lower one is like someone who has gone to another existence. For it is precisely by the power of the respective fruits that the noble ones gain the names 'Stream-enterer' and so on. If they were also endowed with another fruit, their name 'Stream-enterer', etc., would be established. Just as for one who has taken rebirth through a particular jhāna, that respective fruit is like the bhavaṅga for that respective noble one. Therefore, for one in a higher stage, there is not even a trace of the state of being endowed with a lower fruit; how then could there be the attainment of it? This should be understood. As for the phrase 'The lower and the higher', the connection is: the lower noble ones, such as Stream-enterers, do not attain the higher, such as the fruit of Once-returning, etc. Therein, the reason is stated: 'Because it has not been attained.' For indeed, it is not possible to enter into an attainment that has not been attained.

“Attano attanoyeva pana phalaṃ samāpajjantī”ti iminā sabbepi ariyā attano attano phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjantīti atthe āpanne tattha kesañci matibhedaṃ dassetuṃ “keci panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ete hi samādhismiṃ paripūrakārinoti yasmā hi te “uparimā dve”ti vuttā anāgāmino, arahanto ca samādhismiṃ paripūrakārino, itare pana sīlesu paripūrakārino, tasmā dve eva phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjantīti. Na hi samādhipāripūriyā vinā samāpattivaḷañjanaṃ sambhavatīti adhippāyo. Tanti “samādhismiṃ paripūrakārino”ti tehi vuttakāraṇaṃ. Akāraṇamevāti ayuttiyeva. Kasmāti ce? Āha “puthujjanassāpī”tiādi. Tassattho – sabbaso asamucchinnakilesassa puthujjanassāpi attanā paṭiladdhalokiyasamāpattisamāpajjanaṃ labbhati, kimaṅgaṃ pana samucchinnekaccakilesānaṃ heṭṭhimānaṃ ariyānaṃ, tasmā tesaṃ samādhismiṃ aparipūrakāritā attano phalasamāpattiṃ asamāpajjanassa akāraṇanti. Yutticintā nāma pāḷianāruḷhe atthe yuttā, ayaṃ panattho pāḷiāruḷhoti kāraṇāpadese anādarakaraṇamukhena pāḷiṃ dassento “kiñcetthā”tiādimāha. Sotāpattimaggapaṭilābhatthāyāti sotāpattimaggassa samadhigamāya. Sotāpattiphalasamāpattatthāyāti sotāpattiphalasamāpattiyā samāpajjanatthaṃ. Esa nayo sesesupi.

When, by this statement, "They attain their own respective fruit," the meaning is established that all noble ones attain their own respective fruition attainment, the passage beginning with "But some..." is stated to show that on this matter, some have a different opinion. The reason is: "For these are fulfillers in concentration." Because those called "the two higher ones," namely the non-returners and the arahants, are fulfillers in concentration, while the others are fulfillers in virtue, therefore, only those two attain fruition attainment. The intention is that, indeed, without the fulfillment of concentration, the practice of attainment is not possible. That statement, "fulfillers in concentration," is the reason given by them. "It is not a reason at all" means it is simply illogical. If it is asked, "Why?" he said, "Even for a worldling..." and so on. Its meaning is this: Even for a worldling whose defilements are not cut off at all, it is possible to enter a mundane meditative attainment that has been obtained by oneself. How much more so for the lower noble ones, some of whose defilements have been utterly eradicated? Therefore, their not being fulfillers in concentration is not a reason for their not attaining their own fruition attainment. Logical reasoning is appropriate for a meaning not established in the Pāli, but this meaning is established in the Pāli. Therefore, showing the Pāli by way of disregarding the presentation of reasons, he said, "What is here..." and so on. "For the sake of obtaining the stream-entry path" means for the acquisition of the stream-entry path. "For the sake of the fruition-attainment of stream-entry" means for the purpose of entering the fruition-attainment of stream-entry. This is the method in the remaining cases as well.

Ettha [M 2.0517][V 2.0486] ca “suññatavihārasamāpattatthāya animittavihārasamāpattatthāyā”tiādinā sarūpato uddhaṭattā tato pubbe āgatā maggaphalavārā appaṇihitavasena vuttā. Tattha anattānupassanāmukhena, aniccānupassanāmukhena ca pavattānaṃ phalasamāpattīnaṃ purecarā gotrabhudhammā navadasabhāvena vuttāti veditabbā. “Sotāpattiphalasamāpattatthāyā”tiādinā pana catūsupi phalesu ekasadisaṃ desanāya āgatattā sotāpannasakadāgāminopi attano phalaṃ samāpajjantīti viññāyati. Maggānantaraphalavasena taṃ vuttanti ca na sakkā vattuṃ vipassanāvasena dasannaṃ gotrabhudhammānaṃ dassanavasena desanāya āraddhattā, maggavāreneva ca tadatthasiddhito. Na ca maggānantaraṃ phalaṃ “phalasamāpattī”ti vuccati visuṃ parikammābhāvato. Tasmā phalasamāpattivacaneneva sotāpannādīnampi phalasamāpattisamāpajjanaṃ siddhaṃ. Tenāha “tasmā”tiādi.

And here, since the phrases 'for the purpose of the attainment of the dwelling in emptiness,' 'for the purpose of the attainment of the signless dwelling,' and so on, are extracted in their own form, the sections on path and fruition that came before are said to be by way of the undirected. Therein, it should be known that the change-of-lineage states that are forerunners to the fruition attainments—which occur by way of the contemplation of non-self as the entrance and the contemplation of impermanence as the entrance—are spoken of as being the ninth and tenth. However, by means of 'for the purpose of the attainment of the fruition of stream-entry,' and so on, since the teaching has come in the same way for all four fruitions, it is understood that stream-enterers and once-returners also attain their own fruition. And it cannot be said that this is spoken of by way of the fruition immediately following the path, because the teaching was undertaken by way of showing the ten change-of-lineage states through insight, and because that meaning is accomplished by the path section itself. And the fruition immediately following the path is not called 'fruition attainment' because of the absence of separate preliminary work. Therefore, by the very utterance of 'fruition attainment,' the attainment of fruition attainment by stream-enterers and others is established. For that reason, he said, 'therefore,' and so on.

861. Payojanampi tadatthāya paṭipattiyā kāraṇaṃ hoti tannimittaṃ paṭipajjanatoti “kasmā samāpajjantī”ti kāraṇaṃ pucchitvā “diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārattha”nti payojanaṃ vissajjitaṃ. Kasmāti vā sampadāne nissakkavacanaṃ, kissāti vuttaṃ hoti. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāratthanti diṭṭheva dhamme kilesadarathapariḷāhavūpasamena santena sukhavihārena viharaṇatthaṃ. Satipi vipākabhāve parikammena vinā anuppajjanato phalasamāpattidhammānaṃ tassa tassa ariyassa rucivaseneva pavatti, yato nesaṃ sādhipatitāti āha “addhāna…pe… samāpajjantī”ti.

861. The purpose is also a reason for the practice for that purpose, because one practices on account of that. Thus, having asked the reason, 'Why do they attain it?', the purpose was answered as 'for the sake of a pleasant dwelling in the here and now.' Or, the word 'kasmā' is an ablative word in the dative sense; it means 'for what?' 'For the sake of a pleasant dwelling in the here and now' means for the purpose of dwelling in this very life with a peaceful, pleasant dwelling, through the calming of the distress and fever of defilements. Although they are resultant states, because they do not arise without preliminary work, the occurrence of the fruition attainment states is only by way of the inclination of each respective noble one. Because they have a dominant influence, he said, 'Surely... they attain.'

862. Dvīhi ākārehīti dvīhi kāraṇehi. Yathā hi lokiyajjhānānaṃ samadhigamo sampayogasamaṅgibhāvena sijjhamāno pahānaṅgasamatikkamamukhena vuccati tathā samadhigantabbattā, evaṃ phalasamāpattipi nibbānamanasikārena sijjhamānā tadaññārammaṇāmanasikāramukhena vuccati sabbasaṅkhārato vinivaṭṭitamānasatāvasena samijjhanato. Tenāha “nibbānato”tiādi. Udayabbayañāṇādiñāṇaparamparavasena hi sabbaphalacittaṃ saṅkhārato sabbaso nibbinnavirattacittassa tato vinissaṭanibbānārammaṇaṃ pavattati. Evaṃ pavattamānañca taṃ nibbānato aññassa ārammaṇassa amanasikārā, nibbānassa ca manasikārā pavattatīti vuccati.

862. “In two ways” means for two reasons. Just as the attainment of mundane jhānas, being achieved through the presence of associated factors, is spoken of in terms of overcoming the factors to be abandoned, because it is to be attained in that way, so too the fruition attainment, being achieved through attention to Nibbāna, is spoken of in terms of non-attention to other objects, because it is achieved by way of a mind turned away from all formations. Thus, he said, “from Nibbāna,” etc. For, through the sequence of knowledges such as the knowledge of arising and passing away, all fruition consciousness, belonging to one whose mind is altogether disenchanted with and dispassionate towards formations, occurs with Nibbāna as its object, having emerged therefrom. And, occurring in this way, it is said to occur through non-attention to any object other than Nibbāna, and through attention to Nibbāna.

Animittāya [M 2.0518] cetovimuttiyāti animittavimokkhadvayāya phalasamāpattiyā, aniccānupassanāmukhena [V 2.0487] vā samāpajjitabbāya phalasamāpattiyā. Samāpattiyāti samāpajjanatthāya. Sabbanimittānanti rūpādisabbasaṅkhāranimittānaṃ. Amanasikāroti ādīnavato disvā vissaṭṭhatāya anāvajjanaṃ asamannāhāro. Animittāya ca dhātuyā manasikāroti sabbasaṅkhāranimittābhāvato animittāya. Kehici paccayehi na saṅkhatattā ca asaṅkhatāti laddhanāmāya asaṅkhatāya dhātuyā phalasamāpattisahajātena manasikārena manasikaraṇaṃ, tassā vā dhātuyā phalasamāpatticittasaṅkhāte manasikaraṇaṃ.

“Through the signless liberation of mind” means through the fruition attainment that follows upon the signless liberation, or through the fruition attainment to be entered by way of contemplation of impermanence. “Attainment” means for the purpose of attaining. “All signs” refers to all signs of formations, such as form, etc. “Non-attention” means not adverting and not applying the mind, because they are abandoned after seeing their danger. “Attention to the signless element” means attention to the element that is signless due to the absence of all signs of formations. And it means attention to the unconditioned element, which has obtained the name “unconditioned” because it is not conditioned by any causes, through the attention co-arisen with fruition attainment, or the making of that element an object in the mind designated as fruition attainment consciousness.

863. Udayabbayādivasenāti udayabbayabhaṅgabhayatupaṭṭhānādivasena pavattanakānaṃ navannampi ñāṇānaṃ byāpāraṃ vadati. Tenāha “pavattānupubbavipassanassā”ti. Saṅkhārārammaṇagotrabhuñāṇānantaranti saṅkhārārammaṇassa “vodāna”nti laddhanāmassa gotrabhuñāṇassa anantaraṃ. Kasmā panettha gotrabhuñāṇaṃ maggañāṇapurecārikaṃ viya nibbānārammaṇaṃ na hotīti? Phaladhammānaṃ aniyyānikabhāvato. Ariyamaggadhammā eva hi niyyānikā. Vuttañhetaṃ “katame dhammā niyyānikā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā”ti (dha. sa. 1295, 1609). Tasmā ekantena niyyānikasabhāvassa ubhatovuṭṭhānabhāvena pavattamānassa maggañāṇassa anantarapaccayabhūtena ñāṇena nimittato vuṭṭhiteneva bhavitabbanti tassa nibbānārammaṇatā yuttā, na pana ariyamaggassa bhāvitattā tassa vipākabhāvena pavattamānānaṃ kilesānaṃ asamucchindanato aniyyānikattā avuṭṭhānasabhāvānaṃ phalañāṇānaṃ purecārikañāṇassa kadācipi nibbānārammaṇatā ubhayattha anulomañāṇānaṃ atulyākārato. Ariyamaggavīthiyañhi anulomañāṇāni anibbiddhapubbānaṃ thūlathūlalobhakkhandhādīnaṃ sātisayaṃ padālanena lokiyañāṇesu ukkaṃsapāramippattāni maggañāṇānuguṇāni uppajjanti. Phalasamāpattivīthiyaṃ pana tāni tena tena maggena tesaṃ tesaṃ kilesānaṃ samucchinnattā tattha kilesavikkhambhane nirussukkāni kevalaṃ ariyānaṃ phalasamāpattisukhasamaṅgibhāvassa parikammamattāni hutvā uppajjantīti na tesaṃ kutoci vuṭṭhānasambhavo, yato nesaṃ pariyosānañāṇaṃ saṅkhāranimittavuṭṭhānato nibbānārammaṇaṃ siyā.

863. “By way of rise and fall, etc.” refers to the function of all nine knowledges that occur by way of the knowledge of rise and fall, dissolution, the appearance of terror, etc. Hence it is said, “for one whose insight occurs successively.” “Immediately after the change-of-lineage knowledge with formations as object” means immediately after the change-of-lineage knowledge that has formations as its object and has obtained the name “purification.” But why is it that here the change-of-lineage knowledge does not have Nibbāna as its object, like the one that precedes the path knowledge does? Because the fruition states are not leading-out. For only the noble path states are leading-out. And this was said: “Which states are leading-out? The four paths, unincluded” (Dhs. 1295, 1609). Therefore, since the knowledge that is the immediately contiguous condition for the path knowledge—which itself occurs by way of emerging from both and has an absolutely leading-out nature—must have emerged from the sign, it is appropriate for that preceding knowledge to have Nibbāna as its object. But the preliminary knowledge preceding the fruition knowledges—which occur as the result of the noble path's development, are not leading-out because they do not eradicate defilements, and are by nature non-emergent—can never have Nibbāna as its object, because the conformity knowledges in both cases are dissimilar in their mode of operation. For in the noble path process, the conformity knowledges arise in conformity with the path knowledge, having attained the highest excellence among worldly knowledges by excessively piercing the gross masses of greed, etc., which had not been pierced before. But in the fruition-attainment process, since those respective defilements have been eradicated by the respective paths, these knowledges arise merely as a preparation for the noble ones' state of being endowed with the happiness of fruition attainment, being unconcerned with the suppression of defilements there. Thus, there is no possibility of emergence for them from anywhere, by which their concluding knowledge could have Nibbāna as its object by emerging from the sign of formations.

Evañca [M 2.0519] katvā “sekkhassa attano phalasamāpattivaḷañjanatthāya udayabbayādivasena saṅkhāre sammasantassa vipassanāñāṇānupubbiyā phalameva uppajjati, na maggo”ti idañca aṭṭhakathāvacanaṃ samatthitaṃ hoti. Tenāha “sekkhassāpi phalameva uppajjati, na maggo”ti. Nibbānārammaṇe appanajjhānavasena yathāparicchinnakālaṃ nirantaraṃ phalacittasseva pavattanaṃ samāpajjanaṃ [V 2.0488] phalasamāpattīti āha “phalasamāpattivasena nirodhe cittaṃ appetī”ti. Yadi anupubbavipassanānaṃ vasena phalasamāpattisamāpajjanaṃ, tena nīhārena sekkhassa uparimaggenāpi bhavitabbanti anuyogaṃ sandhāyāha “phalasamāpattininnatāyā”tiādi. Tena aññoyeva vipassanācāro ariyamaggāvaho, añño phalasamāpattiāvahoti dasseti, svāyaṃ vipassanāya vibhāgo vutto eva. Ye panāti abhayagirivāsino sandhāyāha. Te hi maggaphalavipassanāya āloḷetvā vadanti. Teneva hi “evaṃ satī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Arahā paccekabuddho bhavissati yadi itaratthāpi vipassanā tadatthāya saṃvatteyyāti adhippāyo. Pāḷivaseneva ca paṭikkhittanti “dasa gotrabhudhammā vipassanāvasena uppajjantī”ti maggatthā phalatthā vipassanā visuṃ katvā pavattapāḷivaseneva tesaṃ vacanaṃ paṭikkhittantipi na gahetabbaṃ, aññathā “dasa gotrabhudhammā”ti vacanaṃ virujjheyyāti. Idameva pana gahetabbanti vuttassevatthassa nigamanaṃ. Phalañcassātiādi mahaggatavipākānaṃ viya lokuttaravipākānañca kusalasarikkhatādassanaṃ. Jhānato sarikkhatādassaneneva cettha bojjhaṅgamaggaṅgavasenāpi sarikkhatā dassitāyevāti veditabbaṃ.

For this reason, the statement in the commentary—'For a trainee who contemplates formations by way of rise and fall, etc., for the purpose of making use of his own attainment of fruition, through the succession of insight-knowledges, only fruition arises, not the path'—is also established. Therefore, he said, 'Even for a trainee, only fruition arises, not the path.' The attainment of fruition is the uninterrupted occurrence of only the fruition-consciousness for a predetermined duration by way of absorption jhāna with Nibbāna as its object. Therefore, he said, 'He directs the mind to cessation by way of the attainment of fruition.' If the attainment of fruition were entered into by way of successive insights, then by that method, it should be possible for the trainee to attain even the higher path. With reference to this objection, he said, 'due to the inclination towards the attainment of fruition,' etc. By that, he shows that the practice of insight that brings the noble path is one thing, and that which brings the attainment of fruition is another. This distinction of insight has indeed been stated. With 'But those who...', he speaks with reference to the Abhayagirivāsins. For they speak after having confused the insight for the path and fruition. For that very reason, 'this being so,' etc., was said. The intention is that an Arahant or a Paccekabuddha would come to be if insight for another purpose were to lead to that result. And [the argument that their view] is refuted by the Pāḷi itself—because their statement is refuted by the very Pāḷi that proceeds by distinguishing insight for the sake of the path and insight for the sake of fruition, as in 'the ten gotrabhū-dhammas arise by way of insight'—this [argument] also should not be accepted. Otherwise, the statement 'the ten gotrabhū-dhammas' would be contradicted. But 'This very thing should be accepted' is the conclusion of the meaning that has just been stated. 'And his fruition,' etc., shows the similarity of supramundane resultants to wholesome states, just like the exalted resultants. And here, by showing the similarity with respect to jhāna, it should be understood that the similarity by way of the factors of enlightenment and the path factors is also shown.

864. Ṭhitiyāti pabandhaṭṭhitiyā. Yathāparicchinnakālañhi samāpattiyā pabandhavasenāvaṭṭhānaṃ idha ṭhitīti. “Cande vā sūriye vā ettakaṃ ṭhānaṃ gate vuṭṭhahissāmī”ti kālāvadhiggahaṇavasena samāpajjanaṃ cittassa abhisaṅkharaṇaṃ abhisaṅkhāro.

864. By 'stability' (ṭhiti) is meant the stability of continuity (pabandhaṭṭhiti). For here, stability is the abiding of the attainment (samāpatti) by way of continuity for a predetermined duration. Volitional formation (abhisaṅkhāro) is the determining (abhisaṅkharaṇaṃ) of the mind to enter the attainment by grasping a time limit, such as, “I will emerge when the moon or sun has reached this position.”

865. Sabbānevetānīti rūpanimittādisabbāneva etāni ekato kāmaṃ na manasi karoti asambhavato. Sabbasaṅgāhikavasenāti anavasesapariyādānavasena. Samudāyasaddā hi avayavesupi pavattanti[M 2.0520], avayavabyatirekena ca samudāyo na labbhatīti avayavagatampi kiccaṃ samudāyavasena vuttaṃ. Tasmāti sabbesaṃ saṅkhāranimittānaṃ ekato manasikārābhāvato. Yasmā bhavaṅgacitte uppanne phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhito nāma hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “yaṃ bhavaṅgassā”tiādi. Bhavaṅgassa ārammaṇaṃ nāma kammādi. Manasi karototi bhavaṅgasahagatena manasikārena manasi karoto, taṃ vā ārammaṇaṃ bhavaṅgamanasi karoto.

865. By 'all these indeed' is meant that one does not, it is true, attend to all these, such as the form-sign, at once, because of the impossibility. By 'by way of being all-encompassing' is meant by way of complete inclusion. For words for 'aggregate' also apply to the parts, and since an aggregate is not found apart from the parts, even a function pertaining to the parts is spoken of by way of the aggregate. Therefore: because of the absence of simultaneous attention to all conditioned signs. Since one is said to have emerged from the attainment of fruition when the life-continuum consciousness has arisen, it is for that reason said, 'that which is of the life-continuum,' etc. The object of the life-continuum is kamma, etc. By 'one attends' is meant: for one who attends with the attention associated with the life-continuum, or for one who makes that object the object in the life-continuum mind.

866. Phalassa phalameva vā anantaraṃ hoti purimassa purimassa pacchimaṃ pacchimaṃ. Bhavaṅgaṃ [V 2.0489] vā sabbapacchimassa. Phalānantaraṃ maggavīthiyaṃ, phalasamāpattiyañca. “Yena phalena nirodhā vuṭṭhānaṃ hotī”ti idaṃ phaluppattiyā nirodhā vuṭṭhānabhāvato vuttaṃ. Tanti nirodhāvuṭṭhānabhāvena vuttaṃ anāgāmiphalaṃ vā aggaphalaṃ vā. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanānantaranti nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa kusalassa, kiriyassa vā anantaraṃ satipi sattāhātikkame vijātiyena antarikattā.

866. Immediately after each preceding fruition is only the succeeding fruition. Or, after the very last fruition, there is the life-continuum. In the path-process and in the fruition-attainment-process, a state occurs immediately after fruition. This statement, 'emergence from cessation occurs through that fruition,' is said because emergence from cessation is by means of the arising of fruition. That which is spoken of as the emergence from cessation is either the fruition of non-returning or the highest fruition. By 'immediately after the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception' is meant: immediately after the wholesome or functional consciousness of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, even though seven days have passed, because of being interrupted by something of a different nature.

Paṭippassaddhadarathanti sabbaso passaddhakilesadarathaṃ. Amatārammaṇanti nibbānārammaṇaṃ. Subhanti asobhanatāya kilesassāpi abhāvato sobhanaṃ. Taṇhāsaṅkhātaṃ lokāmisaṃ vantaṃ chaḍḍitaṃ etenāti vantalokāmisaṃ. Vūpasantakilesatāya, susantatāya ca santaṃ. Yena dhammena yogato samaṇo nāma hoti, tassa ariyamaggasaṅkhātassa sāmaññassa phalanti sāmaññaphalaṃ.

By 'pacified distress' is meant the complete pacification of the distress that is the defilements. By 'having the deathless as its object' is meant having Nibbāna as its object. By 'beautiful' is meant beautiful because of the absence of the state of being unbeautiful and of even a defilement. By this, the worldly bait designated as craving has been vomited and discarded, hence 'one who has vomited worldly bait'. Peaceful because the defilements are pacified and because of its perfect peacefulness. One is called an ascetic (samaṇa) due to connection with a certain Dhamma; it is the fruit of that asceticism (sāmañña), which is designated as the noble path, hence 'the fruit of asceticism' (sāmaññaphala).

Ojavantenāti sabhāvasampannena. Sucināti kilesāsucivirahato parisuddhena. Sukhenāti anuttarasukhena. Abhisanditanti sabbaso lūkhabhāvāpagamanena sinehitaṃ. Sātātisātenāti mahaggatasātato, lokuttarakusalasātato ca ativiya sātena madhurena. Maggasukhatopi hi phalasukhaṃ santataratāya paṇītataraṃ. Amatena sammoditaṃ. “Madhuṃ viyā”ti iminā sātātisātataṃyeva vibhāveti.

By 'endowed with savor' is meant complete in its own nature. By 'pure' is meant utterly purified, being free from the impurity of defilements. By 'happiness' is meant unsurpassed happiness. By 'thoroughly saturated' is meant well-moistened, being completely free from coarseness. By 'exceedingly pleasant' is meant exceedingly pleasant and sweet, more so than the pleasantness of sublime happiness and the pleasantness of supramundane wholesome states. For indeed, the happiness of fruition is more sublime than the happiness of the path, due to its state of being more peaceful. Mixed with the deathless. By 'like honey', it reveals its very state of being exceedingly pleasant.

Tassa ariyassa phalassa rasabhūtaṃ sārabhūtaṃ taṃ sukhaṃ paññaṃ bhāvetvā yasmā paṇḍito vindati paṭilabhatīti yojanā.

The connection is that the wise one, having developed wisdom, attains and obtains that happiness, which is the flavor and essence of that Noble Fruition.

Nirodhasamāpattikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Attainment of Cessation

867. Tatrāti [M 2.0521] tasmiṃ “nirodhasamāpattiyā samāpajjanasamatthatā”ti saṃkhittavacane. Idaṃ sarūpādivasena pañhākammaṃ. Katthāti kasmiṃ bhave.

867. By 'herein' is meant: in that concise statement, 'the ability to enter the attainment of cessation.' This is the posing of a question by way of its nature, etc. By 'where?' is meant: in which existence?

868. Anupubbanirodhavasenāti vipassanānugatā aṭṭha samāpattiyo ārohantena taṃtaṃpaṭipakkhanirodhamukhena tiṇṇaṃ saṅkhārānaṃ anupubbato nirodhavasena. Yathāparicchinnakālaṃ yā cittacetasikānaṃ appavatti, ayaṃ nirodhasamāpattīti attho. Ke samāpajjanti, ke na samāpajjantīti [V 2.0490] kāmaṃ samāpajjanasamatthā padhānatāya paṭhamaṃ pucchitā, tabbissajjanaṃ pana garubhāvato pacchā vissajjetuṃ asamāpajjanake tāva dassento “sabbepi…pe… na samāpajjantī”ti āha yathā “vāmaṃ muñca, dakkhiṇaṃ gaṇhā”ti. Tattha “sabbepī”ti idaṃ puthujjanādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ visesanaṃ. Te hi aṭṭhannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ lābhinopi alābhino viya samādhismiṃ aparipūrakāritāya nirodhaṃ samāpajjituṃ na sakkonti. Kāmacchandādisamucchindanena hi samādhismiṃ paripūrakāritā, na jhānādhigamamattena. Anāgāmino, arahantoti ettha sukkhavipassakā ca anāgāmino, sukkhavipassakā ca arahantoti sukkhavipassakasaddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Ubhayepi cete satipi vipassanābale samādhibalassa abhāvato nirodhaṃ na samāpajjanti. Anupubbavihārasambhavataññevettha samādhibalaṃ icchitabbaṃ. Purimakā pana tayo satipi samādhibale vipassanābalassa abhāvato, aparipuṇṇattā ca samāpajjituṃ na sakkonti. Aparipuṇṇatā cassa saṅkhārānaṃ na sammā parimadditattā. Aṭṭha samāpatti…pe… samāpajjantī”ti vatvā tattha kāraṇaṃ pāḷivaseneva dassetuṃ “dvīhi balehī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tayo ca saṅkhārānanti ettha tayoti sāmiatthe paccattavacanaṃ, tiṇṇanti attho. Ñāṇacariyāhīti ñāṇappavattīhi. Nirodhasamāpattiyāti nirodhasamāpajjanāya ñāṇaṃ. Ayañca sampadāti ayaṃ baladvayasamannāgamādikā yathāvuttanirodhasamāpattiāvahā sampatti. Anāgāmikhīṇāsaveti anāgāmino ceva khīṇāsave ca.

868. By 'by way of successive cessation' is meant: for one ascending the eight attainments accompanied by insight, it is by way of the successive cessation of the three formations, through the cessation of their respective opposing factors. The non-occurrence of mind and mental factors for a defined period is the meaning of 'attainment of cessation'. As to 'Who attains it, and who does not?': although those capable of attaining it are asked about first due to their prominence, in order to give the answer for them later due to its gravity, he first indicates those who do not attain it, saying, 'All... do not attain it,' just as one might say, 'Leave the left, take the right.' Therein, the word 'all' is a qualifier for the three persons, beginning with the worldling. For they, even though they are attainers of the eight attainments, are like those who have not attained them; due to the incomplete fulfillment of their practice in regard to concentration, they are not able to attain cessation. For the complete fulfillment of the practice in regard to concentration is by means of cutting off sensual desire and so forth without remainder, not merely by the attainment of jhāna. Here, in the phrase 'non-returners, arahants,' the word 'dry-insight practitioner' should be applied to each separately, as: 'dry-insight non-returners' and 'dry-insight arahants.' And both of these, even though the power of insight is present, do not attain cessation due to the absence of the power of concentration. In this context, the power of concentration that is required is that which is accumulated through successive abidings. But the former three persons, even though the power of concentration is present, are not able to attain it due to the absence of the power of insight and due to its incompleteness. And this incompleteness is due to the formations not being properly subdued. Having said, 'Eight attainments... they attain,' in order to show the reason for that by means of the Pāḷi itself, 'by two powers,' etc., was stated. And here, in 'the three formations,' the word `tayo` is in the nominative case used in the sense of the genitive, meaning 'of the three.' By 'courses of knowledge' is meant 'the occurrences of knowledge.' By 'for the attainment of cessation' is meant 'knowledge for entering cessation'. And by 'this accomplishment' is meant this accomplishment which consists of being endowed with the two powers and so forth, and which brings about the attainment of cessation as described. By 'non-returners and those with cankers destroyed' is meant non-returners and arahants.

869. Samathabalanti kāmacchandādike paccanīkadhamme sametīti samatho, so eva paṭipakkhehi akampiyaṭṭhena balaṃ. Aniccādivasena vividhehi [M 2.0522] ākārehi passatīti vipassanā, sā eva vuttanayena balanti vipassanābalaṃ. Nekkhammavasenātiādīsu kāmacchandavikkhambhanassa nekkhammasaṅkappassa, alobhapadhānassa vā tathāpavattakusalacittuppādassa vasena cittassa ekaggatāsaṅkhāto yo avikkhepo, taṃ samathabalaṃ. Byāpādavikkhambhanassa abyāpādavitakkassa, adosapadhānassa vā tathāpavattakusalacittuppādassa vaseneva. Thinamiddhavikkhambhikāya vibhūtaṃ katvā manasikaraṇena upaṭṭhitaālokasaññāya vasena. Uddhaccavikkhambhanassa avikkhepassa samādhānassa vasena. Sakalamicchāvitakkavikkhambhanassa sikhāpattaānāpānassatisiddhapaṭinissaggānupassiassāsapassāsānaṃ vasena cittassa ekaggatāsaṅkhāto yo avikkhepo, taṃ samathabalanti atthayojanā.

869. The power of tranquility (samathabala): It pacifies opposing states such as sensual desire; thus, it is tranquility (samatha). That very tranquility is power (bala) in the sense of being unshakable by opposing forces. The power of insight (vipassanābala): It sees in various ways by means of impermanence and so forth; thus, it is insight (vipassanā). That very insight is power (bala) in the manner stated. In the passage beginning 'by way of renunciation,' the power of tranquility is that non-distraction of the mind, termed one-pointedness. It is established by means of the thought of renunciation which suppresses sensual desire, or by means of the arising of wholesome consciousness predominated by non-greed that occurs in such a way; by means of the thought of non-ill will which suppresses ill will, or by means of the arising of wholesome consciousness predominated by non-aversion that occurs in such a way; by means of the perception of light that has been established through attention that has made it manifest, which suppresses sloth and torpor; and by means of non-distraction and composure which suppresses restlessness. Furthermore, that non-distraction of the mind, termed one-pointedness, by means of the in-breaths and out-breaths observing relinquishment, accomplished by mindfulness of breathing that has reached its peak and which suppresses all wrong thoughts, is the power of tranquility. This is the application of the meaning.

Evaṃ [V 2.0491] upacārassa jhānassa vasena samathabalaṃ dassetvā idāni taṃ aṭṭhannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ vasena paṭipakkhehi anabhibhavanīyatāya ca balappattivasena dassetuṃ “paṭhamajjhānenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha nīvaraṇeti nīvaraṇanimittaṃ nīvaraṇapaccayā. Na kampati jhānasamaṅgipuggalo, jhānasampayuttasamādhi vā. So hi visesato idha “samathabala”nti adhippeto. Tathā hi kenaṭṭhena samathabalanti balaṭṭho pucchito. Uddhacceti uddhaccanimittaṃ. Uddhaccasahagatakileseti uddhaccena sampayuttamohaahirikādikilesahetu. Khandheti uddhaccasampayuttacatukkhandhanimittaṃ. Na kampatītiādīni aññamaññavevacanāni. Kampanaṃ vā ṭhānāpagamo. Calanaṃ paribbhamanaṃ. Vedhanaṃ sandhāvanaṃ. Uddhacce na kampati, uddhaccasahagatakilese na calati, uddhaccasahagatakkhandhe na vedhatīti vā yojetabbaṃ. Uddhaccaggahaṇañcettha samathassa ujupaṭipakkhatāya tadabhibhavena balappattidassanatthaṃ. Tenetaṃ aṭṭhannampi samāpattīnaṃ sādhāraṇato kiccātisayadassanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Idaṃ samathabalanti yāyaṃ nekkhammādivasena laddhāya cittekaggatāya nīvaraṇādīhi akampanīyatā, tāni ca abhibhavitvā avaṭṭhānaṃ, idaṃ samathabalaṃ.

Having thus shown the power of tranquility by means of access jhāna, now, in order to demonstrate it by way of the eight attainments, and by way of its unconquerability by opposing factors and its attainment of power, it is said, 'by the first jhāna,' and so on. Therein, 'by hindrances' means on account of the condition of hindrances. The person endowed with jhāna does not waver, nor does the concentration associated with jhāna. For that is specifically intended here as 'the power of tranquility.' Thus indeed, the meaning of 'power' is asked: 'In what sense is it the power of tranquility?' By 'restlessness' is meant on account of the condition of restlessness. By 'defilements accompanied by restlessness' is meant on account of the cause, which is the defilements such as delusion, shamelessness, and so on, associated with restlessness. By 'aggregates' is meant on account of the condition of the four mental aggregates associated with restlessness. 'Does not waver,' and so on, are synonyms for one another. Wavering is departure from stability. Shaking is spinning about. Trembling is running about. Or it should be connected thus: one does not waver on account of restlessness, one does not shake on account of defilements accompanied by restlessness, and one does not tremble on account of the aggregates accompanied by restlessness. And the taking up of restlessness here is for the purpose of showing the attainment of power by overcoming it, due to its being the direct opposite of tranquility. Therefore, this should be seen as showing the excellence of function common to all eight attainments. As to 'this is the power of tranquility': that unshakability by hindrances and the like, of the unification of mind attained by way of renunciation and so on, and its standing firm having overcome them—this is the power of tranquility.

Idāni vipassanābalaṃ niddisanto yasmā vipassanā saṅkhepato sattahi anupassanāhi saṅgahitā, tasmā tato tato samāpattito vuṭṭhāya tāsaṃ vasena anupassanā kātabbā, tattakeneva cettha anupassanākiccaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hotīti “aniccānupassanā vipassanābalaṃ…pe… paṭinissaggānupassanā vipassanābala”nti sarūpato dassetvā puna tā heṭṭhā [M 2.0523] vuttanayena visayavibhāgena dassetuṃ “rūpe aniccānupassanā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Idhāpi paṭipakkhehi anabhibhavanīyatāva balaṭṭhoti dassetuṃ “kenaṭṭhena vipassanābala”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha avijjāyāti dvādasasu akusalacittuppādesu avijjānimittaṃ. Avijjāsahagatakileseti avijjāya sampayuttalobhadosādikilesavatthunimittaṃ. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā suviññeyyameva. Avijjaggahaṇañcettha vipassanāya ujupaṭipakkhatāya tadabhibhavena balappattidassanatthaṃ. Tenetaṃ sattannampi anupassanānaṃ sādhāraṇato kiccātisayadassanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Idaṃ vipassanābalanti yāyaṃ aniccānupassanādivasena laddhassa vipassanāñāṇassa niccasaññādinimittaṃ akampanīyatā, tā ca abhibhavitvā avaṭṭhānaṃ, idaṃ vipassanābalaṃ.

Now, wishing to point out in detail the power of insight, since insight is briefly comprised of seven contemplations, therefore, having arisen from each respective attainment, contemplation should be done according to them. And by that much the task of contemplation here is fully accomplished. Thus, having shown it in essence, saying, 'Contemplation of impermanence is the power of insight... contemplation of relinquishment is the power of insight,' then to show them again by distinguishing the objects in the way stated below, it is said, 'Contemplation of impermanence in form,' and so on. Here too, to show that the meaning of power is precisely being unconquerable by opposing forces, it is begun, 'In what sense is the power of insight?' and so on. Therein, 'by ignorance' means on account of the cause which is ignorance in the twelve unwholesome consciousnesses. By 'defilements associated with ignorance' is meant on account of the cause which is the basis of defilements such as greed and hatred associated with ignorance. The rest is easily understood, being explained in the manner stated previously. And the mention of ignorance here is for the purpose of showing the attainment of power by overcoming it, due to its being the direct opponent of insight. Therefore, this should be seen as showing the surpassing function common to all seven contemplations. By 'this is the power of insight' is meant that unshakability of the insight-knowledge—attained by way of contemplation of impermanence and so on—against the sign of the perception of permanence and so on, and its standing firm having overcome them—this is the power of insight.

Vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhārā vācaṃ saṅkharonti pavattentīti katvā. Tenāha “pubbe kho, āvuso visākha, vitakketvā vicāretvā pacchā vācaṃ bhindati, tasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro”ti [V 2.0492] (ma. ni. 1.463; saṃ. ni. 4.348). Te pana dutiyajjhāne vūpasantā hontīti āha “dutiyajjhānaṃ…pe… paṭippassaddhā hontī”ti. Kāyena saṅkharīyantīti kāyasaṅkhārā, assāsapassāsā. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “assāsapassāsā kho, āvuso visākha, kāyikā ete dhammā kāyappaṭibaddhā, tasmā assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro”ti (ma. ni. 1.463; saṃ. ni. 4.348). Te pana yasmā catutthajjhāne vūpasantā honti, tasmā āha “catutthajjhānaṃ…pe… paṭippassaddhā hontī”ti. Cittena saṅkharīyantīti cittasaṅkhārā, saññā vedanā. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā ete dhammā cittappaṭibaddhā, tasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.463; saṃ. ni. 4.348). Te pana yasmā nirodhaṃ samāpannassa vūpasamanti, tasmā vuttaṃ “saññāvedayita…pe… paṭippassaddhā hontī”ti.

Initial thought and sustained thought are verbal formations (vacīsaṅkhārā) because they form and produce speech. Therefore, it is said: 'First, friend Visākha, having applied initial thought and sustained thought, one afterwards utters speech; that is why initial thought and sustained thought are the verbal formation.' However, since these are stilled in the second jhāna, it is said: 'The second jhāna... they are tranquilized.' In-breaths and out-breaths are bodily formations (kāyasaṅkhārā) because they are conditioned by the body. For it is said: 'In-breaths and out-breaths, friend Visākha, are bodily phenomena, bound up with the body; that is why in-breaths and out-breaths are the bodily formation.' Yet, since these are stilled in the fourth jhāna, it is said: 'The fourth jhāna... they are tranquilized.' Perception and feeling are mental formations (cittasaṅkhārā) because they are conditioned by the mind. For it is said: 'Perception and feeling are mental phenomena, bound up with the mind; that is why perception and feeling are the mental formation.' However, since these are stilled for one who has attained cessation, it is said: 'The cessation of perception and feeling... they are tranquilized.'

Ñāṇacariyāsu vivaṭṭānupassanāggahaṇeneva tassa ādibhūtā sesānupassanāpi gahitāva honti tadavinābhāvato. Maggo ñāṇacariyā, phalasamāpatti ñāṇacariyāti maggaphalasamāpattīnaṃ ñāṇacariyābhāvavacanaṃ maggaphaladhammānaṃ ñāṇapadhānattā, ñāṇena vā indriyādhipatihetumaggapaccayādivasena sātisayapaccayabhūtena sesā maggaphaladhammā caritā pavattitāti katvā tathā vuttaṃ. Samādhicariyāsupi eseva nayo[M 2.0524]. Imāhi soḷasahīti aṭṭhannaṃ anupassanānaṃ, aṭṭhannañca maggaphalañāṇānaṃ vasena imāhi soḷasahi ñāṇapavattīhi.

Among the practices of knowledge, by the very grasping of the contemplation of turning away, the remaining contemplations which are its basis are also grasped, due to their inseparability from it. The path is a practice of knowledge, the attainment of fruition is a practice of knowledge—thus, the statement that the path and the attainment of fruition are practices of knowledge is due to the predominance of knowledge in the states of path and fruition. Alternatively, it is so called because the remaining states of path and fruition are made to occur by knowledge, which has become a surpassing condition by way of the faculty, dominance, root, and path conditions, and so on. The same principle applies to the practices of concentration. The phrase 'by these sixteen' refers to these sixteen occurrences of knowledge, by way of the eight contemplations and the eight knowledges of path and fruition.

Navahi samādhicariyāhīti aṭṭha samāpattiyo aṭṭha samādhicariyā, tāsaṃ upacārasamādhi upacārasamādhibhāvanāsāmaññena ekā samādhicariyāti evaṃ navahi samādhicariyāhi. Tenāha “paṭhamajjhānaṃ samādhicariyā”tiādi. Paṭhamajjhānapaṭilābhatthāya vitakko cātiādi nānāvajjanupacāravasena vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ, uparisamāpattīnampi upacārassa tatheva vuttattā. Na hi ekāvajjane catutthajjhānādiupacāre pītiādayo sambhavanti. Ettha ca “paṭhamajjhānapaṭilābhatthāyā”tiādivacanena upacārasamādhissāpi pāripūrī icchitabbāti dasseti. Kiṃ panettha samathabalasamādhicariyānaṃ nānattaṃ, kiṃ vā vipassanābalalokiyañāṇacariyānaṃ? Yathā samathabalepi “nekkhammavasenā”tiādinā upacārasamādhinā saddhiṃ aṭṭhasu samāpattīsu appanāsamādhiyeva vutto, tathā samādhicariyāsu, vipassanābalalokiyañāṇacariyāsu ca vipassanāva vuttāti? Kiñcāpi vuttā, vivaṭṭānupassanā pana purecarañāṇādivipassanābale avuttā [V 2.0493] eva ñāṇacariyāsu vuttā. Apica paṭipakkhehi akampiyaṭṭho balaṭṭho, pañcannaṃ vasībhāvānaṃ vasena suciṇṇatā cariyaṭṭho, eteneva samathabalasamādhicariyānampi nānattaṃ saṃvaṇṇitanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

"By nine practices of concentration": The eight attainments are eight practices of concentration; their access concentration, by reason of the commonality of being the cultivation of access concentration, is one practice of concentration. Thus, there are nine practices of concentration. Therefore, it is said, "The first jhāna is a practice of concentration," and so on. It should be understood that the statement beginning, "For the attainment of the first jhāna, there is initial application..." is stated by way of various advertences and access concentrations, since the access concentration of the higher attainments is also spoken of in the same way. For in the access concentration of the fourth jhāna and so on, which has a single advertence, rapture and so on do not arise. And here, by the statement beginning, "for the attainment of the first jhāna," it is shown that the fulfillment of access concentration is also intended. What, here, is the difference between the power of serenity and the practice of concentration? Or what is the difference between the power of insight and the worldly practice of knowledge? Is it that just as in the power of serenity, by the phrase beginning, "by way of renunciation," only absorption concentration is spoken of in the eight attainments, together with access concentration, so too in the practices of concentration, and in the power of insight and the worldly practices of knowledge, only insight is spoken of? Although it is so spoken, the contemplation of turning away, however, which is not spoken of at all in the power of insight which includes the preceding knowledges and so on, is spoken of in the practices of knowledge. Furthermore, the meaning of "power" is the state of being unshaken by opposing factors; the meaning of "practice" is the state of being well-practiced by way of the five masteries. By this very distinction, it should be understood that the difference between the power of serenity and the practice of concentration is also explained.

Vasībhāvatā paññāti ettha vaso etassa atthīti vasī, tassa bhāvo vasībhāvo, sā eva vasībhāvatā. “Vasiyo”ti pana pāḷiyaṃ itthiliṅgavasena vuttattā tāyo dassetuṃ “vasīti pañca vasiyo”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha jhānaṃ āvajjantassa nirantaraṃ jhānaṅgesu cittappavattanasamatthatā āvajjanavasī. Samāpajjitukāmassa sīghaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjanasamatthatā samāpajjanavasī. Accharāmattaṃ vā katipayaccharāmattaṃ vā khaṇaṃ jhānaṃ ṭhapetuṃ samatthatā adhiṭṭhānavasī. Tatheva lahuṃ vuṭṭhātuṃ samatthatā vuṭṭhānavasī. Paccavekkhaṇavasī pana āvajjanavasiyā eva sijjhati. Paccavekkhaṇajavanāneva hi tattha āvajjanānantarānīti. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana heṭṭhā āgato eva. Ayañca vasībhāvo samādhicariyānaṃ vasena vutto. Ñāṇacariyāsu pana lokuttarānaṃ ñāṇacariyānaṃ vasībhāvāpādanakiccaṃ nāma natthi. Paṭipakkhassa suvihatattā sabhāvasiddho tattha [M 2.0525] vasībhāvo, lokiyānaṃ pana paguṇabalavabhāvāpādanena vasībhāvo labbhateva.

Herein, regarding the term `vasībhāvatā`: one is a `vasī` (master) because 'control (`vaso`) over this exists for him'; the state (`bhāvo`) of that master is `vasībhāva` (mastery); that very state is `vasībhāvatā`. However, since in the Pāli it is stated in the feminine gender as `vasiyo`, in order to indicate them, the passage beginning 'The five masteries (`vasiyo`)...' is stated. Therein, for one who adverts to a jhāna, the ability to continuously direct the mind toward the jhāna factors is the mastery of advertence. For one who wishes to attain, the ability to attain jhāna quickly is the mastery of attainment. The ability to establish the jhāna for a period of a finger-snap or a few finger-snaps is the mastery of resolve. Likewise, the ability to emerge swiftly is the mastery of emergence. The mastery of reviewing, however, is accomplished by means of the mastery of advertence itself, for therein, the moments immediately following advertence are indeed the reviewing impulsion moments. This is the summary here; the detailed explanation has already been given below. And this mastery is spoken of in terms of the practices of concentration. In the practices of knowledge, however, for the supramundane practices of knowledge, there is no such task as bringing about mastery. Because the opposing factor has been thoroughly eliminated, mastery therein is accomplished by its own intrinsic nature. For the mundane practices, however, mastery is indeed obtained by bringing about a state of proficiency and strength.

870. Ukkaṭṭhaniddesoti anavasesaniddeso. Cuddasahi ñāṇacariyāhi hoti aggamaggaphalānaṃ anadhigatattāti. Yadi evanti yadi ukkaṭṭhaniddesavasena “soḷasahi ñāṇacariyāhī”ti vuttaṃ, tato avakaṃsavasenapi icchitabbaṃ, evaṃ sante kiṃ na hoti nirodhasamāpajjananti adhippāyo. Pañca kāmaguṇā vatthubhūtā etassa santīti pañcakāmaguṇiko, kāmarāgo. Appahīnattā asamucchinnattā. Na hi kāmarāgassa vikkhambhanappahānamattaṃ nirodhassa adhiṭṭhānaṃ bhavituṃ sakkoti. Tasmāti samādhipāripanthikassa kāmarāgassa supahīnattā. Etena kāmaṃ maggaphalañāṇacariyā lokiyañāṇasamādhicariyā viya nirodhasamāpajjane sarūpena na viniyujjanti tadā appavattanato, tassa tassa pana paṭipakkhassa samucchindanena balacariyānaṃ visesapaccayatāya nirodhasamāpattiyā adhiṭṭhānaṃ hotīti dasseti. Esāti anāgāmī. Idañhi “nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassā”tiādivacanaṃ anāgāminova nirodhā vuṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusala”nti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.417) vacanato, aññathā “nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakiriyā”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.417) vucceyya.

870. The term `ukkaṭṭhaniddeso` means an explanation without remainder. It is by fourteen practices of knowledge because the supreme path and fruition have not yet been attained. If this is so—that if 'by sixteen practices of knowledge' is spoken of by way of an exhaustive explanation—then it should also be desired by way of a lesser scope. This being so, why does the attainment of cessation not occur? This is the intention. The five strands of sensual pleasure exist as the basis for this, hence it is called `pañcakāmaguṇiko`, which is sensual desire, because it has not been abandoned or eradicated. Indeed, the mere suppression-abandonment of sensual desire cannot become the foundation for cessation. Therefore: because sensual desire, which is an obstacle to concentration, is thoroughly abandoned. By this, it is shown that although the path-and-fruition practices of knowledge, like the worldly practices of knowledge and practices of concentration, are not employed in their own nature in the attainment of cessation due to their non-occurrence at that time, they are nevertheless a foundation for the attainment of cessation by being a special condition for the powers and practices through the eradication of their respective opposing factors. `Esā` refers to the non-returner. Indeed, this statement beginning with 'for one emerging from cessation' was spoken in reference to the emergence from cessation of a non-returner only, because it is said, 'wholesome [consciousness] of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.' Otherwise, it would be said, 'functional [consciousness] of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.'

871. “Pañcavokārabhave”ti [V 2.0494] kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu catuvokārabhavepi arūpajjhānavasena yathārahaṃ anupubbasamāpatti labbhatīti? Kāmaṃ labbhati, sā pana “anupubbasamāpattī”ti na vuccati ekadesabhāvato. Aṭṭhasamāpattivaseneva ca “anupubbasamāpattī”ti vuccatīti dassento āha “paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ uppatti natthī”ti. Vatthussa abhāvāti hadayavatthuno abhāvāti vadanti, karajakāyasaṅkhātassa pana vatthuno abhāvāti attho. Yadi hi āruppe nirodhaṃ samāpajjeyya, cittacetasikānaṃ, aññassa ca kassaci abhāvato apaññattikova bhaveyya anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbutasadiso. Kiñcāyaṃ upādāya nirodhaṃ samāpannoti vucceyya, kiṃ vā etāya vatthucintāya. Aṅgavekallatova natthi āruppe nirodhasamāpattisamāpajjanaṃ.

871. Why is it said, 'in the five-constituent existence'? Is it not that in the four-constituent existence, too, the sequential attainment is obtained as appropriate by means of the formless absorptions? It is indeed obtained, but that is not called 'sequential attainment' because it is partial. And showing that it is called 'sequential attainment' only by means of the eight attainments, he said, 'there is no arising of the first jhāna, and so on.' 'Due to the absence of a basis': some say this means due to the absence of the heart-basis, but the meaning is the absence of the basis called the physical body. For if one were to attain cessation in the formless realm, due to the absence of mind and mental factors and of anything else whatsoever, one would become undesignatable, similar to one who has attained Parinibbāna with the Nibbāna element without residue. And with reference to what could it be said of this person, 'He has attained cessation'? Or what is the use of this consideration of a basis? It is precisely due to a deficiency of factors that there is no entering into the attainment of cessation in the formless realm.

872. Saṅkhārānaṃ [M 2.0526] pavattibhedeti saṅkhatadhammānaṃ khaṇe khaṇe uppajjane, bhijjane ca, tesaṃ vā kusalādibhedabhinne yathārahaṃ tīhi dukkhatāhi upaddute pavattivibhāge. Cittacetasikavigamehi rūpadhammesu labbhamānāpi saṅkhāradukkhatā abbohārikataṃ āpajjati. Ukkaṇṭhitvāti nibbinditvā. Nibbānaṃ patvāti anupādisesanibbānaṃ patvā viya. Sukhanti niddukkhaṃ.

872. 'In the differentiation of the occurrence of formations' means: in the moment-by-moment arising and breaking up of conditioned phenomena, or alternatively, in the distinct occurrence of those formations—differentiated by the divisions of wholesome and so on—which is, as appropriate, afflicted by the three kinds of suffering. Indeed, when mind and mental factors are absent, the suffering of formations, although found in material phenomena, becomes undesignated. 'Having become disgusted' means having become disenchanted. 'Having attained Nibbāna' is like having attained Nibbāna without residue. 'Happily' means free from suffering.

873. Samathavipassanāvasenāti yuganaddhānaṃ viya aññamaññūpakāritāya sahitānaṃ vasena. Ussakkitvāti ukkaṃsaṃ patvā yāva nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā, yāva ca anulomañāṇā āruhitvā. Nirodhayatoti nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjitvā taṃ nirodhentassa. Aññassa kassacipi cittassa anuppajjanena evamassā nirodhasamāpattiyā samāpajjanaṃ hoti. “Yo hī”tiādinā “samathavipassanāvasenā”ti vuttamevatthaṃ byatirekamukhena vivarati. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiṃ patvā tiṭṭhati taduddhaṃ suddhasamathavipassanāya abhāvato. Yo vipassanāvaseneva ussakkati sace ariyo phalasamāpattatthiko, so attano phalasamāpattiṃ patvā tiṭṭhati. Atha puthujjano, sekho vā maggatthiko tāya ce vipassanāya maggaṃ patvā phale ṭhito, sopi phalasamāpattiṃ patvā tiṭṭhaticceva vuccati. Soti ubhayavasena paṭipanno. Tanti nirodhasamāpattiṃ.

873. 'By the power of serenity and insight' means: by the power of those that are conjoined, by the state of being mutually beneficial, like a yoked pair. 'Having ascended step-by-step' means: having reached excellence, having ascended up to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and up to conformity-knowledge. 'For one who causes to cease' means: for one who, having attained the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, causes it to cease. Thus, through the non-arising of any other consciousness, the attainment of this attainment of cessation occurs. By the text beginning with, “For one who…,” he explains, by way of exclusion, the very meaning that was stated as “by the power of serenity and insight.” Having reached the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one remains, due to the absence of pure serenity and insight beyond that. If a noble one, desirous of the attainment of fruition, ascends by the power of insight alone, he, having reached his own attainment of fruition, remains. Or, if a worldling or a trainee, desirous of the path, having reached the path by that insight, is established in the fruition, he too is indeed said to remain, having reached the attainment of fruition. 'He' refers to one who has practiced by means of both. 'That' refers to the attainment of cessation.

874. Yena phaladvayasamannāgamādinā nirodhaṃ samāpajjituṃ samattho hoti, so vidhi pageva vibhāvitoti samāpajjanākārameva dassento “katabhattakicco”tiādimāha. Tañhi sabbāsampi [V 2.0495] bhāvanānaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ pubbakiccaṃ. Tattha saṅkhāreti tasmiṃ paṭhamajjhāne, paṭhamajjhānacittuppāde vā saṅkhāre.

874. Because the procedure—such as being endowed with the two fruitions—by which one is able to attain cessation has already been explained, therefore, showing only the mode of attainment, he stated the text beginning with, “having completed the meal-duty.” For that is a preliminary duty common to all developments. Therein, 'the formations' means the formations in that first jhāna, or in the arising of the first jhāna consciousness.
